achaval-ferrer.name: Achával-Ferrer
achaval-ferrer.line: A Mendoza estate known for single vineyard Malbecs from old vines.
achaval-ferrer.tell: Achával-Ferrer bottles Malbec by vineyard: Finca Altamira, Finca Bella Vista and Finca Mirador. Each is concentrated and deep, with dark fruit and violet. A great comparison for a Malbec lover.

agrapart.name: Agrapart
agrapart.line: A celebrated Avize grower making mineral, low-dosage grand cru Blanc de Blancs.
agrapart.tell: Agrapart is one of the great grower names in Avize. The wines are pure Chardonnay, intense and chalky, often with little or no added sugar. A bottle for a guest who loves precise, serious Champagne.

akutain.name: Bodega Akutain
akutain.line: A small family bodega in Rioja.
akutain.tell: Akutain is a small family winery in Rioja. Expect classic Tempranillo: red fruit, spice and a touch of oak. Ask the sommelier about the ageing category of this bottle.

alain-chavy.name: Domaine Alain Chavy
alain-chavy.line: A family estate in Puligny making classic whites.
alain-chavy.tell: Alain Chavy is a Puligny-Montrachet family estate. Champ Gain is a premier cru, and the village Puligny is floral and fine.

alain-graillot.name: Alain Graillot
alain-graillot.line: The domaine that set the standard for Crozes-Hermitage, making fresh, whole cluster Syrah; now run by his son Maxime.
alain-graillot.tell: Graillot made Crozes-Hermitage famous for quality. The Syrah is fresh, peppery and dark fruited. A great value choice with lamb or steak.

albert-bichot.name: Albert Bichot
albert-bichot.line: A large family négociant in Beaune that also owns domaines, among them Clos Frantin in Nuits and Domaine du Pavillon in Pommard.
albert-bichot.tell: Bichot is a big Beaune house that owns its own vineyards as well as buying grapes; bottles marked Clos Frantin or Domaine du Pavillon come from those estates. The style is polished and dependable. A good way to give a guest a named village or premier cru from a trusted house.

albert-boxler.name: Albert Boxler
albert-boxler.line: A small, revered estate in Niedermorschwihr, famed for grand cru Riesling from the Brand and Sommerberg.
albert-boxler.tell: Boxler is one of Alsace's most admired small estates. Brand and Sommerberg are grand crus, and the Rieslings are intense, dry and mineral. The Muscat and Edelzwicker blend are lighter, aromatic surprises.

albert-ponnelle.name: Albert Ponnelle
albert-ponnelle.line: A Beaune négociant house bottling village and premier cru wines across the Côte d'Or in a classic, traditional style.
albert-ponnelle.tell: Ponnelle is a long established Beaune house. Its Volnay is the gentle, perfumed side of the Côte de Beaune: red cherry, soft tannin, made to go with food. Ask the sommelier how this vintage is drinking.

alberto-nanclares.name: Alberto Nanclares
alberto-nanclares.line: A small Galician grower best known for Albariño, also making red from Ribeira Sacra.
alberto-nanclares.tell: Alberto Nanclares is a small Galician grower known for fresh, natural minded Albariño. This red comes from Ribeira Sacra, steep river terraces inland: light, fresh and mineral. Ask the sommelier about the grape.

alex-foillard.name: Alex Foillard
alex-foillard.line: The son of Jean Foillard, making his own natural leaning cru Beaujolais, here Brouilly.
alex-foillard.tell: Alex Foillard is the son of Jean Foillard, one of the great Morgon names. His Brouilly is juicy, bright and fresh. Great with lighter dishes, and serve it slightly cool.

alex-moreau.name: Domaine Alex Moreau
alex-moreau.line: The newer label of Alex Moreau, of the Bernard Moreau family in Chassagne-Montrachet, focused on precise wines from family vineyards.
alex-moreau.tell: Alex Moreau comes from a well regarded Chassagne family and now bottles under his own name. The red Chassagne from old vines is a fresh, firm Pinot Noir, and the Passe-Tout-Grains is a light, easy blend of Pinot and Gamay. Both suit lighter meat dishes.

alexana.name: Alexana
alexana.tell: Alexana is an Oregon winery. Hillsides is a fresh white; ask the sommelier about its grapes.

alexander-valley-vineyards.name: Alexander Valley Vineyards
alexander-valley-vineyards.line: A family estate in the Alexander Valley making approachable, fairly priced reds.
alexander-valley-vineyards.tell: Alexander Valley Vineyards is a long standing family estate in northern Sonoma. The Merlot is soft and plummy, easy to enjoy. Here in half bottle, a good value pick for one or two guests.

alice-olivier-de-moor.name: Alice et Olivier De Moor
alice-olivier-de-moor.line: A small organic estate in Courgis making natural-leaning Chablis and Aligoté.
alice-olivier-de-moor.tell: The De Moors farm organically and make wines with little intervention. Mont de Milieu is a premier cru; Bel Air et Clardy and L'Humeur du Temps are Chablis; Plantation 1902 is an old-vine Aligoté.

altesino.name: Altesino
altesino.line: A Montalcino estate known for its Brunello from the famous Montosoli hill.
altesino.tell: Altesino is a well known Montalcino estate. Its Brunello is classic and balanced; Montosoli is a famous hill north of town, giving a finer, more perfumed Brunello. Great with beef.

altos-ibericos.name: Altos Ibéricos
altos-ibericos.line: A Rioja label from the Torres family of Catalonia.
altos-ibericos.tell: Altos Ibéricos is the Torres family's Rioja. The Reserva is Tempranillo aged in oak: red fruit, vanilla and spice. A smooth, reliable Rioja at a fair price.

amon-ra.name: Amon-Ra (Glaetzer)
amon-ra.line: A Barossa Shiraz from the Glaetzer family, made from old vines.
amon-ra.tell: Amon-Ra is the Glaetzer family's old vine Barossa Shiraz: dense, dark and rich, with blackberry and spice. A big wine for a guest who loves Australian Shiraz.

amuse-bouche.name: Amuse Bouche
amuse-bouche.line: A small Napa winery making a Merlot led, Pomerol style blend, created with winemaker Heidi Barrett.
amuse-bouche.tell: Amuse Bouche was set up with Heidi Barrett, a celebrated Napa winemaker, to make a Pomerol style red: Merlot with Cabernet Franc. It is plush, round and dark fruited. A great choice for a guest who loves Merlot or Right Bank Bordeaux.

anakota.name: Anakota
anakota.line: A Knights Valley estate making powerful mountain Cabernet from volcanic hillsides.
anakota.tell: Anakota farms volcanic hillsides in Knights Valley, between Napa and Sonoma. The Cabernets are dark, firm and concentrated; Helena Montana is a single vineyard. Good with beef; decant if young.

ancient-oak-cellars.name: Ancient Oak Cellars
ancient-oak-cellars.line: A small family winery in Sonoma working with family vineyards, known for Cabernet Franc.
ancient-oak-cellars.tell: Ancient Oak is a small family winery in Sonoma. Alcaeus is a Cabernet Franc based blend from Sonoma Mountain: red and black fruit, herbs and fine tannin. A thoughtful pick for a guest who likes Loire or Right Bank reds.

andre-perret.name: André Perret
andre-perret.line: A Chavanay family estate, a reference for Condrieu, including the steep Chéry hillside.
andre-perret.tell: André Perret is a leading name in Condrieu, pure Viognier. Chéry is a famous steep site; Clos Chanson another. Floral, apricot-scented and rich, wonderful with crab and spiced dishes.

andrew-geoffrey.name: Andrew Geoffrey Vineyards
andrew-geoffrey.line: A small hillside estate high on Diamond Mountain, making Cabernet Sauvignon from volcanic soils.
andrew-geoffrey.tell: Andrew Geoffrey farms a small vineyard high on Diamond Mountain, above Calistoga, on pale volcanic soil. The Cabernet is firm and concentrated, with dark currant fruit and a herbal edge. The half bottle is a handy way to give two guests a mountain Napa Cabernet.

andrew-will.name: Andrew Will
andrew-will.line: A respected Washington winery making Bordeaux style blends from Columbia Valley vineyards.
andrew-will.tell: Andrew Will makes blends in the Bordeaux style from Washington vineyards. Sorella, from Horse Heaven Hills, is the flagship: Cabernet led, structured and fine. A good choice for a Bordeaux lover who wants something new.

anne-gros.name: Domaine Anne Gros
anne-gros.line: One of Vosne-Romanée's most admired domaines, run by Anne Gros, known for silky, pure, elegant reds from Bourgogne up to Richebourg.
anne-gros.tell: Anne Gros makes some of the most graceful wines in Vosne-Romanée. Even the regional wines show polish, and the grand crus are rare and refined. A strong recommendation for a guest who prizes elegance over power.

antica-terra.name: Antica Terra
antica-terra.line: An Eola-Amity Hills estate known for intense, perfumed Pinot Noir made in very small amounts.
antica-terra.tell: Antica Terra farms a steep, rocky site in the Eola-Amity Hills. Its Pinot Noirs are layered and fragrant, with real depth; Obelin is one of its named cuvées. Rare and much admired. A treat for a Pinot lover; ask the sommelier about the vintage.

antinori.name: Marchesi Antinori
antinori.line: One of Italy's oldest wine families, whose Tignanello and Solaia helped create the Super Tuscan style.
antinori.tell: Antinori is one of the great Florentine wine families. Tignanello, Sangiovese with Cabernet, was one of the first Super Tuscans; Solaia, mostly Cabernet, is the grander one. Both are rich, polished and long lived. Guests often know the names.

antoine-graillot-raul-perez.name: Antoine Graillot and Raúl Pérez
antoine-graillot-raul-perez.line: A collaboration in Bierzo between a winemaker from the Rhône and Raúl Pérez.
antoine-graillot-raul-perez.tell: Encinas is a Bierzo red made as a collaboration between Antoine Graillot, from a Crozes-Hermitage family, and Raúl Pérez. Mencía from Bierzo: fresh, peppery and red fruited. A good swap for a Northern Rhône lover.

antoine-jobard.name: Antoine Jobard
antoine-jobard.line: A Meursault family domaine famous for long lived, tightly wound white wines, which also makes small amounts of red from the Côte de Beaune.
antoine-jobard.tell: Jobard is a name white Burgundy lovers know well, so a red from this cellar is something of a curiosity. Expect a precise, firm Pinot Noir that rewards a little air. A good talking point for a guest who already drinks the whites.

antonin-guyon.name: Antonin Guyon
antonin-guyon.line: A family domaine based in Savigny-lès-Beaune with vineyards from the Hautes-Côtes to Corton and Volnay, making traditional, well structured reds.
antonin-guyon.tell: Guyon farms a wide spread of vineyards across both Côtes. Their Volnay Clos des Chênes comes from one of the village's best known premier crus, a slope that gives a bit more grip than most Volnay. Recommend it with roast meats and game birds.

antonin-rodet.name: Antonin Rodet
antonin-rodet.line: A Mercurey based négociant house bottling wines from across Burgundy, here a Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru.
antonin-rodet.tell: Rodet is a long standing house from the Côte Chalonnaise. Clos de Thorey is a premier cru in Nuits-Saint-Georges, so expect darker fruit and firmer tannin than the villages to the north. A sturdy partner for beef or duck.

aphelion.name: Aphelion Wine Co.
aphelion.line: A McLaren Vale label devoted to Grenache from old bush vines.
aphelion.tell: Aphelion focuses on Grenache from old bush vines in McLaren Vale. Brini, Wait and Hickinbotham are separate vineyards, picked early for freshness: red fruit, spice and silky texture. Great for a Pinot or Rhône lover.

ar-pe-pe.name: Ar.Pe.Pe.
ar-pe-pe.line: A family estate in alpine Valtellina making fine, long lived Nebbiolo from steep terraces.
ar-pe-pe.tell: Ar.Pe.Pe. farms steep terraces in Valtellina, in the Alps near Switzerland, where Nebbiolo is called Chiavennasca. The wines are lighter and more delicate than Barolo: fragrant, fresh and fine. Sassella, Grumello and Inferno are named sites. A great pick for a Burgundy lover.

araujo.name: Araujo (Eisele Vineyard)
araujo.line: The estate built on the Eisele Vineyard near Calistoga, one of the historic great Cabernet sites of Napa.
araujo.tell: Eisele Vineyard, near Calistoga, has been famous for Cabernet for decades, and Araujo made it a cult name. The wine is deep, structured and fine, built to age. This magnum is a celebration bottle; involve the sommelier for decanting and service.

arcadian.name: Arcadian
arcadian.line: A Central Coast winery making restrained, Burgundy minded Pinot Noir and Chardonnay, often released with some age.
arcadian.tell: Arcadian makes Pinot Noir in a quiet, Burgundian way, picking for freshness and often holding wines back before release. Expect red fruit, earth and a silky texture rather than power. The magnum of Francesca is a good bottle for a table that loves Pinot.

arcanum.name: Arcanum
arcanum.line: A Tuscan estate near Castelnuovo Berardenga making Bordeaux style reds.
arcanum.tell: Arcanum is a Tuscan estate making Bordeaux style reds in the south of Chianti country. The Toscana Rosso is rich and polished, with dark fruit. A good choice for a guest who loves Napa or Bordeaux.

argyle.name: Argyle
argyle.line: A Dundee Hills winery built around traditional method sparkling wine, one of Oregon's pioneers in the style.
argyle.tell: Argyle makes sparkling wine the Champagne way in Oregon. The Brut is crisp and appley; Extended Tirage spends longer on its lees, toastier; Julia Lee's Block is a single vineyard Blanc de Blancs. An American bubble with real finesse.

arkenstone.name: Arkenstone
arkenstone.tell: Arkenstone is a Howell Mountain estate in Napa. Its Sauvignon Blanc is rich and textured, a serious white.

armand-de-brignac.name: Armand de Brignac
armand-de-brignac.line: The Champagne in the metallic gold "Ace of Spades" bottle, ripe and rich in style.
armand-de-brignac.tell: Armand de Brignac is the Ace of Spades, known on sight for its gold metallic bottle. The Gold Brut is ripe and full, with a creamy texture. Guests who ask for it usually want the bottle as much as the wine, so present it with ceremony.

armand-rousseau.name: Domaine Armand Rousseau
armand-rousseau.line: Perhaps the most famous name in Gevrey-Chambertin, revered for elegant, perfumed reds from Chambertin and the Clos Saint-Jacques premier cru.
armand-rousseau.tell: Rousseau is a reference point for all of Burgundy. Clos Saint-Jacques is a premier cru often spoken of in the same breath as the grand crus. A trophy bottle: handle it with ceremony and suggest a gentle decant.

arnaldo-caprai.name: Arnaldo Caprai
arnaldo-caprai.line: The estate that championed Sagrantino di Montefalco, a dark, very tannic Umbrian red.
arnaldo-caprai.tell: Caprai did more than anyone to make Sagrantino known. It is one of the most tannic reds in the world: dark, powerful and long. The 25 Anni bottling is the flagship. Decant, and pair with braised meat or game.

arnaud-mortet.name: Arnaud Mortet
arnaud-mortet.line: The son of the late Denis Mortet, who now runs the family domaine and also bottles wines under his own name in Gevrey-Chambertin.
arnaud-mortet.tell: Arnaud took over the Mortet domaine and added a small range under his own label. The wines are deep coloured, ripe and carefully made Gevrey. A good choice for a guest who wants a powerful red Burgundy.

ashanta.name: Ashanta
ashanta.line: A small natural-wine label founded by Chenoa Ashton-Lewis and Will Basanta, working with organic vineyards.
ashanta.tell: Ashanta is a small natural-wine label from a young California couple. Calypso is a Chardonnay made with nothing added or taken away, so it is crisp, zesty and mineral, far from buttery California. A good talking point for an adventurous guest.

au-bon-climat.name: Au Bon Climat
au-bon-climat.region: Santa Maria Valley, Santa Barbara County
au-bon-climat.line: The Santa Barbara winery founded by Jim Clendenen, which championed balanced, Burgundy style Pinot Noir and Chardonnay in California.
au-bon-climat.tell: Au Bon Climat helped put Santa Barbara on the map with fresh, balanced wines in the Burgundy mould. The Pinot Noirs, like Isabelle, Knox Alexander and La Bauge au Dessus, are bright and savoury rather than heavy. Hildegard is a richer white blend. A smart choice for a guest who likes Burgundy.

aubry.name: Aubry
aubry.line: A family grower near Reims known for reviving Champagne's rare old grapes alongside the classic three.
aubry.tell: Aubry is a family estate just west of Reims, run by two brothers. They are known for growing Champagne's forgotten grapes such as Arbane and Petit Meslier alongside the classic ones, so their wines taste lively and a little different.

auguste-clape.name: Auguste Clape
auguste-clape.line: The reference domaine of Cornas, making traditional, unfiltered Syrah of great depth that ages for decades.
auguste-clape.tell: Clape is the most respected name in Cornas. The wines are dark, savoury and powerful, made in a traditional way; Renaissance is the younger vines cuvée; Le Vin des Amis is their simple, friendly red, so decant the Cornas.

aurelien-verdet.name: Aurélien Verdet
aurelien-verdet.line: A small family domaine from the Hautes-Côtes de Nuits, organic for decades, making fresh, honest village wines including Morey-Saint-Denis.
aurelien-verdet.tell: Verdet is a small grower from the hills above the Côte de Nuits, working organically. His Morey-Saint-Denis is a straightforward, fresh village red at a fair price. A good pour for a table that wants real Burgundy without a big spend.

ayala.name: Ayala
ayala.line: An Aÿ house owned by the Bollinger family since 2005, known for a pure, low-dosage, Chardonnay-driven style.
ayala.tell: Ayala is an old Aÿ house now in the Bollinger family. Its style is lean and pure, with little sugar added, so the wines taste crisp and precise. The Majeur rosé is dry and delicate, good with seafood.

bacio-divino.name: Bacio Divino
bacio-divino.line: A Napa winery whose Janzen label bottles single vineyard Cabernets from famous Beckstoffer sites.
bacio-divino.tell: Bacio Divino makes its Janzen Cabernets from Beckstoffer vineyards: To Kalon in Oakville and Missouri Hopper. The style is rich, ripe and opulent, with dark fruit and spice. A strong choice for a guest who wants big Napa Cabernet with a famous vineyard name.

badenhorst.name: A.A. Badenhorst
badenhorst.tell: Badenhorst is a Swartland family estate. Klip Klop is a Chenin Blanc, and the Palomino is an unusual, textured white.

banfi.name: Banfi
banfi.line: A large Montalcino estate making Brunello, Super Tuscan blends and a sweet Moscadello.
banfi.tell: Banfi is one of the largest estates in Montalcino. Summus is a rich red blend, Stilnovo another Tuscan red, and Florus is a sweet late harvest Moscadello di Montalcino for dessert.

barbadillo.name: Barbadillo
barbadillo.line: A large Sherry house in Sanlúcar de Barrameda.
barbadillo.tell: Barbadillo is a big Sherry house in Sanlúcar. Pale Cream is a sweetened pale Sherry: light, nutty and gently sweet. Serve chilled with dessert or as an aperitif.

barnaut.name: Barnaut
barnaut.line: A grower in Bouzy, a grand cru village famed for Pinot Noir, making rich, red-fruited Champagne.
barnaut.tell: Barnaut farms in Bouzy, one of the great Pinot Noir villages. Their Blanc de Noirs, white wine from black grapes, is full and red-fruited, a Champagne with real body for richer dishes.

barruol-lynch.name: Barruol and Lynch
barruol-lynch.line: A partnership between Louis Barruol of Château de Saint Cosme and importer Kermit Lynch, making a Côte-Rôtie called Les Roses.
barruol-lynch.tell: Louis Barruol, who runs Saint Cosme in Gigondas, makes this Côte-Rôtie with the American importer Kermit Lynch. Expect perfumed, peppery Syrah. A good value Côte-Rôtie.

bartolo-mascarello.name: Bartolo Mascarello
bartolo-mascarello.line: A revered traditional estate in the village of Barolo that blends several vineyards into one wine.
bartolo-mascarello.tell: Bartolo Mascarello makes one Barolo, blended from several vineyards, the old way. It is fragrant, firm and very long lived, and collectors treasure it. The list holds many vintages; ask the sommelier which is ready and decant.

bastide-blanche.name: Domaine de la Bastide Blanche
bastide-blanche.line: A Bandol family domaine making Mourvèdre led reds from named cuvées.
bastide-blanche.tell: Bastide Blanche is a Bandol family estate. Estagnol and Fontanéou are their cuvées. Dark, savoury Mourvèdre.

beaulieu-vineyard.name: Beaulieu Vineyard
beaulieu-vineyard.line: A historic Rutherford estate; its Georges de Latour Private Reserve is one of Napa's benchmark Cabernets.
beaulieu-vineyard.tell: Beaulieu, called BV, is one of the old names of Napa. Georges de Latour Private Reserve, named for the founder, has been a benchmark Rutherford Cabernet for generations: dark fruit, cedar and the dusty earthiness Rutherford is known for.

beaumont.name: Beaumont
beaumont.line: A family farm in Bot River, near the coast of the Western Cape.
beaumont.tell: Beaumont is a family farm in Bot River. Pinotage is South Africa's own grape, a cross of Pinot Noir and Cinsault: dark berries and a little smoke. Theirs is fresh and balanced. A fun pick for a curious guest.

beaux-freres.name: Beaux Frères
beaux-freres.tell: Beaux Frères is a Willamette Valley estate best known for Pinot Noir. This is its Chardonnay, fresh and fine.

bedrock.name: Bedrock Wine Co.
bedrock.line: A Sonoma winery devoted to old vineyards, known for field blends, Zinfandel and Syrah.
bedrock.tell: Bedrock works with some of California's oldest vineyards. The Syrah is peppery and savoury, with dark fruit. A great choice for a guest who likes Rhône wines.

belle-glos.name: Belle Glos
belle-glos.region: Sonoma Coast and Santa Maria Valley
belle-glos.line: A Pinot Noir label from the family behind Caymus, known for ripe, dark, generous single vineyard wines.
belle-glos.tell: Belle Glos is the Pinot Noir side of the Wagner family of Caymus, and the style matches: ripe, dark fruited and plush. Taylor Lane comes from the Sonoma Coast. A great Pinot for a guest who usually drinks Napa Cabernet; here in magnum for a big table.

benanti.name: Benanti
benanti.line: A pioneering family estate of the modern Etna revival.
benanti.tell: Benanti helped start the modern revival of Mount Etna. Their Etna Rosso is Nerello Mascalese: fragrant, light bodied and mineral, often compared to Pinot Noir. A great choice with tuna, pork or poultry.

benoit-ente.name: Benoît Ente
benoit-ente.line: A small Puligny estate making precise whites.
benoit-ente.tell: Benoît Ente is a small Puligny-Montrachet estate. His village Puligny is crisp, floral and fine.

benoit-lahaye.name: Benoît Lahaye
benoit-lahaye.line: An organic grower in Bouzy making precise, low-dosage Champagne, much of it single-plot.
benoit-lahaye.tell: Benoît Lahaye farms organically in Bouzy and adds little or no sugar, so the wines are dry, vivid and true to place. Several bottles are single plots like Le Jardin de la Grosse Pierre. Ask the sommelier how Violaine is made.

bergstrom.name: Bergstrom
bergstrom.line: A family estate in the northern Willamette Valley, farming biodynamically and known for rich, layered Pinot Noir and Chardonnay.
bergstrom.tell: Bergstrom is a family winery in Oregon's Willamette Valley, farmed biodynamically. Their Pinot Noirs are deep and silky, with more richness than many Oregon wines. Le Pré du Col and Shea are single vineyards, Silice comes from sandy soils, and Reserve blends the best barrels.

bernard-bonin.name: Bernard Bonin
bernard-bonin.line: A small Meursault estate making textured, precise wines.
bernard-bonin.tell: Bernard Bonin is a small Meursault estate. Genevrières and Charmes are premier crus; Clos du Cromin, La Rencontre and Les Tillets village sites; Initiales is Bourgogne.

bernard-faurie.name: Bernard Faurie
bernard-faurie.line: A small, traditional grower on the hill of Hermitage, making tiny amounts of classic Syrah.
bernard-faurie.tell: Faurie is a small traditional grower whose Hermitage is rare. The wine blends the Gréffieux and Bessards parcels on the hill. Powerful and savoury; decant it.

bernard-moreau.name: Domaine Bernard Moreau et Fils
bernard-moreau.line: A well regarded Chassagne-Montrachet family domaine, better known for white wine, also making fresh, firm red Chassagne.
bernard-moreau.tell: Moreau is a respected Chassagne family. Red Chassagne is less known than the whites but can be very good value, and this old vine bottling has depth. A good match for pork or roast chicken.

bertani.name: Bertani
bertani.line: A historic Verona house known for traditional, long aged Amarone.
bertani.tell: Bertani is a historic name in Valpolicella. Its Amarone Classico is made traditionally from dried grapes and aged long: rich, dried cherry and spice, but dry. A classic choice for braised meats or hard cheese.

berthelemot.name: Domaine Berthelemot
berthelemot.line: A Côte de Beaune domaine making wines across several villages, here a Monthélie red with some bottle age.
berthelemot.tell: Monthélie sits next to Volnay and gives similar charm for less money. This bottle has a few years on it, so expect softer fruit and savoury notes. An easy value pick for a guest who likes mature red.

bethel-heights.name: Bethel Heights
bethel-heights.line: A family estate and one of the early names in the Eola-Amity Hills, making fresh, balanced Oregon Pinot Noir and Chardonnay.
bethel-heights.tell: Bethel Heights is a family estate that has farmed the Eola-Amity Hills for decades. Afternoon winds from the coast keep the wines fresh. The Pinot Noir is bright and red fruited, with fine acidity, and the half bottle is perfect for one or two guests with fish or duck.

bibi-graetz.name: Bibi Graetz
bibi-graetz.line: A Tuscan winemaker and artist, known for Testamatta, a vivid Sangiovese.
bibi-graetz.tell: Bibi Graetz is an artist and winemaker based near Florence. Testamatta, meaning crazy head, is his top Sangiovese: bright, fragrant and intense. A modern Tuscan red for beef or veal.

billard-gonnet.name: Domaine Billard-Gonnet
billard-gonnet.line: A traditional Pommard family domaine with holdings in the village's top premier crus, including Les Rugiens.
billard-gonnet.tell: Billard-Gonnet is a Pommard family estate. Les Rugiens is Pommard's most famous premier cru, giving a firm, deep red that softens with age. A good pick with beef or lamb.

billaud-simon.name: Billaud-Simon
billaud-simon.line: A historic Chablis estate known for pure, crisp wines, now owned by Faiveley.
billaud-simon.tell: Billaud-Simon is a historic Chablis estate, now owned by Faiveley. Vaillons is a premier cru, and the village Chablis, also in magnum, is crisp, fresh and lemony.

billecart-salmon.name: Billecart-Salmon
billecart-salmon.line: A family-run house in Mareuil-sur-Aÿ, prized for finesse, freshness and one of Champagne's most admired rosés.
billecart-salmon.tell: Billecart-Salmon is still family run and loved for elegance: fine bubbles, fresh fruit and a clean finish. The rosé is the one guests know; Elisabeth Salmon is its prestige rosé, Nicolas François the prestige white, and Clos St Hilaire a rare single vineyard Pinot Noir.

bindi.name: Bindi
bindi.line: A small family estate in the cool Macedon Ranges, making fine Pinot Noir and Chardonnay.
bindi.tell: Bindi is a small estate in the Macedon Ranges, one of Australia's coolest regions. Dixon is a Pinot Noir: fine, fragrant and fresh. A treat for a Burgundy lover.

biondi-santi.name: Biondi-Santi (Tenuta Greppo)
biondi-santi.line: The family estate credited with creating Brunello di Montalcino, famous for long lived Riservas.
biondi-santi.tell: Biondi-Santi is the family that created Brunello at Tenuta Greppo. The wines are fresh, firm and built for decades: the Annata is the standard Brunello, the Riserva the long lived flagship, and the Rosso the younger wine. Historic bottles; decant.

biserno.name: Tenuta di Biserno
biserno.line: A coastal Tuscan estate founded by Lodovico and Piero Antinori, making Bordeaux style reds.
biserno.tell: Biserno is a coastal Tuscan estate of Lodovico Antinori, who founded Ornellaia, and his brother Piero. Il Pino di Biserno is the second wine; Biserno the grand one. Rich, polished Bordeaux style reds.

bisson.name: Bisson
bisson.tell: Bisson is a Ligurian estate. This rosé is from Ciliegiolo, a red grape, fresh and fruity.

bitouzet-prieur.name: Bitouzet-Prieur
bitouzet-prieur.line: A family domaine straddling Volnay and Meursault, making traditional, quietly classic Volnay and white Meursault.
bitouzet-prieur.tell: A traditional family estate. Their Volnay is the elegant, perfumed style the village is known for: red fruit, silky tannin, nothing forced. With some age now, it is a lovely partner for poultry and veal.

blain-gagnard.name: Domaine Blain-Gagnard
blain-gagnard.line: A Chassagne-Montrachet family domaine with fine white holdings that also makes red Chassagne in a supple, fresh style.
blain-gagnard.tell: Blain-Gagnard is a respected Chassagne name. Their red Chassagne is a bright, medium bodied Pinot Noir, an under the radar value on a list this deep. Good with chicken, pork or fish in a red wine sauce.

bodega-chacra.name: Bodega Chacra
bodega-chacra.line: A Patagonian estate in Río Negro.
bodega-chacra.tell: Chacra is a Patagonian estate in Río Negro. Mainqué is its Chardonnay, fresh and precise.

bollinger.name: Bollinger
bollinger.line: A family house in Aÿ with a rich, Pinot Noir-led style shaped by barrel fermentation and long ageing.
bollinger.tell: Bollinger is Pinot Noir country Champagne: full, toasty and vinous, partly fermented in oak. Special Cuvée is the house blend, La Grande Année the vintage, R.D. a vintage aged long on its lees and disgorged late, and Vieilles Vignes Françaises a tiny, legendary Blanc de Noirs.

bon-ve.name: Bon Vé
bon-ve.line: A rosé the list files under the United States.
bon-ve.tell: The list files Bon Vé under the United States and names Georgia. Ask the sommelier about the producer and style before you describe it.

bond.name: BOND
bond.line: The Harlan family's project bottling Cabernet from single hillside vineyards: Melbury, Quella, St. Eden, Vecina and Pluribus.
bond.tell: BOND comes from the family behind Harlan Estate. Each wine is Cabernet from one hillside site: St. Eden and Vecina are dark and powerful, Melbury and Quella more perfumed, Pluribus from Spring Mountain. Rare, costly bottles across several vintages; decant and involve the sommelier.

boom-shucka.name: Boom Shucka
boom-shucka.line: A Chenin Blanc white from the Limoux area of the Languedoc.
boom-shucka.tell: Boom Shucka is a Chenin Blanc from the Limoux area of the Languedoc. Ask the sommelier about the producer before you tell its story.

borgo-san-daniele.name: Borgo San Daniele
borgo-san-daniele.tell: Borgo San Daniele is a Friuli estate. Friulano is a round, almond-scented white, good with lighter dishes.

borgo-scopeto.name: Borgo Scopeto
borgo-scopeto.line: A Chianti Classico estate near Siena, in the same family as Caparzo and Altesino.
borgo-scopeto.tell: Borgo Scopeto is a Chianti Classico estate near Siena. Its Vin Santo is a sweet wine made from dried grapes and aged in small barrels: nutty, honeyed and warm. Here in half bottle, lovely with dessert.

borgogno.name: Borgogno
borgogno.line: One of the oldest houses in the village of Barolo, known for long aged Riservas.
borgogno.tell: Borgogno is a historic house in the village of Barolo. The Riserva is aged longer before release and is classic, savoury and long. Ask the sommelier about the vintage before you recommend it.

bouard-bonnefoy.name: Bouard-Bonnefoy
bouard-bonnefoy.line: A family estate in Chassagne-Montrachet making precise whites.
bouard-bonnefoy.tell: Bouard-Bonnefoy is a family estate in Chassagne-Montrachet. Les Macherelles and Les Petits Clos Morgeot are premier crus, Le Charmois a Saint-Aubin premier cru, and the Aligoté and Bourgogne are value bottles.

bouchard-pere-et-fils.name: Bouchard Père & Fils
bouchard-pere-et-fils.line: One of the largest landholders on the Côte d'Or, a historic Beaune house whose own premier and grand cru vineyards anchor a broad range.
bouchard-pere-et-fils.tell: Bouchard owns a large spread of top vineyards, especially in Beaune. Vigne de l'Enfant Jésus is their famous parcel in the Beaune Grèves premier cru. The half bottles here are a handy way to give a couple a proper premier cru Burgundy.

bouchard-pere-fils.name: Bouchard Père et Fils
bouchard-pere-fils.line: One of Burgundy's largest and oldest houses, based in Beaune.
bouchard-pere-fils.tell: Bouchard is one of Burgundy's largest and oldest houses, based in Beaune. Corton-Charlemagne is a grand cru white, and this one comes in magnum for a table to share.

brick-and-mortar.name: Brick & Mortar
brick-and-mortar.line: A small California producer making single vineyard wines in limited amounts, here a Napa Valley Pinot Noir.
brick-and-mortar.tell: Brick & Mortar is a small producer working with single vineyards. Cougar Rock Vineyard Pinot Noir comes from Napa, unusual for a grape usually grown in cooler spots. Ask the sommelier about its weight and style before you recommend it.

brigitte-fallon.name: Brigitte Fallon (Michel Fallon)
brigitte-fallon.line: A tiny Avize label from Michel Fallon, who long worked at Jacques Selosse, making grand cru Blanc de Blancs.
brigitte-fallon.tell: Brigitte Fallon is a very small label made in Avize by Michel Fallon, whose experience comes from years in the Selosse cellar. It is a grand cru Blanc de Blancs, rich and precise. Production is tiny; the list spells it Bridgette.

broadbent.name: Broadbent
broadbent.line: A Madeira label from wine importer Bartholomew Broadbent, here as single cask bottlings.
broadbent.tell: Broadbent bottles Madeira, the fortified wine of the Atlantic island, aged in warm conditions. Malvasia is the richest and sweetest style; Verdelho is medium dry. Both have burnt sugar, nut and citrus notes, with bright acidity. In 500 ml bottles.

broc-cellars.name: Broc Cellars
broc-cellars.line: An urban winery in Berkeley making light, natural style wines from organically farmed vineyards.
broc-cellars.tell: Broc Cellars is a Berkeley winery making natural wines. Vine Starr Zinfandel is lighter and fresher than most, juicy and bright. A fun choice for a guest who wants a gentle red.

brocard-pierre.name: Pierre Brocard
brocard-pierre.line: A grower in the Côte des Bar, the Pinot Noir country in the south of Champagne.
brocard-pierre.tell: Pierre Brocard farms in the Aube. Saignée de la Côte is a rosé made by bleeding juice off Pinot Noir skins, so it is deep in colour and full of red fruit, a rosé Champagne with body for food.

brovia.name: Brovia
brovia.line: A traditional family estate in Castiglione Falletto, making classic Barolo.
brovia.tell: Brovia is a family estate in Castiglione Falletto, making Barolo the traditional way: fragrant, firm and long lived. A classic choice for a Nebbiolo lover.

brundlmayer.name: Bründlmayer
brundlmayer.line: A leading Kamptal estate in Langenlois, famous for Riesling from the Heiligenstein and Grüner Veltliner, plus fine sparkling wine.
brundlmayer.tell: Bründlmayer is one of Austria's great names. The Heiligenstein Rieslings are taut and mineral, the Grüner Veltliners peppery and fresh. Their sparkling wine is made the Champagne way and is among the best outside Champagne.

bruno-clair.name: Domaine Bruno Clair
bruno-clair.line: A leading Marsannay domaine with vineyards from Marsannay to Gevrey and Savigny, making clean, precise, classically built reds.
bruno-clair.tell: Bruno Clair is one of the top growers in the northern Côte de Nuits. La Dominode is an old vine premier cru in Savigny-lès-Beaune, and gives a structured, fragrant wine for a fair price. A good value premier cru recommendation.

bruno-clavelier.name: Bruno Clavelier
bruno-clavelier.line: A Vosne-Romanée grower farming biodynamically, known for old vines and a terroir focused, transparent style across Vosne, Chambolle and Gevrey.
bruno-clavelier.tell: Clavelier farms old vines biodynamically and makes wines that show where they grow rather than how they were made. Expect fragrant, fine Pinot Noir with a savoury edge. A strong recommendation for a guest who likes Burgundy with detail and finesse.

bruno-colin.name: Bruno Colin
bruno-colin.line: A Chassagne-Montrachet grower, part of the large Colin family, best known for whites but also making reds from the southern Côte de Beaune.
bruno-colin.tell: Bruno Colin comes from one of Chassagne's best known families. His Santenay red is a bright, fresh Pinot Noir from old vines, a good value step into the Côte de Beaune. Easy with lighter meats and mushrooms.

bruno-giacosa.name: Bruno Giacosa
bruno-giacosa.line: One of the great traditional names of Barbaresco and Barolo; Asili is among its most celebrated Barbarescos.
bruno-giacosa.tell: Bruno Giacosa is one of the legends of Piedmont. Asili is a famous Barbaresco vineyard: fragrant, fine and long lived. A celebration bottle for a Nebbiolo lover; decant.

burgess.name: Burgess Cellars
burgess.line: A long standing Napa winery on the hillsides above St. Helena, making classic, balanced Cabernet.
burgess.tell: Burgess has worked the hillsides above St. Helena for decades. The Reserve Cabernet is classic and balanced, with dark fruit and firm structure. A good traditional Napa choice for beef.

burklin-wolf.name: Dr. Bürklin-Wolf
burklin-wolf.tell: Bürklin-Wolf is a large biodynamic Pfalz estate. R Wachenheim is a dry Riesling, here in magnum.

burn-cottage.name: Burn Cottage
burn-cottage.line: A biodynamic estate in Central Otago making fine Pinot Noir.
burn-cottage.tell: Burn Cottage is a biodynamic estate in Central Otago, in the mountains of New Zealand's South Island. Its Pinot Noir is fine and fragrant; Moonlight Race is a second bottling. A strong Burgundy alternative.

by-farr.name: By Farr
by-farr.line: A Geelong family estate known for Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and Shiraz.
by-farr.tell: By Farr is a Geelong family estate. Its Shiraz blend is peppery and fresh, with dark fruit, more Rhône than Barossa. A thoughtful pick for lamb.

c-da-silva.name: C. da Silva (Dalva)
c-da-silva.line: A Port house whose Dalva brand is known for aged tawny and Colheita Ports.
c-da-silva.tell: Dalva is the brand of C. da Silva, known for aged tawny Ports from single vintages. Expect nuts, dried fruit and caramel. Lovely with pecan or chocolate desserts; ask about the vintage.

ca-del-bosco.name: Ca' del Bosco
ca-del-bosco.line: A leading Franciacorta house making traditional method sparkling wine in Lombardy.
ca-del-bosco.tell: Ca' del Bosco is one of the great names of Franciacorta, Italy's answer to Champagne. Annamaria Clementi is the top wine, a Riserva aged long on its lees; this one has no added sugar.

ca-marcanda.name: Ca' Marcanda (Gaja)
ca-marcanda.line: The Gaja family's estate on the Tuscan coast near Bolgheri, making Bordeaux style reds.
ca-marcanda.tell: Ca' Marcanda is the Gaja family's estate near Bolgheri, on the Tuscan coast. The reds use Bordeaux grapes. Promis is the friendly entry, Magari the middle wine, and Camarcanda the top: polished and deep. Magari comes in half bottle too.

ca-rome.name: Ca' Rome'
ca-rome.line: A family estate in Barbaresco making traditional Barbaresco and Barolo.
ca-rome.tell: Ca' Rome' is a family estate in Barbaresco. Rio Sordo and Chiaramanti are Barbaresco vineyards, perfumed and firm; Rapet is a Barolo from Serralunga, deeper and sterner. Classic Nebbiolo for beef or game.

cade.name: Cade
cade.line: A Howell Mountain estate from the PlumpJack group, making powerful mountain Cabernet from volcanic soils.
cade.tell: Cade is the PlumpJack family winery up on Howell Mountain, above the Napa Valley fog. Mountain fruit gives a dark, firm Cabernet with plenty of structure. The estate magnum is a strong, generous bottle for a table eating steak.

caillez-lemaire.name: Caillez Lemaire
caillez-lemaire.line: A family grower in Damery in the Marne valley, with a low-dosage, Meunier-rich style.
caillez-lemaire.tell: Caillez Lemaire is a family estate in Damery. Pur is a Blanc de Noirs with no added sugar, crisp and fruity; Éclats is the blend, here in magnum, which suits a table of four or more.

cakebread.name: Cakebread Cellars
cakebread.line: A Rutherford family winery whose Napa Chardonnay is a long-time restaurant favourite.
cakebread.tell: Cakebread is a family winery in Rutherford. The Chardonnay is a classic Napa style, ripe fruit, gentle oak and a fresh finish, and many guests know and ask for it.

calera.name: Calera
calera.line: A Central Coast pioneer that planted Pinot Noir on the limestone of remote Mount Harlan, the soil of Burgundy.
calera.tell: Calera went looking for limestone, like Burgundy, and found it high on Mount Harlan. Its single vineyard Pinot Noirs, Jensen, Mills, Reed and Ryan, are fresh, fine and long lived, each a little different. A favourite for guests who love Burgundy. Doux is a sweet Viognier for dessert.

cambria.name: Cambria
cambria.region: Santa Maria Valley, Santa Barbara County
cambria.line: A Santa Maria Valley estate making cool climate Pinot Noir and Chardonnay; Julia's Vineyard is its best known Pinot.
cambria.tell: Cambria farms the cool, foggy Santa Maria Valley. Julia's Vineyard Pinot Noir is bright and red fruited, with a little spice, approachable and fairly priced. An easy, friendly California Pinot for poultry or salmon.

camille-giroud.name: Camille Giroud
camille-giroud.line: A small Beaune négociant known for a traditional, unhurried style, with wines that are built to age rather than to impress young.
camille-giroud.tell: Giroud is a small Beaune house with a reputation for classic, age worthy reds. The Chambertin here has had time in bottle, and the Marsannay is a lighter, fresher village wine. Ask the sommelier how the older bottle is showing before you promise anything.

camille-thiriet.name: Domaine Camille Thiriet
camille-thiriet.line: A young domaine in the southern Côte de Nuits making lively reds from Côte de Nuits-Villages vineyards.
camille-thiriet.tell: Camille Thiriet is a newer name making fresh, vibrant Pinot Noir from small named sites in the Côte de Nuits-Villages. These are bright and juicy rather than heavy. A fun pick for a guest who likes natural leaning wines.

caneva-da-nani.name: Caneva da Nani
caneva-da-nani.line: A small Veneto grower making col fondo, a lightly sparkling wine finished in the bottle with its lees left in.
caneva-da-nani.tell: Caneva da Nani makes col fondo in the Veneto: the Prosecco grape refermented in the bottle and left with its lees, so it can be cloudy, dry and lightly fizzy. A rustic, food-friendly sparkler.

canopus.name: Canopus
canopus.line: A small Mendoza producer making natural minded Malbec.
canopus.tell: Canopus is a small Mendoza producer. De Sed is a Malbec made with a light hand: fresh, juicy and floral, lighter than the classic style. A fun, good value red.

cantina-terlano.name: Cantina Terlano
cantina-terlano.line: An Alto Adige cooperative famous for long lived wines, here a Pinot Noir.
cantina-terlano.tell: Terlano is a celebrated cooperative in Alto Adige, best known for whites that age for decades. Monticol is its Pinot Noir: fine, fresh and red fruited. An elegant choice for salmon, veal or duck.

canvasback.name: Canvasback
canvasback.line: Duckhorn's Washington State winery, making Cabernet Sauvignon from the warm, small Red Mountain area.
canvasback.tell: Canvasback is the Duckhorn family in Washington. Red Mountain is a warm, dry corner of the state that gives dark, firm Cabernet with good freshness. A smart pick for a Napa drinker who wants something different at a fair price; here in magnum.

caparzo.name: Caparzo
caparzo.line: A Montalcino estate whose La Casa is a single vineyard Brunello.
caparzo.tell: Caparzo is a Montalcino estate. La Casa is its single vineyard Brunello: deep, firm Sangiovese with cherry and spice. A solid, classic choice with steak.

capensis.name: Capensis
capensis.tell: Capensis is a South African Chardonnay project. The Western Cape Chardonnays are rich and fine, and Silene is its Stellenbosch bottling.

cappellano.name: Cappellano
cappellano.line: A small, very traditional Serralunga estate with a devoted following; Pie Rupestris is one of its Barolos.
cappellano.tell: Cappellano is a tiny traditional estate in Serralunga. Otin Fiorin Pie Rupestris is a Barolo from their old vineyard: fragrant, firm and savoury. Rare; ask the sommelier about it.

capture.name: Capture
capture.tell: Capture is a mountain winery in northern Sonoma. Its Sauvignon Blanc is crisp and bright.

carbonnieux.name: Château Carbonnieux
carbonnieux.line: A classed growth of Graves in Pessac-Léognan, well known for its white.
carbonnieux.tell: Carbonnieux is a classed growth of Graves with a famous white of Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon. It is crisp, citrusy and lightly oaked, lovely with fish and crab.

cardinale.name: Cardinale
cardinale.line: A Napa estate blending Cabernet from mountain and valley vineyards into one polished, powerful wine.
cardinale.tell: Cardinale blends Cabernet from mountain and valley floor vineyards across Napa into one wine. It is dark, polished and long, built for steak and for celebration. The list holds several vintages; ask the sommelier which is drinking best tonight.

carrette.name: Domaine Carrette
carrette.tell: Carrette is a family estate in Pouilly-Fuissé in southern Burgundy. Les Crays is a single site, here in magnum: ripe and round.

casanova-di-neri.name: Casanova di Neri
casanova-di-neri.line: A Montalcino estate known for rich, modern Brunello; Tenuta Nuova is its best known wine.
casanova-di-neri.tell: Casanova di Neri makes Brunello in a rich, modern style. Tenuta Nuova is its most famous wine: dark, ripe and polished. A good Brunello for a guest who likes fuller reds.

castello-conti.name: Castello Conti
castello-conti.line: A small family estate in the hills of northern Piedmont making fragrant Nebbiolo based wines.
castello-conti.tell: Castello Conti is a small family estate in northern Piedmont, near the Alps. Il Rosso delle Donne is from Boca, Nebbiolo with local grapes: fragrant, fresh and mineral. A lighter cousin of Barolo.

castello-di-ama.name: Castello di Ama
castello-di-ama.line: A leading Chianti Classico estate in Gaiole, known for fine Sangiovese and contemporary art.
castello-di-ama.tell: Castello di Ama is a top Chianti Classico estate, also famous for the art installed around its hamlet. San Lorenzo is its Gran Selezione: fine, firm Sangiovese. Haiku is a blend. Elegant Tuscan reds for beef or veal.

castello-di-volpaia.name: Castello di Volpaia
castello-di-volpaia.line: A medieval hilltop village estate in Radda, one of the leading names of Chianti Classico.
castello-di-volpaia.tell: Volpaia is a hilltop village estate in Radda, high in Chianti Classico. Its Vin Santo is made from dried grapes and aged slowly: amber, nutty and sweet. A lovely half bottle with dessert.

catena-zapata.name: Catena Zapata
catena-zapata.line: The family that led Argentina to high altitude vineyards and world class Malbec.
catena-zapata.tell: Catena Zapata led the move to high altitude vineyards in Mendoza. Argentino is a Malbec blending several sites; River comes from the Adrianna Vineyard, very high up. Rich, dark and fresh. The half bottle Malbec suits two guests.

catherine-et-pierre-breton.name: Catherine & Pierre Breton
catherine-et-pierre-breton.line: A Bourgueil couple farming biodynamically, among the best known natural leaning names in the Loire, making fresh, savoury Cabernet Franc.
catherine-et-pierre-breton.tell: The Bretons are leading growers in Bourgueil, and their Cabernet Franc is fresh, red fruited and a little herbal. Les Perrières is their serious, age worthy bottling; Franc de Pied comes from ungrafted vines. A great choice for a guest who likes lighter, savoury reds.

caymus.name: Caymus
caymus.line: A Wagner family winery in Rutherford, famous for rich, velvety Napa Cabernet; Special Selection is the top wine.
caymus.tell: Caymus is one of the best known Napa names. The style is ripe, round and velvety, with dark fruit and soft tannin, easy to enjoy young. Special Selection is the richer flagship, and the 50th Anniversary bottling comes in a three litre double magnum.

cecchi.name: Cecchi
cecchi.line: A long established Tuscan family house making reliable Chianti.
cecchi.tell: Cecchi is a family wine house in Tuscany. Its Chianti is fresh and easy, with cherry and a savoury finish. A friendly value red for pasta or poultry.

cerbaiona.name: Cerbaiona
cerbaiona.line: A small, celebrated Montalcino estate making refined, traditional Brunello.
cerbaiona.tell: Cerbaiona is a small, much admired estate in Montalcino. Its Brunello is fine, fragrant and long lived. A treat for a Brunello lover; decant.

cesarini-sforza.name: Cesarini Sforza
cesarini-sforza.line: A Trentino sparkling house making Trento DOC wine by the Champagne method in the mountains.
cesarini-sforza.tell: Cesarini Sforza makes sparkling wine in Trento, in the Alps, the same way Champagne is made. The rosé brut is crisp, dry and lightly red fruited. A smart, good value alternative to Champagne for a toast.

ch-berres.name: C.H. Berres
ch-berres.line: A family estate in Ürzig on the Middle Mosel, making bright, slate-grown Riesling.
ch-berres.tell: Berres is a family estate in Ürzig on the Mosel. The Old Vines Riesling is crisp and lightly fruity, with the stony edge slate soil gives, and it is a friendly first white for a guest who thinks Riesling is always sweet.

chalk-hill.name: Chalk Hill
chalk-hill.line: A Sonoma estate in its own small appellation, known for rich Chardonnay.
chalk-hill.tell: Chalk Hill is a Sonoma estate known for Chardonnay. Expect a round, ripe style with toasty oak. Here in half-bottle, right for one or two guests.

champalou.name: Champalou
champalou.line: A family estate in Vouvray making pure Chenin Blanc in dry and off-dry styles.
champalou.tell: Champalou is a family estate in Vouvray. Their wine is Chenin Blanc, fresh, floral and gently fruity. Ask the sommelier whether this bottle is dry or off-dry before promising a guest either.

chapel-down.name: Chapel Down
chapel-down.line: One of England's best known sparkling wine producers, in Kent, making wine by the Champagne method.
chapel-down.tell: Chapel Down is a leading English sparkling wine house in Kent, where chalky soils and a cool climate echo Champagne. The rosé brut is crisp and red fruited. A fun, good value alternative to Champagne and a nice talking point.

chapelle-st-theodoric.name: Chapelle St. Théodoric
chapelle-st-theodoric.line: A small Châteauneuf-du-Pape producer making Grenache led wines from sandy sites.
chapelle-st-theodoric.tell: A small Châteauneuf producer. Le Grand Pin is a Grenache led wine. Ask the sommelier for the story.

chappellet.name: Chappellet
chappellet.line: A family estate that pioneered the rocky slopes of Pritchard Hill in Napa, making firm, long lived Cabernet.
chappellet.tell: Chappellet was one of the first to plant high on Pritchard Hill, east of the valley floor. The wines are dark and structured. Mountain Cuvée is the friendly, approachable blend; Signature is the classic Cabernet; Pritchard Hill is the estate's flagship, built to age.

charles-audoin.name: Charles Audoin
charles-audoin.line: A family domaine in Marsannay, the northernmost village of the Côte de Nuits, making crisp, red fruited Pinot Noir from named sites.
charles-audoin.tell: Marsannay sits at the top of the Côte de Nuits and gives lighter, brighter reds. Audoin is a local family grower, and Les Favières is one of their named vineyards. A good value Burgundy for a guest who likes freshness.

charles-heidsieck.name: Charles Heidsieck
charles-heidsieck.line: A Reims house famous for using a high share of old reserve wines, giving rich, toasty, creamy Champagne.
charles-heidsieck.tell: Charles Heidsieck ages its wines in old chalk cellars and blends in a lot of older reserve wine, so even the Brut Réserve tastes rich and toasty. Blanc des Millénaires is the long-aged prestige Blanc de Blancs; Champagne Charlie revives a historic name.

charles-joguet.name: Charles Joguet
charles-joguet.line: A leading Chinon domaine, making single vineyard Cabernet Franc in a structured, age worthy style.
charles-joguet.tell: Joguet is one of the most respected names in Chinon. The single vineyard wines, like Clos du Chêne Vert and Les Varennes du Grand Clos, have depth and structure. Cuvée Terroir is the fresher, younger one.

charles-mignon.name: Charles Mignon
charles-mignon.line: A family house in Épernay making approachable, fruit-forward Champagne.
charles-mignon.tell: Charles Mignon is a family house in Épernay. Comte de Marne is its grand cru cuvée, rounder and fuller; the Premium Réserve rosé is soft and fruity. Good value against the big names.

charles-smith.name: Charles Smith
charles-smith.line: A Washington winemaker known for bold labels and dark, powerful Syrah; Royal City is his top Syrah.
charles-smith.tell: Charles Smith is a showman of Washington wine. Royal City is his flagship Syrah: dark, dense and meaty, with smoke and pepper. For a guest who loves big reds.

chartogne-taillet.name: Chartogne-Taillet
chartogne-taillet.line: A grower in Merfy, northwest of Reims, known for single-parcel wines that show their soils.
chartogne-taillet.tell: Chartogne-Taillet is a family estate in Merfy, a quiet corner north of Reims. Alexandre Chartogne bottles single parcels such as Les Barres and Orizeaux separately, so each one shows its own soil. Sainte Anne is the fresh, approachable blend.

chateau-armens.name: Château Armens
chateau-armens.line: A Saint-Émilion estate in Saint-Pey-d'Armens owned by the Malet Roquefort family of Château La Gaffelière.
chateau-armens.tell: Armens is owned by the family behind La Gaffelière. A friendly, good value Saint-Émilion.

chateau-beau-sejour-becot.name: Château Beau-Séjour Bécot
chateau-beau-sejour-becot.line: A Saint-Émilion premier grand cru classé on the limestone plateau, owned by the Bécot family.
chateau-beau-sejour-becot.tell: Beau-Séjour Bécot is a premier grand cru on Saint-Émilion's limestone plateau. Fine, fresh Merlot and Cabernet Franc.

chateau-belle-brise.name: Château Belle-Brise
chateau-belle-brise.line: A tiny Pomerol estate of about two hectares, owned by Henri-Bruno de Coincy, making fine, elegant Merlot.
chateau-belle-brise.tell: Belle-Brise is a tiny Pomerol estate near Le Pin, made in very small amounts. Elegant, fine Merlot. A rare find for a Pomerol lover.

chateau-bellegrave.name: Château Bellegrave
chateau-bellegrave.line: A small Pomerol estate making supple Merlot led wine.
chateau-bellegrave.tell: Bellegrave is a Pomerol, so expect soft, plummy Merlot. A gentle price for the appellation.

chateau-bernon-becot.name: Château Bernon Bécot
chateau-bernon-becot.line: A Puisseguin-Saint-Émilion estate bought in 2015 by the Bécot family of Beau-Séjour Bécot.
chateau-bernon-becot.tell: Bernon Bécot is owned by the family behind Beau-Séjour Bécot. Soft, friendly Merlot at a gentle price.

chateau-calon-segur.name: Château Calon-Ségur
chateau-calon-segur.line: A Saint-Estèphe third growth famous for the heart on its label, making firm, long lived Cabernet led wines.
chateau-calon-segur.tell: Calon-Ségur is the château with the heart on the label, a lovely story for a celebration. Saint-Estèphe gives firm, structured Cabernet that ages for decades. A great anniversary bottle.

chateau-canon.name: Château Canon
chateau-canon.line: A Saint-Émilion premier grand cru classé on the limestone plateau, owned by the family behind Chanel, making fine, fresh wine.
chateau-canon.tell: Canon is a premier grand cru on the limestone plateau, owned by the family behind Chanel. Fine, fragrant and fresh.

chateau-cantenac-brown.name: Château Cantenac Brown
chateau-cantenac-brown.line: A Margaux third growth with a striking Tudor style château, making firm, structured Margaux.
chateau-cantenac-brown.tell: Cantenac Brown is a third growth in Margaux with a famously English looking château. Structured, fragrant claret.

chateau-chasse-spleen.name: Château Chasse-Spleen
chateau-chasse-spleen.line: A well known Moulis estate making classic, firm claret.
chateau-chasse-spleen.tell: Chasse-Spleen is one of the best known names in Moulis. Classic, firm claret at a fair price.

chateau-cheval-blanc.name: Château Cheval Blanc
chateau-cheval-blanc.line: The great Saint-Émilion estate, rich in Cabernet Franc, which stood at the top of the classification until it withdrew in 2022; Le Petit Cheval is its second wine.
chateau-cheval-blanc.tell: Cheval Blanc is one of the world's great wines, unusual for its high share of Cabernet Franc. Le Petit Cheval is the second wine. Decant.

chateau-clarke.name: Château Clarke
chateau-clarke.line: A Listrac estate owned by the Edmond de Rothschild family, making Merlot rich claret.
chateau-clarke.tell: Clarke is a Listrac estate owned by a branch of the Rothschild family. The magnum is good for a table.

chateau-climens.name: Château Climens
chateau-climens.line: A first growth of Barsac, admired for sweet wines with unusual freshness and finesse.
chateau-climens.tell: Climens is a top estate in Barsac, next to Sauternes. Its sweet wine is famously fresh and fine: honey, citrus and apricot, with bright acidity. A beautiful match for fruit tarts, blue cheese or foie gras.

chateau-clinet.name: Château Clinet
chateau-clinet.line: A Pomerol estate on the high plateau, making rich, modern Merlot led wine.
chateau-clinet.tell: Clinet is a leading Pomerol, rich and plush. A great choice with duck or beef.

chateau-cordet.name: Château Cordet
chateau-cordet.line: A small Margaux estate making approachable claret.
chateau-cordet.tell: Cordet is a small Margaux producer. A fragrant, approachable Margaux at a friendly price.

chateau-cos-d-estournel.name: Château Cos d'Estournel
chateau-cos-d-estournel.line: A Saint-Estèphe second growth, known for its pagoda towered chai, making rich, exotic, polished Cabernet and Merlot blends.
chateau-cos-d-estournel.tell: Cos d'Estournel is the leading name in Saint-Estèphe, famous for its oriental style towers. The wine is rich and polished, more opulent than most of its neighbours. Decant younger vintages; the magnums are perfect for big celebrations.

chateau-cos-labory.name: Château Cos Labory
chateau-cos-labory.line: A Saint-Estèphe fifth growth neighbouring Cos d'Estournel, making classic, firm claret at fair prices.
chateau-cos-labory.tell: Cos Labory sits next door to Cos d'Estournel and gives classic Saint-Estèphe at a gentler price. The magnum is a fine pick for a table of four or more.

chateau-d-esclans.name: Château d'Esclans
chateau-d-esclans.line: Sacha Lichine's Provence estate, maker of Whispering Angel.
chateau-d-esclans.tell: Whispering Angel is the famous pale Provence rosé from Château d'Esclans. It is dry, crisp and delicate, a guest favourite.

chateau-d-yquem.name: Château d'Yquem
chateau-d-yquem.line: The most famous sweet wine estate in the world, alone in its own top class in the Sauternes classification.
chateau-d-yquem.tell: Yquem is the most famous sweet wine in the world, given its own rank above every other Sauternes. It is rich, layered and extremely long lived, with honey, apricot and spice. The list has several vintages, half bottles and a magnum; involve the sommelier.

chateau-de-beaucastel.name: Château de Beaucastel
chateau-de-beaucastel.line: The Perrin family's famous Châteauneuf-du-Pape estate, known for using all permitted grapes and a high share of Mourvèdre; Coudoulet is its Côtes du Rhône.
chateau-de-beaucastel.tell: Beaucastel is one of Châteauneuf's great names, and Hommage à Jacques Perrin is their rare, Mourvèdre rich top wine. Coudoulet is the Côtes du Rhône from vines next door, and Oenothèque bottles are older releases from the estate's cellar.

chateau-de-beru.name: Château de Béru
chateau-de-beru.line: A biodynamic family estate in Béru, at the edge of Chablis.
chateau-de-beru.tell: Château de Béru farms biodynamically at the edge of Chablis. Clos de Béru is a walled vineyard the estate owns alone, Montserre another site and Athénaïs a Bourgogne: precise and stony.

chateau-de-breze.name: Château de Brezé
chateau-de-breze.line: A historic château estate in Saumur, making Cabernet Franc and Chenin Blanc from limestone slopes.
chateau-de-breze.tell: Brezé is a château in Saumur with deep limestone cellars, known for Chenin Blanc and Cabernet Franc. This Clos de l'Étoile is from 2014, so it has some age. Ask the sommelier how it is showing before recommending it.

chateau-de-camensac.name: Château de Camensac
chateau-de-camensac.line: A Haut-Médoc fifth growth making classic claret.
chateau-de-camensac.tell: Camensac is a fifth growth in the Haut-Médoc. Classic claret at a fair price.

chateau-de-chorey.name: Domaine du Château de Chorey
chateau-de-chorey.line: A family estate based in a château at Chorey-lès-Beaune.
chateau-de-chorey.tell: Château de Chorey is a family estate near Beaune. Les Combottes is a white Pernand-Vergelesses, fresh and good value from the Côte de Beaune.

chateau-de-fonsalette.name: Château de Fonsalette
chateau-de-fonsalette.line: The Côtes du Rhône estate of the Reynaud family of Château Rayas.
chateau-de-fonsalette.tell: Fonsalette belongs to the family of Château Rayas. Its white Côtes du Rhône is rich and textured, far above the usual.

chateau-de-la-maltroye.name: Château de la Maltroye
chateau-de-la-maltroye.line: A Chassagne-Montrachet estate making reds and whites from Chassagne and neighbouring villages.
chateau-de-la-maltroye.tell: Maltroye is a Chassagne estate with a château. Red Chassagne is a bright, fresh Pinot Noir. A smart value pick.

chateau-des-eyrins.name: Château des Eyrins
chateau-des-eyrins.line: A small Margaux estate owned by Xavier and Julie Gonet-Médeville, with a prized parcel beside Château Margaux; La Closerie des Eyrins is its second wine.
chateau-des-eyrins.tell: Eyrins is a tiny Margaux estate with vines next to Château Margaux and Palmer. La Closerie des Eyrins is the second wine. Fragrant, fine Margaux at a fair price.

chateau-des-jacques.name: Château des Jacques
chateau-des-jacques.line: The Moulin-à-Vent estate owned by Louis Jadot, making structured, Burgundy minded cru Beaujolais.
chateau-des-jacques.tell: Château des Jacques is Jadot's Beaujolais estate. Moulin-à-Vent gives a firmer, deeper Gamay that can age. Clos du Grand Carquelin is one of their walled sites.

chateau-des-tours.name: Château des Tours
chateau-des-tours.line: The Vacqueyras estate of Emmanuel Reynaud of Château Rayas, making fragrant Grenache in a similar spirit.
chateau-des-tours.tell: Château des Tours is run by the same hand as Rayas. The Vacqueyras and Côtes du Rhône are fragrant, pure Grenache. A great value way into the Rayas style.

chateau-du-breuil.name: Châteaux du Breuil et de la Roche
chateau-du-breuil.line: An organic Anjou estate with a Savennières plot, focused on dry Chenin Blanc.
chateau-du-breuil.tell: This organic estate in Anjou has a parcel in Savennières and is serious about dry Chenin Blanc. Clos du Breuil is dry, textured and mineral. The list prints Château de La Roche; ask the sommelier if a guest asks about the name.

chateau-du-cedre.name: Château du Cèdre
chateau-du-cedre.line: A leading Cahors estate making deep Malbec.
chateau-du-cedre.tell: Du Cèdre is a leading Cahors estate. Cahors is Malbec from France: dark, firm and savoury. Good with steak.

chateau-ducru-beaucaillou.name: Château Ducru-Beaucaillou
chateau-ducru-beaucaillou.line: A Saint-Julien second growth on the Gironde owned by the Borie family, known for refined, long lived Cabernet.
chateau-ducru-beaucaillou.tell: Ducru-Beaucaillou is one of Saint-Julien's great estates. The wine is refined, balanced and long lived. A classic choice for beef or lamb.

chateau-duhart-milon.name: Château Duhart-Milon
chateau-duhart-milon.line: A Pauillac fourth growth owned by the Lafite Rothschild family; Moulin de Duhart is its second wine.
chateau-duhart-milon.tell: Duhart-Milon is Lafite's sister estate in Pauillac, and Moulin de Duhart is its second wine. It is an easy, fair priced way into the Lafite family.

chateau-ferriere.name: Château Ferrière
chateau-ferriere.line: A small third growth in Margaux making fragrant, elegant claret.
chateau-ferriere.tell: Ferrière is a small third growth in Margaux, the appellation known for perfume and finesse. Expect red and black fruit, violets and fine tannin. The half bottle is a lovely classed growth for two guests.

chateau-figeac.name: Château Figeac
chateau-figeac.line: A Saint-Émilion estate on gravel, unusually rich in Cabernet, promoted to premier grand cru classé A in 2022.
chateau-figeac.tell: Figeac is unusual in Saint-Émilion for its high share of Cabernet. It was promoted to the top rank in 2022. Fine and long lived.

chateau-gilette.name: Château Gilette
chateau-gilette.line: A small Sauternes estate that ages its wines for many years in vat before release.
chateau-gilette.tell: Gilette is unique in Sauternes: it holds its wine for many years before bottling, so it arrives mature. Crème de Tête is the top selection: deep gold, with caramel, dried apricot and orange peel. A rare, lovely dessert wine.

chateau-giscours.name: Château Giscours
chateau-giscours.line: A large Margaux third growth making generous, fragrant claret.
chateau-giscours.tell: Giscours is a big Margaux third growth, generous and fragrant. A good value classified growth.

chateau-gombaude-guillot.name: Château Gombaude-Guillot
chateau-gombaude-guillot.line: A small family estate in Pomerol making Merlot led wine.
chateau-gombaude-guillot.tell: Gombaude-Guillot is a small family Pomerol. Soft, plummy Merlot. The several vintages here make for a good comparison.

chateau-grand-puy-lacoste.name: Château Grand-Puy-Lacoste
chateau-grand-puy-lacoste.line: A Pauillac fifth growth owned by the Borie family, admired for classic, cassis scented, honest Pauillac at a fair price.
chateau-grand-puy-lacoste.tell: Grand-Puy-Lacoste is classic Pauillac, Cabernet with cassis and cedar, owned by the same family as Ducru-Beaucaillou. Many think it drinks above its classification. A strong value for steak.

chateau-gruaud-larose.name: Château Gruaud-Larose
chateau-gruaud-larose.line: A Saint-Julien second growth making rich, firm, generous Cabernet led wine.
chateau-gruaud-larose.tell: Gruaud-Larose is a generous, full style of Saint-Julien. A great value second growth with steak.

chateau-guiraud.name: Château Guiraud
chateau-guiraud.line: A Sauternes first growth; G is its dry white.
chateau-guiraud.tell: Guiraud is a great Sauternes estate. G is its dry white, Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon, crisp and lightly rich, a value Bordeaux white.

chateau-haut-bages-liberal.name: Château Haut-Bages Libéral
chateau-haut-bages-liberal.line: A Pauillac fifth growth with vines near Latour, making firm, fresh Cabernet led wine.
chateau-haut-bages-liberal.tell: Haut-Bages Libéral is a fifth growth with some vines near Château Latour. It gives classic, firm Pauillac at a sensible price. Good with red meat.

chateau-haut-brion.name: Château Haut-Brion
chateau-haut-brion.line: The only first growth outside the Médoc, in Pessac-Léognan, owned by Domaine Clarence Dillon; Bahans Haut-Brion was its second wine's name.
chateau-haut-brion.tell: Haut-Brion is the only first growth from Graves, with a smoky, earthy, silky style. Bahans Haut-Brion is the older name of the second wine. Decant.

chateau-l-arrosee.name: Château L'Arrosée
chateau-l-arrosee.line: A Saint-Émilion Grand Cru Classé on the slopes below the town, making fresh, fine wine.
chateau-l-arrosee.tell: L'Arrosée is a classified Saint-Émilion. Fresh, fine Merlot and Cabernet Franc.

chateau-l-eglise-clinet.name: Château L'Église-Clinet
chateau-l-eglise-clinet.line: A small Pomerol estate on the plateau, long run by the late Denis Durantou, making deep, fine wines.
chateau-l-eglise-clinet.tell: L'Église-Clinet is a small, much admired Pomerol. Deep, fine and long lived. A special bottle.

chateau-l-evangile.name: Château L'Évangile
chateau-l-evangile.line: A Pomerol estate owned by the Lafite Rothschild family, between Pétrus and Cheval Blanc, making rich, deep Merlot.
chateau-l-evangile.tell: L'Évangile is owned by the Lafite Rothschild family and sits between Pétrus and Cheval Blanc. Rich, deep Pomerol. Decant.

chateau-la-fleur-petrus.name: Château La Fleur-Pétrus
chateau-la-fleur-petrus.line: A Pomerol estate of the Moueix family, near Pétrus, making silky, fine Merlot.
chateau-la-fleur-petrus.tell: La Fleur-Pétrus belongs to the Moueix family and sits near Pétrus. Silky, fine Pomerol. A lovely choice for duck or beef.

chateau-la-lagune.name: Château La Lagune
chateau-la-lagune.line: A Haut-Médoc third growth near Bordeaux city, making fragrant, fine claret.
chateau-la-lagune.tell: La Lagune is a third growth in the southern Médoc. Fragrant and fine. The magnum is good for a table.

chateau-la-mission-haut-brion.name: Château La Mission Haut-Brion
chateau-la-mission-haut-brion.line: The great Pessac-Léognan estate across the road from Haut-Brion, under the same ownership, making rich, deep wines.
chateau-la-mission-haut-brion.tell: La Mission is Haut-Brion's neighbour, under the same owners, and in many years just as admired. Rich, deep and smoky. A trophy bottle.

chateau-la-nerthe.name: Château La Nerthe
chateau-la-nerthe.line: A historic Châteauneuf-du-Pape estate making classic Grenache led wines.
chateau-la-nerthe.tell: La Nerthe is one of Châteauneuf's historic estates. Expect a rich, warm red with dark fruit and spice. Good with lamb.

chateau-la-tour-carnet.name: Château La Tour Carnet
chateau-la-tour-carnet.line: A Haut-Médoc fourth growth owned by Bernard Magrez, making rich, modern claret.
chateau-la-tour-carnet.tell: La Tour Carnet is a classified Haut-Médoc. Rich, modern claret at a fair price.

chateau-la-tour-haut-brion.name: Château La Tour Haut-Brion
chateau-la-tour-haut-brion.line: A former classified Graves estate under the same ownership as La Mission Haut-Brion, now absorbed into La Mission's vineyard.
chateau-la-tour-haut-brion.tell: La Tour Haut-Brion was a sister estate of La Mission and no longer exists as a separate wine. This 1982 is a rare, mature bottle; ask the sommelier how it is showing.

chateau-la-vieille-forge.name: Château La Vieille Forge
chateau-la-vieille-forge.line: A Lalande-de-Pomerol estate making Merlot led wine.
chateau-la-vieille-forge.tell: Lalande-de-Pomerol sits next to Pomerol and gives soft Merlot at a gentler price. A good value choice.

chateau-lafite-rothschild.name: Château Lafite Rothschild
chateau-lafite-rothschild.line: The first growth of Pauillac owned by the Rothschild family since 1868, famous for its elegance and perfume.
chateau-lafite-rothschild.tell: Lafite is perhaps the most famous name in Bordeaux. It is a first growth known for elegance and fragrance rather than raw power. These are trophy bottles: involve the sommelier, decant, and let the moment breathe.

chateau-lafleur.name: Château Lafleur
chateau-lafleur.line: A tiny, revered Pomerol estate of the Guinaudeau family, rich in Cabernet Franc, among the most sought after wines of Bordeaux.
chateau-lafleur.tell: Lafleur is a tiny Pomerol estate that collectors prize as highly as Pétrus. It has more Cabernet Franc than most Pomerol. Rare bottles; decant.

chateau-lalande.name: Château Lalande
chateau-lalande.line: A Saint-Julien estate owned by the Meffre family since 1964, once part of Château Lagrange.
chateau-lalande.tell: Lalande is a family run Saint-Julien that was once part of Château Lagrange. It is classic, approachable claret at a friendly price.

chateau-lalande-borie.name: Château Lalande-Borie
chateau-lalande-borie.line: A Saint-Julien estate of the Borie family, owners of Ducru-Beaucaillou.
chateau-lalande-borie.tell: Lalande-Borie comes from the family that owns Ducru-Beaucaillou. It is a softer, earlier drinking Saint-Julien at a friendly price.

chateau-lassegue.name: Château Lassègue
chateau-lassegue.line: A Saint-Émilion Grand Cru Classé; Les Cadrans de Lassègue is its second wine.
chateau-lassegue.tell: Les Cadrans de Lassègue is the second wine of Château Lassègue. Soft, friendly Saint-Émilion at a gentle price.

chateau-latour.name: Château Latour
chateau-latour.line: The Pauillac first growth beside the Gironde, owned by the Pinault family, famous for powerful, long lived Cabernet.
chateau-latour.tell: Latour is the most powerful of the first growths, famed for consistency and longevity. The estate releases its wines only when it judges them ready. Decant, and serve with beef or lamb.

chateau-le-puy.name: Château Le Puy
chateau-le-puy.line: A biodynamic family estate on the Bordeaux plateau, long organic.
chateau-le-puy.tell: Le Puy is a family estate long farmed without chemicals. Marie-Cécile is its white, Sémillon: textured and gentle.

chateau-leoville-las-cases.name: Château Léoville Las Cases
chateau-leoville-las-cases.line: A Saint-Julien second growth run by the Delon family, beside Latour, often ranked with the first growths for power and longevity.
chateau-leoville-las-cases.tell: Las Cases is one of the most prestigious second growths, its Grand Enclos running right up to Latour. The wine is serious and long lived. Decant, and give it time in the glass.

chateau-leoville-poyferre.name: Château Léoville Poyferré
chateau-leoville-poyferre.line: A Saint-Julien second growth owned by the Cuvelier family, known for rich, plush, modern Cabernet.
chateau-leoville-poyferre.tell: Poyferré is the plushest of the three Léovilles. Rich, ripe and generous. A crowd pleasing second growth.

chateau-les-clauzots.name: Château les Clauzots
chateau-les-clauzots.line: A family estate in the south of the Graves, making white Bordeaux from Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon.
chateau-les-clauzots.tell: Les Clauzots has been in the same family for generations in the Graves, south of Bordeaux. The white is Sauvignon Blanc with Sémillon, aged on its lees: citrus and peach, with a round, silky texture. Great value with fish and shellfish.

chateau-les-grands-chenes.name: Château Les Grands Chênes
chateau-les-grands-chenes.line: A Médoc cru bourgeois making classic, approachable claret.
chateau-les-grands-chenes.tell: Les Grands Chênes is a Médoc cru bourgeois. Classic, approachable claret at a friendly price.

chateau-lynch-bages.name: Château Lynch-Bages
chateau-lynch-bages.line: A Pauillac fifth growth owned by the Cazes family, much loved for rich, generous, cassis rich wine that drinks above its rank.
chateau-lynch-bages.tell: Lynch-Bages is one of the most loved names in Bordeaux, often compared with second growths. Rich, generous Cabernet with cassis and cedar. The magnum is a great pick for a celebration.

chateau-margaux.name: Château Margaux
chateau-margaux.line: The first growth of the Margaux appellation, famous for perfume and silk; Pavillon Rouge is its second wine.
chateau-margaux.tell: Château Margaux is the first growth of its appellation, famed for fragrance and silky elegance. Pavillon Rouge is the second wine, a gentler price for the same estate. Decant.

chateau-marquis-d-alesme.name: Château Marquis d'Alesme
chateau-marquis-d-alesme.line: A Margaux third growth, renewed in recent years, making fragrant, polished wine.
chateau-marquis-d-alesme.tell: Marquis d'Alesme is a third growth in Margaux. Fragrant, polished claret at a fair price.

chateau-massereau.name: Château Massereau
chateau-massereau.line: An organic family estate in Barsac that makes dry red Bordeaux Supérieur with minimal intervention.
chateau-massereau.tell: Massereau sits in Barsac, sweet wine country, but makes red too. Cuvée K blends Merlot and the Cabernets with Petit Verdot, farmed organically and made with little intervention: blackberry, tobacco and graphite, with some age. Remarkable value for mature Bordeaux.

chateau-meyney.name: Château Meyney
chateau-meyney.line: A Saint-Estèphe estate near the Gironde; La Chapelle de Meyney is its second wine.
chateau-meyney.tell: La Chapelle de Meyney is the second wine of Château Meyney in Saint-Estèphe. It is a softer, earlier drinking claret at a friendly price.

chateau-montelena.name: Chateau Montelena
chateau-montelena.line: A historic Calistoga estate, famous since its Chardonnay won the 1976 Paris tasting, and known for long lived Estate Cabernet.
chateau-montelena.tell: Montelena's Chardonnay beat top white Burgundy at the 1976 Paris tasting, a great story at the table. Its Estate Cabernet, from the foot of Mount St. Helena, is firm, classic and long lived. A traditional Napa pick for beef.

chateau-montrose.name: Château Montrose
chateau-montrose.line: A Saint-Estèphe second growth on gravel near the Gironde estuary, known for powerful, long lived Cabernet led wines.
chateau-montrose.tell: Montrose overlooks the Gironde and makes one of the most powerful wines of the Médoc. It needs time and rewards it. Decant, and pair with beef or lamb.

chateau-mouton-rothschild.name: Château Mouton Rothschild
chateau-mouton-rothschild.line: The Pauillac first growth, promoted in 1973, famous for its rich, opulent wine and labels painted by a different artist each year.
chateau-mouton-rothschild.tell: Mouton is the first growth with an artist's label every year, a great story at the table. The wine is rich and opulent. Ask the sommelier who painted this vintage's label, and decant.

chateau-musar.name: Château Musar
chateau-musar.line: Lebanon's famous estate in the Bekaa Valley, releasing long lived reds only when it judges them ready.
chateau-musar.tell: Musar is the great wine of Lebanon, made by the Hochar family in the Bekaa Valley. The red blends Cabernet, Cinsault and Carignan and is released with age: spicy, earthy and layered, unlike any other wine. Hochar is the younger red. Older vintages are listed.

chateau-palmer.name: Château Palmer
chateau-palmer.line: A Margaux third growth, farmed biodynamically, often priced beside the first growths, known for Merlot rich, perfumed, silky wine.
chateau-palmer.tell: Palmer is a third growth that often sells for close to first growth prices. Rich in Merlot, perfumed and silky. Historical XIX Century Wine is a special blend recalling an older Bordeaux custom; ask the sommelier about it.

chateau-pape-clement.name: Château Pape Clément
chateau-pape-clement.line: A historic Pessac-Léognan estate named after Pope Clement V, owned by Bernard Magrez, making rich, modern Graves.
chateau-pape-clement.tell: Pape Clément is named after a medieval pope who once owned the vineyard. Rich, smoky Graves. Good with beef.

chateau-pavie.name: Château Pavie
chateau-pavie.line: A Saint-Émilion premier grand cru classé A owned by the Perse family, making rich, powerful wine.
chateau-pavie.tell: Pavie is one of Saint-Émilion's top estates. Rich and powerful. Decant.

chateau-pedesclaux.name: Château Pedesclaux
chateau-pedesclaux.line: A Pauillac fifth growth that has been extensively renewed in recent years, making modern, polished Cabernet.
chateau-pedesclaux.tell: Pedesclaux is a fifth growth in Pauillac that has invested heavily recently. Expect a modern, polished Cabernet at a fair price.

chateau-pichon-lalande.name: Château Pichon Longueville Comtesse de Lalande
chateau-pichon-lalande.line: A Pauillac second growth facing Latour, owned by the Roederer Champagne family, known for silky, perfumed, Merlot rich Pauillac.
chateau-pichon-lalande.tell: Pichon Lalande is one of the most elegant Pauillacs, with more Merlot than most, which gives a silky texture. The half bottle is a beautiful option for two.
