chateau-pontet-canet.name: Château Pontet-Canet
chateau-pontet-canet.line: A Pauillac fifth growth owned by the Tesseron family, farmed biodynamically, making deep, pure, highly regarded Cabernet.
chateau-pontet-canet.tell: Pontet-Canet is famous for biodynamic farming and wines many rate alongside second growths. Deep, pure Cabernet. Decant younger vintages.

chateau-pradeaux.name: Château Pradeaux
chateau-pradeaux.line: A traditional Bandol estate making powerful, long lived Mourvèdre.
chateau-pradeaux.tell: Pradeaux is a traditional Bandol estate. The Mourvèdre is powerful and savoury and needs age. This bottle has some.

chateau-rauzan-segla.name: Château Rauzan-Ségla
chateau-rauzan-segla.line: A Margaux second growth owned by the owners of Chanel, making fragrant, refined Margaux; Ségla is its second wine.
chateau-rauzan-segla.tell: Rauzan-Ségla is a second growth in Margaux, owned by the family behind Chanel. Fragrant and refined. Ségla is the second wine, a friendly price.

chateau-rayas.name: Château Rayas
chateau-rayas.line: The cult Châteauneuf-du-Pape estate of the Reynaud family, famous for pure, fragrant Grenache from sandy soils; also Pignan, Fonsalette and La Pialade.
chateau-rayas.tell: Rayas is the most cult name in Châteauneuf, and the Grenache is fine and fragrant, more Burgundy than Rhône. Pignan comes from the same family; Fonsalette and La Pialade are their Côtes du Rhône, all of them rare.

chateau-saint-cosme.name: Château de Saint Cosme
chateau-saint-cosme.line: The historic Gigondas estate of Louis Barruol, making fine, spicy Gigondas and also a Châteauneuf-du-Pape.
chateau-saint-cosme.tell: Saint Cosme is the leading name in Gigondas. Their Gigondas is spicy and deep. The magnum is great for a big table.

chateau-simone.name: Château Simone
chateau-simone.line: The estate that dominates the tiny Palette appellation near Aix.
chateau-simone.tell: Château Simone is almost all of Palette, a tiny appellation near Aix. Its white is textured, herbal and long-lived.

chateau-sociando-mallet.name: Château Sociando-Mallet
chateau-sociando-mallet.line: An unclassified Haut-Médoc estate built up by Jean Gautreau, often compared with classified growths.
chateau-sociando-mallet.tell: Sociando-Mallet is often rated alongside the classified growths. Cuvée Jean Gautreau honours the man who built the estate. Firm, long lived claret.

chateau-suduiraut.name: Château Suduiraut
chateau-suduiraut.line: A first growth of Sauternes, next to Yquem, making rich, golden sweet wine.
chateau-suduiraut.tell: Suduiraut is a first growth in Sauternes, a neighbour of Yquem. The wine is rich and golden, with honey, apricot and pineapple. A generous choice with crème brûlée, fruit desserts or blue cheese; the half bottle suits two.

chateau-talbot.name: Château Talbot
chateau-talbot.line: A Saint-Julien fourth growth making round, generous, approachable claret.
chateau-talbot.tell: Talbot is a well known Saint-Julien with a round, friendly style. A good value classified growth.

chateau-tertre-de-la-mouleyre.name: Château Tertre de la Mouleyre
chateau-tertre-de-la-mouleyre.line: A small Saint-Émilion family estate run by Éric Jeanneteau.
chateau-tertre-de-la-mouleyre.tell: Tertre de la Mouleyre is a small family estate in Saint-Émilion. Fine, fresh Merlot.

chateau-troplong-mondot.name: Château Troplong-Mondot
chateau-troplong-mondot.line: A Saint-Émilion premier grand cru classé on a high point of the appellation.
chateau-troplong-mondot.tell: Troplong-Mondot sits on one of the highest points in Saint-Émilion. The half bottle is a lovely treat for two.

chateau-trotanoy.name: Château Trotanoy
chateau-trotanoy.line: A Pomerol estate of the Moueix family, making powerful, deep Merlot.
chateau-trotanoy.tell: Trotanoy is a Moueix Pomerol, powerful and deep. A great choice for a Pomerol lover.

chateau-vieux-taillefer.name: Château Vieux Taillefer
chateau-vieux-taillefer.line: A small Saint-Émilion estate farmed organically, whose Pavillon de Taillefer is a Merlot Grand Cru.
chateau-vieux-taillefer.tell: Pavillon de Taillefer is the main wine of Château Vieux Taillefer, a small organic estate in Saint-Émilion. All Merlot, soft and plummy.

cheval-des-andes.name: Cheval des Andes
cheval-des-andes.line: A partnership in Mendoza between Château Cheval Blanc and Terrazas de los Andes.
cheval-des-andes.tell: Cheval des Andes is a joint venture between Château Cheval Blanc of Saint-Émilion and Terrazas de los Andes. It is a Malbec blend: fine, polished and fresh, Bordeaux style with Argentine fruit. A great choice for a Bordeaux lover.

chimney-rock.name: Chimney Rock
chimney-rock.line: A Stags Leap District winery making supple, elegant Cabernet from estate vineyards.
chimney-rock.tell: Chimney Rock farms the Stags Leap District, known for soft, silky Cabernet often called an iron fist in a velvet glove. The Estate Cabernet is polished, with dark cherry and fine tannin. A good classic Napa pick.

christophe-billon.name: Domaine Christophe Billon
christophe-billon.line: A small northern Rhône estate making Condrieu.
christophe-billon.tell: This is Condrieu, Viognier from the northern Rhône. Les Matisses is floral and rich, with apricot and a silky texture.

cinelli-colombini.name: Donatella Cinelli Colombini
cinelli-colombini.line: A Montalcino estate run by Donatella Cinelli Colombini, known for its team of women winemakers.
cinelli-colombini.tell: Donatella Cinelli Colombini runs a Montalcino estate with an all women team. Prime Donne is a Brunello: elegant and fragrant. They also make a sweet Vin Santo, here in half bottle for dessert.

clandestin.name: Clandestin
clandestin.line: A small house in the Aube founded by Burgundian Benoît Doussot, working with organic growers and adding no dosage.
clandestin.tell: Clandestin is Benoît Doussot's project in the Côte des Bar. He buys from about a dozen organic growers, ferments in barrel and adds no sugar. Les Semblables and Les Grandes Lignes are single-grape wines; dry, vinous, food-friendly.

clau-de-nell.name: Clau de Nell
clau-de-nell.line: A small biodynamic estate in Anjou, owned by the Leflaive family of Burgundy.
clau-de-nell.tell: Clau de Nell is a small biodynamic estate in Anjou owned by the Leflaive family of Burgundy. Fontene is Chenin Blanc: dry, textured and precise, lovely with rich fish.

claude-dugat.name: Domaine Claude Dugat
claude-dugat.line: A small, highly prized Gevrey-Chambertin domaine, cousin to Dugat-Py, making deep, rich wines in tiny quantities.
claude-dugat.tell: Claude Dugat's wines are scarce and much sought after. They are dark, generous and polished Gevrey with real depth. These are collector bottles: decant and serve with red meat or game.

clemens-busch.name: Clemens Busch
clemens-busch.tell: Clemens Busch farms organically on the Mosel. Nonnengarten Trocken is a dry Riesling, mineral and fine.

clendenen-family.name: Clendenen Family Vineyards
clendenen-family.region: Santa Maria Valley, Santa Barbara County
clendenen-family.line: Jim Clendenen's personal label, made alongside Au Bon Climat, with Italian grapes such as Nebbiolo.
clendenen-family.tell: Clendenen Family is the personal label of Jim Clendenen of Au Bon Climat, where he worked with Italian grapes. Punta Exclamativa is a Nebbiolo from the Santa Maria Valley: perfumed, firm and savoury. A fun swap for a Barolo lover.

clos-cancaillau.name: Clos Cancaillau
clos-cancaillau.tell: This is Jurançon, from the foothills of the Pyrenees. Au Lavoir is a dry white, crisp and exotic.

clos-des-lambrays.name: Domaine des Lambrays
clos-des-lambrays.line: Owner of nearly all of the Clos des Lambrays grand cru in Morey-Saint-Denis, now owned by the LVMH group.
clos-des-lambrays.tell: Clos des Lambrays is a grand cru that this domaine owns almost entirely. The wine is fragrant, fine and often made with whole bunches. A special occasion Burgundy.

clos-du-caillou.name: Domaine du Clos du Caillou
clos-du-caillou.line: A Châteauneuf-du-Pape domaine at Courthézon making rich Grenache led wines; the Réserve is its top bottling.
clos-du-caillou.tell: Clos du Caillou makes rich, deep Châteauneuf. The Réserve is their top cuvée, and this bottle has some age. Ask the sommelier how it is drinking.

clos-du-val.name: Clos du Val
clos-du-val.line: One of the early Stags Leap District wineries, founded with a French winemaker and known for balanced, elegant Cabernet.
clos-du-val.tell: Clos du Val was among the first wineries in the Stags Leap District and has always aimed for balance over power. The Cabernets are polished and food friendly. Hirondelle is their estate vineyard, Three Graces the top blend; the many vintages and magnums give plenty of choice.

clos-l-eglise.name: Clos l'Église
clos-l-eglise.line: A small Pomerol estate on the plateau making rich Merlot led wine.
clos-l-eglise.tell: Clos l'Église is a small Pomerol estate. Rich, plummy Merlot. A good choice for duck.

clos-la-chance.name: Clos la Chance
clos-la-chance.tell: Clos la Chance is a Central Coast winery. This Monterey Chardonnay is an older vintage, so ask the sommelier how it is drinking.

clos-manou.name: Clos Manou
clos-manou.line: A small family estate in the northern Médoc making carefully made claret.
clos-manou.tell: Clos Manou is a small Médoc estate. Petit Manou is the second wine. Good value claret.

clos-mogador.name: Clos Mogador
clos-mogador.line: One of the pioneering estates that revived Priorat in the late twentieth century.
clos-mogador.tell: Clos Mogador was one of the estates that brought Priorat back to fame. The wines grow on steep slate called llicorella: deep, mineral and powerful. Manyetes is mostly Carignan from one site. Big wines for lamb or beef.

clos-rougeard.name: Clos Rougeard
clos-rougeard.line: The cult Saumur-Champigny estate built by the Foucault brothers, making some of the most sought after Cabernet Franc in the world; now owned by Martin Bouygues.
clos-rougeard.tell: Clos Rougeard is a legend among Loire lovers. Le Clos, Les Poyeaux and Le Bourg are long lived, fine Cabernet Franc that collectors chase. These are rare bottles; decant and treat them like great Burgundy.

clos-saint-jean.name: Clos Saint Jean
clos-saint-jean.line: A Châteauneuf-du-Pape domaine known for rich, ripe, powerful top cuvées.
clos-saint-jean.tell: Clos Saint Jean makes rich, powerful Châteauneuf. La Combe des Fous and Sanctus Sanctorum are their top cuvées. Big wines for big meats.

clos-sainte-anne.name: Clos Sainte-Anne
clos-sainte-anne.line: A small Côtes de Bordeaux property of the Courselle family, making Merlot led red.
clos-sainte-anne.tell: Clos Sainte-Anne is a small family property in the Côtes de Bordeaux. Soft, Merlot led red, one of the best values on the list.

clos-thierriere.name: Clos Thierrière
clos-thierriere.line: A small Vouvray name making Chenin Blanc.
clos-thierriere.tell: This is Vouvray, Chenin Blanc from the middle Loire, where wines run from dry to sweet. Les Pleurs is a single cuvée; ask the sommelier how dry it is before you describe it to a guest.

clusel-roch.name: Domaine Clusel-Roch
clusel-roch.line: A Côte-Rôtie family domaine farming organically, making fragrant, traditional Syrah from steep schist slopes.
clusel-roch.tell: Clusel-Roch is a Côte-Rôtie family estate. Classique is the entry wine, and Les Grandes Places is their famous old vine site. Peppery, floral Syrah.

coche-dury.name: Domaine Coche-Dury
coche-dury.line: The Meursault domaine whose white wines are among the most coveted in the world; its small production of reds is just as hard to find.
coche-dury.tell: Coche-Dury is a legendary Meursault name, famous for white wine. The reds, from Volnay, Monthélie, Auxey-Duresses and Pommard, are made in tiny amounts and rarely seen. For a guest who knows the name, this is the treat; the price reflects the scarcity, not the appellation.

cocito.name: Cocito
cocito.line: A small family estate in the Barbaresco zone.
cocito.tell: Cocito is a small family producer in Barbaresco. Baluchin Riserva is aged longer before release: perfumed Nebbiolo with red fruit, rose and firm tannin. Ask the sommelier how the vintage is drinking.

cockburns.name: Cockburn's
cockburns.line: A historic Port house, known for its Vintage Ports.
cockburns.tell: Cockburn's is a historic Port house. Vintage Port is made only in the best years and aged in bottle: dark, rich and sweet. Older vintages need decanting; ask the sommelier.

col-d-orcia.name: Col d'Orcia
col-d-orcia.line: A large, historic Montalcino estate, farmed organically; Poggio al Vento is its Riserva.
col-d-orcia.tell: Col d'Orcia is one of the largest estates in Montalcino. Poggio al Vento is its single vineyard Riserva, aged longer: deep, savoury and long. A classic Brunello for beef or game.

collazzi.name: Collazzi
collazzi.line: An estate in the hills south of Florence making Chianti Classico and Tuscan reds.
collazzi.tell: Collazzi is an estate in the hills just south of Florence. Bastioni is its Chianti Classico: fresh Sangiovese with cherry and herbs. A good value Tuscan red for pasta or veal.

collecapretta.name: Collecapretta
collecapretta.tell: Collecapretta is a small family estate in Umbria. Trebbiano Spoletino from old vines is a textured, characterful white.

colleleva.name: Colleleva
colleleva.line: A small estate in the hills of the Marche near the Adriatic, making fresh, good value wines from local grapes.
colleleva.tell: Colleleva is a small estate in the Marche, between the Apennines and the Adriatic. The Rosso Piceno is mostly Montepulciano with some Sangiovese: juicy, red fruited and easy, made in steel to keep it fresh. A great value red for pasta or a casual meal.

comando-g.name: Comando G
comando-g.line: A celebrated Sierra de Gredos project making fine, fragrant mountain Garnacha.
comando-g.tell: Comando G makes Garnacha in the granite mountains of the Sierra de Gredos, and it tastes more like Burgundy than big Spanish red: fragrant, fresh and fine. Las Iruelas, Navatalgordo, Rozas 1er and Tumba del Rey Moro are separate sites. A must for a curious Pinot lover.

comte-abbatucci.name: Domaine Comte Abbatucci
comte-abbatucci.line: A biodynamic Corsican estate known for reviving native grapes.
comte-abbatucci.tell: Abbatucci is a famous Corsican estate. Ministre Impérial is a blend of native grapes. Fragrant and fine.

comte-georges-de-vogue.name: Domaine Comte Georges de Vogüé
comte-georges-de-vogue.line: The historic Chambolle-Musigny domaine and the largest owner of the Musigny grand cru, making powerful, slow developing wines.
comte-georges-de-vogue.tell: De Vogüé owns most of the Musigny grand cru and is one of Burgundy's great names. The wines are deep and structured when young and need years to open. Recommend decanting, and treat any bottle here as a special occasion wine.

comtes-lafon.name: Domaine des Comtes Lafon
comtes-lafon.line: A great Meursault name, famous for whites, whose red Volnay Santenots-du-Milieu is a long lived, serious wine.
comtes-lafon.tell: Lafon is one of the greatest names in white Burgundy. Their red Volnay Santenots-du-Milieu is firm and deep for Volnay. A fine choice for a guest who knows the name.

comtesse-de-cherisey.name: Comtesse Bernard de Chérisey
comtesse-de-cherisey.line: A family estate in the hamlet of Blagny above Meursault and Puligny, owner of the La Genelotte premier cru.
comtesse-de-cherisey.tell: Blagny is a tiny hamlet high on the slope where reds carry the Blagny name. This is a rarely seen premier cru red with a fresh, mineral feel. A good choice for a curious guest who wants something off the beaten track.

conestabile-della-staffe.name: Conestabile della Staffe
conestabile-della-staffe.line: A small Umbrian estate making natural wines from local grapes.
conestabile-della-staffe.tell: Conestabile della Staffe is a small natural wine estate in Umbria. Ciliegio is made from Ciliegiolo, a local grape whose name means cherry: light, juicy and lively. A fun red for an adventurous guest, lovely slightly cool.

conterno-fantino.name: Conterno Fantino
conterno-fantino.line: A Monforte d'Alba estate making polished, modern minded Barolo.
conterno-fantino.tell: Conterno Fantino is a family estate in Monforte d'Alba. Mosconi Vigna Ped is a single vineyard Barolo: rich, dark and firm. A good Barolo for steak or braised meat.

contino.name: Contino
contino.line: A single estate in Rioja Alavesa, one of the first Rioja wines from one vineyard.
contino.tell: Contino is a single estate on a bend of the Ebro in Rioja Alavesa, unusual in a region of blends. The Gran Reserva is deep, fine and long lived. A great choice for a Rioja lover.

continuum.name: Continuum
continuum.line: The Mondavi family estate on Pritchard Hill, run by Tim Mondavi, making one Cabernet led blend.
continuum.tell: Continuum is the next chapter of the Mondavi family, on rocky Pritchard Hill above the valley. It makes one wine, a Cabernet led blend with Cabernet Franc: deep, structured and fine. The list holds many vintages; ask the sommelier which is ready.

copain.name: Copain
copain.line: A California winery known for restrained, fresh Pinot Noir, Syrah and Chardonnay from cool vineyards.
copain.tell: Copain picks early for freshness, making wines in a restrained, European style. Kiser is a Pinot Noir vineyard in the Anderson Valley, bright and fragrant, here in magnum. Tous Ensemble Syrah is peppery and lively. A good pick for guests who want lighter California reds.

cos.name: COS
cos.line: A Sicilian estate known for natural winemaking and Cerasuolo di Vittoria.
cos.tell: COS is a natural minded estate in south east Sicily. Cerasuolo di Vittoria blends Nero d'Avola with Frappato: bright, juicy and floral. Lovely slightly cool with fish or poultry.

costers-del-priorat.name: Costers del Priorat
costers-del-priorat.line: A Priorat producer working old vines on steep slopes, with minimal intervention.
costers-del-priorat.tell: Costers del Priorat works old vineyards in Priorat. Clos Alzina is Carignan from a high, north facing site planted long ago: fresh for Priorat, mineral and fine. A great pick for a curious red drinker.

couhins.name: Château Couhins
couhins.line: A classed growth of Graves in Pessac-Léognan, owned by France's national agricultural research institute.
couhins.tell: Couhins is a classed growth white of Pessac-Léognan. It is Sauvignon-led, crisp and citrusy, good with seafood.

cristom.name: Cristom
cristom.line: A family estate in the Eola-Amity Hills known for single vineyard Pinot Noirs, several named for family members.
cristom.tell: Cristom farms its own hills in the Eola-Amity area and bottles vineyards separately. Paul Gerrie Vineyard is named for the founder: a dark, spicy, structured Pinot Noir. A fine Oregon choice for duck or lamb.

croce-di-febo.name: Croce di Febo
croce-di-febo.line: A small estate making Vino Nobile di Montepulciano.
croce-di-febo.tell: Croce di Febo makes Vino Nobile di Montepulciano, a Sangiovese from the hill town of Montepulciano in Tuscany, not the Montepulciano grape. Expect cherry, earth and firm tannin. A fair priced Tuscan red.

crocus.name: Crocus
crocus.line: A Cahors project of Paul Hobbs with Bertrand-Gabriel Vigouroux, making Malbec.
crocus.tell: Crocus is a Cahors Malbec from the American winemaker Paul Hobbs and a local partner. L'Atelier is the entry wine. Dark and juicy.

cuatro-monos.name: 4 Monos
cuatro-monos.line: A small group making fresh Garnacha from the mountains west of Madrid.
cuatro-monos.tell: 4 Monos, four monkeys, is a small project in the Sierra de Gredos west of Madrid. Vino de los Tres Pueblos is a Garnacha blend from three villages: fresh, red fruited and lightly herbal. A lovely, lighter red.

cvne.name: CVNE
cvne.line: A historic Rioja house in Haro, known for Imperial and Viña Real.
cvne.tell: CVNE, said coo-nay, is a historic house in Haro. Imperial is its classic Rioja Alta line, elegant and long lived; Viña Real is fuller, from Rioja Alavesa. Reserva and Gran Reserva bottles are aged long before release, smooth and savoury.

d-ventura.name: D. Ventura
d-ventura.line: A small Ribeira Sacra producer bottling Mencía from single vineyards on the river slopes.
d-ventura.tell: D. Ventura bottles single vineyards in Ribeira Sacra. Viña Caneiro is a Mencía from steep slate slopes: fresh, red fruited and mineral. A light, lively red for food.

dakel.name: Dakél
dakel.line: A coastal Chilean project making single vineyard Pinot Noir and Chardonnay in the Itata Valley.
dakel.tell: Dakél makes Pinot Noir from a single vineyard near the Pacific in the Itata Valley, southern Chile, on granite soils. It is fresh and elegant, with red fruit and spice. A smart value Pinot.

dal-forno.name: Dal Forno Romano
dal-forno.line: A cult estate east of Verona making extremely concentrated Amarone and Valpolicella.
dal-forno.tell: Dal Forno makes some of the most powerful wines in Italy, in the Val d'Illasi east of Verona. Even the Valpolicella is dense and dark; the Amarone, from dried grapes, is huge, sweet fruited and long. A rare bottle for a guest who loves big wine; decant.

dalla-valle.name: Dalla Valle
dalla-valle.line: A family estate on the Oakville hillside, famous for its estate Cabernet and for Maya, a Cabernet and Cabernet Franc blend.
dalla-valle.tell: Dalla Valle sits on the eastern hills of Oakville. Its Cabernet is rich and firm, and Maya, blended with Cabernet Franc, is one of Napa's most sought after wines. Celebration bottles; decant and give them time in the glass.

damien-laureau.name: Damien Laureau
damien-laureau.line: A small Savennières grower making precise, dry Chenin Blanc.
damien-laureau.tell: Damien Laureau is a small grower in Savennières. L'Alliance is dry Chenin Blanc, taut and mineral, with apple and honey and a long finish. Good with rich fish.

damien-martin.name: Domaine Damien Martin
damien-martin.line: A family estate in Davayé in the Mâconnais, making straightforward Bourgogne for everyday drinking.
damien-martin.tell: Damien Martin is a family domaine in the south of Burgundy. This Bourgogne Pinot Noir is light and fruity, red cherry and strawberry with soft tannin, a gentle red for fish, chicken or a guest who wants red with a lighter dish.

daniel-bouland.name: Daniel Bouland
daniel-bouland.line: A small Beaujolais grower making traditional, old vine cru wines, here Côte de Brouilly.
daniel-bouland.tell: Bouland is a small traditional grower. Côte de Brouilly comes from the slopes of Mont Brouilly. Fresh and fruity, a good value red.

daniel-rion.name: Domaine Daniel Rion & Fils
daniel-rion.line: A family domaine in Prémeaux, at the southern end of Nuits-Saint-Georges, making firm, classic reds across the Côte de Nuits.
daniel-rion.tell: Rion is a family estate in the Nuits-Saint-Georges area. Their village Nuits from Les Lavières is a sturdy, dark fruited red. A good partner for steak or game.

daou.name: DAOU
daou.line: A Paso Robles winery founded by two brothers, making rich, Bordeaux style reds on the hills west of town; Patrimony is the top wine.
daou.tell: DAOU farms steep limestone hills west of Paso Robles. The wines are ripe, dark and polished. Caves des Lions and Soul of a Lion are Cabernet led, and Patrimony is the flagship, here also in magnum. A good choice for a guest who loves rich Napa style red.

dard-et-ribo.name: Dard & Ribo
dard-et-ribo.line: A cult natural leaning domaine in Crozes-Hermitage, making fresh, juicy Syrah with little intervention.
dard-et-ribo.tell: Dard & Ribo makes fresh, lively Syrah in Crozes-Hermitage. C'est le Printemps is their bright, spring-like red. Fun and food friendly.

dard-ribo.name: Dard et Ribo
dard-ribo.tell: Dard et Ribo make low-intervention wines in Crozes-Hermitage. Their white is textured, fresh and a little wild.

darioush.name: Darioush
darioush.line: A Napa estate with a winery inspired by ancient Persia, making rich, polished Cabernet.
darioush.tell: Darioush is a Napa winery whose founder drew on his Persian heritage for its striking building. The Cabernet is ripe, plush and polished, with dark fruit and soft tannin. A crowd pleaser for steak.

dauvissat.name: Domaine René et Vincent Dauvissat
dauvissat.line: A great traditional Chablis estate, with Raveneau the reference for the region.
dauvissat.tell: Dauvissat stands beside Raveneau at the top of Chablis. The wines are aged partly in old barrels and taste pure, deep and stony. Les Clos and Les Preuses are grand crus; Vaillons a premier cru; Petit Chablis the entry.

david-arthur.name: David Arthur
david-arthur.line: A family estate on Pritchard Hill making concentrated mountain Cabernet.
david-arthur.tell: David Arthur is a family winery on the rocky slopes of Pritchard Hill. Old Vines Cabernet is concentrated and firm, with dark fruit and mountain structure. A good choice with beef or lamb.

david-duband.name: David Duband
david-duband.line: A grower based in the Hautes-Côtes de Nuits making fragrant, whole cluster influenced reds across the Côte de Nuits.
david-duband.tell: Duband is known for perfumed, lifted Pinot Noir with plenty of energy. His Nuits-Saint-Georges is a village wine with good structure. A nice match for duck or mushrooms.

david-leclapart.name: David Leclapart
david-leclapart.line: A tiny biodynamic grower in Trépail making intense, mineral Blanc de Blancs.
david-leclapart.tell: David Leclapart farms biodynamically in Trépail, a Chardonnay outpost on the Montagne de Reims. His wines are low in dosage and very pure; L'Artiste and L'Apôtre are two of the cult names in grower Champagne, made in small amounts.

david-sautereau.name: Domaine David Sautereau
david-sautereau.line: A Sancerre family domaine making white and red; red Sancerre is light, fresh Pinot Noir.
david-sautereau.tell: Red Sancerre is Pinot Noir from the Loire: light, fresh and red fruited. A good choice for fish or chicken when a guest wants red.

de-montille.name: Domaine de Montille
de-montille.line: A Volnay family domaine, run by Étienne de Montille, known for elegant, whole cluster reds; Maison de Montille is its négociant label.
de-montille.tell: De Montille is a leading Volnay family making fragrant, fresh, finely structured wines. Pommard Rugiens and Beaune Sizies are classic premier crus. A trusted choice.

de-villaine.name: A. et P. de Villaine
de-villaine.line: Aubert de Villaine's own estate in Bouzeron, known for Aligoté and Rully.
de-villaine.tell: This is the estate of Aubert de Villaine, long co-director of Domaine de la Romanée-Conti. The Bouzeron is Aligoté, crisp and fresh; the Rully wines are Chardonnay. Great value from a great name.

del-dotto.name: Del Dotto
del-dotto.line: A Napa family winery known for its wine caves, also bottling Sonoma Coast Chardonnay.
del-dotto.tell: Del Dotto is a Napa family winery famous for its caves. This Chardonnay comes from Fort Ross-Seaview, a cool, high corner of the Sonoma Coast, so it has freshness under its ripe fruit.

delamotte.name: Delamotte
delamotte.line: A small Le Mesnil-sur-Oger house, sister to Salon, devoted to Chardonnay from the Côte des Blancs.
delamotte.tell: Delamotte is Salon's sister house in Le Mesnil, heart of the Côte des Blancs. Its Blanc de Blancs is crisp, chalky and elegant, with lemon and brioche, a great step toward Salon's style at a gentler price.

delarche.name: Domaine Delarche
delarche.tell: Delarche is a family estate in Pernand-Vergelesses. Les Combettes is a white from the village, fresh and mineral, a value Côte de Beaune bottle.

delas-freres.name: Delas Frères
delas-freres.line: A Rhône négociant and grower based near Hermitage, making wines across the northern and southern Rhône.
delas-freres.tell: Delas is a well known Rhône house. Sainte-Épine is a Saint-Joseph, and Haute Pierre is a Châteauneuf-du-Pape. Reliable, good value.

demarie.name: Demarie
demarie.line: A family estate in the Roero hills of Piedmont, across the river from the Langhe, making Arneis and Nebbiolo.
demarie.tell: Demarie is a family winery in the Roero, sandy hills north of Alba. Arneis is the local white grape: dry, soft and lightly floral, with pear and almond. An easy, good value white for shellfish or salads.

denis-mortet.name: Domaine Denis Mortet
denis-mortet.line: A leading Gevrey-Chambertin domaine founded by the late Denis Mortet and now run by his son Arnaud, known for deep coloured, intense reds.
denis-mortet.tell: Mortet is one of the benchmark names in Gevrey. The wines are dark, concentrated and long, from the village wine Mes Cinq Terroirs up to the premier crus. A safe recommendation for a guest who wants a full bodied red Burgundy.

descendientes-de-j-palacios.name: Descendientes de J. Palacios
descendientes-de-j-palacios.line: The Palacios family estate in Bierzo, which helped make Mencía famous.
descendientes-de-j-palacios.tell: Descendientes de J. Palacios is the Bierzo estate of Ricardo Pérez Palacios and his uncle Álvaro Palacios. Corullón comes from old vines on steep slate: fresh, floral and mineral Mencía. A beautiful red for a Burgundy lover.

deutz.name: Deutz
deutz.line: An Aÿ house, part of the Louis Roederer group, with a fine, elegant style.
deutz.tell: Deutz is an Aÿ house in the Roederer family of wines, known for finesse rather than power. The rosé is fresh and red-fruited, a lovely aperitif or partner for lighter seafood.

deux-montille.name: Maison Deux Montille
deux-montille.line: A négoce of siblings from the de Montille family, focused on whites.
deux-montille.tell: Deux Montille is the white wine house of Étienne and Alix de Montille. Sous Frétille is a Pernand-Vergelesses premier cru, crisp, fine and good value.

dhondt-grellet.name: Dhondt-Grellet
dhondt-grellet.line: A young-generation grower in the Côte des Blancs making precise, single-site Chardonnay Champagne.
dhondt-grellet.tell: Dhondt-Grellet is a family estate in the Côte des Blancs, now run by Adrien Dhondt. Les Nogers and Les Terres Fines are single sites; Le Bateau and Dans un Premier Temps are the blends. Dry, chalky, lively.

diamond-creek.name: Diamond Creek
diamond-creek.line: A Diamond Mountain pioneer that bottles its Cabernet by vineyard: Volcanic Hill, Red Rock Terrace and Gravelly Meadow.
diamond-creek.tell: Diamond Creek was among the first in Napa to bottle each vineyard separately, so guests can compare. Volcanic Hill is the firmest, Red Rock Terrace the most fragrant, Gravelly Meadow fine and mineral. These are long lived mountain Cabernets; older vintages need a word with the sommelier and a decanter.

didier-dagueneau.name: Didier Dagueneau
didier-dagueneau.line: The most celebrated name in Pouilly-Fumé, making intense, barrel-fermented Sauvignon Blanc.
didier-dagueneau.tell: Dagueneau made Pouilly-Fumé famous among collectors; his son Louis-Benjamin now runs it. Pur Sang is Sauvignon Blanc of real intensity, smoky and long. Far beyond everyday Sauvignon.

didier-fornerol.name: Didier Fornerol
didier-fornerol.line: A small grower in the southern Côte de Nuits making Côte de Nuits-Villages and other modest appellations with care.
didier-fornerol.tell: A small family grower from the villages at the southern end of the Côte de Nuits. Côte de Nuits-Villages gives honest, red fruited Pinot Noir at a gentle price. Good for a table that wants an easy, food friendly Burgundy.

diebolt-vallois.name: Diebolt-Vallois
diebolt-vallois.line: A family grower in Cramant making fine, creamy Blanc de Blancs.
diebolt-vallois.tell: Diebolt-Vallois is a family estate in Cramant, a grand cru for Chardonnay. The Blanc de Blancs is fine, floral and creamy; here in magnum for a larger table.

diego-magana.name: Diego Magaña
diego-magana.line: A small Rioja producer bottling single vineyard wines.
diego-magana.tell: Diego Magaña is a small Rioja producer. San Ginés is a single site red: classic Rioja fruit with a savoury edge. Ask the sommelier about its style before you describe it.

dirler-cade.name: Dirler-Cadé
dirler-cade.line: A biodynamic family estate in Bergholtz in southern Alsace.
dirler-cade.tell: Dirler-Cadé is a biodynamic family estate in southern Alsace. Edelzwicker is a traditional blend of Alsace grapes: aromatic, fresh and easy.

division-winemaking.name: Division Winemaking Company
division-winemaking.line: An urban winery in Portland making lively, Loire and Beaujolais inspired wines from Oregon vineyards.
division-winemaking.tell: Division is a small Portland winery that takes its cue from the Loire and Beaujolais. Renardière is Gamay from the Eola-Amity Hills: juicy, bright and lightly peppery, lovely a touch cool. A great pick for a guest who wants a light red with fish or poultry.

do-ferreiro.name: Do Ferreiro
do-ferreiro.line: A Rías Baixas estate known for old-vine Albariño.
do-ferreiro.tell: Do Ferreiro makes Albariño in Rías Baixas. Cepas Vellas comes from very old vines and has more depth than most.

dog-point.name: Dog Point Vineyard
dog-point.line: A Marlborough estate run by two families, known for Sauvignon Blanc and Pinot Noir.
dog-point.tell: Dog Point is a family estate in Marlborough. The Pinot Noir is fresh and savoury, with red cherry and spice. A good value Pinot for salmon or duck.

dom-perignon.name: Dom Pérignon
dom-perignon.line: Moët & Chandon's prestige vintage Champagne; the P2 release is held far longer on its lees.
dom-perignon.tell: Dom Pérignon is always a vintage and always a blend of Chardonnay and Pinot Noir. P2 is the same wine released at its second peak, after many more years on the lees, deeper and more toasty. The rosé is rarer still.

domaine-af-gros.name: Domaine A.F. Gros
domaine-af-gros.line: The Pommard based domaine of Anne-Françoise Gros, of the Gros family of Vosne-Romanée, making supple, ripe reds across the Côte d'Or.
domaine-af-gros.tell: A.F. Gros belongs to the wide Gros family of Vosne-Romanée. Their Chambolle-Musigny is the fragrant, silky side of the Côte de Nuits. A gentle, crowd pleasing red Burgundy.

domaine-arlaud.name: Domaine Arlaud
domaine-arlaud.line: A Morey-Saint-Denis family domaine farming biodynamically, making bright, fresh, finely tuned reds from regional wine to grand cru.
domaine-arlaud.tell: Arlaud is a Morey family estate known for clean, energetic Pinot Noir. The Roncevie is their excellent Bourgogne, and the grand cru Clos Saint-Denis is a serious, fragrant wine. Good value at every level.

domaine-carneros.name: Domaine Carneros
domaine-carneros.line: Taittinger's California estate in Carneros, making elegant traditional method sparkling wine.
domaine-carneros.tell: Domaine Carneros was founded by the Taittinger family in Carneros. Le Rêve is its prestige Blanc de Blancs, creamy, fine and long. A good bridge for a guest who loves Taittinger.

domaine-charvin.name: Domaine Charvin
domaine-charvin.line: A traditional Châteauneuf-du-Pape family domaine making pure, unoaked Grenache led wine.
domaine-charvin.tell: Charvin is a traditional Châteauneuf family. The wine is pure, fresh and fragrant, made without new oak. A great choice for lamb.

domaine-collotte.name: Domaine Collotte
domaine-collotte.line: A family grower in Marsannay, making village wines from named sites; this bottle has considerable age.
domaine-collotte.tell: Marsannay gives light, red fruited Pinot Noir. This is an older bottle, so expect gentle, savoury flavours rather than fresh fruit. Ask the sommelier to check it before recommending it as a showpiece.

domaine-coudert.name: Domaine Coudert
domaine-coudert.line: The Fleurie family domaine behind Clos de la Roilette, making firm, deep, age worthy Fleurie and Moulin-à-Vent.
domaine-coudert.tell: Coudert's Clos de la Roilette is a famous Fleurie site that gives a firmer, darker wine than most Fleurie. A great value red with poultry or pork.

domaine-d-aupilhac.name: Domaine d'Aupilhac
domaine-d-aupilhac.line: A Montpeyroux domaine run by Sylvain Fadat, farming organically and making deep southern French reds.
domaine-d-aupilhac.tell: Aupilhac is a respected Languedoc estate. Expect a deep, spicy southern red. A great value choice.

domaine-d-eugenie.name: Domaine d'Eugénie
domaine-d-eugenie.line: The Vosne-Romanée domaine owned by the Pinault family, also owners of Château Latour, built on the former Engel vineyards.
domaine-d-eugenie.tell: Eugénie is owned by the same family as Château Latour, so a Bordeaux lover may like the connection. Aux Brûlées is a respected Vosne premier cru giving rich, spicy Pinot Noir. A good bridge for a guest moving from Bordeaux to Burgundy.

domaine-de-beaurenard.name: Domaine de Beaurenard
domaine-de-beaurenard.line: A Châteauneuf-du-Pape family domaine farming biodynamically, making balanced, fresh Grenache led wines.
domaine-de-beaurenard.tell: Beaurenard is a family estate in Châteauneuf. Their wine is balanced and spicy. A good value Châteauneuf.

domaine-de-chevalier.name: Domaine de Chevalier
domaine-de-chevalier.line: A Graves classed growth whose white is one of Bordeaux's finest.
domaine-de-chevalier.tell: Domaine de Chevalier makes one of Bordeaux's finest whites. It is Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon, precise and long.

domaine-de-courcel.name: Domaine de Courcel
domaine-de-courcel.line: A historic Pommard family domaine, owner of a large share of the Grand Clos des Épenots, making whole cluster, long lived reds.
domaine-de-courcel.tell: Courcel is one of Pommard's best domaines. Its Grand Clos des Épenots is the flagship, a firm, fragrant wine that ages for years. A strong pick for a guest who wants a serious Côte de Beaune red.

domaine-de-durban.name: Domaine de Durban
domaine-de-durban.line: A hillside estate above Beaumes-de-Venise in the southern Rhône, famous for Muscat and also making Grenache-led reds.
domaine-de-durban.tell: Durban sits high above Beaumes-de-Venise, a village better known for sweet Muscat. Their red is Grenache-led: warm red fruit, a little spice and garrigue, and soft enough for a guest who wants something easy with meat.

domaine-de-ferrand.name: Domaine de Ferrand
domaine-de-ferrand.line: A small Châteauneuf-du-Pape domaine making Grenache led wine.
domaine-de-ferrand.tell: A small Châteauneuf estate. Expect a warm, spicy Grenache led red. A good value Châteauneuf.

domaine-de-l-alliance.name: Domaine de l'Alliance
domaine-de-l-alliance.tell: Domaine de l'Alliance is a small Bordeaux estate. Définition is a white; ask the sommelier about its grapes and style.

domaine-de-l-aurage.name: Domaine de l'Aurage
domaine-de-l-aurage.line: A Castillon estate run by Louis Mitjavile, son of François of Tertre Rôtebœuf, making rich Merlot led wine.
domaine-de-l-aurage.tell: L'Aurage is run by Louis Mitjavile, whose family makes Tertre Rôtebœuf. Rich, ripe Castillon. Good value.

domaine-de-l-ecu.name: Domaine de l'Écu
domaine-de-l-ecu.line: A biodynamic estate in the Muscadet country, best known for white, also making red such as this Pinot Noir sold as Vin de France.
domaine-de-l-ecu.tell: Domaine de l'Écu is known for its Muscadet. Ange is a Pinot Noir from the estate, bottled as Vin de France. Light and fresh; ask the sommelier how it is tasting.

domaine-de-l-enclos.name: Domaine de l'Enclos
domaine-de-l-enclos.tell: This is village Chablis from a family estate. It is crisp, lemony and stony Chardonnay, an easy partner for oysters and lighter seafood.

domaine-de-la-chapelle.name: Domaine de la Chapelle
domaine-de-la-chapelle.line: The estate created by the Frey family, owners of Paul Jaboulet Aîné, to make the famous Hermitage La Chapelle from the 2021 vintage on.
domaine-de-la-chapelle.tell: Hermitage La Chapelle was Jaboulet's famous wine; from 2021 it is made under the Domaine de la Chapelle name. Deep, powerful Syrah from the hill of Hermitage. Decant.

domaine-de-la-charbonniere.name: Domaine de la Charbonnière
domaine-de-la-charbonniere.line: A Châteauneuf-du-Pape family domaine also making Vacqueyras, in a ripe, generous style.
domaine-de-la-charbonniere.tell: Charbonnière is a family estate. Their Châteauneuf is ripe and warm, and the Vacqueyras Cuvée Spéciale is a good value alternative. Good with lamb.

domaine-de-la-cote.name: Domaine de la Côte
domaine-de-la-cote.region: Sta. Rita Hills, Santa Barbara County
domaine-de-la-cote.line: A Sta. Rita Hills estate of densely planted vineyards near the ocean, making taut, Burgundy minded single vineyard Pinot Noir.
domaine-de-la-cote.tell: Domaine de la Côte farms windy, cool hillsides at the western edge of the Sta. Rita Hills. The Pinot Noirs are fresh, savoury and fine, nearer Burgundy than ripe California. Bloom's Field, La Côte, Memorious and Sirens Call are separate sites. Great with duck, salmon or mushrooms.

domaine-de-la-mandeliere.name: Domaine de la Mandelière
domaine-de-la-mandeliere.line: A Chablis estate; Les Fourneaux is a premier cru, here in magnum.
domaine-de-la-mandeliere.tell: This is a Chablis premier cru, Les Fourneaux, in magnum. Expect crisp, stony Chardonnay without heavy oak, a good bottle to share around a table of oysters.

domaine-de-la-noblaie.name: Domaine de la Noblaie
domaine-de-la-noblaie.line: A Chinon family domaine making fresh and structured Cabernet Franc from tuffeau limestone.
domaine-de-la-noblaie.tell: Noblaie is a Chinon family estate. Le Temps des Cerises is a bright, cherry fruited Cabernet Franc meant to be enjoyed young. Lovely slightly cool.

domaine-de-la-pepiere.name: Domaine de la Pépière
domaine-de-la-pepiere.line: A benchmark Muscadet estate making crisp, mineral, long-lived wines from old vines and named crus.
domaine-de-la-pepiere.tell: Pépière is one of the estates that made people take Muscadet seriously. Château-Thébaud and Monnières-Saint-Fiacre are crus, aged longer on their lees: crisp, saline and deep. Perfect with raw oysters; magnums suit a table.

domaine-de-la-romanee-conti.name: Domaine de la Romanée-Conti
domaine-de-la-romanee-conti.line: The most famous estate in Burgundy, sole owner of Romanée-Conti and La Tâche, with holdings in Richebourg, Romanée-Saint-Vivant, Échezeaux and Grands-Échezeaux.
domaine-de-la-romanee-conti.tell: DRC is the most celebrated wine estate in the world for many collectors. Romanée-Conti and La Tâche are wholly owned grand crus. These bottles are extremely rare; involve the sommelier for service, decanting and any questions about the vintage.

domaine-de-la-vougeraie.name: Domaine de la Vougeraie
domaine-de-la-vougeraie.line: The Boisset family estate, farmed biodynamically, with vines across the Côte d'Or, including the rare white Le Clos Blanc de Vougeot.
domaine-de-la-vougeraie.tell: Vougeraie is the Boisset family's Burgundy estate, farmed biodynamically. Le Clos Blanc is a rare thing: a white premier cru from Vougeot, a village known for red. Fine and mineral Chardonnay, here in magnum and double magnum for a celebration.

domaine-de-marcoux.name: Domaine de Marcoux
domaine-de-marcoux.line: A Châteauneuf-du-Pape family domaine farming biodynamically, known for fragrant old vine Grenache.
domaine-de-marcoux.tell: Marcoux is a family estate known for its old vine Châteauneuf. The Vieilles Vignes is fragrant and deep. A special Rhône bottle.

domaine-de-nalys.name: Domaine de Nalys
domaine-de-nalys.line: A Châteauneuf-du-Pape estate making red and white.
domaine-de-nalys.tell: Nalys is a Châteauneuf-du-Pape estate. Its white is round, floral and rich, a southern white for spiced dishes.

domaine-de-trevallon.name: Domaine de Trévallon
domaine-de-trevallon.line: The cult Provence estate founded by Éloi Dürrbach, blending Cabernet Sauvignon and Syrah in the Alpilles.
domaine-de-trevallon.tell: Trévallon is a famous Provence estate blending Cabernet and Syrah. Deep, savoury and long lived. A good value choice for a Bordeaux drinker.

domaine-de-villaine.name: A. et P. de Villaine
domaine-de-villaine.line: The Bouzeron estate founded by Aubert de Villaine of the Domaine de la Romanée-Conti and his wife Pamela, making pure, unshowy Côte Chalonnaise wines.
domaine-de-villaine.tell: This is the family estate of Aubert de Villaine, long the co-director of Romanée-Conti, down in the quieter Côte Chalonnaise. The reds are fresh, red fruited Pinot Noir with real finesse for the price. A smart pick for a guest who loves Burgundy but not grand cru prices.

domaine-des-baumard.name: Domaine des Baumard
domaine-des-baumard.line: A family estate in Anjou making Chenin Blanc, dry and sweet.
domaine-des-baumard.tell: Baumard is a family estate in Anjou. Clos Sainte Catherine is a Coteaux du Layon: sweet Chenin Blanc, honeyed but fresh, with quince and apricot. Lovely with fruit desserts or cheese.

domaine-des-tours.name: Domaine des Tours
domaine-des-tours.line: An estate of Emmanuel Reynaud of Château Rayas.
domaine-des-tours.tell: Domaine des Tours is from the Reynaud family of Château Rayas. The Réserve white is round and aromatic.

domaine-du-coulet.name: Domaine du Coulet
domaine-du-coulet.line: A Cornas domaine run by Matthieu Barret, farming biodynamically, making fresh, vibrant Syrah.
domaine-du-coulet.tell: Coulet makes a fresher, brighter style of Cornas. Brise Cailloux is their main Cornas. Good with lamb.

domaine-du-pegau.name: Domaine du Pegau
domaine-du-pegau.line: The Féraud family's traditional Châteauneuf-du-Pape domaine, known for powerful, savoury, old school Grenache; Château Pégau is a related family estate.
domaine-du-pegau.tell: Pégau is one of the most traditional names in Châteauneuf. Cuvée Réservée is the main wine; Cuvée Laurence spends longer in barrel. Big, savoury reds; large formats here are great for a big table.

domaine-du-pelican.name: Domaine du Pélican
domaine-du-pelican.line: The Jura estate of Marquis d'Angerville of Volnay, making Chardonnay, Savagnin, Vin Jaune and sparkling wine.
domaine-du-pelican.tell: Domaine du Pélican is the Jura home of the d'Angerville family from Volnay. Grand Curoulet is a precise Chardonnay; the Savagnin Ouillé is topped up and fresh; the Vin Jaune is aged under a veil of yeast, nutty and intense.

domaine-du-petit-metris.name: Domaine du Petit Métris
domaine-du-petit-metris.line: A family estate in Anjou making Savennières and sweet Chenin Blanc.
domaine-du-petit-metris.tell: Petit Métris is a family estate in Anjou. Les Fougeraies is a dry Savennières: Chenin Blanc with apple, honey and a stony finish, a serious white for rich fish.

domaine-dubois.name: Domaine Dubois
domaine-dubois.line: A Côte de Beaune family grower, here a Chorey-lès-Beaune with real bottle age.
domaine-dubois.tell: Chorey-lès-Beaune is a modest village giving soft, fruity reds. This bottle is mature, so expect savoury, gentle flavours. One of the cheapest reds in the section.

domaine-duclaux.name: Domaine Benjamin & David Duclaux
domaine-duclaux.line: A Côte-Rôtie family domaine run by brothers Benjamin and David Duclaux, making fragrant, traditional Syrah.
domaine-duclaux.tell: The Duclaux brothers make fragrant, fresh Côte-Rôtie. La Germine is their main cuvée. A good recommendation with lamb or duck.

domaine-dujac.name: Domaine Dujac
domaine-dujac.line: The Morey-Saint-Denis domaine founded by Jacques Seysses and run by his family, known for whole cluster fermentation and silky, perfumed reds.
domaine-dujac.tell: Dujac is one of Burgundy's most loved names. They ferment with whole bunches, which gives a spicy, floral lift and silky texture; Dujac Fils et Père is the family's négociant label from bought grapes. From village wine to Clos de la Roche, these are elegant, fragrant bottles.

domaine-durand.name: Domaine Durand
domaine-durand.line: A family estate in the Loire and Sancerre, run by brothers, making crisp everyday Sauvignon Blanc.
domaine-durand.tell: Domaine Durand is a family estate in the Loire. This Sauvignon Blanc is the region in a glass: crisp, citrusy and green-edged, unoaked and easy with salads, goat cheese and lighter fish.

domaine-gautheron.name: Domaine Alain Gautheron
domaine-gautheron.line: A family estate in Chablis making crisp, mineral wines up to grand cru.
domaine-gautheron.tell: Gautheron is a family estate in Chablis. Bougros and Preuses are grand crus, richer and longer than village Chablis but still crisp and stony; the Bourgogne is the easy entry.

domaine-grosbois.name: Domaine Grosbois
domaine-grosbois.line: A Chinon family domaine farming organically and biodynamically, making fresh, characterful Cabernet Franc.
domaine-grosbois.tell: Grosbois is a Chinon family estate. La Cuisine de Ma Mère is the easy, fresh one; Gabare is deeper. Both are friendly with food and great value.

domaine-huet.name: Domaine Huet
domaine-huet.line: Vouvray's reference estate, biodynamic, bottling three great vineyards from dry to sweet.
domaine-huet.tell: Huet is the name in Vouvray. It bottles three vineyards, Le Haut-Lieu, Le Mont and Clos du Bourg, and each comes Sec (dry), Demi-Sec (gently sweet) or Moelleux (sweet). Always say which style before pouring; the sweeter ones love spice.

domaine-jamet.name: Domaine Jamet
domaine-jamet.line: A much admired Côte-Rôtie family domaine making traditional, whole cluster, savoury Syrah.
domaine-jamet.tell: Jamet is one of the great Côte-Rôtie names. Their Syrah is peppery, floral and savoury. The Côtes du Rhône is a lovely value way into their style.

domaine-labet.name: Domaine Labet
domaine-labet.line: A family estate in the Jura, known for wines from distinct parcels.
domaine-labet.tell: Labet is a family estate in the Jura, in eastern France. Chercheurs d'Or sits with the dessert wines here, in half bottle. Ask the sommelier how sweet it is and how it is made before you describe it.

domaine-labet-beaune.name: Domaine Labet (Beaune)
domaine-labet-beaune.line: A Beaune premier cru bottled under the Labet name, here Aux Coucherias.
domaine-labet-beaune.tell: Aux Coucherias is a Beaune premier cru giving a balanced, red fruited wine. Ask the sommelier about this producer.

domaine-larue.name: Domaine Larue
domaine-larue.line: A family domaine based in Saint-Aubin making wines from Saint-Aubin, Chassagne-Montrachet and Blagny.
domaine-larue.tell: Larue is a family grower from Saint-Aubin. Their red Chassagne La Boudriotte and Blagny premier cru are firm and fresh. Good value premier cru reds.

domaine-ledogar.name: Domaine Ledogar
domaine-ledogar.line: A Corbières family domaine making natural leaning southern reds.
domaine-ledogar.tell: Ledogar is a Corbières family estate. Le Mariole is Carignan. Fresh, juicy and fun.

domaine-leflaive.name: Domaine Leflaive
domaine-leflaive.line: The great biodynamic estate of Puligny-Montrachet, with premier and grand cru vineyards.
domaine-leflaive.tell: Leflaive is the name for Puligny-Montrachet: pure, floral, long whites from biodynamic vines. Clavoillon, Pucelles, Folatières and Combettes are premier crus, with Bâtard, Bienvenues and Chevalier-Montrachet at the top. The Mâcon-Verzé, by the glass and by the bottle, is the gentle door into the house.

domaine-matrot.name: Domaine Matrot
domaine-matrot.line: A Meursault family domaine, run by Thierry and Pascale Matrot, known mostly for whites, also making reds from the southern Côte de Beaune.
domaine-matrot.tell: Matrot is a well known Meursault family. Their reds from Saint-Aubin and Maranges are light, fresh and modestly priced. Good choices for a lighter meal.

domaine-newman.name: Domaine Newman
domaine-newman.line: A small domaine with grand cru holdings in the Côte de Nuits, here a Bonnes-Mares.
domaine-newman.tell: Domaine Newman is a small estate with parcels in some famous grand crus. Bonnes-Mares gives a deep, structured wine. Comparatively modest in price for a grand cru; ask the sommelier how this bottle is drinking.

domaine-ponsot.name: Domaine Ponsot
domaine-ponsot.line: A famous Morey-Saint-Denis domaine, a great name in Clos de la Roche, known for a traditional style without new oak and cuvées named after birds and insects.
domaine-ponsot.tell: Ponsot is one of the great Morey names, with grand crus from Clos de la Roche to Chambertin. Cuvée names like Grives, Pinson and Abeille mean thrush, finch and bee. The wines are fragrant and long; suggest decanting the grand crus.

domaine-roulot.name: Domaine Roulot
domaine-roulot.line: A celebrated Meursault domaine run by Jean-Marc Roulot, famous for pure white wines, which also makes a little red Monthélie.
domaine-roulot.tell: Roulot is one of the most sought after names in Meursault whites. The red Monthélie is a rare, fresh, finely made Pinot Noir. A treat for a guest who knows the name.

domaine-saint-damien.name: Domaine Saint Damien
domaine-saint-damien.line: A Gigondas family domaine making old vine, Grenache led wines.
domaine-saint-damien.tell: Saint Damien makes old vine Gigondas, rich, spicy and good value. Ask the sommelier where the name of La Louisianne comes from; a Louisiana link would be a good story to tell, if it is true.

domaine-saint-martin.name: Domaine Saint-Martin
domaine-saint-martin.line: A little seen Burgundy name, here a Bonnes-Mares grand cru with some bottle age.
domaine-saint-martin.tell: A rarely seen bottling of Bonnes-Mares, the grand cru shared by Chambolle and Morey. This bottle has had years to soften. Ask the sommelier about the producer and how it is drinking.

domaine-serene.name: Domaine Serene
domaine-serene.tell: Domaine Serene is a Dundee Hills estate. Evenstad Reserve is its top Chardonnay, rich yet fresh.

domaine-serrigny.name: Domaine Serrigny
domaine-serrigny.line: A small Côte de Beaune grower, here a village Savigny-lès-Beaune.
domaine-serrigny.tell: Savigny-lès-Beaune gives fresh, red fruited Pinot Noir at friendly prices. A good value choice for a lighter red with chicken or pork.

domaine-tempier.name: Domaine Tempier
domaine-tempier.line: The famous Bandol domaine of the Peyraud family, making Mourvèdre led reds from named sites.
domaine-tempier.tell: Tempier is the most famous name in Bandol. La Migoua and La Tourtine are single site wines; Lulu et Lucien is a special cuvée. Big, savoury reds for lamb.

domaine-trapet.name: Domaine Trapet
domaine-trapet.line: A historic Gevrey-Chambertin domaine run biodynamically by Jean-Louis Trapet, with Chambertin, Latricières and Chapelle-Chambertin.
domaine-trapet.tell: Trapet is a long established Gevrey family with excellent grand crus. The wines are pure and fragrant. Capita is listed among the Gevrey premier crus; ask the sommelier about it.

domaine-vacheron.name: Domaine Vacheron
domaine-vacheron.line: A biodynamic family estate in Sancerre making precise, single-site Sauvignon Blanc and Pinot Noir.
domaine-vacheron.tell: Vacheron is a biodynamic family estate in Sancerre. Le Paradis is a single site Sauvignon Blanc with more depth and minerals than most Sancerre, lovely with goat cheese and fish.

domaine-viret.name: Domaine Viret
domaine-viret.line: A southern Rhône family domaine practising its own form of biodynamic farming, here a Vin de France.
domaine-viret.tell: Viret is an unusual southern Rhône estate with its own farming philosophy. Renaissance is a deep, spicy red. Ask the sommelier about how it is made.

domaine-vocoret.name: Domaine Vocoret et Fils
domaine-vocoret.line: A long-established family estate in Chablis.
domaine-vocoret.tell: Vocoret is a family estate in Chablis. Les Clos is the great grand cru, rich and powerful for Chablis; the village wine is crisp and fresh.

domaines-barons-de-rothschild.name: Domaines Barons de Rothschild (Lafite), Légende range
domaines-barons-de-rothschild.line: The Légende wines from the Lafite Rothschild family company, appellation blends made to show each Bordeaux appellation's character.
domaines-barons-de-rothschild.tell: Légende Pauillac comes from the family that owns Château Lafite. It is a friendly, Cabernet led Pauillac at an approachable price. A good way to give a guest the Lafite connection without the first growth price.

dominio-de-pingus.name: Dominio de Pingus
dominio-de-pingus.line: A cult Ribera del Duero estate founded by Peter Sisseck; Flor de Pingus is its second wine.
dominio-de-pingus.tell: Pingus is one of Spain's cult wines, made in tiny amounts by Peter Sisseck in Ribera del Duero. Flor de Pingus is the more available second wine: deep, dark and polished Tempranillo. A celebration red for beef.

dominio-del-challao.name: Dominio del Challao
dominio-del-challao.line: A young biodynamic estate in Labastida, Rioja Alavesa, from a family with wineries in Bierzo and Argentina.
dominio-del-challao.tell: Challao is a young biodynamic estate in Labastida, Rioja Alavesa, worked partly with horses. Challao is a field blend led by Tempranillo; Vino de Labastida is the village wine. Fresh, modern, terroir minded Rioja.

dominus.name: Dominus Estate
dominus.line: Christian Moueix's Napa estate near Yountville, making a refined, Bordeaux minded Cabernet blend.
dominus.tell: Dominus belongs to Christian Moueix, whose family is famous in Pomerol. The wine comes from the old Napanook vineyard near Yountville and is fine, firm and less showy than many Napa reds. A great choice for a Bordeaux lover.

domus-aurea.name: Domus Aurea
domus-aurea.line: A family estate in the foothills of the Andes near Santiago, making long lived Cabernet.
domus-aurea.tell: Domus Aurea is a family estate in Maipo Alto, at the foot of the Andes. The Cabernet is fresh and fine, with dark fruit and mint, and it ages well. A thoughtful alternative to Bordeaux.

donnhoff.name: Dönnhoff
donnhoff.tell: Dönnhoff is the Nahe's greatest name. Hermannshöhle and Brücke are famous sites; the GG is dry, while Spätlese and Auslese are sweeter.

dows.name: Dow's
dows.line: A great Port house of the Symington family, known for drier styled Vintage Ports.
dows.tell: Dow's is one of the great Port houses, known for a slightly drier finish than most. The Vintage Ports are dark and firm, and the list holds several years and a half bottle. Decant older bottles.

doyard.name: Doyard
doyard.line: A family grower in Vertus making traditional, oak-touched Chardonnay Champagne.
doyard.tell: Doyard is a family estate in Vertus. Vendémiaire is a premier cru Blanc de Blancs, partly oak-aged, with a rich, nutty side to its crisp fruit.

dr-hermann.name: Dr. Hermann
dr-hermann.tell: Dr. Hermann is a family estate in Erden on the Mosel. The Spätlese and Auslese bottles are sweeter Rieslings, lovely with spice or dessert.

dr-konstantin-frank.name: Dr. Konstantin Frank
dr-konstantin-frank.tell: Konstantin Frank pioneered European grapes in the Finger Lakes. The Dry Riesling is crisp and good value.

drappier.name: Drappier
drappier.line: A family house in the Aube, deep in Pinot Noir country, with a lightly dosed style and a love of large bottles.
drappier.tell: Drappier is a family house in the Côte des Bar in the south of Champagne, where Pinot Noir rules. The wines are fruit-driven and often low in added sugar; Brut Nature has none. Grande Sendrée is their prestige vintage.

drc.name: Domaine de la Romanée-Conti
drc.line: The most famous estate in Burgundy; its whites are Le Montrachet and Corton-Charlemagne.
drc.tell: Domaine de la Romanée-Conti is Burgundy's most famous name. Its whites are Le Montrachet and Corton-Charlemagne, rare and very costly, so always involve the sommelier.

droin.name: Jean-Paul et Benoît Droin
droin.line: A long-established family estate in Chablis making grand and premier cru wines with some oak.
droin.tell: Droin is an old family estate in Chablis. Valmur and Vaudésir are grand crus, richer and deeper; Montée de Tonnerre, Montmains and Vaillons are premier crus. Hommage à Louis honours a family elder.

dubreuil-fontaine.name: Domaine Dubreuil-Fontaine
dubreuil-fontaine.line: A family domaine in Pernand-Vergelesses with holdings on the hill of Corton, making traditional, firm reds that age well.
dubreuil-fontaine.tell: Dubreuil-Fontaine is rooted on the hill of Corton. Their Corton grand crus, Bressandes, Clos du Roi and Perrières, are firm, structured reds, and several here have some age. Good value grand cru for red meat.

duckhorn.name: Duckhorn
duckhorn.line: The Napa house that made Merlot famous in California, now also known for polished Cabernet; Three Palms is its celebrated Merlot vineyard.
duckhorn.tell: Duckhorn made its name with Merlot when few in Napa took it seriously. Three Palms Vineyard Merlot is the famous one: plush, plummy and deep. The Napa Cabernet is smooth and reliable. A safe, recognisable name, and the large bottles suit a big table.

dugat-py.name: Domaine Bernard Dugat-Py
dugat-py.line: A cult Gevrey-Chambertin domaine, now run by Loïc Dugat-Py, known for very old vines, tiny yields and dense, concentrated, long lived reds.
dugat-py.tell: Dugat-Py is one of the most sought after names in Gevrey. Old vines and very low yields give deep, dark, powerful wines that need time and air. These are rare bottles: suggest decanting, and let the guest know they are holding something collectors chase.

dujac.name: Domaine Dujac
dujac.line: A great Morey-Saint-Denis estate, famous for reds, with fine whites too.
dujac.tell: Dujac is a great Morey-Saint-Denis estate, best known for reds. Monts Luisants is a rare white premier cru in Morey, and Les Combettes and Les Folatières are Puligny premier crus.

dumol.name: DuMOL
dumol.line: A Russian River Valley winery known for rich yet fresh Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and Syrah from cool Sonoma sites.
dumol.tell: DuMOL makes Pinot Noir in the Russian River Valley with ripe fruit and good freshness. Ryan and Wester Reach are vineyard bottlings, dark cherried and silky. A good choice for a guest who likes a fuller Pinot that still tastes lively.

dunn.name: Dunn Vineyards
dunn.line: A family estate on Howell Mountain famous for firm, long lived Cabernet in a restrained style.
dunn.tell: Dunn makes some of Napa's longest lived reds, high on Howell Mountain: firm, dark and less alcoholic than many. Young bottles are tight and need decanting. Ask the sommelier about this one, which the list groups with Petite Sirah.

dureuil-janthial.name: Domaine Dureuil-Janthial
dureuil-janthial.line: A leading Rully domaine in the Côte Chalonnaise, making fresh, precise reds and whites.
dureuil-janthial.tell: Dureuil-Janthial is one of the best names in Rully. Their red is bright and crisp, an excellent value Burgundy. Good with lighter meats.

duval-leroy.name: Duval-Leroy
duval-leroy.line: A family-owned house in Vertus at the south of the Côte des Blancs, with a Chardonnay-rich, elegant style.
duval-leroy.tell: Duval-Leroy is family owned, based in Vertus in the Côte des Blancs. Femme de Champagne is their prestige cuvée, long-aged and Chardonnay-led: creamy, refined and complex.

egly-ouriet.name: Egly-Ouriet
egly-ouriet.line: An Ambonnay grower making powerful, long-aged, Pinot Noir-rich Champagne, among the most sought after.
egly-ouriet.tell: Egly-Ouriet farms Ambonnay, a grand cru for Pinot Noir, and rests its wines a long time on their lees, so they taste deep and vinous. Les Crayères is an old-vine Blanc de Noirs and the Millésime is the vintage, a wine-lover's Champagne for rich dishes.

egon-muller.name: Egon Müller
egon-muller.line: The most famous estate of the Saar, owner of the Scharzhofberg.
egon-muller.tell: Egon Müller is the Saar's great name and the leading owner on the Scharzhofberg hill. The Kabinett is light and gently sweet, delicate and very rare.

el-enemigo.name: El Enemigo
el-enemigo.line: A Mendoza project of Alejandro Vigil and Adrianna Catena.
el-enemigo.tell: El Enemigo is a Mendoza project of Alejandro Vigil and Adrianna Catena. Its Chardonnay is fresh and good value.

elena-walch.name: Elena Walch
elena-walch.line: A leading family estate in Alto Adige, known for fresh, precise whites and Pinot Nero.
elena-walch.tell: Elena Walch is a family estate in Alto Adige, the Italian Alps. Ludwig is their top Pinot Nero: fresh, fine and red fruited, with good depth. An elegant red for salmon, duck or veal.

eleni-edouard-vocoret.name: Domaine Eleni et Edouard Vocoret
eleni-edouard-vocoret.line: A young couple's estate in Chablis making precise, organic-leaning premier crus.
eleni-edouard-vocoret.tell: Eleni and Edouard Vocoret started their own estate in Chablis. Butteaux and Forêts are premier crus, Bas de Chapelot a village site. Pure, crisp and stony.

elk-cove.name: Elk Cove
elk-cove.line: A family estate among the older wineries of the Willamette Valley, known for Pinot Noir and Pinot Gris.
elk-cove.tell: Elk Cove is a family winery in the northern Willamette Valley. Roosevelt Vineyard is one of their single sites: a darker, deeper Pinot Noir with fine tannin. The list holds several vintages in magnum, a good way to bring an Oregon Pinot to a big table.

els-jelipins.name: Els Jelipins
els-jelipins.line: A tiny Penedès producer known for natural wine from the local Sumoll grape.
els-jelipins.tell: Els Jelipins is a tiny producer in Penedès, working the local red grape Sumoll in a natural way. The wine is fresh, wild and fragrant. A rare, adventurous pick.

elvio-cogno.name: Elvio Cogno
elvio-cogno.line: A family estate in Novello, in the Barolo zone, known for elegant Barolo from the Ravera vineyard.
elvio-cogno.tell: Elvio Cogno is a family estate in Novello, at the south west of the Barolo zone. Ravera is their top Barolo: fine, perfumed and firm. Montegrilli is a Langhe Nebbiolo, younger and friendlier, a gentle introduction to the grape at a fair price.

emidio-pepe.name: Emidio Pepe
emidio-pepe.line: A legendary Abruzzo family estate making Montepulciano by hand and releasing older vintages from its cellar.
emidio-pepe.tell: Emidio Pepe makes Montepulciano d'Abruzzo the traditional way and holds bottles back for years. The wines are earthy, deep and long lived. The list holds several vintages; ask the sommelier which is ready and decant carefully.

emmerich-knoll.name: Emmerich Knoll
emmerich-knoll.tell: Knoll is a classic Wachau family estate. Kellerberg is a famous Riesling site, and this mature bottle is dry, rich and mineral.

emrich-schonleber.name: Emrich-Schönleber
emrich-schonleber.tell: Emrich-Schönleber is a top Nahe estate. Halgans Trocken is a dry Riesling, crisp and mineral.

enclos-de-carbonnieux.name: L'Enclos de Carbonnieux
enclos-de-carbonnieux.line: A white Pessac-Léognan with the Carbonnieux name.
enclos-de-carbonnieux.tell: This is white Pessac-Léognan, Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon, crisp and citrusy. Ask the sommelier how it relates to Château Carbonnieux.

envinate.name: Envínate
envinate.line: A group of friends making fresh, low intervention wines from Atlantic and mountain vineyards across Spain.
envinate.tell: Envínate is four friends making wine in the Canary Islands, Galicia and Almansa. Their reds are fresh and savoury: Lousas is Mencía from Ribeira Sacra, Táganan, Benje and Migan come from volcanic Tenerife, and Albahra is Garnacha Tintorera. Light, smoky and lively, great with food.

eric-forest.name: Eric Forest
eric-forest.line: A small Pouilly-Fuissé grower in Vergisson.
eric-forest.tell: Eric Forest is a small grower in Pouilly-Fuissé. 24 Carats is a ripe, round Chardonnay with a fresh finish.

eric-rodez.name: Eric Rodez
eric-rodez.line: An Ambonnay grower working plot by plot, with some oak, for detailed grand cru Champagne.
eric-rodez.tell: Eric Rodez is a grower in Ambonnay who vinifies plot by plot and uses some oak. Empreinte Blanche is Chardonnay-led and fine; Les Genettes is a single site. Expect depth and detail rather than big-brand polish.

etienne-becheras.name: Étienne Bécheras
etienne-becheras.line: A small Crozes-Hermitage grower making natural leaning Syrah.
etienne-becheras.tell: Bécheras is a small Crozes grower. Le Prieuré d'Arras is a fresh, peppery Syrah. A good value pick.

etienne-sauzet.name: Domaine Etienne Sauzet
etienne-sauzet.line: A leading Puligny estate making finely chiselled whites up to grand cru.
etienne-sauzet.tell: Sauzet is a top Puligny-Montrachet estate with finely chiselled whites. Les Combettes, Les Referts and La Garenne are premier crus and Le Montrachet is the summit; Jardin du Calvaire is a Hautes Côtes white.

evening-land.name: Evening Land Vineyards
evening-land.line: An Eola-Amity Hills winery built around the Seven Springs vineyard, known for taut, mineral Pinot Noir and Chardonnay.
evening-land.tell: Evening Land farms Seven Springs, one of Oregon's most respected vineyards. Summum is the top selection: a fine, intense Pinot Noir with real structure. A strong pick for a Burgundy drinker who wants to try Oregon.

ex-post-facto.name: Ex Post Facto
ex-post-facto.line: A Syrah project from Santa Barbara winemaker Greg Brewer, whole cluster fermented and aged in old barrels.
ex-post-facto.tell: Ex Post Facto is Greg Brewer's Syrah, from cool Santa Barbara County. It is made with whole bunches and no new oak, so it is peppery, floral and fresh. A smart pick for a Northern Rhône lover.

eyrie.name: The Eyrie Vineyards
eyrie.line: The winery that planted the first Pinot Noir in the Willamette Valley in the 1960s, still family run and making light, graceful wines.
eyrie.tell: Eyrie is where Oregon Pinot Noir began. Original Vines comes from those first plantings; South Block and Sisters are other old sites. The wines are pale, fragrant and fine, and age beautifully. They also make a rare Pinot Meunier. A must for a guest who loves history and finesse.

faiveley.name: Domaine Faiveley
faiveley.line: A historic Nuits-Saint-Georges house and one of Burgundy's biggest vineyard owners, making structured, modern, well made reds from Mercurey to Chambertin.
faiveley.tell: Faiveley owns a remarkable spread of vineyards, many in the Côte de Nuits and the Côte Chalonnaise. The reds are dark, firm and reliable, from Mercurey up to the Chambertin grand crus. A safe, quality recommendation at almost any price.

familia-torres.name: Familia Torres
familia-torres.line: Spain's great family wine house, from Penedès, with estates across the country.
familia-torres.tell: Torres is Spain's best known wine family. Mas La Plana is their famous Penedès Cabernet; Salmos and Secret del Priorat come from Priorat, deep and mineral; Celeste is a Ribera del Duero Tempranillo. Reliable, quality reds at many price points.

famille-mousse.name: Famille Moussé
famille-mousse.line: A family grower in the Marne valley devoted to Meunier, making expressive Blanc de Noirs.
famille-mousse.tell: Moussé is a family estate in the Marne valley, champions of Meunier. Les Fortes Terres is a Blanc de Noirs: fruity, rounded and savoury. Good with fried seafood and richer starters.

famille-perrin.name: Famille Perrin
famille-perrin.line: The Perrin family's négociant range, from the owners of Château de Beaucastel.
famille-perrin.tell: The Perrin family, of Beaucastel, make this Côtes du Rhône-Villages. The half bottle is a handy, easy red.

fantino.name: Alessandro e Gian Natale Fantino
fantino.line: A small family estate in Monforte d'Alba making traditional Nebbiolo.
fantino.tell: Fantino is a small family estate in Monforte d'Alba. Rosso dei Dardi is a Nebbiolo from their vineyard: fragrant and savoury, with firm tannin. A thoughtful, fair priced Piedmont red.

far-niente.name: Far Niente
far-niente.line: An Oakville estate that makes only Chardonnay and Cabernet Sauvignon.
far-niente.tell: Far Niente is an Oakville estate that makes just Chardonnay and Cabernet. The Chardonnay is rich and creamy, with polished oak, here in magnum for a larger table.

faust.name: Faust
faust.line: A Napa Cabernet label from the Huneeus family of Quintessa, ripe and polished in style.
faust.tell: Faust comes from the family behind Quintessa. It is a ripe, generous Napa Cabernet, with dark fruit and smooth tannin, easy to like. Here in magnum, it is a strong value choice for a table that wants big Napa red.

faustino.name: Bodegas Faustino
faustino.line: A large family house in Rioja Alavesa; Faustino I is its famous Gran Reserva.
faustino.tell: Faustino is a well known family house in Rioja. Faustino I Gran Reserva is aged for years before release: mellow, with dried cherry, leather and vanilla. A classic, mature Rioja at a fair price.

feist.name: Feist
feist.line: A Port house known mainly for ruby and tawny Ports.
feist.tell: Feist is a Port house known for ruby and tawny styles. Late Bottled Vintage Port is from a single year, aged longer in wood before bottling: rich, dark and ready to drink. Good with chocolate desserts.

felsina.name: Fattoria di Fèlsina
felsina.line: A Chianti Classico estate in Castelnuovo Berardenga, known for Rancia and for pure Sangiovese.
felsina.tell: Fèlsina is a top estate at the southern edge of Chianti Classico. Rancia Riserva is one of the region's classic single vineyard Sangioveses: firm and long. Maestro Raro is their Cabernet. Great Tuscan reds for beef.

ferrari.name: Ferrari
ferrari.line: A family-owned house in Trento making traditional method sparkling wine from mountain vineyards.
ferrari.tell: Ferrari, no relation to the cars, is Trento's great sparkling house. The Brut is crisp and appley; Perlé is a vintage Blanc de Blancs; the Rosé is fruity and dry. The half-bottle suits one or two.

ferraton.name: Ferraton Père & Fils
ferraton.line: A northern Rhône house, linked to Chapoutier, farming biodynamically and making wines across the northern appellations.
ferraton.tell: Ferraton is a northern Rhône house. Les Grands Mûriers is a Cornas. Dark, powerful Syrah.

ferruccio-carlotto.name: Ferruccio Carlotto
ferruccio-carlotto.line: A small Alto Adige family estate known for Pinot Nero from Mazzon.
ferruccio-carlotto.tell: Carlotto is a small family estate in Alto Adige. Mazzon is a famous slope for Pinot Nero, and Filari di Mazzon is fragrant and fine, with red fruit and spice. A lovely, lighter red for fish or poultry.

fisher.name: Fisher Vineyards
fisher.line: A family estate high in the Mayacamas mountains on the Sonoma side.
fisher.tell: Fisher is a family winery on the mountain ridge between Sonoma and Napa. Mountain Estate Chardonnay is concentrated and balanced, and this bottle has some age.

florent-garaudet.name: Domaine Florent Garaudet
florent-garaudet.line: A small estate in Monthelie making Meursault.
florent-garaudet.tell: Garaudet is a small estate based in Monthelie. This is a village Meursault from old vines, here in magnum for a table to share.

folktale.name: Folktale Winery
folktale.line: A Carmel Valley winery blending Monterey County fruit, with literary names on its wines.
folktale.tell: Folktale is a Carmel Valley winery with storybook names. The Ruler is a Pinot Noir blended from several Monterey County sites, including the Santa Lucia Highlands: earthy, savoury and full. A good, generous Pinot for heartier dishes.

follin-arbelet.name: Domaine Follin-Arbelet
follin-arbelet.tell: Follin-Arbelet is a small estate in Aloxe-Corton. Corton-Charlemagne is its grand cru white, powerful and mineral.

fontanafredda.name: Fontanafredda
fontanafredda.line: A historic Serralunga estate founded on land once owned by Italy's first king.
fontanafredda.tell: Fontanafredda is a historic estate in Serralunga, linked to Italy's first king. La Rosa, La Villa and Lazzarito are single vineyard Barolos, and the Riserva is aged longer. Firm, classic Nebbiolo for beef and game.

foradori.name: Foradori
foradori.line: A biodynamic Trentino estate, led by Elisabetta Foradori, that revived the local Teroldego grape.
foradori.tell: Foradori is the great name for Teroldego, a dark grape of the Trentino mountains. Sgarzon is aged in clay amphorae: fresh, juicy and lightly earthy, with dark berries. A fun magnum for a table that likes lighter, natural style reds.

forge-cellars.name: Forge Cellars
forge-cellars.line: A Seneca Lake winery co-founded by Louis Barruol of Saint Cosme.
forge-cellars.tell: Forge Cellars is a Finger Lakes winery on Seneca Lake. Les Alliés is a dry Riesling, crisp and mineral.

forlorn-hope.name: Forlorn Hope
forlorn-hope.tell: Forlorn Hope works with unusual grapes in California. Rorick Vineyard is in the Sierra Foothills, and the Picpoul is crisp and saline.

forman.name: Forman Vineyard
forman.line: Winemaker Ric Forman's small Napa estate, known for restrained, Bordeaux style Cabernet and lean Chardonnay.
forman.tell: Ric Forman makes a small amount of Cabernet in a restrained, Bordeaux like style: medium bodied, fresh and made to age. A thoughtful pick for a guest who wants classic Napa without heavy oak. Several vintages are on the list.

fourrier.name: Domaine Fourrier
fourrier.line: A Gevrey-Chambertin domaine run by Jean-Marie Fourrier, prized for old vines and pure, transparent, fragrant reds.
fourrier.tell: Fourrier is one of the most sought after growers in Gevrey. The wines are fresh, fragrant and precise rather than heavy, with old vines throughout. Clos Saint-Jacques is the star; the village Vieilles Vignes is a lovely entry point.

francois-bertheau.name: Domaine François Bertheau
francois-bertheau.line: A small Chambolle-Musigny family domaine, here a bottle of the famous Les Amoureuses premier cru.
francois-bertheau.tell: Les Amoureuses is Chambolle's most famous premier cru, often priced like a grand cru. Bertheau is a small local family. A fragrant, silky red for a special evening.

francois-carillon.name: François Carillon
francois-carillon.line: François Carillon's own Puligny estate, made after the family domaine divided in 2010.
francois-carillon.tell: François Carillon makes pure, precise Puligny. Les Folatières is a premier cru; Les Enseignères a village site; Les Murgers des Dents de Chien a Saint-Aubin premier cru.

francois-chidaine.name: François Chidaine
francois-chidaine.line: A biodynamic grower and the leading name in Montlouis, making dry and sweet Chenin Blanc.
francois-chidaine.tell: Chidaine is the star of Montlouis, across the river from Vouvray. Les Tuffeaux is Chenin Blanc, often with a touch of sweetness; ask the sommelier how dry this vintage is. Lovely with spiced dishes.

francois-lumpp.name: Domaine François Lumpp
francois-lumpp.line: A Givry grower in the Côte Chalonnaise, known as one of the village's leading names for red Pinot Noir.
francois-lumpp.tell: Lumpp is a leading name in Givry, south of the Côte d'Or. His wines are bright, red fruited and well made, good value next to the big villages. A friendly, food ready red Burgundy.

francois-mikulski.name: François Mikulski
francois-mikulski.line: A Meursault grower known mainly for whites, also making red Pommard.
francois-mikulski.tell: Mikulski is a respected Meursault name. This village Pommard is a firm, dark fruited red. A good match for steak.

francoise-bedel.name: Françoise Bedel
francoise-bedel.line: A biodynamic grower at the western end of the Marne valley, working mostly with Meunier.
francoise-bedel.tell: Françoise Bedel farms biodynamically in the far west of the Marne valley, where Meunier is king. The wines are generous, aromatic and long-aged before release. Originelle, Dis Vin Secret and Entre Ciel et Terre are three different blends.

frank-cornelissen.name: Frank Cornelissen
frank-cornelissen.line: A Belgian born winemaker on Etna, known for natural wines and single contrada Munjebel reds.
frank-cornelissen.tell: Frank Cornelissen makes natural wine on Etna. His Munjebel reds come from single contrade, the local name for vineyards, each a little different: fragrant, savoury and mineral. An adventurous pick for a curious guest.

frank-family.name: Frank Family Vineyards
frank-family.line: A Napa winery in Calistoga making approachable Cabernet, Zinfandel and Chardonnay.
frank-family.tell: Frank Family is a popular Napa name with an easygoing style. The Zinfandel is ripe and spicy, with jammy berry fruit, a good partner for barbecue flavours or a rich, peppery dish.

franz-hirtzberger.name: Franz Hirtzberger
