franz-hirtzberger.tell: Hirtzberger is a top Wachau name. Honivogl and Singerriedel are famous sites, and Smaragd is the ripest dry style: rich yet fresh.

frecciarossa.name: Frecciarossa
frecciarossa.line: A long established estate in the Oltrepò Pavese hills of southern Lombardy.
frecciarossa.tell: Frecciarossa is a family estate in the Oltrepò Pavese, hills south of Milan. Its Pinot Grigio is fresh and clean, with a little more texture than the everyday kind. A safe, friendly white for fish or salads.

frederic-magnien.name: Frédéric Magnien
frederic-magnien.line: The négociant label of Frédéric Magnien in Morey-Saint-Denis, bottling wines from bought grapes across the Côte de Nuits.
frederic-magnien.tell: Frédéric Magnien buys grapes from growers across the Côte de Nuits and makes them in Morey. The wines are fresh and clear. A good value route into Clos Vougeot and Morey.

freemark-abbey.name: Freemark Abbey
freemark-abbey.line: A historic St. Helena winery and an early champion of single vineyard Cabernet, notably Bosché and Sycamore.
freemark-abbey.tell: Freemark Abbey is one of the old names of Napa. Bosché and Sycamore were among the first vineyard named Cabernets in California: classic, cedary and long lived. The Napa Valley Cabernet is the easier entry.

frischengruber.name: Frischengruber
frischengruber.line: A family estate in the Wachau.
frischengruber.tell: Frischengruber is a family estate in the Wachau. Federspiel is a lighter dry style of Grüner Veltliner, crisp and peppery.

fritz-haag.name: Fritz Haag
fritz-haag.tell: Fritz Haag is a top Mosel estate in Brauneberg. The Kabinett is light and gently sweet, here with some bottle age.

frogs-leap.name: Frog's Leap
frogs-leap.line: A Rutherford winery farming organically without irrigation, making balanced, food friendly Cabernet, Merlot and Zinfandel.
frogs-leap.tell: Frog's Leap farms organically and dry farms its vines in Rutherford. The wines are balanced and lower in alcohol than many Napa reds: the Cabernet is fresh and savoury, the Merlot supple. A good pick for a guest who wants Napa that goes with food.

fuligni.name: Fuligni
fuligni.line: A family estate in Montalcino making elegant, traditional Brunello.
fuligni.tell: Fuligni is a family estate just east of Montalcino. Its Brunello is fine and fragrant rather than heavy, with cherry, leather and herbs. The Riserva in magnum is a grand choice for a table eating beef.

gabrielskloof.name: Gabriëlskloof
gabrielskloof.line: A Bot River estate making fresh, balanced wines.
gabrielskloof.tell: Gabriëlskloof is an estate in Bot River, near the cool coast. The Blend is a Bordeaux style red: dark fruit and fresh acidity. A good value alternative to Bordeaux.

gaia.name: Gaia
gaia.line: A Greek estate making Assyrtiko on Santorini.
gaia.tell: Gaia makes Assyrtiko on the volcanic island of Santorini. Wild Ferment is crisp, saline and textured, superb with seafood.

gainey.name: Gainey Vineyard
gainey.region: Santa Ynez Valley and Sta. Rita Hills, California
gainey.line: A family estate in Santa Barbara County, farming cool Sta. Rita Hills fruit for Chardonnay and Pinot Noir.
gainey.tell: Gainey is a family winery in Santa Barbara County. Their Sta. Rita Hills Chardonnay comes from a cool, windy pocket near the Pacific, so it keeps fresh acidity under its ripe fruit and gentle oak: California richness without heaviness.

gaja.name: Gaja
gaja.line: The most famous name in Barbaresco, known for its Barbaresco and single vineyards such as Sorì San Lorenzo, Sorì Tildìn and Costa Russi.
gaja.tell: Gaja put Barbaresco on the world map. The Barbaresco is fine and perfumed; Sorì San Lorenzo, Sorì Tildìn and Costa Russi are single vineyards sold as Langhe, and Darmagi is a rare Piedmont Cabernet. Celebration bottles. The family also owns Pieve Santa Restituta, Ca' Marcanda and IDDA.

gamet.name: Gamet
gamet.line: A family grower in the Marne valley; Rive Gauche is its left-bank blend, here in magnum.
gamet.tell: Gamet is a family estate in the Marne valley. Rive Gauche is a blend from the river's left bank, here in magnum. Ask the sommelier for the grape mix before you describe it in detail.

ganevat.name: Jean-François Ganevat
ganevat.line: A cult Jura grower making natural leaning wines, many sold as Vin de France.
ganevat.tell: Ganevat is a cult name in the Jura. De Toute Beauté is a Vin de France red. Light, fresh and fragrant.

garmon.name: Bodegas Garmón
garmon.line: A Ribera del Duero estate making rich, polished Tempranillo.
garmon.tell: Garmón is a Ribera del Duero estate. The wine is Tempranillo, called Tinto Fino here: dark, ripe and polished, with firm tannin. Good with beef or lamb.

gaston-chiquet.name: Gaston Chiquet
gaston-chiquet.line: A Dizy family grower known for a rare Blanc de Blancs from Aÿ, a village planted mostly to Pinot Noir.
gaston-chiquet.tell: Gaston Chiquet is a family estate in Dizy. Their Blanc de Blancs d'Aÿ is unusual: Chardonnay from Aÿ, where Pinot Noir dominates, so it is fuller and rounder than a Côte des Blancs Chardonnay. Here in magnum.

gavoty.name: Domaine Gavoty
gavoty.tell: Gavoty is a Provence family estate. La Cigale is a pale, dry rosé, crisp and good value.

gd-vajra.name: G.D. Vajra
gd-vajra.line: A family estate in the high hamlet of Vergne, making fresh, fragrant Barolo.
gd-vajra.tell: Vajra farms high vineyards near the village of Barolo, so its wines are fresh and perfumed. Albe is its Barolo blended from several high sites: bright, floral and approachable for Barolo. A smart entry to the region.

geantet-pansiot.name: Domaine Geantet-Pansiot
geantet-pansiot.line: A Gevrey-Chambertin family domaine making generous, ripe and approachable reds from village and premier cru sites.
geantet-pansiot.tell: Geantet-Pansiot makes a rich, rounded style of Gevrey that is easy to enjoy young. The old vine bottlings are a good step up. A safe recommendation for a guest who wants fruit and body.

genot-boulanger.name: Domaine Génot-Boulanger
genot-boulanger.line: A Côte de Beaune domaine with vineyards spread from Mercurey to Clos Vougeot, making clean, precise reds and whites.
genot-boulanger.tell: Génot-Boulanger farms across the Côte de Beaune and beyond. Their reds here range from Aloxe-Corton and Pommard to Corton and Clos Vougeot grand cru. A reliable choice with balanced, modern Pinot Noir.

georg-breuer.name: Georg Breuer
georg-breuer.line: A Rheingau estate known for dry Riesling.
georg-breuer.tell: Breuer is a Rheingau estate known for dry Riesling. Rauenthaler Nonnenberg is one of its sites, and the Trocken is dry, firm and fine.

georges-roumier.name: Domaine Georges Roumier
georges-roumier.line: The Chambolle-Musigny domaine of Christophe Roumier, one of the most celebrated names in Burgundy, known for intense, precise reds.
georges-roumier.tell: Roumier is among the most sought after names in all of Burgundy. Bonnes-Mares and the Clos de la Bussière monopole in Morey are both here. These wines are rare and highly prized; suggest decanting and treat them as the occasion.

georges-vernay.name: Domaine Georges Vernay
georges-vernay.line: The family domaine credited with saving Condrieu, now run by Christine Vernay, also making fine Côte-Rôtie and Saint-Joseph.
georges-vernay.tell: Vernay is famous for white Condrieu, and its reds are elegant. Maison Rouge and Blonde du Seigneur are Côte-Rôtie; Terre d'Encre is Saint-Joseph. Fragrant, fine Syrah.

gerard-duplessis.name: Gérard Duplessis
gerard-duplessis.line: A small, traditional Chablis estate making long-lived wines.
gerard-duplessis.tell: Duplessis is a small, traditional estate. Les Clos is a grand cru; Mont de Milieu and Montmains premier crus. The wines are firm and slow to open.

gerard-raphet.name: Domaine Gérard Raphet
gerard-raphet.line: A Morey-Saint-Denis family domaine with a range across Gevrey, Morey, Chambolle and Clos Vougeot, in a traditional style.
gerard-raphet.tell: Raphet is a quiet family estate in Morey-Saint-Denis. The wines are traditional, firm and fruity, from village wines up to Clos Vougeot. A good value name on a list of famous ones.

geyer-wine-co.name: Geyer Wine Co.
geyer-wine-co.line: A small Barossa producer making characterful reds.
geyer-wine-co.tell: Geyer Wine Co. is a small Barossa label. Big Easy is a Petit Verdot blend: dark, juicy and fun. A good value red with a New Orleans friendly name.

giaconda.name: Giaconda
giaconda.line: A Beechworth estate famed for Chardonnay.
giaconda.tell: Giaconda is a Beechworth estate famed for Chardonnay. It is rich, complex and rare, among Australia's most sought-after whites.

gilbert-picq.name: Gilbert Picq et ses Fils
gilbert-picq.line: A family estate in Chichée making crisp Chablis.
gilbert-picq.tell: Picq is a family estate in Chichée, near Chablis. Their village Chablis is crisp, fresh and mineral, a classic with raw oysters.

giovanni-viberti.name: Giovanni Viberti
giovanni-viberti.line: A family estate in the Barolo zone making traditional Riserva Barolo.
giovanni-viberti.tell: Viberti is a family estate near the village of Barolo. Bricco delle Viole and San Pietro are Riserva Barolos: fragrant, savoury and firm. Good with beef, lamb or game.

giuseppe-mascarello.name: Giuseppe Mascarello e Figlio
giuseppe-mascarello.line: A great traditional family estate whose Monprivato Barolo is one of the most admired in Piedmont.
giuseppe-mascarello.tell: Giuseppe Mascarello is one of the great traditional names of Barolo. Monprivato is their famous vineyard in Castiglione Falletto: fragrant, fine and long lived. They also make a lovely Dolcetto from Santo Stefano di Perno. Rare; decant the Barolo.

goldeneye.name: Goldeneye
goldeneye.line: Duckhorn's Pinot Noir estate in the cool Anderson Valley of Mendocino, making rich, polished Pinot.
goldeneye.tell: Goldeneye is the Pinot Noir home of the Duckhorn family, in the foggy Anderson Valley north of Sonoma. The wine is ripe and generous, with dark cherry and a silky texture. A good choice for a Cabernet drinker trying Pinot for the first time; also in half bottle and magnum.

gonet-medeville.name: Gonet-Médeville
gonet-medeville.line: A family grower whose family also owns property in Sauternes, making textured, food-friendly Champagne.
gonet-medeville.tell: Gonet-Médeville joins a Champagne family and a Bordeaux one. Champ d'Alouette is a single site Extra Brut, dry, deep and vinous, made for the table rather than the toast.

gosset.name: Gosset
gosset.line: An Aÿ house that traces its wine roots to 1584 and usually avoids malolactic fermentation, keeping wines taut and fresh.
gosset.tell: Gosset claims to be the oldest wine house in Champagne and makes wines with bright, firm acidity because it usually blocks the softening malolactic step. Grande Réserve is the house blend; Celebris is the prestige vintage. Ideal with rich food.

gourt-de-mautens.name: Gourt de Mautens
gourt-de-mautens.line: A small Rasteau domaine, run by Jérôme Bressy, making deep, fine Grenache led wine sold under a regional name.
gourt-de-mautens.tell: Gourt de Mautens is a much admired small estate near Rasteau. Expect a deep, fragrant Grenache led wine. The magnum is great for a big table.

goutorbe-bouillot.name: Goutorbe-Bouillot
goutorbe-bouillot.line: A family grower in Damery on the Marne making fruity, approachable blends.
goutorbe-bouillot.tell: Goutorbe-Bouillot is a family estate in Damery. Reflets de Rivière and Le Ru des Charmes are their blends, built on Pinot Noir and Meunier from the river valley: fruity, round and easy to enjoy.

grahams.name: Graham's
grahams.line: A great Port house of the Symington family, known for rich, sweet Vintage Ports.
grahams.tell: Graham's is one of the great Port names, known for a rich, sweet style. The Vintage Ports are dark and luscious, and several years are listed. Decant older bottles; wonderful with chocolate or blue cheese.

granbazan.name: Granbazán
granbazan.tell: Granbazán is a Rías Baixas estate. Don Álvaro is an Albariño, crisp and citrusy.

grange-des-peres.name: Domaine de la Grange des Pères
grange-des-peres.line: A cult Languedoc estate making tiny amounts of red and white.
grange-des-peres.tell: Grange des Pères is a cult name in the Languedoc. Its white is rich and rare, made in tiny amounts.

gregory-perez.name: Gregory Pérez (Brezo)
gregory-perez.line: A Bierzo winemaker whose Brezo label offers fresh, good value Mencía.
gregory-perez.tell: Brezo is Gregory Pérez's Bierzo Mencía: fresh, floral and red fruited, with a peppery lift. A great value, food friendly red, lovely with poultry or pork.

grgich-hills.name: Grgich Hills
grgich-hills.line: The estate of Mike Grgich, who made the winning 1976 Paris Chardonnay at Montelena, now farming organically across Napa.
grgich-hills.tell: Grgich Hills was founded by Mike Grgich, the winemaker behind the Chardonnay that won the 1976 Paris tasting. The estate farms organically. The Cabernet is balanced and classic, the Zinfandel spicy, and Violetta is a sweet late harvest wine for dessert.

gros-frere-et-soeur.name: Domaine Gros Frère et Soeur
gros-frere-et-soeur.line: A Vosne-Romanée domaine of the Gros family, making ripe, plush reds including a Clos Vougeot from the Musigni parcel.
gros-frere-et-soeur.tell: Another branch of the Gros family in Vosne-Romanée, with a generous, ripe style. Their Clos Vougeot comes from the top of the vineyard near Musigny. A good bet for a guest who likes a fuller Burgundy.

grosjean.name: Grosjean
grosjean.line: A family estate in the alpine Valle d'Aosta, making fresh mountain wines.
grosjean.tell: Grosjean is a family estate in the Valle d'Aosta, high in the Alps. Their Gamay is light, bright and red fruited, like a mountain Beaujolais. A gentle red for fish or poultry, best a little cool.

guigal.name: E. Guigal
guigal.line: The most famous house of the northern Rhône, based in Ampuis, known for its single vineyard Côte-Rôtie La Mouline, La Landonne and La Turque.
guigal.tell: Guigal is the big name of the Rhône, and the single vineyard Côte-Rôties, La Mouline, La Landonne and La Turque, are among the most collected Rhône wines. Château d'Ampuis is a blend; Vignes de l'Hospice is their Saint-Joseph. Decant the big ones.

guillaume-gilles.name: Guillaume Gilles
guillaume-gilles.line: A small Cornas grower making traditional, deep Syrah.
guillaume-gilles.tell: Gilles is a small Cornas grower who makes classic, dark, savoury Syrah. A good pick for lamb or game.

guillaume-selosse.name: Guillaume Selosse
guillaume-selosse.line: Anselme Selosse's son, who makes small lots under his own name.
guillaume-selosse.tell: Guillaume Selosse is Anselme's son and makes his own wines in tiny amounts. Largillier is a rosé, and the date in brackets on the list is its disgorgement, so this is a rare find for a guest who already knows the Selosse name.

guimaro.name: Guímaro
guimaro.line: A family estate on the steep slopes of Ribeira Sacra, making fresh Mencía.
guimaro.tell: Guímaro is a family estate in Ribeira Sacra, where vines grow on dizzying river terraces. Camino Real is a Mencía: fresh, peppery and red fruited, with mineral depth. A great swap for a Pinot or Cru Beaujolais lover.

gunderloch.name: Gunderloch
gunderloch.tell: Gunderloch is a Rheinhessen estate in Nackenheim. Hipping GG is a dry grand cru Riesling from red slate soil.

gut-oggau.name: Gut Oggau
gut-oggau.line: A biodynamic estate in Burgenland whose labels show imagined family members, one for each wine.
gut-oggau.tell: Gut Oggau farms biodynamically by Lake Neusiedl, and every label is a portrait of an imagined family member. Joschuari is Blaufränkisch: fresh, savoury and juicy, natural in style. A great talking point for an adventurous guest.

guy-bocard.name: Domaine Guy Bocard
guy-bocard.line: A family estate in Meursault devoted to white wine.
guy-bocard.tell: Guy Bocard is a Meursault family estate devoted to white wine. Genevrières is a premier cru and Limozin a village site next to the premier crus; the list spells it Brocard.

guy-breton.name: Guy Breton
guy-breton.line: One of the original natural wine growers of Beaujolais, based in Morgon.
guy-breton.tell: Guy Breton was one of the growers who brought natural, carefully made Beaujolais back into fashion. His Fleurie is fragrant and silky, with red berries and flowers. Serve it slightly cool; the magnum is fun for a big table.

guy-mea.name: Guy Méa
guy-mea.line: A family estate in Louvois on the Montagne de Reims, blending Pinot Noir and Chardonnay from grand and premier cru villages.
guy-mea.tell: Guy Méa is a family estate in Louvois. L'Assemblage is a Pinot Noir-led blend with Chardonnay, low in dosage, with citrus, white flowers and a bready edge. A grower bottle at a fair price.

guy-robin.name: Domaine Guy Robin
guy-robin.line: A traditional Chablis estate known for old vines.
guy-robin.tell: Guy Robin is a traditional estate. Valmur is a grand cru; the Vieilles Vignes Chablis comes from old vines, with more depth than most village wine.

hand-work.name: Hand Work
hand-work.line: An organic La Mancha label from the Parra brothers.
hand-work.tell: Hand Work is made by three brothers who farm organically in La Mancha. The Garnacha is juicy and bright, with red cherry and strawberry. A great value, easy red for casual dishes.

hans-wirsching.name: Hans Wirsching
hans-wirsching.line: A Franken estate known for Silvaner.
hans-wirsching.tell: Wirsching is a Franken estate known for Silvaner. The Trocken is dry and earthy, with some bottle age.

hanzell.name: Hanzell
hanzell.line: One of the oldest Pinot Noir and Chardonnay estates in California, in the hills above the Sonoma Valley, built in homage to Burgundy.
hanzell.tell: Hanzell was set up long ago to make Burgundy style wine in Sonoma and still farms some of the oldest Pinot Noir vines in the state. The Pinot is firm, savoury and long lived, not a fruit bomb. A classic, collectable California name; decant younger bottles.

harlan-estate.name: Harlan Estate
harlan-estate.line: The Oakville hillside estate of Bill Harlan, one of the most celebrated and costly Cabernets in America.
harlan-estate.tell: Harlan Estate farms the western hills of Oakville and makes one of Napa's most famous Cabernet blends: deep, layered and very long lived. The list holds many vintages. These are trophy bottles; involve the sommelier, decant and give it time.

hartford-court.name: Hartford Court
hartford-court.line: A Sonoma winery focused on cool climate Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and old vine Zinfandel from the Russian River Valley and beyond.
hartford-court.tell: Hartford Court makes Pinot Noir from cool sites in Sonoma and Mendocino. The Russian River Valley bottling is ripe and silky, with red cherry and a little spice, an easy crowd pleaser. The half bottle suits two guests; Muldane Trail comes from Anderson Valley.

haut-brion.name: Château Haut-Brion
haut-brion.line: The first growth of Pessac-Léognan, whose white is among the rarest in Bordeaux.
haut-brion.tell: Haut-Brion is a first growth. Its white is Sémillon and Sauvignon Blanc, rich and long, made in small amounts and very costly, so involve the sommelier.

haynes-vineyard.name: Haynes Vineyard
haynes-vineyard.line: A vineyard estate in cool Coombsville, Napa, making fresh, low oak Syrah and Pinot Noir.
haynes-vineyard.tell: Haynes Vineyard sits in Coombsville, one of Napa's coolest corners. Forgeron is a Syrah made with whole bunches and old barrels: floral, peppery and fresh. Unusual for Napa, and lovely with lamb or duck.

heinrich.name: Heinrich
heinrich.line: A biodynamic family estate in Gols, by Lake Neusiedl, making Blaufränkisch and other Austrian reds.
heinrich.tell: Heinrich is a biodynamic family estate in Gols, near Lake Neusiedl. Alter Berg is a Blaufränkisch from an old hillside site: dark cherry, pepper and firm freshness. A lovely red for duck, pork or game.

heitz-cellar.name: Heitz Cellar
heitz-cellar.line: A historic Napa winery whose Martha's Vineyard Cabernet is among California's most famous single vineyard wines.
heitz-cellar.tell: Heitz made one of Napa's first famous single vineyard Cabernets, Martha's Vineyard, often described with a minty, eucalyptus note. Trailside and Linda Falls are other sites. The list holds a long run of vintages; for older ones, ask the sommelier how they are drinking and decant gently.

henri-bourgeois.name: Henri Bourgeois
henri-bourgeois.line: A large family house in Chavignol making Sauvignon Blanc across Sancerre and nearby appellations.
henri-bourgeois.tell: Henri Bourgeois is a family house in Sancerre country. This bottle sits under Menetou-Salon on the list, a neighbour of Sancerre: crisp, citrusy Sauvignon Blanc at a gentler price.

henri-gilles-buisson.name: Domaine Henri et Gilles Buisson
henri-gilles-buisson.line: A family estate in Saint-Romain, high in the hills of the Côte de Beaune.
henri-gilles-buisson.tell: Buisson is a family estate in Saint-Romain, high in the cool hills of the Côte de Beaune. La Perrière is a crisp, mineral white and good value.

henri-giraud.name: Henri Giraud
henri-giraud.line: An old Aÿ family house that ages its wines in oak from the nearby Argonne forest.
henri-giraud.tell: Henri Giraud is a family house in Aÿ that ferments and ages in casks made from Argonne oak, close to Champagne. The wines are rich, vinous and nutty; Argonne is the top cuvée and Fût de Chêne the oak-aged blend.

henri-gouges.name: Domaine Henri Gouges
henri-gouges.line: The reference domaine of Nuits-Saint-Georges, making firm, dark, long lived reds from the village's best premier crus.
henri-gouges.tell: Gouges is the name most people think of in Nuits-Saint-Georges. The wines are sturdy and structured, with dark fruit and an earthy edge, and they age very well. The half bottles are a great option for two guests with red meat.

henri-prudhon.name: Domaine Henri Prudhon
henri-prudhon.line: A Saint-Aubin family domaine, best known for white wine, also making red Saint-Aubin premier cru.
henri-prudhon.tell: Saint-Aubin sits in a side valley behind Puligny and Chassagne. Its reds are light and fresh, and these bottles have some age. A modest price for a premier cru red.

henriot.name: Henriot
henriot.line: A Reims family house with a Chardonnay-rich style, fine and lightly toasty.
henriot.tell: Henriot leans on Chardonnay for a fine, creamy, lightly toasty style. The Blanc de Blancs is crisp; the Millésime is the vintage; Cuvée des Enchanteleurs and Hemera are the long-aged prestige wines.

henriques-and-henriques.name: Henriques & Henriques
henriques-and-henriques.tell: Henriques & Henriques is a classic Madeira house. Founder's Solera Verdelho is medium dry: nutty, tangy and caramel edged, with bright acidity. Lovely with nuts, cheese or a light dessert.

heritance.name: Heritance
heritance.line: A Napa label of the Taub family, making classic Cabernet from mid valley sites such as Beckstoffer Georges III in Rutherford.
heritance.tell: Heritance bottles Napa Cabernet in a classic style. Georges III is a famous Beckstoffer vineyard in Rutherford, once part of the Beaulieu holdings, and gives a rich, dark wine with Rutherford's dusty earthiness. A good value way to a famous vineyard name.

heritiers-comte-lafon.name: Les Héritiers du Comte Lafon
heritiers-comte-lafon.line: The Lafon family's Mâconnais estate, making bright Chardonnay.
heritiers-comte-lafon.tell: This is the Mâconnais estate of the Lafon family of Meursault. Milly-Lamartine is fresh and floral, Lafon style at a value price.

hermann-ludes.name: Hermann Ludes
hermann-ludes.tell: Hermann Ludes is a Mosel grower. Ask the sommelier how dry this Riesling is before you describe it.

hermann-moser.name: Hermann Moser
hermann-moser.tell: Hermann Moser is a family estate in Kremstal. Gebling Hannah is a Grüner Veltliner Reserve, round and peppery, with some bottle age.

hexamer.name: Hexamer
hexamer.tell: Hexamer is a Nahe family estate. Kabinett and Spätlese are sweeter, while the Trocken is dry.

hickinbotham.name: Hickinbotham Clarendon Vineyard
hickinbotham.line: A historic hillside vineyard in Clarendon, McLaren Vale.
hickinbotham.tell: Hickinbotham is a historic vineyard on the hills of Clarendon in McLaren Vale. Trueman is its Cabernet Sauvignon: dark, firm and fresh. A good alternative to Bordeaux.

hirsch.name: Weingut Hirsch
hirsch.line: A Kamptal family estate, organic and biodynamic, known for Heiligenstein Riesling and Grüner Veltliner.
hirsch.tell: Hirsch is an organic family estate in the Kamptal. Lamm is a Grüner Veltliner site, and Gaisberg and Heiligenstein are Riesling sites: crisp, mineral and precise.

hirsch-vineyards.name: Hirsch Vineyards
hirsch-vineyards.line: A pioneering vineyard on the ridges of the far Sonoma Coast, near the Pacific, making taut, fragrant Pinot Noir and Chardonnay.
hirsch-vineyards.tell: Hirsch farms steep ridges a few miles from the ocean on the far Sonoma Coast. The Pinot Noirs are fresh, savoury and fine, closer to Burgundy than to ripe California. East Ridge, West Ridge and San Andreas Fault are separate parts of the estate. Lovely with salmon, duck or mushrooms.

hourglass.name: Hourglass
hourglass.region: St. Helena and Calistoga, Napa Valley
hourglass.line: A family estate in the narrow north of Napa Valley, making dark, polished Cabernet and blends.
hourglass.tell: Hourglass takes its name from the shape of the valley where it narrows near St. Helena. The Estate Cabernet is dark, rich and smooth, with good freshness. A strong modern Napa choice for steak.

hubert-lamy.name: Domaine Hubert Lamy
hubert-lamy.line: A Saint-Aubin domaine famous for precise white wines from densely planted vines, also making small amounts of red.
hubert-lamy.tell: Lamy is one of the stars of Saint-Aubin, mainly for whites. This red Santenay is a rarer bottling, fresh and finely made. A good conversation bottle for a guest who knows the name.

hubert-lignier.name: Domaine Hubert Lignier
hubert-lignier.line: A Morey-Saint-Denis family domaine making deep, traditional reds from village wine up to Clos de la Roche.
hubert-lignier.tell: Lignier is a respected Morey family. The wines are deep and classic, with a long life. Clos de la Roche is their grand cru; the Morey premier crus are good value.

hudelot-baillet.name: Domaine Hudelot-Baillet
hudelot-baillet.line: A Chambolle-Musigny family domaine making fresh, fragrant reds.
hudelot-baillet.tell: Hudelot-Baillet is a Chambolle family grower. Their reds are fragrant and fresh. The old vine Chambolle is a lovely silky red with chicken or duck.

hudson-vineyards.name: Hudson Vineyards
hudson-vineyards.line: A famous Carneros grower whose fruit goes to many top wineries, also bottling its own wines.
hudson-vineyards.tell: Hudson is a renowned grower in Carneros whose grapes appear on many famous labels. Its own Syrah is cool climate in style: dark fruit, pepper and fresh acidity. Good with lamb.

hundred-acre.name: Hundred Acre
hundred-acre.line: A cult Napa winery making very ripe, opulent single vineyard Cabernets such as Ark, Kayli Morgan and Wraith.
hundred-acre.tell: Hundred Acre makes Cabernet in a big, opulent style: very ripe, dense and velvety. Ark, Kayli Morgan and Wraith are separate vineyards. Rare and costly; for a guest who loves the richest Napa, and a bottle to decant.

hure-freres.name: Huré Frères
hure-freres.line: A family grower in Ludes on the Montagne de Reims, run by siblings, with a fresh, precise style.
hure-freres.tell: Huré Frères is a family estate on the Montagne de Reims. 4 Éléments is a single-grape, single-site series; ask the sommelier which grape this bottle is. Low dosage, crisp and focused.

hyde-de-villaine.name: Hyde de Villaine
hyde-de-villaine.line: A partnership between the Hyde family of Carneros and Aubert de Villaine of Burgundy's Romanée-Conti, making elegant wines.
hyde-de-villaine.tell: Hyde de Villaine joins a Carneros farming family with Aubert de Villaine of Burgundy. Belle Cousine is their Merlot led red blend: fresh, fine and restrained, California fruit with European balance. A thoughtful pick for a Bordeaux lover.

i-vigneri.name: I Vigneri di Salvo Foti
i-vigneri.line: Salvo Foti's group of Etna growers, working old vines by hand in the traditional way.
i-vigneri.tell: Salvo Foti is one of Etna's most respected viticulturists, and I Vigneri works old vines by traditional methods. Vinupetra is a deep, mineral Etna Rosso. A wine with real character.

idda.name: IDDA
idda.line: A partnership between Angelo Gaja and Sicilian grower Alberto Graci on Mount Etna.
idda.tell: IDDA is Angelo Gaja's project on Etna with local grower Alberto Graci. The Etna Rosso is fragrant and fine, with red fruit and volcanic minerality. A good story for a guest who knows Gaja.

il-marroneto.name: Il Marroneto
il-marroneto.line: A small Montalcino estate admired for pale, perfumed, traditional Brunello.
il-marroneto.tell: Il Marroneto is a small estate just outside the town of Montalcino. Its Brunello is fragrant and fine rather than heavy; Madonna delle Grazie is the celebrated single vineyard. A great pick for a guest who loves elegance.

il-poggione.name: Il Poggione
il-poggione.line: A historic family estate in the south of Montalcino making classic Brunello.
il-poggione.tell: Il Poggione is a historic family estate in southern Montalcino. Its Brunello is classic and generous, with cherry, leather and spice. A reliable choice for steak.

inglenook.name: Inglenook
inglenook.line: A historic Rutherford estate restored by Francis Ford Coppola, whose flagship red is Rubicon.
inglenook.tell: Inglenook is one of Napa's historic estates in Rutherford, brought back together by Francis Ford Coppola. Rubicon is the flagship Cabernet blend, deep and structured; Blancaneaux is the estate's white blend, rounder and richer.

ink-grade.name: Ink Grade
ink-grade.line: A Howell Mountain estate making Cabernet from high, rocky vineyards.
ink-grade.tell: Ink Grade farms on Howell Mountain, high above the Napa fog. Mountain Cabernet here is dark, firm and concentrated. A strong pick for beef; ask the sommelier about decanting.

inniskillin.name: Inniskillin
inniskillin.line: A Niagara winery that helped make Canadian icewine famous.
inniskillin.tell: Inniskillin helped put Canadian icewine on the map. Icewine is made from grapes frozen on the vine. This one is Cabernet Franc: sweet, with strawberry and red berry flavours and bright acidity. A pretty match for fruit or chocolate desserts.

isabel-ferrando.name: Famille Isabel Ferrando
isabel-ferrando.line: The family label of Isabel Ferrando, known for Domaine Saint-Préfert in Châteauneuf-du-Pape.
isabel-ferrando.tell: Isabel Ferrando is a respected Châteauneuf grower. Expect a fragrant, fine Grenache led red. A good pick for lamb.

j-davies.name: J. Davies
j-davies.line: The red wine estate of the Davies family of Schramsberg, making Cabernet on Diamond Mountain.
j-davies.tell: J. Davies is the Cabernet side of the family behind Schramsberg sparkling wine, from their vineyards on Diamond Mountain. The wine is structured and dark, with mountain firmness. A nice story if the table started with Schramsberg.

j-dumangin.name: J. Dumangin & Fils
j-dumangin.line: A family grower in Chigny-les-Roses making round, approachable Champagne at a fair price.
j-dumangin.tell: Dumangin is a family estate on the Montagne de Reims. The Brut is fruity, round and easy to love, a great grower Champagne for a guest who wants something beyond the big brands without paying a lot.

j-lassalle.name: J. Lassalle
j-lassalle.line: A family estate in Chigny-les-Roses, long run by the women of the family, with a fine, gentle style.
j-lassalle.tell: J. Lassalle is a small family house on the Montagne de Reims, known for finesse. The Special Club is their prestige bottle under the growers' club that sets a strict standard; the Blanc de Blancs is crisp and delicate.

jacques-frederic-mugnier.name: Domaine Jacques-Frédéric Mugnier
jacques-frederic-mugnier.line: A celebrated Chambolle-Musigny domaine, run by Frédéric Mugnier, known for weightless, ethereal reds from Musigny and Bonnes-Mares.
jacques-frederic-mugnier.tell: Mugnier is one of the most admired names in Chambolle. The wines are delicate, fragrant and long. Bonnes-Mares here is a rare treat; recommend it to a guest who loves finesse.

jacques-girardin.name: Domaine Jacques Girardin
jacques-girardin.line: A Santenay family domaine making reds from Santenay and neighbouring villages including Pommard.
jacques-girardin.tell: A family grower from Santenay at the southern end of the Côte de Beaune. The Santenay Clos Rousseau premier cru and the Pommard are honest, firm reds. Good value with roasts.

jacques-selosse.name: Jacques Selosse
jacques-selosse.line: Anselme Selosse's Avize estate, the most influential grower in modern Champagne, making rich, oxidative, barrel-aged wines.
jacques-selosse.tell: Selosse changed grower Champagne: barrel-fermented, bold, nutty and savoury, almost like great white Burgundy with bubbles. Substance is built from a perpetual reserve and Initial is the entry Blanc de Blancs; the date the list prints in brackets is the disgorgement.

jaeger-defaix.name: Domaine Jaeger-Defaix
jaeger-defaix.line: An organic Rully estate run by Hélène Jaeger-Defaix, with premier cru vines.
jaeger-defaix.tell: Jaeger-Defaix farms organically in Rully, in the Côte Chalonnaise. Rabourcé is a premier cru, and the list prints the name as Defaix Frères.

jansz.name: Jansz
jansz.line: A Tasmanian sparkling specialist using cool-climate fruit for traditional method wine.
jansz.tell: Jansz is a Tasmanian sparkling house. The island's cool climate keeps acidity bright, so the Premier Cuvée is fresh and creamy, made the Champagne way at a friendly price.

jarvis.name: Jarvis
jarvis.line: A Napa estate known for its winery built entirely inside caves, making rich Cabernet.
jarvis.tell: Jarvis makes its wine inside a network of caves in the hills east of Napa. The Reserve Cabernet is rich and long, with dark fruit and polish. A good celebratory Napa pick.

jauma.name: Jauma
jauma.line: A natural wine producer in the Adelaide Hills making light, juicy reds.
jauma.tell: Jauma makes natural wine in the Adelaide Hills. Birdsey is a Cabernet Franc from the Seaview area of McLaren Vale: light, juicy and lively. An adventurous pick, lovely slightly cool.

jb-becker.name: J.B. Becker
jb-becker.line: A Walluf estate known for traditional, long-aged Riesling.
jb-becker.tell: Becker makes traditional Rheingau Riesling in Walluf, aged long before release. Walkenberg and Sonnenberg are sites; Trocken means dry, and the Spätlese without it is sweeter.

jean-baptiste-hardy.name: Jean-Baptiste Hardy
jean-baptiste-hardy.region: Mouzillon, Muscadet Sèvre et Maine, Loire
jean-baptiste-hardy.line: A young vigneron who took over his family vines in Mouzillon in 2018, after training in Burgundy.
jean-baptiste-hardy.tell: Jean-Baptiste Hardy came home to his family's Muscadet vines after working in Burgundy. Fief de Chaintre is his top wine from an old plot, aged on its lees: textured, saline and serious Muscadet.

jean-chauvenet.name: Domaine Jean Chauvenet
jean-chauvenet.line: A Nuits-Saint-Georges family domaine making classic, firm village and premier cru wines.
jean-chauvenet.tell: Chauvenet is a traditional Nuits family. The village Nuits is a sturdy, dark red. A good value match for steak.

jean-claude-bachelet.name: Jean-Claude Bachelet
jean-claude-bachelet.tell: Bachelet is a family estate in Saint-Aubin. Les Champlots is a premier cru, crisp and mineral and good value against its famous neighbours.

jean-claude-lapalu.name: Jean-Claude Lapalu
jean-claude-lapalu.line: A Brouilly grower making natural leaning, characterful cru Beaujolais.
jean-claude-lapalu.tell: Lapalu makes characterful Brouilly with plenty of energy. A fun, fresh red for a curious guest.

jean-collet.name: Domaine Jean Collet et Fils
jean-collet.line: A family estate in Chablis with grand and premier cru holdings.
jean-collet.tell: Collet is a family estate in Chablis. Valmur is a grand cru, Vaillons a premier cru, here in magnum; the village Chablis is crisp and fresh.

jean-foillard.name: Jean Foillard
jean-foillard.line: One of the original natural wine growers of Morgon, famous for the Côte du Py, making deep, fine, age worthy Gamay.
jean-foillard.tell: Foillard is one of the original Beaujolais growers who changed how the region is seen. Côte du Py is a famous hill in Morgon. The wines have depth and freshness; serve them slightly cool.

jean-grivot.name: Domaine Jean Grivot
jean-grivot.line: A leading Vosne-Romanée domaine run by Étienne Grivot and family, making fine, expressive reds from village wine to Richebourg.
jean-grivot.tell: Grivot is one of the great Vosne-Romanée names, with a range from village Vosne up to Richebourg. The wines are refined and long, with a lovely spicy fruit. A safe, distinguished choice at many price points.

jean-jacques-girard.name: Jean-Jacques Girard
jean-jacques-girard.line: A family estate in Savigny with vines in Pernand-Vergelesses.
jean-jacques-girard.tell: Jean-Jacques Girard is a family estate with vines in Pernand-Vergelesses. Les Belles Filles is a white village site, fresh and good value.

jean-laurent.name: Jean Laurent
jean-laurent.line: A family grower in the Aube making Pinot Noir and Chardonnay Champagne, including rosé.
jean-laurent.tell: Jean Laurent is a family estate in the Côte des Bar. The rosé is fruity and full; the Blanc de Blancs, here in magnum, is fresher. Good value next to the big houses.

jean-louis-chave.name: Domaine Jean-Louis Chave
jean-louis-chave.line: The great family domaine of Hermitage, whose blended Hermitage is one of the most revered wines of the Rhône.
jean-louis-chave.tell: Chave is the most respected name on the hill of Hermitage. Their Hermitage blends several parcels into a deep, long lived Syrah. A trophy bottle; decant.

jean-marc-boillot.name: Domaine Jean-Marc Boillot
jean-marc-boillot.line: A Pommard estate with whites from Puligny and Rully.
jean-marc-boillot.tell: Jean-Marc Boillot makes whites across Burgundy. Meix Cadot is a Rully premier cru, crisp and good value.

jean-marc-pavelot.name: Domaine Jean-Marc Pavelot
jean-marc-pavelot.line: A family domaine in Savigny-lès-Beaune making fresh, well priced reds, including Beaune premier cru.
jean-marc-pavelot.tell: Pavelot is a respected Savigny family. Their Beaune Bressandes premier cru is a balanced, red fruited wine at a fair price. A friendly pick for most red meats.

jean-marc-pillot.name: Domaine Jean-Marc Pillot
jean-marc-pillot.line: A Chassagne estate with vines in Montagny.
jean-marc-pillot.tell: Jean-Marc Pillot is a Chassagne-Montrachet estate. Les Bassets is a Montagny white, crisp and good value.

jean-marc-vincent.name: Domaine Jean-Marc Vincent
jean-marc-vincent.line: A small Santenay estate making taut whites.
jean-marc-vincent.tell: Jean-Marc Vincent is a small Santenay estate with taut whites. Les Vignes Denses comes from very closely planted vines.

jean-marie-bouzereau.name: Domaine Jean-Marie Bouzereau
jean-marie-bouzereau.line: A Meursault family domaine, part of the large Bouzereau clan, also making red from the Santenots vineyard.
jean-marie-bouzereau.tell: Santenots lies in Meursault but its red wine is sold as Volnay premier cru. Expect a firmer, slightly darker Volnay. A good match for duck or pork.

jean-michel-gaunoux.name: Domaine Jean-Michel Gaunoux
jean-michel-gaunoux.line: A Meursault domaine of the Gaunoux family, making traditional Côte de Beaune wines, including red Pommard.
jean-michel-gaunoux.tell: Gaunoux makes traditional Burgundy that rewards patience. This Pommard premier cru has had time to soften. A good value mature red for game or beef.

jean-michel-stephan.name: Domaine Jean-Michel Stephan
jean-michel-stephan.line: A small Côte-Rôtie grower making natural leaning Syrah from named hillside sites.
jean-michel-stephan.tell: Stephan is a small Côte-Rôtie grower. Côteaux de Bassenon and Côteaux du Tupin are named slopes. Fragrant Syrah; ask the sommelier how these bottles are tasting.

jean-paul-thevenet.name: Domaine Jean-Paul Thévenet
jean-paul-thevenet.line: One of the founding natural wine growers of Morgon, making old vine, fresh, deep Gamay.
jean-paul-thevenet.tell: Thévenet was one of the original natural growers of Morgon. The old vine Morgon in magnum is a fun pick for a big table.

jean-philippe-fichet.name: Jean-Philippe Fichet
jean-philippe-fichet.line: A Meursault grower making taut, mineral whites.
jean-philippe-fichet.tell: Fichet is a respected Meursault grower with taut, mineral whites. His Bourgogne and Rully are crisp value bottles with real Côte de Beaune style.

jerome-galeyrand.name: Jérôme Galeyrand
jerome-galeyrand.line: A small grower and négociant based near Gevrey-Chambertin making fresh, lively reds.
jerome-galeyrand.tell: Galeyrand is a small producer making bright, fresh Pinot Noir. En Billard is a village Gevrey site. A good value pick for a lighter red.

jimenez-landi.name: Bodegas Jiménez-Landi
jimenez-landi.line: A family estate in the Sierra de Gredos making fresh, mountain Garnacha.
jimenez-landi.tell: Jiménez-Landi makes Garnacha in the Sierra de Gredos. El Reventón is a high altitude site: fresh, fragrant and fine, with red fruit and herbs. A great swap for a Pinot drinker.

jj-prum.name: Joh. Jos. Prüm
jj-prum.tell: JJ Prüm is a legendary Mosel name. Wehlener Sonnenuhr Kabinett is light and gently sweet, and it ages beautifully.

jl-vergnon.name: JL Vergnon
jl-vergnon.line: A Le Mesnil grower making razor-sharp, low-dosage grand cru Blanc de Blancs.
jl-vergnon.tell: JL Vergnon makes Chardonnay from Le Mesnil, some of the most chalky ground in Champagne. Les Hautes Mottes is a Brut Nature, no sugar added, so it is bone-dry and electric. Lovely with oysters.

jm-seleque.name: JM Sélèque
jm-seleque.line: A young-generation grower in Pierry, near Épernay, making precise, single-parcel Champagne.
jm-seleque.tell: Jean-Marc Sélèque runs his family estate in Pierry and is one of the rising grower names. Solessence is the blend; the Soliste wines are single parcels and single grapes. Crisp, chalky and dry.

johanneshof-reinisch.name: Johanneshof Reinisch
johanneshof-reinisch.line: A family estate in Tattendorf, south of Vienna, known for Pinot Noir and the local red grapes.
johanneshof-reinisch.tell: The Reinisch family farms in Tattendorf, in the Thermenregion south of Vienna, a good spot for Pinot Noir. Ried Holzspur is a single vineyard Pinot: fresh, fine and red fruited. A smart alternative to Burgundy.

jonata.name: Jonata
jonata.line: An estate in Ballard Canyon, Santa Barbara County, making rich, intense reds.
jonata.tell: Jonata farms sandy hills in Ballard Canyon. Todos is an estate red blend: ripe, dark and spicy. Ask the sommelier for the exact grape mix of the vintage.

jordan.name: Jordan
jordan.line: A Sonoma estate in the Alexander Valley making one Cabernet in an elegant, food friendly style inspired by Bordeaux.
jordan.tell: Jordan is a famous Sonoma name with a quieter style than most Napa Cabernet: medium bodied, fresh and balanced, made to go with food. Guests often know it from restaurants. The magnum and double magnum suit a celebration table.

joseph-drouhin.name: Joseph Drouhin
joseph-drouhin.line: A family owned Beaune house with large organic and biodynamic holdings, known for graceful, elegant wines and its Beaune Clos des Mouches.
joseph-drouhin.tell: Drouhin is one of Beaune's great family houses, with a style built on elegance. Clos des Mouches is their signature Beaune premier cru, and they also own parcels in Musigny and Les Amoureuses. A trusted name for any guest.

joseph-phelps.name: Joseph Phelps
joseph-phelps.line: A leading Napa estate whose Insignia was one of the first proprietary Bordeaux style blends in California.
joseph-phelps.tell: Joseph Phelps makes classic Napa Cabernet. Insignia, the flagship blend, is rich, layered and long lived, and it is one of the best known Napa reds. The list holds it from half bottle to magnum and across vintages. The Napa Valley Cabernet is the easier entry.

joseph-voillot.name: Domaine Joseph Voillot
joseph-voillot.line: A Volnay family domaine making traditional, fragrant reds from Volnay and Pommard.
joseph-voillot.tell: Voillot is a classic Volnay grower. The old vine Volnay and Bourgogne are charming, red fruited and soft. Easy recommendations with poultry and pork.

jules-desjourneys.name: Jules Desjourneys
jules-desjourneys.line: A Beaujolais grower making serious, structured cru wines, here Fleurie.
jules-desjourneys.tell: Desjourneys makes deep, structured Beaujolais that is priced more like Burgundy. Les Moriers is a Fleurie site. Ask the sommelier how it is drinking.

julian-haart.name: Julian Haart
julian-haart.tell: Julian Haart is a young Mosel grower. 1,000L Trocken is a dry Riesling, crisp and mineral.

julien-cruchandeau.name: Julien Cruchandeau
julien-cruchandeau.line: A small grower making wines from the Hautes-Côtes and lesser known villages, here Ladoix.
julien-cruchandeau.tell: Ladoix sits beside Corton and gives sturdy, good value reds. Les Ranches is a named site there. A gentle priced, older red.

justin.name: Justin
justin.tell: Justin is a Paso Robles winery. Its Sauvignon Blanc is bright and fruity, good value.

justin-boxler.name: Domaine Justin Boxler
justin-boxler.line: A family estate in Niedermorschwihr with vines in the Sommerberg grand cru.
justin-boxler.tell: Justin Boxler is a family estate in Niedermorschwihr. Sommerberg is a steep granite grand cru, and the Riesling is crisp and stony.

justin-girardin.name: Domaine Justin Girardin
justin-girardin.line: A Santenay family domaine making Côte de Beaune reds and whites, here a village Pommard.
justin-girardin.tell: A family grower from Santenay. Village Pommard gives a firm, dark fruited red. A sensible value choice for steak.

kaiken.name: Kaiken
kaiken.line: The Mendoza winery of Chilean winemaker Aurelio Montes.
kaiken.tell: Kaiken is the Argentine winery of the Montes family from Chile. Ultra is its Malbec: dark, ripe and smooth. A friendly, good value red for steak.

kalin-cellars.name: Kalin Cellars
kalin-cellars.line: A small California winery that holds its wines for years before release, so bottles arrive with maturity and layers.
kalin-cellars.tell: Kalin Cellars is known for patience: wines are aged for years before they are sold. Cuvée DD is a Pinot Noir from the Alexander Valley, so expect mature, earthy, layered flavours rather than fresh fruit. Ask the sommelier how the vintage is drinking.

kathryn-kennedy.name: Kathryn Kennedy Winery
kathryn-kennedy.line: A small estate in Saratoga in the Santa Cruz Mountains, making long lived Cabernet from its own vineyard.
kathryn-kennedy.tell: Kathryn Kennedy is a tiny estate in the Santa Cruz Mountains. The Estate Cabernet is firm, fresh and long lived, in a classic style. Older vintages are listed; ask the sommelier how they are drinking.

keenan.name: Keenan Winery
keenan.line: A Spring Mountain estate known for structured mountain Merlot, Cabernet Franc and blends.
keenan.tell: Keenan farms high on Spring Mountain. Mailbox Vineyard is its celebrated Merlot, deep and firm; Upper Bowl is a Cabernet Franc, and Holy Trinity a blend. Mountain wines with more grip than valley versions.

keller.name: Keller
keller.tell: Keller is a cult name in Rheinhessen. Von der Fels is dry and Limestone Kabinett gently sweet, while Morstein and Hubacker GG are dry grand crus and very sought after.

ken-wright.name: Ken Wright Cellars
ken-wright.line: A Willamette Valley winery known for single vineyard Pinot Noirs that show how each site differs.
ken-wright.tell: Ken Wright helped Oregon think vineyard by vineyard. Shea, Canary Hill, McCrone, Carter and Freedom Hill are separate bottlings from different hills and soils, so a guest can taste the difference. The style is fresh and fruit led; the half bottles and magnums give real choice by table size.

kiralyudvar.name: Királyudvar
kiralyudvar.line: A Tokaj estate making dry and sweet Furmint.
kiralyudvar.tell: Királyudvar is a biodynamic Tokaj estate. This is a dry Furmint, crisp and a little smoky.

kistler.name: Kistler
kistler.line: A Sonoma estate famous for Chardonnay and Pinot Noir made in a Burgundian way from cool vineyards.
kistler.tell: Kistler is one of the great Chardonnay names of California, and its Pinot Noir is made with the same care. The Sonoma Coast Pinot is fine and fragrant, with red fruit and a silky texture. A strong choice for a guest who wants California Pinot with finesse.

kivelstadt.name: Kivelstadt Cellars
kivelstadt.tell: Kivelstadt is a Sonoma winery. The Family Secret is a Sauvignon Blanc, fresh and good value.

knewitz.name: Weingut Knewitz
knewitz.tell: Knewitz is a family estate in Rheinhessen. This is a German Chardonnay, crisp and fine.

koehler-ruprecht.name: Koehler-Ruprecht
koehler-ruprecht.tell: Koehler-Ruprecht is a traditional Pfalz estate. Kallstadter Steinacker is a Riesling site, and there is a dry Pinot Blanc too.

kongsgaard.name: Kongsgaard
kongsgaard.line: A small Napa family winery famous for its Chardonnay, also making deep Syrah and Cabernet.
kongsgaard.tell: Kongsgaard is best known for Chardonnay, but its reds are just as serious. The Syrah is dark, savoury and peppery, the Cabernet deep and firm. Small production; a collector's choice.

kosta-browne.name: Kosta Browne
kosta-browne.line: A Sonoma Pinot Noir house famous for ripe, plush, polished wines that many California Pinot lovers seek out.
kosta-browne.tell: Kosta Browne makes Pinot Noir in a ripe, lush style: dark cherry, spice and a velvety texture. The Sonoma Coast and Russian River bottlings are the core; Gap's Crown is a single vineyard in the windy Petaluma Gap. A sure pick for a guest who loves rich California Pinot.

kracher.name: Kracher
kracher.line: A family estate by Lake Neusiedl, one of the great names in sweet wine.
kracher.tell: Kracher is a family estate by Lake Neusiedl, where autumn mists help sweet wine. The Auslese is honeyed and fresh, with apricot and citrus. A lovely partner for fruit desserts.

krug.name: Krug
krug.line: The Reims house that ferments in small oak casks and builds Grande Cuvée from many vintages, numbered by edition.
krug.tell: Krug is barrel-fermented and deeply complex, toasty, nutty and powerful. Grande Cuvée blends over a hundred wines from many years; the edition number tells you which. Clos du Mesnil and Clos d'Ambonnay are tiny walled vineyards, among Champagne's rarest bottles.

kruger-rumpf.name: Kruger-Rumpf
kruger-rumpf.tell: Kruger-Rumpf is a Nahe family estate. Im Pitterberg GG is a dry grand cru Riesling, here in half-bottle.

kuentz-bas.name: Kuentz-Bas
kuentz-bas.line: An old house in Husseren-les-Châteaux, below the three castles that give one of its wines its name.
kuentz-bas.tell: Kuentz-Bas is an old Alsace house. Geisberg is a grand cru Riesling, and Trois Châteaux is a Sylvaner named for the castles above the village.

kumeu-river.name: Kumeu River
kumeu-river.line: A family estate near Auckland famous for Chardonnay.
kumeu-river.tell: Kumeu River is a family estate near Auckland famous for Chardonnay. Coddington and Estate are fine and taut, and Kumeu Village is the value bottling.

l-arco.name: L'Arco
l-arco.line: A small Valpolicella estate run by Luca Fedrigo, who learned from Giuseppe Quintarelli.
l-arco.tell: L'Arco is a small estate run by Luca Fedrigo, who worked for years with Quintarelli. Pario is a rich, layered Valpolicella; the Verona Rosso is lighter. A smart way into Quintarelli's style at a gentler price.

la-capranera.name: La Capranera
la-capranera.tell: La Capranera is a Campania estate. Falanghina is a fresh, citrusy southern white and good value.

la-chablisienne.name: La Chablisienne
la-chablisienne.line: The Chablis cooperative, a large and reliable producer from village to grand cru.
la-chablisienne.tell: La Chablisienne is the cooperative of Chablis, a large and reliable producer. Grenouilles is a grand cru and Vaillons a premier cru: classic, crisp Chablis at a fair price.

la-cigarrera.name: La Cigarrera
la-cigarrera.line: A small family Sherry house in Sanlúcar, making Manzanilla.
la-cigarrera.tell: La Cigarrera is a small family house in Sanlúcar. Manzanilla is the driest, freshest Sherry: salty, tangy and almondy. Serve chilled, with oysters, fried seafood or salty snacks.

la-crema.name: La Crema
la-crema.line: A well known Sonoma winery making approachable, fruit forward Pinot Noir and Chardonnay from cool coastal vineyards.
la-crema.tell: La Crema is one of the names guests recognise for California Pinot Noir. The Sonoma Coast bottling is soft and fruity, with cherry and a touch of vanilla, easy with almost anything. A safe, friendly choice, and the half bottle is good value for two.

la-jota.name: La Jota
la-jota.line: A historic Howell Mountain winery making dark, firm mountain Cabernet and Merlot.
la-jota.tell: La Jota is an old stone winery on Howell Mountain. Mountain fruit gives a dark, firm Cabernet and a structured Merlot with more grip than most. Both suit beef or lamb.

la-perdida.name: La Perdida
la-perdida.line: A small natural minded producer in Valdeorras, inland Galicia.
la-perdida.tell: La Perdida is a small producer in Valdeorras, inland Galicia. O Trancado is a red from local grapes: fresh, light and savoury. An adventurous choice; ask the sommelier about the blend.

la-rioja-alta.name: La Rioja Alta
la-rioja-alta.line: A classic Haro house famous for long aged Gran Reservas 890 and 904.
la-rioja-alta.tell: La Rioja Alta is a classic house in Haro. 904 and 890 are Gran Reservas aged for years in American oak: silky, savoury and complex, with dried cherry, leather and spice. 890 is the rarer one. Treasures for a Rioja lover.

la-sala.name: La Sala
la-sala.line: A Chianti Classico estate whose Il Torriano is a Gran Selezione, the top tier of the region.
la-sala.tell: La Sala is a Chianti Classico estate. Il Torriano is a Gran Selezione, the region's top category: structured Sangiovese with dark cherry and spice. Good with beef or lamb.

la-soeur-cadette.name: La Soeur Cadette
la-soeur-cadette.line: A small négociant run by Valentin Montaney, buying grapes from Burgundy and Beaujolais, here Juliénas.
la-soeur-cadette.tell: La Soeur Cadette is a small négociant. Their Juliénas is bright and juicy, textbook cru Beaujolais. Great value and slightly cool.

la-spinetta.name: La Spinetta
la-spinetta.line: A family estate known for ripe, modern Barbaresco from single vineyards.
la-spinetta.tell: La Spinetta is the Rivetti family estate, known for a rich, modern style. Bordini and Valeirano are Barbaresco vineyards: dark fruited and polished, more generous than traditional Barbaresco. Bordini comes in half bottle.

la-vinya-del-vuit.name: La Vinya del Vuit
la-vinya-del-vuit.line: A small Priorat project making wine from old vines.
la-vinya-del-vuit.tell: La Vinya del Vuit is a small Priorat project. Expect a deep, mineral red from Garnacha and Carignan grown on slate. Ask the sommelier about the blend.

la-vizcaina.name: La Vizcaína de Vinos
la-vizcaina.line: A Bierzo project from Raúl Pérez, bottling Mencía from single villages and vineyards.
la-vizcaina.tell: La Vizcaína is Raúl Pérez's Bierzo project. La Poulosa and Las Gundiñas are single vineyards: fresh, mineral Mencía with red fruit and spice. Great with poultry, pork or mushrooms.

lail.name: Lail Vineyards
lail.line: The winery of Robin Lail, from the family that founded Inglenook; J. Daniel Cuvée Cabernet honours her father.
lail.tell: Lail comes from one of Napa's oldest wine families, descended from the founders of Inglenook. J. Daniel Cuvée is a refined, long lived Cabernet named for Robin Lail's father. Elegant and classic.

lallier.name: Lallier
lallier.line: An Aÿ house making grand cru Champagne with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay at its heart.
lallier.tell: Lallier is based in Aÿ, a grand cru village for Pinot Noir. The wines are fresh and precise; Ouvrage is its top grand cru Extra Brut, dry and deep. Ask the sommelier what the date in brackets on the list means for this bottle.

lang-and-reed.name: Lang & Reed
lang-and-reed.line: A small winery devoted to Cabernet Franc.
lang-and-reed.tell: Lang & Reed specialises in Cabernet Franc, a grape usually used only for blending in California. Two Fourteen is fresh and fragrant, with red fruit and herbs. A great choice for a guest who loves Chinon or Saumur.

larkmead.name: Larkmead
larkmead.line: A historic Calistoga estate making elegant Cabernet blends and Merlot from its own vineyard.
larkmead.tell: Larkmead is an old estate at the north end of Napa. Dr. Olmo and The Lark are its Cabernet led blends, elegant and long; Firebelle is a Merlot blend. A refined choice for a guest who likes balance.

larmandier-bernier.name: Larmandier-Bernier
larmandier-bernier.line: A biodynamic family estate in Vertus making pure, low-dosage Chardonnay Champagne.
larmandier-bernier.tell: Larmandier-Bernier is a leading biodynamic grower in Vertus. Longitude is a crisp, chalky Blanc de Blancs; Terre de Vertus is a single-village Brut Nature, bone-dry and intense. Superb with shellfish.

laroche.name: Domaine Laroche
laroche.line: A large, well-known Chablis estate making wines from village to grand cru.
laroche.tell: Laroche is a major Chablis name. L'Homme Mort is a part of the Fourchaume premier cru, and the wine is crisp, citrusy and mineral, a classic with shellfish.

larue.name: Domaine Larue
larue.tell: Larue is a family estate in Saint-Aubin. Les Murgers des Dents de Chien is a Saint-Aubin premier cru, crisp and mineral and good value against Puligny.

lassak.name: Lassak
lassak.tell: Lassak is a Württemberg grower. This is a dry Riesling; ask the sommelier about its style.

laurent-combier.name: Laurent Combier
laurent-combier.line: A leading Crozes-Hermitage family domaine farming organically, making ripe, fresh Syrah.
laurent-combier.tell: Combier is one of the best known names in Crozes-Hermitage. Expect ripe, dark fruited Syrah. A good value choice with steak.

laurent-perrier.name: Laurent-Perrier
laurent-perrier.line: A Tours-sur-Marne house known for its rosé made by skin maceration and for Grand Siècle, a blend of three vintages.
laurent-perrier.tell: Laurent-Perrier is famous for its rosé, coloured by soaking Pinot Noir on its skins, and for Grand Siècle, which blends three great vintages; the Iteration number names the release. Harmony is a demi-sec, sweeter, for dessert.

laurent-ponsot.name: Laurent Ponsot
laurent-ponsot.line: The house Laurent Ponsot founded after leaving his family domaine, with cuvées named after trees.
laurent-ponsot.tell: Laurent Ponsot ran his family's Morey domaine for decades before starting his own house. Cuvée de l'Aulne, named for the alder tree, is a village Gevrey. A good talking point for a guest who knows the Ponsot name.

laurent-tribut.name: Laurent Tribut
laurent-tribut.line: A tiny, traditional Chablis estate making pure, quiet wines.
laurent-tribut.tell: Laurent Tribut is a small, traditional Chablis grower. Beauroy is a premier cru and the village Chablis is crisp and mineral, quiet wines that reward attention.

laurenz-v.name: Laurenz V.
laurenz-v.tell: Laurenz V. specialises in Grüner Veltliner, Austria's signature white. Friendly is fresh, peppery and easy, a great value white.

le-ragnaie.name: Le Ragnaie
le-ragnaie.line: A Montalcino estate with some of the highest vineyards in the zone, making fresh, fragrant Brunello.
le-ragnaie.tell: Le Ragnaie farms very high vineyards in Montalcino, so its Brunello is fresh and fragrant, with red fruit and fine tannin. Casanovina Montosoli is a single vineyard bottling. A great Brunello for a guest who likes elegance.

leclerc-briant.name: Leclerc Briant
leclerc-briant.line: An Épernay house that was an early convert to biodynamic farming, making pure, low-dosage wines.
leclerc-briant.tell: Leclerc Briant is an Épernay house known for organic and biodynamic farming. The wines are fresh and dry; Clos des Trois Clochers is a single walled vineyard with no added sugar; the Réserve, here in magnum, is the house blend.

leflaive-associes.name: Leflaive & Associés
leflaive-associes.line: A side label of Domaine Leflaive, made by its team from partner growers' biodynamic vines.
leflaive-associes.tell: Leflaive & Associés is made by the Domaine Leflaive team from partner growers' grapes. The Auxey-Duresses is fresh and floral: Leflaive style at a gentler price.

legras-haas.name: Legras & Haas
legras-haas.line: A family estate in Chouilly making fresh grand cru Chardonnay Champagne and rosé.
legras-haas.tell: Legras & Haas is a family house in Chouilly, a grand cru for Chardonnay. The Blanc de Blancs is fresh and fine; the Millésime is its vintage; Intuition and the Rosé add red fruit.

lelarge-pugeot.name: Lelarge-Pugeot
lelarge-pugeot.line: An organic grower in Vrigny, west of Reims, known for wines that give Meunier a starring role.
lelarge-pugeot.tell: Lelarge-Pugeot farms organically in Vrigny. Les Meuniers de Clémence is a Blanc de Noirs from Meunier, the underrated grape of Champagne: fruity, open and generous, very good with food.

lequin-colin.name: Domaine Lequin-Colin
lequin-colin.line: A Santenay family domaine making wines across the southern Côte de Beaune.
lequin-colin.tell: Lequin-Colin is a family grower from Santenay. Their village Pommard Les Noizons is a firm, fruity red. A sound choice with beef.

les-alexandrins.name: Domaine Les Alexandrins
les-alexandrins.line: A northern Rhône producer making Saint-Joseph and other northern appellations.
les-alexandrins.tell: Saint-Joseph gives fresh, peppery Syrah at fair prices. A good value Syrah for steak.

les-hauts-de-milly.name: Les Hauts de Milly
les-hauts-de-milly.line: A Chablis estate based in Milly; Côte de Léchet is a premier cru on the slopes above the village.
les-hauts-de-milly.tell: This is Chablis premier cru from Côte de Léchet, on the slopes above the village of Milly. Crisp, lemony and stony, it suits oysters and lighter fish.

les-lunes.name: Les Lunes
les-lunes.line: A small natural wine label that farms organically and makes wines with as little intervention as it can.
les-lunes.tell: Les Lunes is a small label making natural wine from vineyards it farms organically. The Sonoma Cabernet is lighter and fresher than most, with bright fruit and an earthy edge. A fun pick for an adventurous guest.

lieu-dit.name: Lieu Dit
lieu-dit.line: A Santa Barbara winery focused on Loire grapes.
lieu-dit.tell: Lieu Dit is a Santa Barbara winery focused on Loire grapes. Its Sauvignon Blanc is crisp and mineral.

liger-belair.name: Liger-Belair
liger-belair.line: A family name in the Côte de Nuits shared by two separate estates.
liger-belair.tell: Two Burgundy estates carry the Liger-Belair name, so ask the sommelier which one made this Aligoté. Expect a crisp, lemony white, a fresh start to a meal.

lioco.name: Lioco
lioco.line: A California winery making restrained, fresh wines from cool vineyards, with little new oak.
lioco.tell: Lioco makes California wine that stays fresh and light on oak. The Pinot Noir from Comptche, in the cool hills of Mendocino, is bright and savoury, with red fruit and spice. A smart pick for a guest who finds most California Pinot too heavy.

lionel-faury.name: Lionel Faury
lionel-faury.line: A northern Rhône family domaine making fresh Saint-Joseph and Côte-Rôtie.
lionel-faury.tell: Faury is a northern Rhône family grower. Les 3 Brunes is a Côte-Rôtie. Fresh, peppery Syrah.

loimer.name: Loimer
loimer.tell: Loimer is a biodynamic estate in the Kamptal. Lois is a fresh, peppery Grüner Veltliner, crisp and good value.

lokoya.name: Lokoya
lokoya.line: A Napa winery bottling mountain Cabernets, one from each of the valley's mountain areas.
lokoya.tell: Lokoya makes separate Cabernets from Napa's mountains: Howell Mountain, Spring Mountain, Mount Veeder and Diamond Mountain. Each is dark, powerful and distinct. Rare bottles; a fine comparison for a serious Cabernet lover.

lompoc-wine-co.name: Lompoc Wine Co.
lompoc-wine-co.tell: Lompoc Wine Company is a small label from the cool, windy Sta. Rita Hills in Santa Barbara County. This older Chardonnay should show some bottle age, so ask the sommelier how it is drinking before you promise freshness.

long-meadow-ranch.name: Long Meadow Ranch
long-meadow-ranch.tell: Long Meadow Ranch is a Napa farm estate. Its Sauvignon Blanc is crisp and fresh.

lopez-de-heredia.name: López de Heredia
lopez-de-heredia.line: Rioja's great traditional house in Haro, ageing its wines for many years before release.
lopez-de-heredia.tell: López de Heredia is Rioja's most traditional house, ageing wines for years before release. Cubillo is the youngest red, a Crianza: fresh, savoury and gently mature. A wonderful introduction to old style Rioja.

louis-jadot.name: Louis Jadot
louis-jadot.line: One of the great Beaune houses, owning large holdings across the Côte d'Or and Beaujolais and bottling an enormous range of reds.
louis-jadot.tell: Jadot is one of Burgundy's most recognised names, owning vineyards from Beaujolais up to Chambertin. The quality is very consistent, and bottles marked Domaine come from their own vineyards. The half bottle is a handy option for a couple.

louis-magnin.name: Domaine Louis Magnin
louis-magnin.line: A Savoie family domaine making mountain reds.
louis-magnin.tell: Magnin is a Savoie family estate. Expect a light, fresh mountain red. A curious pick.

louis-michel.name: Domaine Louis Michel
louis-michel.line: A Chablis estate that ages in steel rather than oak, giving pure, crisp, mineral wines.
louis-michel.tell: Louis Michel uses no oak, so the wines are pure Chablis: crisp, lemony and stony. Grenouilles is a grand cru; Montmains a premier cru in half-bottle. Ideal with oysters and shellfish.

louis-roederer.name: Louis Roederer
louis-roederer.line: A family-owned Reims house, maker of Cristal, with a precise, vinous style.
louis-roederer.tell: Roederer is family owned and farms most of its own vines. Cristal, first made for the Russian tsar, is the prestige wine: fine, chalky, long. Collection is the newer multi-vintage house blend, numbered by release.

luberri.name: Bodegas Luberri
luberri.line: A family winery in Rioja Alavesa.
luberri.tell: Luberri is a family winery in Rioja Alavesa. Biga is a Tempranillo with some oak ageing: ripe, smooth and spicy. A friendly Rioja for lamb or pork.

lucien-boillot.name: Domaine Lucien Boillot et Fils
lucien-boillot.line: A Gevrey-Chambertin based family domaine, run by Pierre Boillot, with vineyards in Gevrey, Nuits, Pommard and Volnay.
lucien-boillot.tell: Boillot is a family estate with roots in both the Côte de Nuits and the Côte de Beaune. The wines are deep and well structured. Their Pommard and Volnay premier crus are good value for the quality.

lucien-crochet.name: Lucien Crochet
lucien-crochet.line: A family estate in Bué, in the heart of Sancerre, making crisp whites and fine Pinot Noir rosé.
lucien-crochet.tell: Lucien Crochet is a family estate in Sancerre. Their rosé is Pinot Noir: pale, dry and delicate, with red berries and citrus, offered in bottle and magnum, and very friendly with food.

luigi-ferrando.name: Luigi Ferrando
luigi-ferrando.line: The leading family of Carema, an alpine Nebbiolo zone on stone terraces near the Valle d'Aosta.
luigi-ferrando.tell: Ferrando is the name in Carema, tiny alpine terraces at the edge of Piedmont. Etichetta Nera, the black label, is their top selection: fragrant, fine and long lived Nebbiolo, lighter than Barolo. A treasure for a Nebbiolo lover.

luigi-giordano.name: Luigi Giordano
luigi-giordano.line: A family estate in Barbaresco making traditional wines, including from the Montestefano vineyard.
luigi-giordano.tell: Luigi Giordano is a family estate in the village of Barbaresco. Montestefano is one of the village's most powerful vineyards: dark, firm and long lived Nebbiolo. Here in magnum for a table to share.

luigi-tecce.name: Luigi Tecce
luigi-tecce.line: A small Campania grower making powerful, natural minded Aglianico.
luigi-tecce.tell: Luigi Tecce makes Aglianico in the hills of Irpinia, Campania. Poliphemo and Puro Sangue are Taurasi: dark, smoky and firm. Satyricon is a little lighter. Big wines for lamb or beef.

luis-pato.name: Luis Pato
luis-pato.line: A Bairrada estate known for single vineyard wines and sparkling wine from local grapes.
luis-pato.tell: Luis Pato is a leading name in Bairrada. Vinha Formal and Vinha Pan are named for single vineyards and both come in magnum. Ask the sommelier about the grapes and style of each before you describe them.

luis-rodriguez.name: Luis Rodríguez
luis-rodriguez.line: A Ribeiro grower who revived local grapes in this corner of Galicia.
luis-rodriguez.tell: Luis Rodríguez works with old local grapes in Ribeiro, Galicia. A Torna dos Pasás is a red: fresh, fragrant and lightly spicy. A fun, unusual pick for fish, pork or poultry.

lukas-hammelmann.name: Lukas Hammelmann
lukas-hammelmann.line: A young Pfalz grower making Pinot Noir and other wines in a fresh style.
lukas-hammelmann.tell: Lukas Hammelmann is a young grower in the Pfalz, in south west Germany, where Pinot Noir, called Spätburgunder, does well. Roter Berg and Dhochsatt are his Pinot Noirs: fresh and red fruited. Ask the sommelier about each before you describe them.

maculan.name: Maculan
maculan.line: A Veneto family estate famous for Torcolato, a sweet wine from dried grapes.
maculan.tell: Maculan is a family estate in Breganze, Veneto. Torcolato is made from grapes dried after harvest: golden, honeyed and rich, with good acidity. A beautiful half bottle with dessert or cheese.

maggy-hawk.name: Maggy Hawk
maggy-hawk.line: An Anderson Valley estate in Mendocino's cool 'deep end', making silky, aromatic single vineyard Pinot Noir.
maggy-hawk.tell: Maggy Hawk farms an estate in the far, cool end of the Anderson Valley, named for a racehorse. Jolie is elegant and silky, with bright raspberry and floral notes. A lovely Pinot for salmon, duck or a guest who wants something fine but not heavy.

mainova.name: Mainova
mainova.line: A young organic estate in the Alto Alentejo making wine with minimal intervention.
mainova.tell: Mainova is a young family estate in the Alto Alentejo, farmed organically. This red is Alicante Bouschet, a dark, deeply coloured grape that does well in Alentejo: dark berries and soft spice. A warm, generous red for meat.

maison-champy.name: Maison Champy
maison-champy.line: A historic Beaune négociant house making wines from across the Côte d'Or.
maison-champy.tell: Champy is an old Beaune house. These bottles range from a young Volnay to grand crus with some age. A dependable name.

maison-leroy.name: Maison Leroy
maison-leroy.line: The négociant house of Lalou Bize-Leroy, one of Burgundy's most legendary figures, known for holding wines until ready.
maison-leroy.tell: Leroy is one of the most legendary names in Burgundy. Their négociant wines are bought and held until they are ready. A rare, prized Beaune premier cru for a guest who knows.

malartic-lagraviere.name: Château Malartic-Lagravière
malartic-lagraviere.line: A Graves classed growth in Pessac-Léognan.
malartic-lagraviere.tell: Malartic-Lagravière is a classed growth of Pessac-Léognan. The white is Sauvignon-led, crisp and fresh with gentle oak; ask the sommelier to confirm the estate, since the list prints Château Malartic Graves.

marc-colin.name: Domaine Marc Colin et Fils
marc-colin.line: A family estate in Saint-Aubin with vines across Chassagne and Puligny.
marc-colin.tell: Marc Colin is a family estate based in Saint-Aubin with vines across Chassagne and Puligny. Les Castets is a Saint-Aubin premier cru, Les Champs Gain a Chassagne premier cru, Cuvée Margot and Cuvée Luce named village wines, and Bâtard-Montrachet the grand cru.

marc-delienne.name: Marc Delienne
marc-delienne.line: A Fleurie grower making fresh, natural leaning Gamay.
marc-delienne.tell: Delienne makes lively, fresh Fleurie. Abbaye Road is his named cuvée. Fresh and fun, slightly cool.

marc-hebrart.name: Marc Hébrart
marc-hebrart.line: A family grower in Mareuil-sur-Aÿ; Rive Gauche Rive Droite blends grand cru vines from both banks of the Marne.
marc-hebrart.tell: Marc Hébrart is a much-admired grower in Mareuil-sur-Aÿ. Rive Gauche Rive Droite blends Pinot Noir and Chardonnay from both sides of the Marne: rich yet fresh, with real depth. Offered in bottle and magnum.

marcassin.name: Marcassin
marcassin.line: Winemaker Helen Turley's tiny estate on the far Sonoma Coast, one of California's most sought after names for Pinot Noir and Chardonnay.
marcassin.tell: Marcassin is a tiny estate on the far Sonoma Coast made famous by winemaker Helen Turley. The Pinot Noir is rich and concentrated, and bottles are hard to find. A collector's wine; involve the sommelier for service and any questions about the vintage.

marcel-deiss.name: Domaine Marcel Deiss
marcel-deiss.line: A Bergheim estate that champions blends of grapes grown together, named for the vineyard rather than the grape.
marcel-deiss.tell: Marcel Deiss names wines for places, not grapes, and blends varieties grown together. Mambourg is a grand cru; Engelgarten a single site. Rich, layered and unusual.

marcel-lapierre.name: Marcel Lapierre
marcel-lapierre.line: The Morgon domaine of the late Marcel Lapierre, pioneer of natural Beaujolais, now run by his children.
marcel-lapierre.tell: Lapierre is the name most associated with natural Beaujolais. The Morgon is fresh, silky and delicious. Serve it slightly cool.

marchand-tawse.name: Marchand-Tawse and Domaine Tawse
marchand-tawse.line: The Nuits-Saint-Georges house of winemaker Pascal Marchand and Canadian owner Moray Tawse: a négociant range plus the Domaine Tawse estate wines.
marchand-tawse.tell: Pascal Marchand is a well known winemaker in Burgundy. Marchand-Tawse bottles from bought grapes, while Domaine Tawse wines come from their own vines. Their Savigny Lavières and Volnay Frémiets are fragrant, well priced premier crus.

marchesi-biscardo.name: Marchesi Biscardo
marchesi-biscardo.line: A Veneto producer making an approachable Corvina based red from near Verona.
marchesi-biscardo.tell: Marchesi Biscardo makes a Verona red from Corvina, the main grape of Valpolicella. It is round and fruity, with cherry and plum. An easy, good value red for pasta or chicken.

marco-de-bartoli.name: Marco De Bartoli
marco-de-bartoli.line: A Sicilian family estate famous for Marsala and for sweet passito from the island of Pantelleria.
marco-de-bartoli.tell: De Bartoli is a great Sicilian family name. Bukkuram is a passito from Pantelleria, made from sun dried Muscat grapes: apricot, honey and orange peel. Wonderful with dessert or blue cheese.

marie-noelle-ledru.name: Marie-Noëlle Ledru
marie-noelle-ledru.line: A small, much-loved grower in Ambonnay making intense, Pinot Noir-based grand cru Champagne.
marie-noelle-ledru.tell: Marie-Noëlle Ledru's wines come from Ambonnay in tiny amounts and are hard to find. Cuvée du Goulté is a Blanc de Noirs, rich and red-fruited. A collector's bottle; ask the sommelier about the vintage and its condition.

marques-de-caceres.name: Marqués de Cáceres
marques-de-caceres.line: A well known Rioja house making classic Reservas and Gran Reservas.
marques-de-caceres.tell: Marqués de Cáceres is a widely known Rioja name. The Gran Reserva is aged long: smooth, with red fruit, vanilla and spice. A safe, classic choice.

marquis-d-angerville.name: Marquis d'Angerville
marquis-d-angerville.line: The great Volnay domaine, owner of the Clos des Ducs monopole, making pure, fragrant reds, farmed biodynamically.
marquis-d-angerville.tell: D'Angerville is perhaps the most famous name in Volnay. Clos des Ducs is their walled vineyard; Champans, Taillepieds and Caillerets are top premier crus. Elegant, fragrant and long lived.

martin-woods.name: Martin Woods
martin-woods.line: A small Oregon winery making fresh, precise single vineyard wines.
martin-woods.tell: Martin Woods is a small Oregon producer. Rockbar Vineyard Syrah comes from The Rocks District, a stony area known for savoury, meaty Syrah. A great choice for a guest who likes Rhône wines.

martinelli.name: Martinelli
martinelli.line: A long established Sonoma farming family, known for ripe, generous Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and Zinfandel from their own vineyards.
martinelli.tell: The Martinellis have farmed in the Russian River Valley for generations. Their style is ripe and generous, so Bella Vigne Pinot Noir is soft, round and full of dark cherry fruit. A friendly bottle for a guest who likes a plush red, and fair value on this list.

mas-de-valeriole.name: Mas de Valériole
mas-de-valeriole.tell: Valériole is an estate in the Camargue. Vé is a pale, dry rosé, offered in bottle and magnum.

masi.name: Masi
masi.line: A leading Valpolicella house and a specialist in wines from dried grapes, including several Amarones.
masi.tell: Masi is one of the great names of Amarone, made from grapes dried for months. Costasera is the classic, rich and velvety; Campolongo di Torbe and Mazzano are single vineyards, deeper and longer. Big wines for braised meats and cheese.

masseria-del-pino.name: Masseria del Pino
masseria-del-pino.line: A small organic and biodynamic farm on Mount Etna, making wine by hand from very old vines.
masseria-del-pino.tell: Masseria del Pino is a tiny farm on Etna that makes wine by hand from very old vines. I Nove Fratelli is mostly Nerello Mascalese: fragrant, savoury and mineral, with cherry and herbs. A great pick for a guest who loves Burgundy or Barolo.

masseto.name: Masseto
masseto.line: The famous Bolgheri Merlot, born at Tenuta dell'Ornellaia, one of Italy's most celebrated and costly wines.
masseto.tell: Masseto is a Merlot from a clay hill in Bolgheri, born at Ornellaia. It is deep, velvety and long lived, one of the most famous wines in Italy. Trophy bottles; involve the sommelier and decant.

massolino.name: Massolino
massolino.line: A family estate in Serralunga d'Alba, known for firm, fine Barolo, above all from the Vigna Rionda vineyard.
massolino.tell: Massolino is a family winery in Serralunga, the village known for the most structured Barolo. Vigna Rionda is their most famous site: deep, firm and long lived, and the list holds Riserva and magnums. The Barbera, Barbaresco and Riesling are friendlier entries.

mastroberardino.name: Mastroberardino
mastroberardino.line: The historic family of Campania wine, guardians of Aglianico and Taurasi.
mastroberardino.tell: Mastroberardino is the great old name of Campania. Radici Taurasi is Aglianico: dark, firm and long lived, sometimes called the Barolo of the south. Good with braised meats.

mathias-hirtzberger.name: Mathias Hirtzberger
mathias-hirtzberger.line: A Wachau grower from the Hirtzberger family.
mathias-hirtzberger.tell: Mathias Hirtzberger is from the Hirtzberger family of the Wachau. Ried Kollmitz is a Smaragd Riesling, the ripest dry style.

matrot.name: Domaine Matrot
matrot.line: A traditional Meursault estate run by Thierry and Pascale Matrot's family.
matrot.tell: Matrot is a traditional Meursault estate. Charmes and Perrières are premier crus, and the half-bottle Bourgogne suits one or two guests.

matthiasson.name: Matthiasson
matthiasson.tell: Matthiasson is a Napa winery known for unusual grapes. Ribolla Gialla is a textured white, here in older vintages.

maurice-schoech.name: Maurice Schoech
maurice-schoech.line: A family estate in Ammerschwihr with grand cru vines in Kaefferkopf and nearby sites.
