maurice-schoech.tell: Schoech is a family estate in Ammerschwihr. Kaefferkopf, Furstentum and Schlossberg are grand crus, and the wines are ripe and aromatic; ask the sommelier which carry sweetness.

max-ferd-richter.name: Max Ferd. Richter
max-ferd-richter.tell: Max Ferd. Richter is a family estate on the Mosel. Juffer-Sonnenuhr GG is a dry grand cru Riesling.

mayacamas.name: Mayacamas Vineyards
mayacamas.line: A historic stone winery high on Mount Veeder, famous for lean, long lived Cabernet and Chardonnay made without heavy oak.
mayacamas.tell: Mayacamas sits near the top of Mount Veeder, above the fog. The Cabernet is firm and restrained, made to age for decades rather than to impress young, and the list holds a run of vintages. The Chardonnay is lean and fresh. Ideal for a guest who prefers classic, less oaky Napa.

mazzei.name: Mazzei (Castello di Fonterutoli)
mazzei.line: An old Tuscan family whose Castello di Fonterutoli estate makes Chianti Classico and the Siepi blend.
mazzei.tell: The Mazzei family has made wine in Tuscany for centuries. Fonterutoli is their Chianti Classico, fresh and classic; Siepi is a richer blend of Sangiovese and Merlot. Philip is another of their reds. Reliable, polished Tuscan wines.

melanie-pfister.name: Mélanie Pfister
melanie-pfister.line: A family estate in northern Alsace, run by Mélanie Pfister.
melanie-pfister.tell: Mélanie Pfister runs her family estate in the north of Alsace. Macération is a skin-contact white, so it has more texture and colour than usual; ask the sommelier about the grape.

mendel.name: Mendel
mendel.line: A Mendoza winery working old vines in Luján de Cuyo.
mendel.tell: Mendel is a Mendoza winery known for old vines. Its Cabernet Sauvignon is ripe and polished, with dark fruit and fresh acidity. A good value alternative to Napa Cabernet.

meo-camuzet.name: Domaine Méo-Camuzet
meo-camuzet.line: A leading Vosne-Romanée domaine run by Jean-Nicolas Méo, linked to the legendary Henri Jayer, making rich, polished reds.
meo-camuzet.tell: Méo-Camuzet is one of Vosne's top names; Henri Jayer once farmed some of its vines. The wines are ripe, deep and polished. Bottles marked Frère et Soeurs are the négociant range from bought grapes, a gentler price for the same hand.

merryvale.name: Merryvale
merryvale.line: A family owned St. Helena winery; Profile is its flagship Cabernet led blend.
merryvale.tell: Merryvale is a family winery in St. Helena. Profile, the flagship, is a Cabernet led blend: rich, layered and polished. A classic Napa choice for steak.

mesclances.name: Château les Mesclances
mesclances.tell: Mesclances is a Provence estate. Romane is a pale, dry rosé, crisp and good value.

meyer-fonne.name: Meyer-Fonné
meyer-fonne.line: A family estate in Katzenthal making precise grand cru Riesling.
meyer-fonne.tell: Meyer-Fonné is a family estate in Katzenthal. Kaefferkopf and Schoenenbourg are grand crus, and the Rieslings are dry and fine.

miani.name: Miani
miani.line: A tiny, revered Friuli estate making very low yield, concentrated wines.
miani.tell: Miani is a tiny Friuli estate with a cult following, known for very low yields. Filip is a Merlot: deep, concentrated and polished. Rare; ask the sommelier about the vintage.

michel-bregeon.name: Michel Brégeon
michel-bregeon.line: A Muscadet estate known for long lees ageing, especially from the Gorges cru.
michel-bregeon.tell: Brégeon is a Muscadet estate that ages its wines a long time on their lees. Gorges is one of the new Muscadet crus, and long ageing gives it depth and a savoury, saline edge. Muscadet with oysters is a classic.

michel-lafarge.name: Domaine Michel Lafarge
michel-lafarge.line: A leading Volnay family domaine, farmed biodynamically, making traditional, long lived reds including the Clos du Château des Ducs monopole.
michel-lafarge.tell: Lafarge is one of the great Volnay families. Clos des Chênes and their own Clos du Château des Ducs are classic premier crus. Pure, fragrant and long lived.

michel-magnien.name: Domaine Michel Magnien
michel-magnien.line: A Morey-Saint-Denis family domaine, run by Frédéric Magnien, farming organically and making fresh, transparent reds.
michel-magnien.tell: The Magnien family domaine in Morey-Saint-Denis. The wines are fresh and focused, with a light touch. The Chambolle premier cru Les Sentiers is fragrant and fine.

michel-niellon.name: Domaine Michel Niellon
michel-niellon.tell: Niellon is a small, revered Chassagne-Montrachet estate. Les Vergers and Clos de la Truffière are premier crus and Chevalier-Montrachet the grand cru.

miner.name: Miner Family Vineyards
miner.tell: Miner is a Napa family winery. Its Sauvignon Blanc is crisp and bright.

minuty.name: Château Minuty
minuty.line: A Provence estate on the Saint-Tropez peninsula, known for pale, dry, Grenache-led rosé.
minuty.tell: Minuty is one of the best-known names in Provence rosé, from near Saint-Tropez. The Prestige is very pale, dry and delicate, with red berry and citrus, the classic poolside style that also flatters lighter Creole dishes.

moet-chandon.name: Moët & Chandon
moet-chandon.line: Champagne's largest house, in Épernay, with a bright, fruity style.
moet-chandon.tell: Moët is the largest Champagne house. Grand Vintage is its vintage wine, made only in chosen years, fuller and toastier than the Impérial. Nectar Impérial Rosé is sweeter, a demi-sec, for guests who like it softer or with dessert.

moillard-grivot.name: Moillard-Grivot
moillard-grivot.line: A Nuits-Saint-Georges négociant house, here a Mercurey red with some age.
moillard-grivot.tell: Mercurey in the Côte Chalonnaise gives sturdy, red fruited reds. This one is from 2013, so it has softened. One of the gentlest prices among the reds.

mongeard-mugneret.name: Domaine Mongeard-Mugneret
mongeard-mugneret.line: A Vosne-Romanée family domaine with a broad range, including Échezeaux and Richebourg, in a ripe, generous style.
mongeard-mugneret.tell: Mongeard-Mugneret is a large Vosne family estate. The wines are generous and approachable, from Hautes-Côtes up to Richebourg. A good way to give a guest a grand cru at a gentler price.

monsecco.name: Monsecco
monsecco.line: An estate in Ghemme in northern Piedmont, making Nebbiolo based wines.
monsecco.tell: Monsecco makes Ghemme, a Nebbiolo zone in northern Piedmont. Expect a fragrant, firm red, lighter than Barolo, with red fruit and earth. Good with mushrooms, game or roast meats.

monte-rio.name: Monte Rio Cellars
monte-rio.tell: Monte Rio is a small California label. Its Lodi Sauvignon Blanc is fresh and easy.

montenidoli.name: Montenidoli
montenidoli.line: A San Gimignano estate run by Elisabetta Fagiuoli, making characterful whites and reds from Tuscan grapes.
montenidoli.tell: Montenidoli is a family estate in San Gimignano, better known for white. Triassico is a red, named for the ancient soils: fresh, savoury and fragrant. The list holds it in magnum across vintages, a good pick for a table sharing pasta or poultry.

monthelie-douhairet-porcheret.name: Domaine Monthelie-Douhairet-Porcheret
monthelie-douhairet-porcheret.line: A historic Monthélie domaine making traditional, long lived reds from Monthélie, Volnay and Pommard.
monthelie-douhairet-porcheret.tell: This Monthélie estate makes traditional wines that need time. The Volnay Champans and Pommard premier crus are firm and serious. Good value for a guest who likes classic Burgundy.

moonflower.name: Moonflower
moonflower.line: A small Willamette Valley label making organically farmed estate Pinot Noir in the northern part of the valley.
moonflower.tell: Moonflower is a small Oregon label with organically farmed estate fruit from the north of the Willamette Valley. The Pinot Noir is light, bright and savoury, with raspberry and a little earth. A gentle, fresh red for fish or poultry.

moreau-naudet.name: Moreau-Naudet
moreau-naudet.line: A family estate in Chablis making ripe yet mineral wines.
moreau-naudet.tell: Moreau-Naudet is a family estate in Chablis. Forêts, Montmains and Vaillons are premier crus, and the village Chablis and Petit Chablis are fresh, crisp entries.

morey-coffinet.name: Domaine Morey-Coffinet
morey-coffinet.line: A family estate in Chassagne, organic and biodynamic in its farming.
morey-coffinet.tell: Morey-Coffinet is a family estate in Chassagne-Montrachet. En Remilly is a premier cru and Les Houillères a village site, with a Bâtard-Montrachet grand cru at the top and a Rully as the value bottle.

morgan.name: Morgan
morgan.tell: Morgan is a Santa Lucia Highlands winery. Rosella's is a famous vineyard, and this older Chardonnay should show bottle age; ask the sommelier how it is drinking.

moric.name: Moric
moric.line: An estate that helped show how fine old vine Blaufränkisch from Burgenland can be.
moric.tell: Moric is one of the names that made Austrian Blaufränkisch famous. The Reserve is fresh and peppery, with dark berries and fine tannin, often compared to Northern Rhône or Burgundy. A thoughtful pick for a curious red drinker.

moritz-kissinger.name: Moritz Kissinger
moritz-kissinger.tell: Moritz Kissinger is a Rheinhessen grower. 0 Ohm is a white blend of Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc.

moulin-d-issan.name: Moulin d'Issan
moulin-d-issan.line: A Bordeaux Supérieur from the family behind Château d'Issan in Margaux, made to drink young.
moulin-d-issan.tell: Moulin d'Issan comes from the people behind Château d'Issan in Margaux, made from vines outside the classed growth. It is a Cabernet-led claret with dark fruit and firm but friendly tannin, a true Bordeaux at a glass price.

mount-brave.name: Mount Brave
mount-brave.line: A Mount Veeder estate making mountain reds, including an unusual Malbec.
mount-brave.tell: Mount Brave farms steep slopes on Mount Veeder. Its Malbec is dark, dense and firm, with mountain structure. An unusual Napa red for a guest who likes Argentinian Malbec.

mugneret-gibourg.name: Domaine Georges Mugneret-Gibourg
mugneret-gibourg.line: A small, much admired Vosne-Romanée domaine run by the Mugneret sisters, celebrated for silky, perfumed, beautifully balanced reds.
mugneret-gibourg.tell: Mugneret-Gibourg is a quiet star of Vosne-Romanée. The wines have finesse, fragrance and a silky texture at every level, from Bourgogne to Échezeaux. These bottles are scarce; any of them is a lovely choice for a guest who knows Burgundy.

mullineux.name: Mullineux
mullineux.tell: Mullineux is a Swartland estate. Old Vines White is a Chenin Blanc-led blend, textured and good value.

muraje.name: Muraje
muraje.line: A small producer in Carema, the alpine Nebbiolo zone of stone terraces.
muraje.tell: Muraje is a small producer in Carema, where Nebbiolo grows on stone terraces in the foothills of the Alps. Sumié is fragrant and fresh, with fine tannin. Ask the sommelier about this rare bottle.

murdoch-hill.name: Murdoch Hill
murdoch-hill.line: A family estate in the cool Adelaide Hills, making fresh, bright wines.
murdoch-hill.tell: Murdoch Hill is a family estate in the Adelaide Hills, a cool part of South Australia. The Sauvignon Blanc is crisp and lively, with citrus and passion fruit. A good value white for seafood or salad.

nicchia.name: Nicchia (Cantina Carafoli)
nicchia.line: A Lambrusco di Modena from the Carafoli family, a long established winery near Modena.
nicchia.tell: Nicchia is made by the Carafoli family near Modena. Lambrusco is a lightly sparkling red, fresh and fruity, and this one blends several Lambrusco grapes. Serve it chilled; it is lovely with rich, salty food and a happy surprise for guests who think red wine cannot sparkle.

nicolas-feuillatte.name: Nicolas Feuillatte
nicolas-feuillatte.line: A large growers' cooperative brand in Chouilly, fresh and fruity, with Palmes d'Or as its prestige cuvée.
nicolas-feuillatte.tell: Nicolas Feuillatte brings together grapes from thousands of growers through a cooperative. The Réserve is fresh, fruity and approachable; Palmes d'Or is the prestige vintage in its studded bottle, and comes as a fuller rosé too.

nicolas-joly.name: Nicolas Joly
nicolas-joly.line: The biodynamic pioneer of Savennières, owner of the monopole Coulée de Serrant.
nicolas-joly.tell: Nicolas Joly is the great champion of biodynamics, and Coulée de Serrant is a vineyard he owns outright. The wines are powerful, dry Chenin Blanc, golden and honeyed, and they often benefit from air: ask the sommelier about decanting.

nicolas-potel.name: Nicolas Potel
nicolas-potel.line: A Nuits-Saint-Georges négociant house bearing the name of its founder, winemaker Nicolas Potel.
nicolas-potel.tell: The house bottles wines from bought grapes across the Côte d'Or. The Romanée-Saint-Vivant here is a grand cru at a gentler price than most. Ask the sommelier how these older bottles are showing.

niepoort.name: Niepoort
niepoort.line: A family Port house in Porto, also a leading maker of Douro and Bairrada table wines.
niepoort.tell: Niepoort is a family Port house known for its Colheitas and Garrafeira, tawny Ports from single vintages aged long. The Vintage Ports are deep and long lived. Lagar de Baixo is a Baga red from Bairrada: fresh and firm.

nikolaihof.name: Nikolaihof
nikolaihof.line: A historic biodynamic Wachau estate known for long-aged releases.
nikolaihof.tell: Nikolaihof is a historic biodynamic Wachau estate. Vinothek is a Riesling held many years in cask before release, so this old vintage is mature and complex.

numanthia.name: Numanthia
numanthia.line: A Toro estate making powerful Tempranillo from old vines; Termanthia is its top wine.
numanthia.tell: Numanthia makes big reds in Toro, a hot region on the Duero. Termanthia is its flagship, from very old vines: dense, dark and powerful. For a guest who loves rich red with steak.

ochota-barrels.name: Ochota Barrels
ochota-barrels.line: An Adelaide Hills winery known for fresh, light, natural minded wines.
ochota-barrels.tell: Ochota Barrels is an Adelaide Hills label known for fresh, lively wines. The Green Room is a Grenache blend from McLaren Vale: bright, juicy and light, lovely a touch cool. A fun pick for poultry or pork.

oddero.name: Oddero
oddero.line: A historic family estate in La Morra with holdings in many of the great Barolo and Barbaresco vineyards.
oddero.tell: Oddero is an old family estate with vines in many famous crus. Brunate and Rocche di Castiglione are perfumed, Bussia Vigna Mondoca and Villero deeper, and Vignarionda firm and grand. Gallina is their Barbaresco. Classic, traditional Nebbiolo, with many magnums on the list.

odette.name: Odette
odette.line: A Stags Leap District estate in the PlumpJack group, making polished Cabernet.
odette.tell: Odette is the PlumpJack family's winery in the Stags Leap District, where Cabernet tends to be supple and silky. The Napa Cabernet is dark, smooth and polished. A good choice for a guest who likes soft, rich red.

olivier-bernstein.name: Olivier Bernstein
olivier-bernstein.line: A small, high end négociant specialising in grand and premier cru Côte de Nuits wines, with a polished, concentrated style.
olivier-bernstein.tell: Bernstein makes a small range of top Côte de Nuits wines from bought grapes. The style is polished, deep and generous. Gevrey Cazetiers and Champeaux are fine premier crus.

opus-one.name: Opus One
opus-one.line: The Oakville estate created by Robert Mondavi and Baron Philippe de Rothschild of Mouton, making one Bordeaux style blend; Overture is its second wine.
opus-one.tell: Opus One began as a partnership between Robert Mondavi and the Rothschilds of Château Mouton. It makes one wine, a Cabernet led blend, polished and long lived. Overture is the estate's second wine. Guests know the name; the list holds half bottles up to a six litre Imperial.

orin-swift.name: Orin Swift
orin-swift.line: A California winery known for bold labels and rich, ripe blends.
orin-swift.tell: Orin Swift is famous for striking labels and generous wines. Advice From John is a Merlot led blend: ripe, round and full. A crowd pleaser for a guest who likes rich red.

ostertag.name: Domaine Ostertag
ostertag.line: A biodynamic estate in Epfig known for site-driven wines and a thoughtful, modern touch.
ostertag.tell: Ostertag is a biodynamic family estate. Muenchberg is a grand cru; Fronholz, Zellberg and Pflanzer are single sites. The Pinot Gris and Gewürztraminer can carry some sweetness; ask the sommelier which are dry.

palari.name: Palari
palari.line: A small estate near Messina known for reviving Faro, a fragrant Sicilian red.
palari.tell: Palari is a small estate in the hills near Messina. Rosso del Soprano is a red from local grapes: fragrant, fine and savoury. A lovely, unusual Sicilian red.

paolo-bea.name: Paolo Bea
paolo-bea.line: A traditional, natural minded family estate in Montefalco, Umbria.
paolo-bea.tell: Paolo Bea makes wine the old way in Montefalco. Pagliaro is a powerful Sagrantino, and Rosso de Veo is a blend. Wild, savoury and deep. An adventurous choice; decant.

pape-clement.name: Château Pape Clément
pape-clement.tell: Pape Clément is an old classed growth of Pessac-Léognan. The white is rich, lightly oaked and long.

pascal-clement.name: Pascal Clément
pascal-clement.line: A Burgundy producer making Puligny and Chassagne.
pascal-clement.tell: Pascal Clément makes Puligny and Chassagne. La Maltroie is a Chassagne premier cru, and the village Puligny is floral and fresh.

pascal-cotat.name: Pascal Cotat
pascal-cotat.line: A traditional Chavignol grower bottling Sancerre from the steep Monts Damnés and Grande Côte hillsides.
pascal-cotat.tell: Pascal Cotat makes old-school Sancerre from Chavignol's steepest slopes. Monts Damnés and La Grande Côte are rich and ripe, sometimes with a hint of sweetness. His rosé, labelled by lot, is a rare treat.

pascal-janvier.name: Pascal Janvier
pascal-janvier.line: A small grower in Jasnières, a little-known Loire corner for crisp, dry Chenin Blanc.
pascal-janvier.tell: Pascal Janvier makes Chenin Blanc in Jasnières, a tiny, cool appellation north of Tours. The wines are dry, sharp and mineral. A great discovery for a guest who likes crisp whites.

passopisciaro.name: Passopisciaro
passopisciaro.line: An Etna estate founded by Andrea Franchetti that bottles single contrade.
passopisciaro.tell: Passopisciaro was one of the first Etna estates to bottle single contrade. Guardiola and Sciaranuova are separate high sites: fragrant, mineral Nerello Mascalese. Elegant reds for poultry or pork.

patricia-green.name: Patricia Green Cellars
patricia-green.tell: Patricia Green is an Oregon winery best known for Pinot Noir. Its Sauvignon Blanc is crisp and fresh.

patrick-piuze.name: Patrick Piuze
patrick-piuze.line: A Québec-born winemaker making precise, site-driven Chablis from bought-in grapes.
patrick-piuze.tell: Patrick Piuze buys grapes from chosen plots across Chablis and bottles them site by site. Bougros is a grand cru; the Côtes d'Auxerre and Tonnerre wines come from just outside Chablis. Pure and mineral.

paul-bara.name: Paul Bara
paul-bara.line: A Bouzy grower devoted to rich, Pinot Noir-led grand cru Champagne.
paul-bara.tell: Paul Bara is a family estate in Bouzy, famous for Pinot Noir. The wines are full and red-fruited. The Special Club bottles, white and rosé, are their prestige wines, made under the growers' club rules.

paul-garaudet.name: Domaine Paul Garaudet
paul-garaudet.line: A Monthélie family domaine making honest, fruity reds from Monthélie and neighbouring Volnay.
paul-garaudet.tell: A small family grower in Monthélie, a village that offers Volnay like charm for less. Cuvée Paul is fresh and red fruited. A friendly, value red.

paul-hobbs.name: Paul Hobbs
paul-hobbs.line: A celebrated California winemaker bottling rich single vineyard Cabernet in Napa, alongside projects in Argentina.
paul-hobbs.tell: Paul Hobbs is one of California's best known winemakers. Beckstoffer Dr. Crane, in St. Helena, and Nathan Coombs, in Coombsville, are single vineyard Cabernets: ripe, dark and plush. He also founded Viña Cobos in Argentina, also on this list.

paul-jaboulet-aine.name: Paul Jaboulet Aîné
paul-jaboulet-aine.line: The historic northern Rhône house, owned by the Frey family since 2006, whose Hermitage La Chapelle is one of the great Rhône names.
paul-jaboulet-aine.tell: La Chapelle is Jaboulet's famous Hermitage. These bottles predate the move to the Domaine de la Chapelle label. Deep, savoury Syrah; ask the sommelier about the vintage.

paul-janin.name: Paul Janin
paul-janin.line: A Moulin-à-Vent family domaine making deep, structured Gamay from the Clos du Tremblay.
paul-janin.tell: Janin is a family grower in Moulin-à-Vent, the cru that gives the deepest Beaujolais. A great value red with meats.

paul-pernot.name: Paul Pernot
paul-pernot.tell: Paul Pernot is a family estate in Puligny-Montrachet. Bienvenues-Bâtard-Montrachet is a grand cru, rich and floral.

paul-pillot.name: Domaine Paul Pillot
paul-pillot.line: A four-generation family estate in Chassagne, run by Thierry Pillot, with a pure, taut style.
paul-pillot.tell: Paul Pillot is a family domaine, run by Thierry Pillot and his sister. The wines are crisp and precise. Cailleret and Clos Saint-Jean are premier crus; Le Charmois a Saint-Aubin premier cru; the Aligoté a value bottle.

pazo-das-bruxas.name: Pazo das Bruxas
pazo-das-bruxas.line: An Albariño from Rías Baixas on the Atlantic coast of Galicia, made by the Torres family.
pazo-das-bruxas.tell: Pazo das Bruxas is Albariño from Rías Baixas, the rainy, sea-facing corner of northwest Spain. It is fresh, citrusy and a little saline, built for seafood, so it sits happily beside oysters, crab and anything with lemon.

peay.name: Peay Vineyards
peay.line: A family estate on the far Sonoma Coast making cool climate Syrah, Pinot Noir and Chardonnay.
peay.tell: Peay farms one of the coolest spots in California, close to the ocean on the far Sonoma Coast. Les Titans Syrah is peppery, savoury and fresh, closer to the Northern Rhône than to ripe California.

penalolen.name: Peñalolén
penalolen.line: A Maipo Valley label from the family behind Domus Aurea, making good value Cabernet.
penalolen.tell: Peñalolén comes from the same family estate as Domus Aurea, in the foothills of the Andes near Santiago. The Cabernet is fresh and dark fruited, with a hint of mint. A great value red for steak.

penfolds.name: Penfolds
penfolds.line: Australia's most famous wine house; Grange is its legendary Shiraz.
penfolds.tell: Penfolds is Australia's most famous name. Grange is its iconic Shiraz: dense, dark and very long lived. Bin 389, a Cabernet Shiraz blend, is nicknamed baby Grange. Celebration bottles; decant.

penner-ash.name: Penner-Ash
penner-ash.tell: Penner-Ash is a Willamette Valley winery. Its Chardonnay and Viognier are offered, fresh and fruity.

perrier-jouet.name: Perrier-Jouët
perrier-jouet.line: An Épernay house with a floral, Chardonnay-led style; Belle Epoque wears the painted anemone bottle.
perrier-jouet.tell: Perrier-Jouët is all about elegance and flowers, built on Chardonnay. Belle Epoque, the vintage prestige wine in the anemone bottle, is the one guests recognise; it is delicate and creamy and photographs beautifully at the table.

peter-lauer.name: Peter Lauer
peter-lauer.line: A Saar family estate that numbers each wine by its cask.
peter-lauer.tell: Lauer is a Saar family estate that names each wine by its cask, or Fass, number. Kern, Feils, Stirn and Neuenberg are sites, mostly dry or nearly so; ask the sommelier which carry sweetness.

peter-michael.name: Peter Michael
peter-michael.line: An estate in the volcanic hills of Knights Valley known for Les Pavots, a Bordeaux style blend, and rich Chardonnay.
peter-michael.tell: Peter Michael farms steep volcanic slopes in Knights Valley. Les Pavots is the estate blend: deep, fine and long lived. L'Esprit des Pavots is the younger drinking version, and Au Paradis comes from Oakville in Napa. A celebration name; several vintages are listed.

petrus.name: Pétrus
petrus.line: The most famous wine of Pomerol, almost entirely Merlot from blue clay, among the most prized wines in the world.
petrus.tell: Pétrus is the most famous Pomerol, almost all Merlot from a blue clay plateau. A trophy bottle; involve the sommelier.

philippe-colin.name: Philippe Colin
philippe-colin.line: A Chassagne estate, part of the Colin family.
philippe-colin.tell: Philippe Colin is part of the Colin family of Chassagne-Montrachet. Clos Saint-Jean and La Maltroie are premier crus, rich and nutty.

philippe-gonet.name: Philippe Gonet
philippe-gonet.line: A family house in Le Mesnil with Chardonnay at its core, from fresh blends to grand cru vintage.
philippe-gonet.tell: Philippe Gonet is a family house in Le Mesnil. TER is a Blanc de Blancs, the Réserve a blend and the Millésime a grand cru vintage Blanc de Blancs. Crisp, chalky and good value for its villages.

philipponnat.name: Philipponnat
philipponnat.line: A Mareuil-sur-Aÿ house with a powerful, Pinot Noir-driven style, owner of the steep walled vineyard Clos des Goisses.
philipponnat.tell: Philipponnat makes structured, Pinot Noir-led Champagne. Clos des Goisses is its famous single walled vineyard on a very steep chalk slope by the Marne: rich, deep and long-lived. Royale Réserve is the house blend, full and food-friendly.

pichler-krutzler.name: Pichler-Krutzler
pichler-krutzler.tell: Pichler-Krutzler is a Wachau estate. In der Wand is a dry Riesling from a steep site, mineral and fine.

piedrasassi.name: Piedrasassi
piedrasassi.line: A small Santa Barbara producer making savoury, fresh Syrah from single vineyards.
piedrasassi.tell: Piedrasassi makes Syrah in a fresh, savoury style. Bien Nacido, in the Santa Maria Valley, and Rim Rock, in Arroyo Grande, are cool sites: pepper, dark fruit and lively acidity. Great with lamb or duck.

piero-benevelli.name: Piero Benevelli
piero-benevelli.line: A small family estate in Monforte d'Alba.
piero-benevelli.tell: Piero Benevelli is a small family producer in Monforte d'Alba. Mosconi is a Barolo vineyard known for depth and structure. Ask the sommelier about its style and readiness.

pierre-andre.name: Domaine Pierre André
pierre-andre.line: A Côte de Beaune house bottling wines from across the Côte, here Pommard Clos de la Commaraine.
pierre-andre.tell: Clos de la Commaraine is a walled premier cru in Pommard. Expect a firm, dark fruited red with a few years of age. A good match for beef.

pierre-cellier.name: Pierre Cellier
pierre-cellier.line: A label from the Gonet family of Le Mesnil, first made for a Paris restaurant friend in the 1970s.
pierre-cellier.tell: Pierre Cellier comes from the Gonet family in Le Mesnil. Cuvée Prestige is a Pinot Noir-led blend with Chardonnay from Le Mesnil: round, toasty and fruity, a crowd-pleaser.

pierre-gelin.name: Domaine Pierre Gelin
pierre-gelin.line: A Fixin family domaine and owner of the Clos Napoléon premier cru, making firm, rustic reds and a Chambertin Clos de Bèze.
pierre-gelin.tell: Gelin is Fixin's best known name, a village next to Gevrey that gives sturdy reds at good prices. Clos Napoléon is their own walled vineyard. The Clos de Bèze is the grand cru treat.

pierre-girardin.name: Pierre Girardin
pierre-girardin.line: A young Meursault-based négociant and grower making precise whites.
pierre-girardin.tell: Pierre Girardin is a young producer based in Meursault. Éclat de Calcaire is a Bourgogne Blanc, crisp and mineral, and the list spells the name Giardin.

pierre-gonon.name: Pierre Gonon
pierre-gonon.line: A Saint-Joseph family domaine, much admired for traditional, fragrant Syrah.
pierre-gonon.tell: Gonon is one of the most admired names in Saint-Joseph. Their Syrah is fragrant, peppery and fresh. Note the list spells it Gonan.

pierre-guillemot.name: Pierre Guillemot
pierre-guillemot.tell: Guillemot is a family estate in Savigny-lès-Beaune. Dessus les Golardes and Vieilles Vignes are whites, fresh and good value.

pierre-meurgey.name: Pierre Meurgey
pierre-meurgey.line: A Burgundy native and part grower, part négociant, with partner growers across the Côte d'Or.
pierre-meurgey.tell: Pierre Meurgey works with partner growers across Burgundy. This bottle is a white Beaune premier cru: Chardonnay with ripe orchard fruit and a fresh finish, a good value step into the Côte de Beaune.

pierre-morey.name: Domaine Pierre Morey
pierre-morey.line: A Meursault domaine farmed biodynamically, best known for whites, also making red Pommard.
pierre-morey.tell: Pierre Morey is a famous name in Meursault whites. This Pommard Grands Épenots has some age, giving a softened, savoury red. A good pick for game birds or beef.

pierre-paillard.name: Pierre Paillard
pierre-paillard.line: A family estate in Bouzy making precise, low-dosage grand cru Champagne.
pierre-paillard.tell: Pierre Paillard is a family estate in Bouzy run by brothers. La Grande Récolte and Les Parcelles are dry, focused grand cru wines; Les Parcelles carries a number for its base year. Crisp and clean, very good with seafood.

pierre-peters.name: Pierre Péters
pierre-peters.line: A leading Le Mesnil grower whose Blanc de Blancs draws on a long-kept perpetual reserve.
pierre-peters.tell: Pierre Péters is one of the benchmark growers of Le Mesnil. Cuvée de Réserve blends young wine with a perpetual reserve, giving depth to its chalky freshness. Les Montjolys and Réserve Oubliée are the top bottles.

pierre-sparr.name: Pierre Sparr
pierre-sparr.line: A long-established Alsace house making Crémant and grand cru whites.
pierre-sparr.tell: Pierre Sparr is an old Alsace house. The Crémant rosé by the glass is Pinot Noir sparkling wine, fresh and fruity; Mambourg and Schoenenbourg are grand cru whites, fuller and more aromatic.

pieve-santa-restituta.name: Pieve Santa Restituta (Gaja)
pieve-santa-restituta.line: The Gaja family's estate in Montalcino, making Brunello including the single vineyards Rennina and Sugarille.
pieve-santa-restituta.tell: Pieve Santa Restituta is the Gaja family estate in Montalcino. The Brunello is polished and deep. Rennina is the more fragrant single vineyard and Sugarille the firmer one. A strong name for a guest who loves Gaja or wants a celebration Brunello.

pilcrow.name: Pilcrow
pilcrow.line: A small Napa label that began with Cabernet from the Pym Rae vineyard on Mount Veeder.
pilcrow.tell: Pilcrow is a small label whose first wines came from the Pym Rae vineyard high on Mount Veeder. Mountain Cabernet here is dark and firm, with black fruit and a floral note. Ask the sommelier how it is drinking.

piper-heidsieck.name: Piper-Heidsieck
piper-heidsieck.line: A large Reims house with a fruity, Pinot Noir-led style; it makes Brennan's own Essential cuvée.
piper-heidsieck.tell: Piper-Heidsieck is a big Reims house with a generous, fruit-forward style led by Pinot Noir. Brennan's Essential is made for the house by Piper, an Extra Brut, so it is drier than most; the Sauvage rosé is fuller and fruitier.

ployez-jacquemart.name: Ployez-Jacquemart
ployez-jacquemart.line: A small family house in Ludes on the Montagne de Reims, making long-aged, refined Champagne.
ployez-jacquemart.tell: Ployez-Jacquemart is a small family house on the Montagne de Reims. Liesse d'Harbonville is its prestige cuvée, aged long before release, so it shows toast, nuts and a fine, creamy mousse. A collector's bottle at less than the famous names.

plumpjack.name: PlumpJack
plumpjack.line: An Oakville estate making ripe, polished Cabernet, the founding winery of a group that includes Cade and Odette.
plumpjack.tell: PlumpJack sits in Oakville, the heart of Napa Cabernet country. The Estate Cabernet is rich and supple, with dark fruit and fine tannin. The magnum is a good bottle for a table of four or more with steak.

podere-santa-maria.name: Podere Santa Maria (Colleoni)
podere-santa-maria.line: A tiny biodynamic Montalcino estate run by the Colleoni family, making elegant, traditional Brunello.
podere-santa-maria.tell: Podere Santa Maria is a tiny biodynamic estate run by Marino and Luisa Colleoni. The Brunello is fine and fragrant, aged in large casks. Poggio Sant'Arna is a rare single parcel Riserva. Ask the sommelier about these small production bottles.

poggio-di-sotto.name: Poggio di Sotto
poggio-di-sotto.line: A Montalcino estate near Castelnuovo dell'Abate, admired for pale, fragrant, traditional Brunello.
poggio-di-sotto.tell: Poggio di Sotto makes some of the most graceful Brunello, from slopes in the south of Montalcino. It is fragrant and fine, with red fruit and spice, and ages superbly. Rare; the Riserva and magnum are celebration bottles.

pol-roger.name: Pol Roger
pol-roger.line: A family-owned Épernay house, elegant and fine, whose Sir Winston Churchill cuvée honours its most famous customer.
pol-roger.tell: Pol Roger is still family owned and known for fine, persistent bubbles. Churchill was a devoted customer, so the prestige cuvée bears his name: powerful, Pinot Noir-rich and long. The Brut and Blanc de Blancs are crisp and polished.

ponsot.name: Domaine Ponsot
ponsot.line: A famous Morey estate; its white Monts Luisants comes from very old Aligoté vines.
ponsot.tell: Ponsot is a great Morey-Saint-Denis name. Clos des Monts Luisants is a white premier cru made from old Aligoté vines, and Corton-Charlemagne and Montrachet are its grand crus.

possa.name: Possa
possa.line: A small Cinque Terre grower on steep terraces.
possa.tell: Possa farms steep terraces in the Cinque Terre on the Ligurian coast. Triple A is a white; ask the sommelier about its grapes.

pousse-d-or.name: Domaine de la Pousse d'Or
pousse-d-or.line: A historic Volnay domaine with several walled monopole vineyards, including Clos de la Bousse d'Or and Clos des 60 Ouvrées.
pousse-d-or.tell: Pousse d'Or owns walled vineyards in Volnay and Pommard. The style is ripe and polished, and Clos de la Bousse d'Or is their signature. A safe premier cru Volnay recommendation.

prager.name: Prager
prager.tell: Prager is a top Wachau name. Bodenstein is a high Grüner Veltliner site, dry, rich and mineral.

prelius.name: Prelius (Castelprile)
prelius.line: The organic Maremma estate of the family behind Castello di Volpaia, near the Tuscan coast.
prelius.tell: Prelius is the Maremma estate of the family who own Castello di Volpaia in Chianti, a few miles from the sea. Castelprile Riserva blends Sangiovese with Bordeaux grapes: ripe, smooth and dark fruited. Good with beef or lamb.

presquile.name: Presqu'ile
presquile.region: Santa Maria Valley, Santa Barbara County
presquile.line: A family winery on a hill in the Santa Maria Valley, close enough to the Pacific to make cool, fresh Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and Syrah.
presquile.tell: Presqu'ile farms its own vineyard in the Santa Maria Valley, where ocean fog keeps things cool. The wines are fresh and light on their feet: bright red fruited Pinot Noir, a dry Pinot rosé and a peppery Syrah. A good pick for a guest who wants California fruit without the weight.

pride-mountain.name: Pride Mountain Vineyards
pride-mountain.line: A family estate high on Spring Mountain whose vineyards straddle the Napa and Sonoma county line, known for dense Merlot and Cabernet.
pride-mountain.tell: Pride sits right on the county line at the top of Spring Mountain, so some rows are in Napa and some in Sonoma. Mountain fruit gives deep, concentrated wines. The Merlot is rich and dark, more powerful than most, and the half bottle suits two guests.

produttori-del-barbaresco.name: Produttori del Barbaresco
produttori-del-barbaresco.line: The village cooperative of Barbaresco, admired for traditional wines and single vineyard Riservas.
produttori-del-barbaresco.tell: Produttori del Barbaresco is the village cooperative, and one of the best in Italy. The Barbaresco is classic and fair priced. Asili, Montefico, Ovello and Rabajà are single vineyards, each with its own character. Great value for Nebbiolo lovers.

proyecto-las-compuertas.name: Proyecto Las Compuertas
proyecto-las-compuertas.line: An Argentine project focused on old vine Malbec and soil differences.
proyecto-las-compuertas.tell: Proyecto Las Compuertas makes Malbec with an eye on soil. Cinco Suelos means five soils, blending parcels from different ground: fresh, dark fruited and floral. Ask the sommelier about its style.

prunier-bonheur.name: Domaine Prunier-Bonheur
prunier-bonheur.tell: Prunier-Bonheur is a family estate in Auxey-Duresses. Their white is crisp and fresh, good value from the Côte de Beaune.

pym-rae.name: Pym-Rae
pym-rae.line: A Mount Veeder estate bought by the Tesseron family of Château Pontet-Canet, bottled under its own name.
pym-rae.tell: Pym-Rae is a hillside estate on Mount Veeder, now owned by the family behind Château Pontet-Canet in Pauillac. The Cabernet is firm and fine, mountain fruit made with a Bordeaux sensibility. A thoughtful pick for a Bordeaux drinker.

quilceda-creek.name: Quilceda Creek
quilceda-creek.line: A family winery whose Columbia Valley Cabernet is among Washington's most celebrated.
quilceda-creek.tell: Quilceda Creek is a family winery and Washington's most famous Cabernet name. The wine is rich, dense and polished, with dark fruit and great length. Several vintages are listed; a celebration bottle.

quinta-do-estranxeiro.name: Quinta do Estranxeiro
quinta-do-estranxeiro.line: A Ribeira Sacra project from the owners of Bodegas Zárate in Rías Baixas, working old bush vines on steep terraces.
quinta-do-estranxeiro.tell: Quinta do Estranxeiro is a young Ribeira Sacra project from the family behind Zárate, a top Albariño house. O Estranxeiro is mostly Mencía from old terraced vines: wild berries, herbs and a juicy texture. A fresh, food friendly red.

quinta-essentia.name: Quinta Essentia
quinta-essentia.line: A Stellenbosch old-vine Chenin Blanc project.
quinta-essentia.tell: Quinta Essentia is an old-vine Chenin Blanc project in Stellenbosch. It is rich, textured and good value.

quintarelli.name: Giuseppe Quintarelli
quintarelli.line: The legendary traditional producer of Valpolicella, famous for Amarone and wines aged for years before release.
quintarelli.tell: Quintarelli is the legend of Valpolicella. The Amarone is deep and layered; Rosso del Bepi is made in years when Amarone is not; Alzero uses dried Cabernet grapes; Ca' del Merlo is a ripasso style red. Amabile del Cere and Recioto are sweet. Rare bottles; decant the reds.

quintessa.name: Quintessa
quintessa.line: A biodynamically farmed estate in Rutherford owned by the Huneeus family, making one elegant Cabernet led blend.
quintessa.tell: Quintessa is a single estate in Rutherford, farmed biodynamically, that makes one blended red. It is polished and fine rather than heavy, with dark fruit and a long finish. The three litre bottle here is for a big celebration; plan it with the sommelier.

racines.name: Racines
racines.line: A Sta. Rita Hills project making cool-climate Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and sparkling wine.
racines.tell: Racines makes taut, cool-climate wines in Sta. Rita Hills, where Pacific wind keeps the grapes fresh. The Chardonnay is lean and mineral rather than buttery, and the Brut is crisp; ask the sommelier about the team behind it before telling the story.

radikon.name: Radikon
radikon.line: A family estate on the Slovenian border in Friuli, pioneers of long skin contact wines.
radikon.tell: Radikon is a family estate near the Slovenian border, famous for its orange wines. The reds are made with the same patience: long aged and savoury. They use 500 ml bottles. An adventurous choice; ask the sommelier how they are drinking.

radio-coteau.name: Radio-Coteau
radio-coteau.line: A Sonoma winery making cool climate Syrah, Pinot Noir and Zinfandel with a light hand and real freshness.
radio-coteau.tell: Radio-Coteau farms and buys from cool coastal sites in western Sonoma. The Syrahs are peppery and savoury, Las Colinas and Timbervine among them, and Lemorel is a fresh, elegant Zinfandel. A great choice for a guest who likes Northern Rhône wines.

ramey.name: Ramey Wine Cellars
ramey.line: A Sonoma winery best known for Chardonnay, also making Bordeaux style reds from Napa and the North Coast.
ramey.tell: Ramey is a leading Sonoma Chardonnay house that also makes serious red. Pedregal is a single vineyard Cabernet from Oakville, dark and structured; Claret is the friendlier North Coast blend.

ramonet.name: Domaine Ramonet
ramonet.line: A legendary Chassagne-Montrachet domaine, famous for white wine, also making serious red Chassagne.
ramonet.tell: Ramonet is one of the most revered names in white Burgundy. Their red Chassagne is firm, fresh and long lived, and Clos Saint-Jean is a classic premier cru. A clever choice for a red drinker who wants a great name.

rare-champagne.name: Rare Champagne
rare-champagne.line: Once Piper-Heidsieck's prestige cuvée, Rare is now its own label: vintage Champagne, rich and spicy, made only in chosen years.
rare-champagne.tell: Rare began as the prestige wine of Piper-Heidsieck and now stands on its own. It is made only in chosen vintages and aged long before release, so it tastes rich and layered, with toast, dried fruit and spice. A celebration bottle.

raspail-ay.name: Domaine Raspail-Ay
raspail-ay.tell: Raspail-Ay is a traditional Gigondas family. Expect a warm, spicy red. The half bottle is handy for a couple.

raul-perez.name: Raúl Pérez
raul-perez.line: An influential winemaker based in Bierzo who works with old vineyards across north west Spain.
raul-perez.tell: Raúl Pérez is one of the most influential winemakers in Spain, working old vines in Bierzo and Galicia. El Pecado is a Ribeira Sacra red: fragrant, mineral and fine. A treat for an adventurous guest.

raveneau.name: Domaine François Raveneau
raveneau.line: The most revered estate in Chablis, making long-lived grand and premier cru wines in tiny amounts.
raveneau.tell: Raveneau is Chablis's most sought-after name. The wines are intense, mineral and built to age, from crus like Montée de Tonnerre, Butteaux and Blanchot. Rare and allocated: treat each bottle as a collector's.

raymond-dupont-fahn.name: Raymond Dupont-Fahn
raymond-dupont-fahn.line: A small Monthelie estate making vivid whites in Meursault and Bourgogne.
raymond-dupont-fahn.tell: Dupont-Fahn is a small estate near Meursault. Les Tillets is a Meursault village site and Chaumes des Perrières a Bourgogne from near the village: vivid and fresh.

raymond-usseglio.name: Domaine Raymond Usseglio & Fils
raymond-usseglio.line: A Châteauneuf-du-Pape family domaine making Grenache led wines; Cuvée Impériale is its old vine top wine.
raymond-usseglio.tell: Usseglio is a family estate in Châteauneuf. Cuvée Girard and Cuvée Impériale are old vine Grenache led wines. Rich, spicy and generous.

regnaudot.name: Domaine Regnaudot
regnaudot.line: A family grower in Maranges, the southernmost village of the Côte de Beaune, making sturdy, good value reds.
regnaudot.tell: Maranges is the last village at the south of the Côte de Beaune, and it gives firm, fruity reds at fair prices. Regnaudot is a local family. These are some of the best value premier crus on the list.

remelluri.name: Remelluri
remelluri.line: A historic estate in the hills of Rioja Alavesa, run by the family of Telmo Rodríguez.
remelluri.tell: Remelluri is an estate high in Rioja Alavesa, farmed organically by the family of winemaker Telmo Rodríguez. The Reserva is fresh and savoury; the Gran Reserva in magnum is deeper and longer. Elegant Rioja for lamb.

remoissenet.name: Remoissenet Père et Fils
remoissenet.line: A Beaune négociant famous for a deep cellar of old vintages, here Richebourg, Clos Vougeot and Volnay going back to the 1950s.
remoissenet.tell: Remoissenet is known for its deep stocks of old Burgundy. These bottles go back decades; their state can vary from bottle to bottle. Involve the sommelier before recommending any of them.

rene-geoffroy.name: René Geoffroy
rene-geoffroy.region: Aÿ and Cumières, Vallée de la Marne
rene-geoffroy.line: A family grower rooted in Cumières, known for rich, vinous Champagne and a fine saignée rosé.
rene-geoffroy.tell: René Geoffroy is a family estate with deep roots in Cumières. Cuvée Expression is the round, fruity house blend, and the Rosé de Saignée is coloured on the skins: deep, fruity and great with food.

rene-rostaing.name: René Rostaing
rene-rostaing.line: A top Côte-Rôtie domaine, now run by Pierre Rostaing, making fine, elegant Syrah including Côte Blonde and La Landonne.
rene-rostaing.tell: Rostaing is a leading Côte-Rôtie name, and Côte Blonde is the softer, more perfumed side of the appellation; La Landonne is the darker, firmer side. Ampodium is their blend; decant.

ridge.name: Ridge Vineyards
ridge.line: A historic California winery famous for Monte Bello Cabernet from the Santa Cruz Mountains and for old vine Zinfandel blends from Sonoma.
ridge.tell: Ridge is one of the great names of California. Monte Bello, from high in the Santa Cruz Mountains, is a firm, long lived Cabernet blend. Lytton Springs, Pagani Ranch and Three Valleys are Zinfandel based: spicy, brambly and generous. Essence is a sweet late harvest wine for dessert.

ridgeview.name: Ridgeview
ridgeview.line: A family winery in Sussex making English sparkling wine from the Champagne grapes.
ridgeview.tell: Ridgeview is a Sussex family estate, part of England's sparkling success. Bloomsbury is Chardonnay-led and fresh, Cavendish Pinot-led and rounder, Fitzrovia a rosé. A fun surprise for a guest who has never tried English bubbles.

riveyrac.name: Riveyrac
riveyrac.line: A Roussillon name for long aged Rivesaltes, a fortified sweet wine of southern France.
riveyrac.tell: Riveyrac is known for Rivesaltes, a sweet fortified wine from Roussillon, near Spain, often aged for decades in wood. Expect dried fruit, nuts, caramel and spice. A great choice with chocolate or coffee desserts; ask about the vintage.

roagna.name: Roagna (I Paglieri)
roagna.line: A deeply traditional family estate in Barbaresco, making long aged wines from old vines.
roagna.tell: Roagna is one of the most traditional estates in Piedmont, with long fermentations and long ageing. Pajè, Crichët Pajé, Asili, Albesani, Faset and Gallina are Barbaresco vineyards; La Pira is Barolo. Fine, fragrant and long lived; decant.

robert-chevillon.name: Domaine Robert Chevillon
robert-chevillon.line: A benchmark Nuits-Saint-Georges domaine with old vines across the village's top premier crus, making classic, structured reds.
robert-chevillon.tell: Chevillon is one of the great names of Nuits. The premier crus, from Les Saints-Georges to Les Vaucrains, show the village's deep fruit and firm tannin. Excellent with beef or game.

robert-denogent.name: Robert Denogent
robert-denogent.line: A family estate in Fuissé making old-vine Pouilly-Fuissé.
robert-denogent.tell: Denogent makes Pouilly-Fuissé in southern Burgundy. Cuvée Claude Denogent is from old vines: rich and long.

robert-foley.name: Robert Foley Vineyards
robert-foley.line: A Howell Mountain winery making bold, structured mountain reds.
robert-foley.tell: Robert Foley makes wine high on Howell Mountain. The Cabernet is bold and dark, with the firm grip mountain fruit gives. A strong choice with beef; decant if it is young.

robert-mondavi.name: Robert Mondavi Winery
robert-mondavi.line: The Oakville winery that did more than any to make Napa famous; its Reserve Cabernet comes from the To Kalon Vineyard.
robert-mondavi.tell: Robert Mondavi built Napa's reputation around the world. The Reserve Cabernet comes from To Kalon, one of the most famous vineyards in America: rich, structured and long lived. A classic name for a celebration.

robert-weil.name: Robert Weil
robert-weil.line: A leading Rheingau estate in Kiedrich.
robert-weil.tell: Robert Weil is a top Rheingau estate in Kiedrich. The Kabinett is gently sweet, while the Trocken wines, Kiedricher and Monte Nostrum, are dry.

roblet-monnot.name: Domaine Roblet-Monnot
roblet-monnot.line: A small Volnay domaine making fragrant, finely textured reds from old vines.
roblet-monnot.tell: Roblet-Monnot is a small Volnay grower. Their Saint-François is fragrant and silky, the charming side of the Côte de Beaune. A lovely pick with chicken or duck.

roc-de-l-abbaye.name: Roc de l'Abbaye
roc-de-l-abbaye.line: A Pouilly-Fumé, Sauvignon Blanc from the right bank of the upper Loire.
roc-de-l-abbaye.tell: Pouilly-Fumé faces Sancerre across the Loire. This is crisp Sauvignon Blanc with citrus and a smoky, flinty edge, a good value step up from house white.

roc-des-boutires.name: Domaine du Roc des Boutires
roc-des-boutires.tell: This is Pouilly-Fuissé from southern Burgundy. En Bertilionne is a single site: ripe, round Chardonnay with a fresh finish.

roches-neuves.name: Domaine des Roches Neuves
roches-neuves.line: The Saumur domaine of Thierry Germain, farmed biodynamically, known for fresh, pure, lively Cabernet Franc.
roches-neuves.tell: Thierry Germain makes bright, pure Cabernet Franc in Saumur-Champigny. Terres Chaudes is a step up from the Domaine bottling. A great value red for poultry, pork or vegetables.

roco.name: Roco
roco.tell: Roco is a Willamette Valley winery. Gravel Road is a Chardonnay, fresh and bright.

roederer-estate.name: Roederer Estate
roederer-estate.line: Louis Roederer's California estate in the cool Anderson Valley, making refined sparkling wine.
roederer-estate.tell: Roederer Estate is the California home of the Champagne house Louis Roederer, in the cool Anderson Valley. L'Ermitage is its prestige wine; the rosé is fine and red-fruited.

roland-champion.name: Roland Champion
roland-champion.line: A family grower in Chouilly making grand cru Blanc de Blancs.
roland-champion.tell: Roland Champion is a family estate in Chouilly. Grand Éclat is a grand cru Blanc de Blancs, here in a six-litre Methuselah, a bottle for a big celebration that needs planning with the sommelier.

roland-lavantureux.name: Roland Lavantureux
roland-lavantureux.line: A family estate in Chablis making crisp, pure wines, including grand crus.
roland-lavantureux.tell: Lavantureux is a family estate in Chablis. Bougros, Preuses and Vaudésir are grand crus and Vau de Vey is a premier cru: clean, stony and precise.

rolly-gassmann.name: Rolly Gassmann
rolly-gassmann.line: A Rorschwihr family estate known for ripe, often off-dry wines released with bottle age.
rolly-gassmann.tell: Rolly Gassmann is a family estate in Rorschwihr. Kappelweg is a single site, and their wines often keep some sweetness, so ask the sommelier before promising dry.

ronchi.name: Azienda Agricola Ronchi
ronchi.line: A small family estate in the Barbaresco zone.
ronchi.tell: Ronchi is a small family estate in Barbaresco. Barbaresco is Nebbiolo, perfumed and firm, with red cherry, rose and fine tannin. This half bottle is a good way for two guests to try it.

roulot.name: Domaine Roulot
roulot.line: Jean-Marc Roulot's Meursault estate, among the most sought-after for pure, precise whites.
roulot.tell: Roulot is one of Meursault's most sought-after estates, with lean, crisp, pure wines. Les Luchets is a village site, Charmes and Bouchères are premier crus, and even the Aligoté and Bourgogne are prized and scarce.

round-pond.name: Round Pond Estate
round-pond.line: A family estate in Rutherford making balanced Cabernet from its own vineyards.
round-pond.tell: Round Pond is a family estate on the valley floor in Rutherford. The Estate Cabernet is balanced and smooth, with dark cherry and a touch of earth. A friendly, fairly priced Napa choice.

rousset-martin.name: François Rousset-Martin
rousset-martin.line: A small Jura grower making Chardonnay and Savagnin.
rousset-martin.tell: Rousset-Martin is a small Jura grower. Terres Blanches is a Chardonnay and Clos Bacchus a Savagnin, both precise and savoury.

rudi-pichler.name: Rudi Pichler
rudi-pichler.tell: Rudi Pichler is a top Wachau name. Hochrain is a Smaragd Riesling, here with some bottle age.

ruinart.name: Ruinart
ruinart.line: Founded in 1729 and often called the oldest established Champagne house, Ruinart is known for Chardonnay.
ruinart.tell: Ruinart dates to 1729 and leans on Chardonnay for a fresh, bright style. Dom Ruinart is the prestige vintage, a long-aged Blanc de Blancs, with a rosé version too. The house rosé is fruity and soft.

sadie.name: Sadie Family Wines
sadie.line: Eben Sadie's Swartland estate, a leader of the new wave of South African wine.
sadie.tell: Sadie Family is the leading name of the Swartland. Columella is the red, Syrah led with other Rhône grapes: deep, fragrant and fine. A treat for a Rhône lover.

saint-damien.name: Domaine Saint Damien
saint-damien.tell: Saint Damien is a family estate in Gigondas. Les Prés is a white from Clairette: fresh and floral.

salon.name: Salon
salon.line: Single cru, single grape, single vintage: Salon is Chardonnay from Le Mesnil, made only in exceptional years.
salon.tell: Salon makes one wine: a Blanc de Blancs from Le Mesnil, only in the finest years and aged about a decade before release. It is intense, chalky and long, one of the rarest Champagnes. Delamotte is its sister house.

sandeman.name: Sandeman
sandeman.line: A historic Port house, famous for its caped figure logo.
sandeman.tell: Sandeman is a historic Port house guests recognise from the caped figure on its label. Late Bottled Vintage is rich and ready to drink; the Vintage Port is deeper and needs decanting.

sandhi.name: Sandhi
sandhi.line: A Sta. Rita Hills winery making lean, mineral Chardonnay.
sandhi.tell: Sandhi makes taut, mineral Chardonnay in the Sta. Rita Hills. Sanford & Benedict and La Rinconada are famous vineyards, and the Central Coast bottling is the value entry.

sang-des-cailloux.name: Domaine Le Sang des Cailloux
sang-des-cailloux.tell: This is Vacqueyras in the southern Rhône. Un Sang Blanc is a white: round, aromatic and warm.

scarpa.name: Scarpa
scarpa.line: A traditional Piedmont house known for holding its wines back for years before release.
scarpa.tell: Scarpa is a traditional house in Piedmont that often releases wines with age. Podere Barberis is their Barbaresco: fragrant and savoury, with mature notes. Ask the sommelier how the vintage is drinking.

schloss-gobelsburg.name: Schloss Gobelsburg
schloss-gobelsburg.line: A historic Kamptal estate with monastic roots, known for Riesling, Grüner Veltliner and the old-style Tradition wines.
schloss-gobelsburg.tell: Schloss Gobelsburg is a historic estate in the Kamptal. The Heiligenstein Riesling is mineral and fine; Tradition is a Grüner-based wine made in an old-fashioned way, aged long in big casks. Their Brut is crisp and elegant.

schloss-lieser.name: Schloss Lieser
schloss-lieser.line: A Mosel estate run by Thomas Haag.
schloss-lieser.tell: Schloss Lieser is a top Mosel estate. Graacher Himmelreich Kabinett is light and gently sweet, and the list prints the name Leiser.

schlossgut-diel.name: Schlossgut Diel
schlossgut-diel.tell: Diel is a Nahe estate. Burg Layer Trocken is a dry Riesling, crisp and fine.

schrader.name: Schrader Cellars
schrader.line: A Napa label famous for powerful Cabernets from the Beckstoffer To Kalon Vineyard in Oakville, with Pinot Noir under the Boar's View name.
schrader.tell: Schrader is known for Cabernet from Beckstoffer To Kalon, one of Napa's most famous vineyards. The wines are dark, rich and polished; T6 and RBS are named for particular clones and blocks. Boar's View is a Pinot Noir from the far Sonoma Coast. Celebration bottles; decant.

schramsberg.name: Schramsberg
schramsberg.line: A historic Calistoga estate devoted to traditional method sparkling wine.
schramsberg.tell: Schramsberg is a Napa sparkling estate with historic caves. The Blanc de Blancs is crisp and lively, here in half-bottle; J. Schram is the prestige wine, richer and longer.

screaming-eagle.name: Screaming Eagle
screaming-eagle.line: One of Napa's most famous cult estates in Oakville; Second Flight is its second wine.
screaming-eagle.tell: Screaming Eagle is perhaps the most famous cult wine in California, made in tiny amounts in Oakville. Second Flight is its second wine, still rare and costly. A trophy bottle; involve the sommelier.

second-line.name: Second Line Wines
second-line.line: A small Napa label with New Orleans roots; Big Chief Cabernet honours the city's Mardi Gras Indian tradition.
second-line.tell: Second Line is a small Napa label with a New Orleans heart: Big Chief is named for the leaders of the Black Masking Indian tribes who parade at Mardi Gras. It is a dark, full Napa Cabernet. A wonderful story to tell a visitor at Brennan's.

seppeltsfield.name: Seppeltsfield
seppeltsfield.line: A historic Barossa estate, famous for fortified wines, also making reds.
seppeltsfield.tell: Seppeltsfield is a historic Barossa estate, famous for its aged fortified wines. Great Terraced Vineyard is a Grenache, fresh and fragrant; The Nothing is a Shiraz. Ask the sommelier about each.

sequoia-grove.name: Sequoia Grove
sequoia-grove.line: A Rutherford winery making classic Napa Cabernet, including single vineyard bottlings.
sequoia-grove.tell: Sequoia Grove is a Rutherford winery named for its grove of redwoods. Tonella is a single vineyard Cabernet: dark, rich and classic, with Rutherford's dusty earthiness. A solid steak wine.

serafin.name: Domaine Serafin
serafin.line: A Gevrey-Chambertin family domaine known for deep, ripe reds with generous oak and old vines.
serafin.tell: Serafin makes rich, dark and polished Gevrey, with old vines and generous oak. The premier crus Cazetiers and Corbeaux are powerful. A good match for steak.

sesti.name: Sesti
sesti.line: A small Montalcino estate known for elegant, traditional Brunello.
sesti.tell: Sesti is a small family estate in the south of Montalcino. The Brunello is elegant and savoury, made in a traditional way. A lovely choice with beef or lamb; the magnum suits a larger table.

sette-cieli.name: Tenuta Sette Cieli
sette-cieli.line: A hillside estate above Bolgheri making Bordeaux style reds.
sette-cieli.tell: Sette Cieli, meaning seven skies, farms high vineyards above the Bolgheri coast. Indaco, Scipio and Yantra are its reds from Bordeaux grapes: fresh, polished and fine. Ask the sommelier which grape leads each.

shafer.name: Shafer Vineyards
shafer.line: A family estate in the Stags Leap District whose Hillside Select Cabernet is one of the most sought after in Napa.
shafer.tell: Shafer is a Napa family winery on the slopes of the Stags Leap District. Hillside Select is the famous Cabernet: rich, velvety and long. One Point Five is the more approachable Cabernet, Relentless a Syrah blend, and the Merlot is plush and polished.

silver-oak.name: Silver Oak
silver-oak.line: A winery that makes only Cabernet, aged in American oak, in Napa Valley and Alexander Valley versions.
silver-oak.tell: Silver Oak makes Cabernet only, aged in American oak, which gives a soft texture and notes of vanilla and coconut. The Alexander Valley bottling is rounder and friendlier, the Napa Valley one firmer. Guests often ask for it by name.

silvio-giamello.name: Silvio Giamello
silvio-giamello.line: A small family producer in the Langhe hills of Piedmont.
silvio-giamello.tell: Silvio Giamello is a small family producer in the Langhe. Villa Gentiana is a Langhe red; ask the sommelier about the grape and style before you describe it.

sixto.name: Sixto
sixto.tell: Sixto is a Washington Chardonnay label. Moxee is a vineyard, and this bottle has some age.

smith-woodhouse.name: Smith Woodhouse
smith-woodhouse.line: A traditional Port house of the Symington family.
smith-woodhouse.tell: Smith Woodhouse is a traditional Port house, often good value. The Vintage Port is dark, rich and firm. Decant older bottles.

snowden.name: Snowden
snowden.line: A small Napa family label making Cabernet from family vineyards.
snowden.tell: Snowden is a small family producer. Brothers Vineyard is a single site Cabernet: dark and structured. Small production, so ask the sommelier about style and readiness.

soter.name: Soter Vineyards
soter.line: An Oregon estate founded by winemaker Tony Soter, built around the Mineral Springs Ranch vineyard.
soter.tell: Soter farms Mineral Springs Ranch in the Yamhill-Carlton area of the Willamette Valley. The Pinot Noir is dark fruited, silky and polished. Here in half bottle, a good Oregon choice for one or two guests.

spioenkop.name: Spioenkop
spioenkop.tell: Spioenkop is an Elgin estate. Its Chenin Blanc is crisp and mineral, here with some age.

spottswoode.name: Spottswoode
spottswoode.line: A family estate in St. Helena, farmed organically, known for elegant, long lived Cabernet; Lyndenhurst is its second wine.
spottswoode.tell: Spottswoode is a family estate on the western edge of St. Helena, farmed organically. The Estate Cabernet is graceful and fine, more about balance than power, and it ages very well. Lyndenhurst is the more approachable second wine. Several vintages and magnums are on the list.

spring-mountain-vineyard.name: Spring Mountain Vineyard
spring-mountain-vineyard.line: A historic estate on the slopes of Spring Mountain above St. Helena, making long lived mountain Cabernet.
spring-mountain-vineyard.tell: Spring Mountain Vineyard farms steep hillsides above St. Helena. The Cabernet is firm and fresh, with mountain structure and the ability to age. Several vintages are on the list; a classic choice with beef.

st-supery.name: St. Supéry
st-supery.tell: St. Supéry is a Napa estate. Dollarhide is its ranch, and the Sauvignon Blanc is crisp and citrusy.

stadt-krems.name: Weingut Stadt Krems
stadt-krems.line: The winery owned by the town of Krems.
stadt-krems.tell: Stadt Krems is the winery owned by the town of Krems. The Classic Grüner Veltliner is crisp, peppery and good value.

staglin.name: Staglin Family Vineyard
staglin.line: A family estate on the Rutherford Bench, making refined Cabernet from organically farmed vines.
staglin.tell: Staglin is a family estate on the Rutherford Bench, one of Napa's classic Cabernet strips. The wine is refined and long, with dark fruit and Rutherford's earthy note. A strong celebration choice.

stags-leap-wine-cellars.name: Stag's Leap Wine Cellars
stags-leap-wine-cellars.line: The winery whose Cabernet won the 1976 Paris tasting; Cask 23 is its flagship.
stags-leap-wine-cellars.tell: Stag's Leap Wine Cellars made the Cabernet that beat top Bordeaux at the 1976 Paris tasting. Cask 23 is the flagship: silky, perfumed and long. Ne Cede Malis is a rare old vine field blend. A great story for the table.

stargazer.name: Stargazer
stargazer.tell: Stargazer is a small Tasmanian estate. Palisander is a Riesling, crisp and fine.

starmont.name: Starmont
starmont.line: The Carneros label of the family that owns Merryvale, best known for Chardonnay and Pinot Noir, with a Napa red here in half bottle.
starmont.tell: Starmont grew out of Merryvale in St. Helena and now makes its wines at Stanly Ranch in Carneros. It is a dependable, fairly priced label. The Napa Valley red here is a half bottle, a sensible pick for one or two guests; ask the sommelier which grapes are in it.

stein.name: Weingut Stein
stein.tell: Stein makes Mosel Riesling. Palmberg is a site; Trocken on the label means dry, Feinherb means off-dry.

stephane-coquillette.name: Stéphane Coquillette
stephane-coquillette.line: A small family grower in the Côte des Blancs area making approachable Champagne and rosé.
stephane-coquillette.tell: Stéphane Coquillette is a small grower. The Brut is fresh and fruity; Marie Aimer is a rosé. Ask the sommelier about the grapes before going into detail.

stephane-ogier.name: Stéphane Ogier
stephane-ogier.line: A Côte-Rôtie family estate making fine Syrah, with good value wines from the wider Rhône.
stephane-ogier.tell: Ogier is a respected Côte-Rôtie estate. Le Temps est Venu is its Côtes du Rhône, led by Grenache: warm red fruit, a little spice and soft tannin, at an easy price. A friendly red for poultry, pork or a mixed table.

steven-kent.name: Steven Kent Winery
steven-kent.line: A Livermore Valley winery making Bordeaux style reds; Lineage is its flagship blend.
steven-kent.tell: Steven Kent makes wine in the Livermore Valley, east of San Francisco, one of California's oldest wine areas. Lineage is a Cabernet led blend, dark and polished. An interesting alternative to Napa.

stonestreet.name: Stonestreet
stonestreet.line: An estate with high mountain vineyards above the Alexander Valley, making powerful Cabernet and Chardonnay.
stonestreet.tell: Stonestreet farms steep vineyards high above the Alexander Valley. The Cabernet is ripe and powerful, kept fresh by altitude. A strong Sonoma choice for beef.

stony-hill.name: Stony Hill
stony-hill.line: A historic Spring Mountain estate known for lean, long-lived Chardonnay.
stony-hill.tell: Stony Hill is a historic estate on Spring Mountain. Its Chardonnay is lean and crisp, made without new oak, and it ages for years.

stout.name: Stout Vineyards
stout.line: A small California family producer bottling Pinot Noir and Cabernet in limited amounts.
stout.tell: Stout is a small family label. This list carries a Sonoma Coast Pinot Noir and a Napa Valley Cabernet. They are made in small amounts, so ask the sommelier about the style of each before you describe them to a guest.

sylvain-morey.name: Sylvain Morey
sylvain-morey.line: A Burgundian making wine in the Luberon.
sylvain-morey.tell: Sylvain Morey comes from a Burgundy family and makes wine in the Luberon. Panorama is a white, fresh and round, and good value.

sylvaine-alain-normand.name: Sylvaine et Alain Normand
sylvaine-alain-normand.line: A family estate in the Mâconnais making fresh Chardonnay.
sylvaine-alain-normand.tell: The Normands are a family estate in the Mâconnais in southern Burgundy. Their Bourgogne is fresh, gentle Chardonnay at a fair price.

sylvie-esmonin.name: Domaine Sylvie Esmonin
sylvie-esmonin.line: A Gevrey-Chambertin domaine with a parcel of the famous Clos Saint-Jacques, making traditional, whole cluster influenced reds.
sylvie-esmonin.tell: Sylvie Esmonin makes classic, savoury Gevrey with plenty of character. Her Clos Saint-Jacques is from one of Gevrey's most famous premier crus. A good pick for a guest who likes traditional Burgundy.

taittinger.name: Taittinger
taittinger.line: A Reims house with a Chardonnay-rich, light and elegant style; Comtes de Champagne is its Blanc de Blancs.
taittinger.tell: Taittinger favours Chardonnay, so its wines are light, fine and elegant. La Française is the house Brut; Comtes de Champagne, the prestige Blanc de Blancs, is creamy and refined; the Prestige rosé is fresh and fruity.

tara.name: Tara
tara.line: Wines from the Atacama desert in northern Chile, among the driest places on earth.
tara.tell: Tara comes from the Atacama desert, where vines grow near the coast in salty, chalky soil. The Pinot Noir is fresh, light and savoury, quite unlike any other. A great conversation bottle for a curious guest.

tardieu-laurent.name: Tardieu-Laurent
tardieu-laurent.line: A Rhône négociant making rich wines from old vines.
tardieu-laurent.tell: Tardieu-Laurent buys from old vines across the Rhône. This Vieilles Vignes Condrieu is rich and aromatic, with apricot and flowers.

taupenot-merme.name: Domaine Taupenot-Merme
taupenot-merme.line: A Morey-Saint-Denis family domaine with grand cru holdings, here Mazoyères-Chambertin.
taupenot-merme.tell: Taupenot-Merme is a family estate in Morey. Mazoyères-Chambertin is a grand cru next to Charmes, giving a rich, ripe red. Good value for a grand cru.

taylor-fladgate.name: Taylor Fladgate
taylor-fladgate.line: One of the great Port houses; Quinta de Vargellas is its famous estate.
taylor-fladgate.tell: Taylor Fladgate is one of the most famous Port houses. Its Vintage Ports are firm and long lived; Quinta de Vargellas is a single estate Vintage Port, made in years that are not declared. Decant older bottles.

te-mata.name: Te Mata
te-mata.line: A historic Hawke's Bay estate known for Bordeaux style reds.
te-mata.tell: Te Mata is one of New Zealand's oldest estates, in Hawke's Bay. Awatea is a Cabernet Merlot blend: fresh, fine and fragrant. A good value Bordeaux alternative.

tempier.name: Domaine Tempier
tempier.line: The great Bandol estate, famous for red and rosé.
tempier.tell: Tempier is the name in Bandol. Its rosé, Mourvèdre-led, is dry and savoury, a rosé for food rather than the pool.

tenshen.name: Tenshen
tenshen.line: A Santa Barbara County label best known for Rhône style blends.
tenshen.tell: Tenshen makes blends in Santa Barbara County, built mainly on Rhône grapes such as Syrah and Grenache. Expect ripe, spicy, dark fruit. Ask the sommelier for the blend of this bottle.

tenuta-san-guido.name: Tenuta San Guido
tenuta-san-guido.line: The Bolgheri estate that created Sassicaia, the first famous Italian Cabernet; Guidalberto is its younger red.
tenuta-san-guido.tell: Tenuta San Guido made Sassicaia, the wine that began the Super Tuscans and has its own appellation. It is Cabernet led: elegant, fresh and long lived. Guidalberto is the younger, friendlier red. Guests know the name.

terre-nere.name: Tenuta delle Terre Nere
terre-nere.line: A leading Etna estate known for single contrada reds, including a wine from ungrafted old vines.
terre-nere.tell: Terre Nere is a top Etna estate. Calderara Sottana and Moganazzi are single contrade; Prephylloxera comes from very old vines that predate phylloxera. Fragrant, mineral reds often compared to Burgundy.

terroir-al-limit.name: Terroir al Límit
terroir-al-limit.tell: Terroir al Límit is a Priorat estate. Historic White is a Muscat of Alexandria, aromatic and dry in style; ask the sommelier to confirm.

tertre-roteboeuf.name: Tertre Rôtebœuf
tertre-roteboeuf.line: A small, cult Saint-Émilion estate of François Mitjavile, making rich, exotic, much admired wine.
tertre-roteboeuf.tell: Tertre Rôtebœuf is a cult Saint-Émilion from François Mitjavile. Rich, exotic and fine. A special bottle.

teutonic.name: Teutonic Wine Co.
teutonic.line: An Oregon winery inspired by German wines.
teutonic.tell: Teutonic is an Oregon winery inspired by German wines. Candied Mushroom is a Riesling; ask the sommelier how dry it is.

textbook.name: Textbook
textbook.line: A Napa label making Cabernet that aims for restraint, with Mise en Place from two Oakville sites.
textbook.tell: Textbook makes Napa Cabernet in a restrained style. Mise en Place, French for everything in its place, comes from two Oakville vineyards: polished and fine. The Reserve is the step up. A kitchen word a guest at Brennan's will enjoy.

the-hilt.name: The Hilt
the-hilt.region: Sta. Rita Hills, Santa Barbara County
the-hilt.line: A Sta. Rita Hills estate making cool climate Pinot Noir and Chardonnay from vineyards swept by Pacific wind.
the-hilt.tell: The Hilt farms in the Sta. Rita Hills, where the ocean wind keeps the grapes cool. The Pinot Noir is bright and fine, with red fruit, spice and fresh acidity. A strong choice for a guest who likes elegant Pinot with salmon or duck.

the-mascot.name: The Mascot
the-mascot.line: A Cabernet from the Harlan family, made from the younger vines of their estates.
the-mascot.tell: The Mascot comes from the family behind Harlan Estate and BOND, made from younger vines on their properties. It is dark, polished and approachable sooner. The best value way to the Harlan family's style.

the-paring.name: The Paring
the-paring.tell: The Paring is a Santa Barbara label. This Chardonnay is fresh and fruity, an easy, good-value white.

the-prisoner.name: The Prisoner
the-prisoner.line: A well known Napa red blend built on Zinfandel, ripe and bold.
the-prisoner.tell: The Prisoner is a famous Napa red blend led by Zinfandel with other dark grapes. It is ripe, bold and jammy, with spice and vanilla. Guests often ask for it; good with richer meats.

theopetra.name: Theopetra Estate
theopetra.line: A family estate in Meteora, central Greece, that revived the vineyards of the area.
theopetra.tell: Theopetra is a family estate below the rock pillars of Meteora in central Greece. 24 is named for its ageing: twenty four months in barrel and the same in bottle. A blend of Syrah, Cabernet and the local Limniona: dark berries, pepper and silky tannin.

thibault-liger-belair.name: Domaine Thibault Liger-Belair
thibault-liger-belair.line: A Nuits-Saint-Georges domaine farmed biodynamically, making fresh, precise reds; Les Saints-Georges is its flagship premier cru.
thibault-liger-belair.tell: Thibault Liger-Belair makes vibrant, fragrant wines. Les Saints-Georges is Nuits' most famous premier cru. A strong recommendation with beef or game.

thierry-allemand.name: Thierry Allemand
thierry-allemand.line: A cult Cornas grower making tiny amounts of pure, deep Syrah from Chaillot and Reynard.
thierry-allemand.tell: Allemand is a cult name in Cornas. Les Chaillot is the fresher one; Reynard is deeper. Rare bottles; decant.

thierry-pillot.name: Thierry Pillot
thierry-pillot.line: The small négoce label of Thierry Pillot of Domaine Paul Pillot, started in 2017.
thierry-pillot.tell: Thierry Pillot makes these from bought-in grapes alongside his family domaine. Les Castets is a Saint-Aubin premier cru, Les Poruzots a Meursault premier cru; there are grand crus too.

thorn-clarke.name: Thorn-Clarke
thorn-clarke.line: A Barossa family winery making good value Shiraz.
thorn-clarke.tell: Thorn-Clarke is a family winery in the Barossa. Shotfire Ridge Shiraz is ripe, dark and smooth. A great value Australian red for steak.

thymiopoulos.name: Thymiopoulos
thymiopoulos.line: A leading Naoussa grower who made Xinomavro fresh and approachable.
thymiopoulos.tell: Thymiopoulos is the leading young name in Naoussa, northern Greece. Xinomavro is a firm, fragrant grape often compared to Nebbiolo. Young Vines is bright and juicy, with cherry and tomato leaf. A great value red for a curious guest.

timo-mayer.name: Timo Mayer
timo-mayer.line: A Yarra Valley winemaker known for fresh, whole bunch, natural minded reds.
timo-mayer.tell: Timo Mayer makes wine in the Yarra Valley with whole bunches and a light hand. His Syrah is fresh, peppery and fragrant, nothing like big Barossa Shiraz. A great pick for a Northern Rhône lover.

tolaini.name: Tolaini
tolaini.line: An estate at the southern end of Chianti Classico making Gran Selezione and the Picconero blend.
tolaini.tell: Tolaini is an estate in the south of Chianti Classico. The Gran Selezione is firm, polished Sangiovese, and Picconero is a richer Bordeaux style blend. Both suit beef and lamb.

tollot-beaut.name: Domaine Tollot-Beaut
tollot-beaut.line: A Chorey-lès-Beaune family domaine making ripe, generous reds from Chorey, Savigny, Beaune, Aloxe-Corton and Corton.
tollot-beaut.tell: Tollot-Beaut is a reliable family estate known for ripe, fruity, crowd pleasing reds. Chorey-lès-Beaune is one of the best values on the list, and the Corton Bressandes is a step up. Safe recommendations.

torbreck.name: Torbreck
torbreck.line: A Barossa estate known for old vine Shiraz and Rhône grapes.
torbreck.tell: Torbreck makes rich Barossa wine from old vines. The Factor is a Shiraz: dense, dark and spicy, with great depth. For a guest who loves big Australian red.

tour-du-bon.name: Domaine de la Tour du Bon
tour-du-bon.line: A Bandol domaine making Mourvèdre led reds.
tour-du-bon.tell: Tour du Bon is a Bandol estate. Saint Ferréol is a Mourvèdre led red. Savoury and dark.

travaglini.name: Travaglini
travaglini.line: The leading estate of Gattinara in northern Piedmont, recognisable by its curved bottle.
travaglini.tell: Travaglini is the best known name in Gattinara, northern Piedmont, and its bottle has a curved shape guests remember. The Riserva is Nebbiolo: fragrant, savoury and firm, with age. A good value Nebbiolo for beef or game.

trefethen.name: Trefethen
trefethen.line: A family estate in the cool Oak Knoll District of southern Napa, making balanced Cabernet, blends and a Malbec blend.
trefethen.tell: Trefethen is a family estate in Oak Knoll, one of Napa's cooler corners, so the reds stay fresh. The Estate Cabernet is balanced and food friendly; Halo is the top Cabernet; Dragon's Tooth is a dark, spicy Malbec blend and Eshcol a Bordeaux style blend.

trevallon.name: Domaine de Trévallon
trevallon.line: A celebrated Provence estate in the Alpilles.
trevallon.tell: Trévallon is a celebrated estate in the Alpilles of Provence. Its white is rich and aromatic, and offered in several vintages.

tribaut-schloesser.name: Tribaut-Schloesser
tribaut-schloesser.line: A family house in the Marne valley making approachable, fruit-forward Champagne.
tribaut-schloesser.tell: Tribaut-Schloesser is a family house in the Marne valley. Origine is a fruity, gentle blend, and here it comes as a half-bottle, the right size for one or two guests.

trimbach.name: Trimbach
trimbach.line: A historic Ribeauvillé house famous for dry, firm, long-lived Riesling, above all Clos Ste Hune.
trimbach.tell: Trimbach makes dry, firm Alsace whites. Clos Ste Hune is one of the world's great Rieslings, from a tiny plot; Cuvée Frédéric Emile is its other top Riesling; Vendanges Tardives means late harvest and is sweeter.

turnbull.name: Turnbull Wine Cellars
turnbull.line: An Oakville winery making classic Napa Cabernet from estate vineyards.
turnbull.tell: Turnbull farms vineyards in Oakville and beyond. Black Label is its top Cabernet: rich, dark and structured. A classic Napa steak wine.

tyrrells.name: Tyrrell's
tyrrells.line: A Hunter Valley family house famous for Semillon and medium bodied Shiraz.
tyrrells.tell: Tyrrell's is a family house in the Hunter Valley. Vat 9 is its Shiraz, labelled Syrah here: medium bodied, earthy and fresh, very different from the Barossa. Ages beautifully.

ulysses.name: Ulysses
ulysses.line: Christian Moueix's Oakville estate, making a refined Cabernet blend.
ulysses.tell: Ulysses is the Oakville estate of Christian Moueix, of Pomerol fame and Dominus. The wine is fine and balanced, with Bordeaux like restraint. A thoughtful pick for a guest who loves classic Bordeaux.

under-the-wire.name: Under the Wire
under-the-wire.line: A small California project bottling single vineyard sparkling wines, from the team at Bedrock Wine Co.
under-the-wire.tell: Under the Wire makes single vineyard sparkling wine in tiny lots. Alder Springs is a cool, high Mendocino site; the wine is an Extra Brut, dry and focused.

val-di-suga.name: Val di Suga
val-di-suga.line: A Montalcino estate with vineyards in different parts of the zone; Vigna del Lago is a single vineyard Brunello.
val-di-suga.tell: Val di Suga makes Brunello from several corners of Montalcino. Vigna del Lago is a single vineyard bottling: deeper and more structured than the standard. Good with beef.

valdespino.name: Valdespino
valdespino.line: A historic Jerez Sherry house known for old, very long aged wines.
valdespino.tell: Valdespino is one of the oldest Sherry houses in Jerez. VOS Solera 1842 is a very old Sherry from Palomino: deep, nutty and complex. Ask the sommelier how sweet it is before you pour; in 500 ml bottles.

valenciso.name: Valenciso
valenciso.line: A small Rioja estate making one elegant Reserva.
valenciso.tell: Valenciso is a small Rioja estate that focuses on a single Reserva: fresh, fine Tempranillo with gentle oak. A modern classic for lamb or pork.

varnier-fanniere.name: Varnier-Fannière
varnier-fanniere.line: A small grower in Avize making fine grand cru Chardonnay Champagne.
varnier-fanniere.tell: Varnier-Fannière is a small family estate in Avize, a grand cru village for Chardonnay. Their Brut is crisp, fine and chalky, a true grower wine at a fair price.

vatan.name: Edmond et Anne Vatan
