vatan.line: A tiny, revered Chavignol estate whose Clos la Néore is one of Sancerre's most sought-after wines.
vatan.tell: Vatan is tiny and revered. Clos la Néore is Sancerre of great depth, made traditionally, with more texture and age-worthiness than most. Here in magnum, a rare find.

vega-sicilia.name: Vega Sicilia
vega-sicilia.line: Spain's most famous estate, in Ribera del Duero; Unico is its legendary long aged red.
vega-sicilia.tell: Vega Sicilia is Spain's most famous wine. Unico is aged for years before release: complex, silky and very long lived. Reserva Especial blends several vintages, and Valbuena 5° is younger. Celebration bottles; involve the sommelier.

verite.name: Vérité
verite.line: A Sonoma estate making three Bordeaux style blends: La Muse led by Merlot, La Joie by Cabernet and Le Désir by Cabernet Franc.
verite.tell: Vérité makes Bordeaux style wine from Sonoma hillsides. La Muse is Merlot led and plush, La Joie Cabernet led and firm, Le Désir Cabernet Franc led and fragrant. Rare and celebrated; several vintages are listed, and a good choice for a Bordeaux collector.

veuve-clicquot.name: Veuve Clicquot
veuve-clicquot.line: A Reims house led by Pinot Noir, named for the widow who ran it in the early 1800s; Yellow Label is its signature.
veuve-clicquot.tell: Veuve Clicquot is the orange label everyone knows, a Pinot Noir-led, round and fruity Brut. La Grande Dame, named for Madame Clicquot, is the prestige vintage, finer and longer; its rosé is a true celebration bottle.

veuve-fourny.name: Veuve Fourny & Fils
veuve-fourny.line: A family house in Vertus run by two brothers, making crisp, low-dosage premier cru Chardonnay.
veuve-fourny.tell: Veuve Fourny is a family house in Vertus. The wines are dry and chalky; Monts de Vertus is a single site; the half-bottles suit one or two guests; Vinothèque MV2000 is a perpetual-reserve blend in magnum.

veyder-malberg.name: Peter Veyder-Malberg
veyder-malberg.line: A small Wachau grower farming steep terraces.
veyder-malberg.tell: Veyder-Malberg farms steep terraces in the Wachau. Elsarner Brandstatt and Wachauer 2B are dry Rieslings, pure and mineral.

vieille-julienne.name: Domaine de la Vieille Julienne
vieille-julienne.line: A Châteauneuf-du-Pape domaine farming biodynamically, making fine, fragrant Grenache.
vieille-julienne.tell: Vieille Julienne makes fine, fragrant Châteauneuf. Les Trois Sources and the Réservé are their bottlings. A strong pick for lamb.

vietti.name: Vietti
vietti.line: A leading Barolo estate in Castiglione Falletto, bottling famous single vineyards.
vietti.tell: Vietti is one of Barolo's best known estates. Ravera, Lazzarito and Cerequio are single vineyards: Ravera fresh and floral, Lazzarito firm, Cerequio silky. Masseria is a Barbaresco. Classic, polished Nebbiolo.

vieux-chateau-certan.name: Vieux Château Certan
vieux-chateau-certan.line: A Pomerol estate run by the Thienpont family, with more Cabernet Franc than most, making fine, fragrant wine.
vieux-chateau-certan.tell: Vieux Château Certan, run by the Thienpont family, is one of Pomerol's great names. The half bottle is a lovely treat for two.

vieux-telegraphe.name: Domaine du Vieux Télégraphe
vieux-telegraphe.line: The Brunier family's Châteauneuf-du-Pape domaine on the stony La Crau plateau, making powerful, long lived reds.
vieux-telegraphe.tell: Vieux Télégraphe is one of Châteauneuf's best known names. La Crau is their stony plateau vineyard. Deep, spicy and long lived.

vignai-da-duline.name: Vignai da Duline
vignai-da-duline.tell: Vignai da Duline is a small Friuli estate. Giallado is a Tocai Giallo white, here in magnum.

vignerons-de-buxy.name: Les Vignerons Réunis à Buxy
vignerons-de-buxy.line: The cooperative of Buxy, making Montagny.
vignerons-de-buxy.tell: This is the Buxy cooperative in the Côte Chalonnaise. The Montagny premier cru is crisp, fresh white Burgundy at a fair price.

vigneti-vecchio.name: Vigneti Vecchio
vigneti-vecchio.line: A small Etna estate working very old vines on the north slope of the volcano.
vigneti-vecchio.tell: Vigneti Vecchio is a small Etna family estate working old vines in volcanic sand. Sciare Vive is mostly Nerello Mascalese with a little of other local grapes: medium bodied, silky and peppery. A fresh, savoury red for poultry or pork.

villa-di-geggiano.name: Villa di Geggiano
villa-di-geggiano.line: A historic villa estate near Siena making traditional Chianti Classico.
villa-di-geggiano.tell: Villa di Geggiano is an old family villa near Siena. The Chianti Classico Riserva is traditional: savoury Sangiovese with cherry, leather and herbs. Several vintages and a magnum are on the list.

vina-cobos.name: Viña Cobos
vina-cobos.line: The Mendoza winery founded by Paul Hobbs, making rich, single vineyard Malbec.
vina-cobos.tell: Viña Cobos was founded by California winemaker Paul Hobbs. Chañares Estate and Marchiori Vineyard are single vineyard Malbecs: rich, dark and polished. Big reds for steak.

vina-maquis.name: Viña Maquis
vina-maquis.line: A family estate in Colchagua making fresh Cabernet and Carmenère.
vina-maquis.tell: Maquis is a family estate in Colchagua, south of Santiago. The Cabernet is fresh and dark fruited; the Carmenère, Chile's signature grape, is supple, with red pepper and spice. Good value reds.

vincent-et-sophie-morey.name: Vincent et Sophie Morey
vincent-et-sophie-morey.line: A Chassagne-Montrachet family estate making clean, fresh whites and reds.
vincent-et-sophie-morey.tell: Vincent and Sophie Morey make wine in Chassagne-Montrachet. Les Embrazées is a Chassagne premier cru: fresh and generous, with citrus, white flowers and a touch of hazelnut. Here in magnum, a fine bottle for a table eating fish or crab.

vincent-girardin.name: Domaine Vincent Girardin
vincent-girardin.line: A Meursault house making whites across the Côte de Beaune.
vincent-girardin.tell: Vincent Girardin makes whites across the Côte de Beaune. Corton-Charlemagne is a grand cru, Sous le Château a Saint-Romain, and the Puligny Vieilles Vignes comes from old vines.

vincent-sophie-morey.name: Vincent et Sophie Morey
vincent-sophie-morey.tell: Vincent and Sophie Morey make Chassagne-Montrachet. Les Embrazées is a premier cru, here in magnum for a table to share.

viuva-gomes.name: Viúva Gomes
viuva-gomes.line: A historic producer in Colares, where vines grow in sand by the Atlantic.
viuva-gomes.tell: Viúva Gomes makes wine in Colares, near Lisbon, where vines grow in deep sand by the ocean. Ramisco is the local red grape: firm, high in acid and long lived. A rare, historic wine; ask the sommelier how it is drinking.

vodopivec.name: Vodopivec
vodopivec.line: A Carso grower devoted to Vitovska.
vodopivec.tell: Vodopivec is devoted to Vitovska, a grape of the Carso near Trieste. This mature bottle is textured and savoury.

vokel.name: Vokel Cellars
vokel.line: A small producer of Chardonnay and Pinot Noir.
vokel.tell: Vokel Cellars is a small producer focused on Chardonnay and Pinot Noir. Heintz Vineyard is a well-known Sonoma Coast site. Ask the sommelier about the style before you describe it.

von-buhl.name: Reichsrat von Buhl
von-buhl.tell: Von Buhl is a historic Pfalz estate. Forster Jesuitengarten is a famous site, and this bottle has some age.

von-winning.name: Von Winning
von-winning.tell: Von Winning is a Pfalz estate. Kirchenstück and Ungeheuer are dry grand cru Rieslings, and Lime Rift is a Sauvignon Blanc.

vougeraie.name: Domaine de la Vougeraie
vougeraie.line: A biodynamic Côte de Nuits estate whose Le Clos Blanc de Vougeot is a rare white in red country.
vougeraie.tell: Vougeraie is a biodynamic estate in the Côte de Nuits. Le Clos Blanc de Vougeot is a rare white premier cru in red wine country, offered in magnum and double magnum, and there is a white Beaune too.

waris-larmandier.name: Waris-Larmandier
waris-larmandier.line: A family grower in the Côte des Blancs making precise, low-dosage grand cru Champagne.
waris-larmandier.tell: Waris-Larmandier is a small family estate in the Côte des Blancs. Les Bauves is a single site, Brut Nature, bone-dry and chalky; L'Instant de Passions is a rosé. Ask the sommelier which grand cru village it comes from.

warres.name: Warre's
warres.line: One of the oldest British Port houses, part of the Symington family.
warres.tell: Warre's is one of the oldest Port houses. The Vintage Port is fragrant and elegant, with dark fruit. Decant older bottles; lovely with chocolate or cheese.

weinbach.name: Domaine Weinbach
weinbach.line: A celebrated family estate in Kaysersberg, around the walled Clos des Capucins, making rich, pure whites.
weinbach.tell: Weinbach is one of Alsace's great family estates. Clos des Capucins is the walled vineyard by the house; Schlossberg and Mambourg are grand crus; Cuvée Théo and Sainte Catherine are named cuvées. Aromatic and generous.

weiser-kunstler.name: Weiser-Künstler
weiser-kunstler.tell: Weiser-Künstler is a small Mosel estate. Ellergrub is a steep slate site; ask the sommelier how dry it is.

wiederstein.name: Winzerin Wiederstein
wiederstein.line: A small estate in Carnuntum, east of Vienna, making Blaufränkisch and other Austrian wines.
wiederstein.tell: Wiederstein is a small estate in Carnuntum, between Vienna and the Slovak border. Wei Damals is Blaufränkisch: fresh, juicy and peppery. A lighter red for poultry or pork.

willamette-valley-vineyards.name: Willamette Valley Vineyards
willamette-valley-vineyards.tell: Willamette Valley Vineyards is an Oregon winery. Its Pinot Gris is fresh and fruity, good value.

william-downie.name: William Downie
william-downie.line: An Australian winemaker known for light, pure, low intervention Pinot Noir from Victoria.
william-downie.tell: Bill Downie makes Pinot Noir in Victoria with very little intervention, aiming for lightness and perfume rather than power. Cathedral is fresh, bright and red fruited, a fun, gentle red that drinks beautifully slightly cool. Steer a Burgundy lover on a budget here.

william-fevre.name: Domaine William Fèvre
william-fevre.line: A major Chablis estate with a large holding of grand crus, making precise, mineral wines.
william-fevre.tell: William Fèvre owns a big share of Chablis's grand crus. The wines are crisp and stony with gentle oak. Bougros Côte Bouguerots is a steep part of Bougros; Preuses and Valmur are grand crus too.

wind-gap.name: Wind Gap
wind-gap.tell: Wind Gap is a California winery. Yuen is a Chardonnay, here from an older vintage, so ask the sommelier how it is drinking.

xavier-monnot.name: Xavier Monnot
xavier-monnot.line: A Meursault estate making taut whites.
xavier-monnot.tell: Xavier Monnot is a Meursault estate with taut whites. Le Limozin is a village site beside the premier crus.

yannick-amirault.name: Yannick Amirault
yannick-amirault.line: A leading Bourgueil grower farming organically, making deep, fine Cabernet Franc from named sites.
yannick-amirault.tell: Amirault is one of the top names in Bourgueil. His Cabernet Franc is deep and fine. A smart pick for a guest who likes Bordeaux but wants something lighter.

zena-crown.name: Zena Crown
zena-crown.line: An Eola-Amity Hills vineyard estate making structured Pinot Noir from its own blocks.
zena-crown.tell: Zena Crown farms a single hillside estate in the Eola-Amity Hills. The Sum is the estate blend and Conifer a block selection: dark fruited, firm and fresh Pinot Noir. Good with duck, pork or mushrooms.

zind-humbrecht.name: Zind-Humbrecht
zind-humbrecht.line: A great biodynamic estate in Turckheim making rich, powerful whites.
zind-humbrecht.tell: Zind-Humbrecht is one of Alsace's leaders, with rich, powerful whites. Goldert is a grand cru, and this one is Muscat, aromatic and rich.

zuccardi.name: Zuccardi
zuccardi.line: A family winery in the Uco Valley known for fresh, terroir focused Malbec.
zuccardi.tell: Zuccardi is a family estate in the high Uco Valley. Piedra Infinita comes from stony soils in Paraje Altamira: fresh, mineral and fine, a lighter, more precise Malbec. A great pick for a guest who thinks Malbec is always heavy.

By the Glass.title: By the glass
By the Glass.line: Fourteen wines poured by the glass, priced per glass: sparkling, white, rosé and red, two of them through Coravin. Ask what the guest usually drinks and how hungry they are, then offer one choice and one step up.

Selections Under $100.title: Selections under $100
Selections Under $100.line: The list's short page of bottles under $100, from sparkling to red. Start here for a guest who wants value: ask white or red, light or full, and point to one bottle in each.

Half-bottles.title: Half-bottles
Half-bottles.line: 375 ml bottles, about two and a half glasses each: right for one or two guests or for a change of wine between courses. Ask how many are drinking and which course it is for.

Large Formats.title: Large formats
Large Formats.line: Magnums and bigger, from 1.5 litres to a 15 litre Nebuchadnezzar. A magnum is two bottles; larger sizes need planning with the sommelier. Ask how many are at the table and what they are celebrating.

Sustainable Selections.title: Sustainable selections
Sustainable Selections.line: Bottles from organic, biodynamic or natural growers, as the list marks each one. Questions about how a wine is made go to the sommelier; steer by style as with any other wine.

Champagne.title: Champagne
Champagne.line: The deepest part of the list: famous houses and grower Champagnes, from about $50 to rare large formats. Ask the occasion, the budget and whether the guest likes crisp and light or rich and toasty.

International ~ Sparkling.title: Sparkling beyond Champagne
International ~ Sparkling.line: Traditional method bubbles from England, Austria, Italy, Portugal, Tasmania, the Jura and the United States, mostly under $250. Offer it to the guest who wants quality bubbles without Champagne prices, or something new.

France ~ Loire ~ White.title: Loire whites
France ~ Loire ~ White.line: Chenin Blanc, Sauvignon Blanc and Muscadet from France's longest river: mostly crisp, from about $50, with rare Savennières and Clos Rougeard at the top. Ask how dry the guest likes it; some Vouvray is sweet.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White.title: White Burgundy
France ~ Burgundy ~ White.line: The heart of the list: Chardonnay from Chablis to the Mâconnais, nearly 400 bottles from about $45 to five figures. Ask crisp and stony (Chablis) or rich and nutty (Meursault, Puligny, Chassagne), then the budget.

France ~ Alsace ~ White.title: Alsace whites
France ~ Alsace ~ White.line: Riesling, Pinot Gris, Gewürztraminer and more from Trimbach, Weinbach, Boxler and Zind-Humbrecht. Aromatic and food-friendly with spice, $50 to $985. Ask how dry the guest likes it; some carry sweetness.

France ~ Rhône~ White.title: Rhône whites
France ~ Rhône~ White.line: Viognier from Condrieu, Marsanne from Hermitage and round southern blends, $80 to $550. Rich, textured whites for crab, shrimp and spiced dishes; ask whether the guest wants floral or nutty.

France ~ Other ~ White.title: Other French whites
France ~ Other ~ White.line: Bordeaux, the Jura, Provence, Jurançon and the Languedoc, from $55 to Haut-Brion. Ask what the guest likes; this corner rewards curiosity.

Austria & Hungary.title: Austria and Hungary
Austria & Hungary.line: Grüner Veltliner and dry Riesling from the Wachau, Kamptal and Kremstal, plus Tokaj Furmint, $50 to $690. Crisp, peppery and mineral; ideal with seafood and vegetables.

Germany ~ White.title: German whites
Germany ~ White.line: Mostly Riesling from the Mosel, Rheingau, Rheinhessen, Nahe and Pfalz, $45 to $950. Ask dry or a touch sweet: Trocken and GG are dry, Kabinett, Spätlese and Auslese are usually sweeter.

Italy & Greece ~ White.title: Italian and Greek whites
Italy & Greece ~ White.line: From Alto Adige to Santorini: crisp, saline, textured whites, mostly under $175. Ask whether the guest wants fresh and crisp or textured and characterful.

Spain ~ White.title: Spanish whites
Spain ~ White.line: Albariño from Rías Baixas, Godello from Bierzo, Canary Island Listán Blanco and aged white Rioja, $65 to $195. Crisp, saline and food-friendly; López de Heredia is the outlier, aged and nutty.

United States ~ Chardonnay.title: American Chardonnay
United States ~ Chardonnay.line: California, Oregon and Washington Chardonnay, $30 to $950, from lean and mineral to rich and creamy. Ask buttery or crisp first, then point to Napa for richness, the coast for freshness.

United States ~ Sauvignon Blanc.title: American Sauvignon Blanc
United States ~ Sauvignon Blanc.line: Crisp, citrusy California and Oregon Sauvignon Blanc, mostly under $100. Easy, fresh picks for salads, fish and lighter dishes.

United States ~ Other ~ White.title: Other American whites
United States ~ Other ~ White.line: Viognier, Riesling, Ribolla, Picpoul and blends from California, Oregon and New York, $45 to $320. For a guest who wants something different from Chardonnay.

International ~ White.title: Whites from the southern hemisphere
International ~ White.line: Argentina, Australia, Chile, New Zealand and South Africa: Chardonnay, Chenin Blanc, Riesling and Semillon, $50 to $560. Ask whether the guest wants classic Chardonnay or something new.

Rosé.title: Rosé
Rosé.line: Fifteen bottles, mostly dry Provence and Sancerre rosé, plus Bandol and Pascal Cotat for depth, $45 to $270. Ask light and crisp or something with more body for food.

France ~ Loire ~ Red.title: Loire reds
France ~ Loire ~ Red.line: Mostly Cabernet Franc from Saumur, Chinon and Bourgueil: fresh, red fruited and a little herbal, lighter than Bordeaux. Good value, good with poultry and pork, and lovely slightly cool. Clos Rougeard is the rare treasure.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red.title: Red Burgundy
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red.line: Pinot Noir from the Côte d'Or and its neighbours, with Gamay from Beaujolais at the end. Ask whether the guest wants light and fragrant or deep and firm, and the budget, before you name a village.

France ~ Bordeaux ~ Red.title: Red Bordeaux
France ~ Bordeaux ~ Red.line: Left Bank Cabernet from Saint-Estèphe, Pauillac, Saint-Julien, Margaux and Graves; Right Bank Merlot from Pomerol and Saint-Émilion. Ask the budget and whether the guest wants firm and classic or soft and plush.

Austria, Germany & Lebanon ~ Red.title: Austria, Germany and Lebanon reds
Austria, Germany & Lebanon ~ Red.line: Austrian Blaufränkisch and Pinot Noir, German Pinot Noir from the Pfalz and Château Musar from Lebanon. Fresh, peppery reds, with Musar as the spicy, mature exception.

France ~ Rhone ~ Red.title: Rhône reds
France ~ Rhone ~ Red.line: North: peppery Syrah from Côte-Rôtie, Hermitage, Cornas and Saint-Joseph. South: warm, spicy Grenache blends from Châteauneuf-du-Pape and Gigondas. Ask whether the guest likes savoury and firm or ripe and generous.

France ~ Other ~ Red.title: Other French reds
France ~ Other ~ Red.line: The rest of France: Provence Bandol and Trévallon, the Languedoc, light Jura and Savoie reds, Cahors Malbec, Corsica and rare still reds from Champagne. Ask what the guest usually drinks and steer by weight.

United States ~ Pinot Noir.title: American Pinot Noir
United States ~ Pinot Noir.line: Pinot Noir from Mendocino, Sonoma, Santa Barbara, the Central Coast and Oregon. Ask whether the guest wants fresh and savoury or ripe and plush, then steer to Oregon or Kosta Browne style.

United States ~ Cabernet Sauvignon.title: American Cabernet Sauvignon
United States ~ Cabernet Sauvignon.line: The deepest page of American red: Napa above all, with Sonoma, the Central Coast and Washington. Ask the budget and whether the guest wants plush and ripe or firm and classic.

United States ~ Other ~ Red.title: Other American reds
United States ~ Other ~ Red.line: Syrah, Merlot, Zinfandel, Cabernet Franc, Petite Sirah and blends. Ask what the guest usually loves, then match: Merlot for plush, Syrah for peppery, Zinfandel for spicy and jammy.

Italy ~ Red.title: Italian reds
Italy ~ Red.line: Piedmont Nebbiolo, Veneto Amarone, Tuscan Sangiovese and Super Tuscans, and reds from the south and Sicily. Ask the region the guest likes, or light and fragrant versus rich and dark.

Spain ~ Red.title: Spanish reds
Spain ~ Red.line: From Atlantic Galicia to Rioja, Priorat, Ribera del Duero, Gredos and the Canary Islands. Ask classic and oak aged or fresh and modern, then steer to Rioja or to Gredos and Galicia.

International - Red.title: International reds
International - Red.line: Reds from Greece, Portugal, Argentina, Chile, South Africa, Australia and New Zealand. Ask which grape the guest likes, then find it here: Malbec, Shiraz, Pinot Noir or Cabernet.

Selections from our Birth Year.title: Selections from our birth year
Selections from our Birth Year.line: Four great 1946 Bordeaux, from the year the restaurant was born: Latour, Trotanoy, Canon and Figeac. Rare, mature bottles for an anniversary or milestone; involve the sommelier for vintage, price and decanting.

Dessert Wines.title: Dessert wines
Dessert Wines.line: Sweet wines by the bottle and half bottle, from Sauternes to Vin Santo and icewine. Ask what the guest is eating: lighter fruit desserts like fresh wines, caramel and nuts like richer ones.

Fortified Wines.title: Fortified wines
Fortified Wines.line: Port, Madeira, Sherry and Rivesaltes. Ask dry or sweet: Manzanilla is dry and salty, Madeira tangy, Port rich and sweet. Vintage Ports need decanting.

By the Glass ~ Sparkling.title: Sparkling by the glass
By the Glass ~ Sparkling.line: Four bubbles: Brennan's Essential Champagne, an Oregon Brut, an Alsace Crémant rosé and Rare 2012 through Coravin. Ask whether it is a celebration; Rare is the splurge glass, Argyle the gentlest price.

By the Glass ~ White.title: White by the glass
By the Glass ~ White.line: Five whites from crisp to rich: Mosel Riesling, Albariño and Loire Sauvignon on the fresh side, California Chardonnay and Leflaive's Mâcon-Verzé through Coravin on the rounder side. Ask crisp or creamy first.

By the Glass ~ Rosé.title: Rosé by the glass
By the Glass ~ Rosé.line: One rosé, Minuty Prestige from Provence: pale, dry and delicate. Offer it to the guest who wants something light that still stands up to Creole flavours.

By the Glass ~ Red.title: Red by the glass
By the Glass ~ Red.line: Four reds from light to bold: Bourgogne Pinot Noir, a southern Rhône Grenache, a Bordeaux Supérieur and Inglenook Rubicon. Ask light or full; Rubicon is the splurge glass for steak.

Selections Under $100 ~ Sparkling.title: Sparkling under $100
Selections Under $100 ~ Sparkling.line: Trento, English and Loire sparkling plus a Lambrusco: Champagne method bubbles at a friendly price, and a chilled sparkling red for the curious. Ask whether the guest wants dry and crisp or fruity.

Selections Under $100 ~ Sauvignon Blanc.title: Sauvignon Blanc under $100
Selections Under $100 ~ Sauvignon Blanc.line: A white Graves and an Adelaide Hills Sauvignon Blanc: crisp, citrusy whites for oysters, salads and fish. Ask whether the guest likes zesty or rounder.

Selections Under $100 ~ Chardonnay.title: Chardonnay under $100
Selections Under $100 ~ Chardonnay.line: Value Chardonnay from Burgundy, Oregon, California and Mendoza, with an Aligoté. Ask whether the guest wants crisp and unoaked or round and creamy, then pick Burgundy or California.

Selections Under $100 ~ Other White Vari.title: Other whites under $100
Selections Under $100 ~ Other White Vari.line: Arneis, Pinot Grigio, Grüner Veltliner, Riesling, an Alsace blend and southern French bottles: aromatic, fresh and food friendly. Ask what the guest usually drinks and steer by aroma and weight.

Selections Under $100 ~ Rosé.title: Rosé under $100
Selections Under $100 ~ Rosé.line: Two dry rosés, from the south of France and Santa Barbara: pale, crisp and good with almost anything on the menu. Easy to recommend to a table that cannot agree.

Selections Under $100 ~ Pinot Noir.title: Pinot Noir under $100
Selections Under $100 ~ Pinot Noir.line: Bourgogne, Sonoma Coast and Victoria Pinot Noir: light to medium reds for fish, poultry and pork. Ask whether the guest likes earthy and fresh or ripe and fruity.

Selections Under $100 ~ Cabernet Sauvign.title: Cabernet under $100
Selections Under $100 ~ Cabernet Sauvign.line: Napa, Bordeaux and Maipo Cabernet at friendly prices: dark, firm reds for beef. Duckhorn and Chappellet are names guests know; Massereau is mature Bordeaux.

Selections Under $100 ~ Other Red Variet.title: Other reds under $100
Selections Under $100 ~ Other Red Variet.line: Montepulciano, Malbec, Gamay, Nebbiolo, Petit Verdot, Beaujolais and Grenache: a tour of good value reds. Ask light or full, then pick Gamay and Grenache for light, Malbec and Petit Verdot for full.

Half-bottles ~ Champagne & Sparkling.title: Sparkling half-bottles
Half-bottles ~ Champagne & Sparkling.line: Krug, Laurent-Perrier, Feuillatte, Veuve Fourny, Ferrari and Schramsberg in half bottle. A perfect toast for two; the Laurent-Perrier Harmony is a sweeter demi-sec for dessert.

Half-bottles ~ White ~ France.title: French white half-bottles
Half-bottles ~ White ~ France.line: Vouvray Demi-Sec, Chablis Montmains, Meursault and Bourgogne Blanc. Chablis for oysters, Meursault for richer fish, and Huet when a touch of sweetness helps a spicy dish.

Half-bottles ~ White ~ Germany.title: German white half-bottles
Half-bottles ~ White ~ Germany.line: Auslese Rieslings from Dönnhoff, Dr. Hermann and Keller: sweet, bright and fine. Pour them with dessert, foie gras or blue cheese, or with a spicy dish.

Half-bottles ~ White ~ Austria.title: Austrian white half-bottles
Half-bottles ~ White ~ Austria.line: Schloss Gobelsburg Grüner Veltliner and Riesling from the Kamptal: dry, peppery or mineral whites for fish, vegetables and lighter courses.

Half-bottles ~ White ~ United States.title: American white half-bottles
Half-bottles ~ White ~ United States.line: A Sonoma Chardonnay and a Napa Viognier: round, ripe whites for a guest who likes California richness.

Half-bottles ~ Red ~ France.title: French red half-bottles
Half-bottles ~ Red ~ France.line: Burgundy, Bordeaux classed growths, Rhône and Beaujolais in half bottle. Mouton and Las Cases for a treat, Jadot Beaujolais-Villages for value, Gouges Nuits-Saint-Georges for beef.

Half-bottles ~ Red ~ Italy.title: Italian red half-bottles
Half-bottles ~ Red ~ Italy.line: Barbaresco from Gaja, La Spinetta and Ronchi, and Gaja's Magari from the Tuscan coast. Fragrant, firm Nebbiolo for beef and game.

Half-bottles ~ Red ~ United States.title: American red half-bottles
Half-bottles ~ Red ~ United States.line: Napa Cabernet and Merlot, Oregon and Sonoma Pinot Noir and Ridge Zinfandel. Opus One and Diamond Creek for a treat; La Crema or Bethel Heights for a lighter red.

Half-bottles ~ Red ~ Argentina.title: Argentine red half-bottle
Half-bottles ~ Red ~ Argentina.line: Catena Malbec: dark, ripe and smooth, a friendly half bottle for steak.

Large Formats ~ Champagne • Large Format.title: Champagne in large format
Large Formats ~ Champagne • Large Format.line: Champagne magnums and bigger, from house blends to Cristal, Salon and Dom Ruinart. A magnum serves a table of six to eight; Methuselahs and larger need the sommelier.

Large Formats ~ Sparkling • Large Format.title: Sparkling in large format
Large Formats ~ Sparkling • Large Format.line: Austrian sparkling magnums from Bründlmayer and Schloss Gobelsburg, made the Champagne way: crisp, elegant and good value for a big toast.

Large Formats ~ White • Large Format ~ U.title: American white magnums
Large Formats ~ White • Large Format ~ U.line: Au Bon Climat, Far Niente and Mayacamas Chardonnay in magnum: from fresh Santa Barbara to rich Napa.

Large Formats ~ White • Large Format ~ A.title: Austrian white magnums
Large Formats ~ White • Large Format ~ A.line: Kamptal Riesling from Hirsch and Schloss Gobelsburg, and Gobelsburg's traditional Tradition. Dry, mineral and fine with seafood.

Large Formats ~ White • Large Format ~ G.title: German white magnums
Large Formats ~ White • Large Format ~ G.line: Dönnhoff and J.J. Prüm Riesling in magnum. Ask the sommelier which are dry and which carry sweetness before pouring.

Large Formats ~ White • Large Format ~ F.title: French white magnums
Large Formats ~ White • Large Format ~ F.line: Chablis, Meursault, Corton-Charlemagne, Alsace Riesling, Muscadet, Sancerre and Grange des Pères in magnum and larger. Muscadet and Chablis for oysters; Meursault and Corton-Charlemagne for richer dishes.

Large Formats ~ Rosé • Large Format.title: Rosé in large format
Large Formats ~ Rosé • Large Format.line: Sancerre and Provence rosé in magnum: pale, dry and a cheerful choice for a big table.

Large Formats ~ Red • Large Format ~ Fra.title: French red magnums
Large Formats ~ Red • Large Format ~ Fra.line: Bordeaux classed growths, Burgundy grand crus, Châteauneuf-du-Pape, Bandol and Beaujolais in magnum and larger. From Morgon for fun to Romanée-Conti for a once in a lifetime night.

Large Formats ~ Red • Large Format ~ Ita.title: Italian red magnums
Large Formats ~ Red • Large Format ~ Ita.line: Barolo, Barbaresco, Brunello, Amarone and Super Tuscans in magnum, with Quintarelli and Oddero well represented. Firm, food loving wines for beef and game.

Large Formats ~ Red • Large Format ~ Spa.title: Spanish red magnum
Large Formats ~ Red • Large Format ~ Spa.line: Remelluri Gran Reserva Rioja in magnum: mature, savoury and fine, a lovely bottle for lamb.

Large Formats ~ Red • Large Format ~ Uni.title: American red magnums
Large Formats ~ Red • Large Format ~ Uni.line: Napa Cabernet from Opus One, BOND, Heitz and Spottswoode, Oregon and California Pinot Noir and more, in magnum and larger. Ask Cabernet or Pinot, and the budget.

Sustainable Selections ~ White.title: Sustainable whites
Sustainable Selections ~ White.line: A Rully, a Bandol and an Alsace grand cru Muscat from organic, natural or biodynamic growers. Aromatic, textured whites for seafood and vegetables.

Sustainable Selections ~ Red.title: Sustainable reds
Sustainable Selections ~ Red.line: Natural, organic and biodynamic reds from Umbria, Etna, Friuli, Beaujolais, Cornas and Australia. Many are lighter and fresher than classic reds; ask whether the guest is adventurous.

Champagne ~ Grower Producers ~ Montagne.title: Growers: Montagne de Reims
Champagne ~ Grower Producers ~ Montagne.line: Family growers from the Pinot Noir villages around Reims, such as Bouzy and Ambonnay: fuller, red-fruited Champagne with body. Steer the guest who likes rich bubbles here, or toward Blanc de Noirs for food.

Champagne ~ Grower Producers ~ Vallée de.title: Growers: Vallée de la Marne
Champagne ~ Grower Producers ~ Vallée de.line: Growers along the Marne river, where Meunier and Pinot Noir dominate: fruity, generous, food-friendly Champagne, often good value. Ask whether the guest wants something round and easy or a single parcel to explore.

Champagne ~ Grower Producers ~ Côtes de.title: Growers: Côte des Blancs
Champagne ~ Grower Producers ~ Côtes de.line: Chardonnay country south of Épernay: Le Mesnil, Avize, Cramant, Vertus. Expect crisp, chalky, elegant Blanc de Blancs, superb with oysters and seafood. Selosse and Agrapart are the cult names; ask the budget first.

Champagne ~ Grower Producers ~ Aube.title: Growers: Aube
Champagne ~ Grower Producers ~ Aube.line: The Côte des Bar in the south of Champagne, Pinot Noir country closer to Burgundy than Reims. Ripe, fruit-driven wines, often low in dosage. A good corner for a curious guest at a gentler price.

Champagne ~ Grande Marques.title: The great houses
Champagne ~ Grande Marques.line: The famous names, from Piper-Heidsieck and Veuve Clicquot to Krug, Cristal, Dom Pérignon and Salon, plus magnums and giant bottles. Ask the budget and the occasion; most guests who name a brand want that brand.

International ~ Sparkling ~ Australia.title: Australian sparkling
International ~ Sparkling ~ Australia.line: One Tasmanian bottle, Jansz: cool-climate sparkling made the Champagne way, fresh and creamy at a friendly price.

International ~ Sparkling ~ Austria.title: Austrian sparkling
International ~ Sparkling ~ Austria.line: Bründlmayer and Schloss Gobelsburg, two great Kamptal estates, making serious traditional method sparkling wine, two of them in magnum. A strong pick for a Champagne lover open to a surprise.

International ~ Sparkling ~ England.title: English sparkling
International ~ Sparkling ~ England.line: Three bottles from Ridgeview in Sussex, where chalk soils echo Champagne. Crisp and lively, all under $100; a fun talking point for a curious guest.

International ~ Sparkling ~ Portugal.title: Portuguese sparkling
International ~ Sparkling ~ Portugal.line: Two magnums from Luis Pato in Bairrada, sparkling wines from local grapes. Good for a table of four or more who want something unusual.

International ~ Sparkling ~ France.title: French sparkling outside Champagne
International ~ Sparkling ~ France.line: One bottle from the Jura, Domaine du Pélican, the d'Angerville family's estate. A sparkling wine for a guest who likes Burgundy and wants something outside Champagne.

International ~ Sparkling ~ Italy.title: Italian sparkling
International ~ Sparkling ~ Italy.line: Franciacorta from Ca' del Bosco, Trento from Ferrari, and a cloudy col fondo from the Veneto. Ask whether the guest wants classic and polished or rustic and dry.

International ~ Sparkling ~ United State.title: American sparkling
International ~ Sparkling ~ United State.line: Oregon and California bubbles from Argyle, Domaine Carneros, Roederer Estate, Schramsberg and others, $70 to $255. A natural pick for a guest who loves Champagne houses and wants their American cousins.

France ~ Loire ~ White ~ Muscadet Sèvre-.title: Muscadet
France ~ Loire ~ White ~ Muscadet Sèvre-.line: Crisp, saline whites from Melon de Bourgogne near the Atlantic, the classic match for raw oysters. These are serious, lees-aged Muscadets from top growers, $70 to $150.

France ~ Loire ~ White ~ Anjou-Saumur.title: Anjou and Saumur
France ~ Loire ~ White ~ Anjou-Saumur.line: Dry Chenin Blanc, much of it Savennières, plus Clos Rougeard's rare Brézé. Firm, honeyed and mineral whites for rich fish and poultry; Nicolas Joly's wines may want air, so check with the sommelier.

France ~ Loire ~ White ~ Vouvray & Toura.title: Vouvray and Touraine
France ~ Loire ~ White ~ Vouvray & Toura.line: Chenin Blanc from dry (Sec) to gently sweet (Demi-Sec) to sweet (Moelleux), led by Domaine Huet, plus crisp Jasnières. Always confirm the style on the label before you pour; the sweeter ones love spice.

France ~ Loire ~ White ~ Menetou-Salon.title: Menetou-Salon
France ~ Loire ~ White ~ Menetou-Salon.line: A neighbour of Sancerre making similar crisp Sauvignon Blanc at a gentler price. One bottle, from Henri Bourgeois.

France ~ Loire ~ White ~ Montlouis-sur-L.title: Montlouis
France ~ Loire ~ White ~ Montlouis-sur-L.line: Across the river from Vouvray, Montlouis makes Chenin Blanc from dry to sweet. One bottle, from François Chidaine; ask the sommelier how dry it is.

France ~ Loire ~ White ~ Pouilly-Fumé &.title: Sancerre and Pouilly-Fumé
France ~ Loire ~ White ~ Pouilly-Fumé &.line: The home of crisp Sauvignon Blanc, here at its most serious: Dagueneau, Cotat, Vatan and Vacheron, from $65 to rare bottles. For a guest who orders Sancerre, ask the budget and offer one classic and one splurge.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Bourgogne.title: Bourgogne
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Bourgogne.line: Regional white Burgundy and Aligoté from great growers, Leflaive, Roulot, Coche-Dury and others, often the best value way into a famous name. Most are under $150; some, like Coche-Dury, are collector's bottles.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Chablis Gran.title: Chablis grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Chablis Gran.line: The seven grand crus on one hill above Chablis: Les Clos, Valmur, Vaudésir, Preuses, Bougros, Grenouilles, Blanchot. Rich yet stony, $195 and up. Raveneau and Dauvissat are the rarest; ask the budget.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Chablis Prem.title: Chablis premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Chablis Prem.line: Crisp, mineral Chardonnay from named slopes such as Montée de Tonnerre, Vaillons and Montmains. The sweet spot for oysters and fish; most sit between $100 and $250.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Chablis.title: Chablis
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Chablis.line: Village Chablis and Petit Chablis: lean, lemony, stony Chardonnay with little or no oak, $80 to $300. A sure choice for raw oysters and a guest who dislikes buttery whites.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Morey-Saint-.title: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Morey-Saint-.line: Rare whites from red wine country: Monts Luisants from Dujac and Ponsot, whose bottling is old-vine Aligoté. Collector's bottles, around $400.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Vougeot Prem.title: Vougeot premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Vougeot Prem.line: Le Clos Blanc de Vougeot from Domaine de la Vougeraie, a rare white in red country, offered only in large bottles. A showpiece for a big table.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Pernand-Verg.title: Pernand-Vergelesses premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Pernand-Verg.line: Sous Frétille, a fine, crisp white premier cru beside the hill of Corton, from Deux Montille and Dugat-Py. Good value for the quality.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Pernand-Verg.title: Pernand-Vergelesses
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Pernand-Verg.line: Village whites from beside the hill of Corton, fresh and mineral, $65 to $110. Among the best values in white Burgundy.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Corton-Charl.title: Corton-Charlemagne
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Corton-Charl.line: The great white grand cru on the hill of Corton: powerful, mineral and long-lived. From Bouchard and Tollot-Beaut to Coche-Dury and Domaine de la Romanée-Conti, $550 to $5,500. Involve the sommelier.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Beaune Premi.title: Beaune premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Beaune Premi.line: White Beaune premier crus, including Jadot's Grèves Le Clos Blanc: round, ripe Chardonnay at fair prices, $105 to $230.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Beaune.title: Beaune
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Beaune.line: One white village Beaune from Domaine de la Vougeraie: round and approachable.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Saint-Romain.title: Saint-Romain
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Saint-Romain.line: Crisp whites from a cool, high village behind Meursault, around $110. Good value for a guest who likes Meursault but not its price.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Meursault Pr.title: Meursault premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Meursault Pr.line: Charmes, Genevrières, Perrières, Poruzots, Santenots: rich, nutty, creamy Chardonnay with depth, mostly $160 to $500 and beyond. Ideal with butter sauces and richer fish.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Meursault.title: Meursault
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Meursault.line: Village Meursault, often from named sites like Les Tillets or Les Luchets: rich and nutty. Prices run from $115 to collector levels for Coche-Dury and Roulot, so ask the budget first.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Saint-Aubin.title: Saint-Aubin premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Saint-Aubin.line: Crisp, mineral whites from the slopes behind Puligny and Chassagne, $135 to $400. The value secret of white Burgundy; Hubert Lamy is the star.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Saint-Aubin.title: Saint-Aubin
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Saint-Aubin.line: Village Saint-Aubin, mostly Hubert Lamy and Marc Colin: precise, mineral Chardonnay.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Puligny-Mont.title: Puligny-Montrachet premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Puligny-Mont.line: Floral, precise, elegant Chardonnay: Pucelles, Folatières, Combettes, Clavoillon, Referts. Leflaive, Sauzet and Carillon lead, mostly $200 to $600. For the guest who wants classic, refined white Burgundy.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Puligny-Mont.title: Puligny-Montrachet
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Puligny-Mont.line: Village Puligny: fine and floral, $230 to $665. A strong sweet spot pick for fish and seafood.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Montrachet G.title: Le Montrachet
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Montrachet G.line: The most famous white vineyard in the world, from Domaine de la Romanée-Conti, Ponsot, Sauzet and Jadot, $1,050 to $11,500. Always bring in the sommelier.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Chevalier-Mo.title: Chevalier-Montrachet
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Chevalier-Mo.line: The grand cru just above Le Montrachet: tense, mineral and long, from Leflaive, Jadot's Les Demoiselles and Niellon. A celebration white.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Bâtard-Montr.title: Bâtard-Montrachet
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Bâtard-Montr.line: The grand cru below Le Montrachet: rich, broad and powerful Chardonnay, $460 to $2,900. For the grandest seafood and butter sauces.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Bienvenue-Bâ.title: Bienvenues-Bâtard-Montrachet
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Bienvenue-Bâ.line: A small grand cru beside Bâtard, a touch more delicate. From Leflaive, Faiveley and Paul Pernot.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Chassagne-Mo.title: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Chassagne-Mo.line: Rich, nutty and round: Caillerets, Morgeot, Clos Saint-Jean, La Maltroie, Les Champs Gain, mostly $150 to $500. Great with crab, shrimp and cream sauces.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Chassagne-Mo.title: Chassagne-Montrachet
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Chassagne-Mo.line: Village Chassagne: rich and nutty, $160 to $350, a good sweet spot pick for richer dishes.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Other Côte d.title: Other Côte d'Or whites
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Other Côte d.line: Whites from less famous villages, Ladoix, Auxey-Duresses, Savigny, Santenay, the Hautes Côtes, often from famous estates. Mostly under $150: the best value white Burgundy on the list.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Côte Chalonn.title: Côte Chalonnaise
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Côte Chalonn.line: Rully, Mercurey, Givry, Montagny and Bouzeron, just south of the Côte d'Or: crisp, fresh whites around $100. A sure value pick.

France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Mâconnais.title: Mâconnais
France ~ Burgundy ~ White ~ Mâconnais.line: Southern Burgundy: Mâcon and Pouilly-Fuissé, riper and rounder Chardonnay, $80 to $325. Leflaive's and Lafon's Mâcons are great value doors into famous names.

France ~ Alsace ~ White ~ Gewürztraminer.title: Gewürztraminer
France ~ Alsace ~ White ~ Gewürztraminer.line: Exotic, rose and lychee-scented whites, often off-dry, some late harvest. Beautiful with spice and rich dishes; confirm sweetness before pouring.

France ~ Alsace ~ White ~ Pinot Gris.title: Pinot Gris
France ~ Alsace ~ White ~ Pinot Gris.line: Rich, smoky, textured Alsace whites, sometimes with sweetness. Good with pork, poultry and spiced Creole flavours.

France ~ Alsace ~ White ~ Riesling.title: Alsace Riesling
France ~ Alsace ~ White ~ Riesling.line: Mostly dry, firm, mineral Riesling, from Trimbach's Clos Ste Hune to Boxler's grand crus. Ideal for a guest who wants Riesling without sweetness.

France ~ Alsace ~ White ~ Sylvaner.title: Sylvaner
France ~ Alsace ~ White ~ Sylvaner.line: Light, fresh, gently herbal Alsace whites, $55 to $75. Easy value bottles.

France ~ Alsace ~ White ~ Other Varietie.title: Other Alsace whites
France ~ Alsace ~ White ~ Other Varietie.line: Muscat, Pinot Blanc, Edelzwicker blends and Marcel Deiss's field blends: aromatic and easygoing, mostly under $150.

France ~ Rhône~ White ~ Condrieu.title: Condrieu
France ~ Rhône~ White ~ Condrieu.line: Viognier at its finest: apricot, flowers and a silky texture, $145 to $250. Wonderful with crab and gentle spice.

France ~ Rhône~ White ~ Hermitage.title: White Hermitage
France ~ Rhône~ White ~ Hermitage.line: Marsanne-led, rich, honeyed and long-lived, from Chave, Jaboulet, Guigal and others. A grand white for rich fish and veal.

France ~ Rhône~ White ~ Châteauneuf-duPa.title: White Châteauneuf-du-Pape
France ~ Rhône~ White ~ Châteauneuf-duPa.line: Round, floral southern whites, a rare style. Two bottles.

France ~ Rhône~ White ~ Other Rhône.title: Other Rhône whites
France ~ Rhône~ White ~ Other Rhône.line: Crozes-Hermitage, Saint-Péray, Côtes du Rhône and southern villages, many from great red wine estates. Round, aromatic and good value, mostly under $150.

France ~ Other ~ White ~ Bordeaux.title: White Bordeaux
France ~ Other ~ White ~ Bordeaux.line: Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon from Pessac-Léognan and beyond: crisp, citrusy, lightly oaked. From $60 to Haut-Brion at $2,500; great with seafood.

France ~ Other ~ White ~ Jurançon.title: Jurançon
France ~ Other ~ White ~ Jurançon.line: One dry white from the foothills of the Pyrenees, crisp and exotic.

France ~ Other ~ White ~ Savoie & Jura.title: Jura
France ~ Other ~ White ~ Savoie & Jura.line: Chardonnay and Savagnin from the Jura, including Vin Jaune, aged under a veil of yeast, nutty and intense. Distinctive and savoury; check the guest wants something unusual.

France ~ Other ~ White ~ Provence.title: Provence whites
France ~ Other ~ White ~ Provence.line: Château Simone, Tempier, Trévallon and the Luberon: herbal, round whites. Ask whether the guest wants rare or easygoing.

France ~ Other ~ White ~ Languedoc-Rouss.title: Languedoc whites
France ~ Other ~ White ~ Languedoc-Rouss.line: Grange des Pères, a cult white, and a Limoux Chenin Blanc: from value to rare.

Austria & Hungary ~ Kamptal.title: Kamptal
Austria & Hungary ~ Kamptal.line: Bründlmayer, Hirsch, Loimer and Schloss Gobelsburg: dry Riesling from the Heiligenstein and peppery Grüner Veltliner. From easy half-bottles to rare magnums.

Austria & Hungary ~ Kremstal.title: Kremstal
Austria & Hungary ~ Kremstal.line: Grüner Veltliner from around the town of Krems, mostly crisp, peppery and good value.

Austria & Hungary ~ Wachau.title: Wachau
Austria & Hungary ~ Wachau.line: Austria's most famous whites, steep Danube terraces. Federspiel is the lighter dry style, Smaragd the ripest; all dry. Great with rich fish.

Austria & Hungary ~ Burgenland.title: Burgenland
Austria & Hungary ~ Burgenland.line: One bottle from Gut Oggau, a biodynamic estate: a textured Grüner Veltliner blend.

Austria & Hungary ~ Hungary.title: Hungary
Austria & Hungary ~ Hungary.line: One dry Furmint from Tokaj, crisp and smoky, $75.

Germany ~ White ~ Riesling ~ Mosel.title: Mosel
Germany ~ White ~ Riesling ~ Mosel.line: Light, delicate, slate-grown Riesling, often low in alcohol, from Egon Müller, JJ Prüm and Peter Lauer. Many are gently sweet; Trocken means dry.

Germany ~ White ~ Riesling ~ Rheingau.title: Rheingau
Germany ~ White ~ Riesling ~ Rheingau.line: Fuller, firm Riesling from J.B. Becker, Robert Weil and Georg Breuer, much of it dry. Becker's wines are released with age.

Germany ~ White ~ Riesling ~ Rheinhessen.title: Rheinhessen
Germany ~ White ~ Riesling ~ Rheinhessen.line: Keller and Gunderloch: powerful dry grand crus and a few gently sweet Kabinetts. Keller's GGs are among the most sought-after whites in Germany.

Germany ~ White ~ Riesling ~ Nahe.title: Nahe
Germany ~ White ~ Riesling ~ Nahe.line: Dönnhoff, Emrich-Schönleber, Diel, Hexamer and Kruger-Rumpf: Riesling between Mosel delicacy and Pfalz power, dry and sweet.

Germany ~ White ~ Riesling ~ Pfalz.title: Pfalz
Germany ~ White ~ Riesling ~ Pfalz.line: Warmer and fuller, mostly dry Riesling from Bürklin-Wolf, Von Winning and von Buhl. Good with richer dishes.

Germany ~ White ~ Other ~ Rheinhessen.title: Other Rheinhessen whites
Germany ~ White ~ Other ~ Rheinhessen.line: Two Chardonnay-based whites from Moritz Kissinger and Knewitz: fresh and fine.

Germany ~ White ~ Other ~ Franken.title: Franken
Germany ~ White ~ Other ~ Franken.line: One dry Silvaner from Hans Wirsching, earthy and good value.

Germany ~ White ~ Other ~ Pfalz.title: Other Pfalz whites
Germany ~ White ~ Other ~ Pfalz.line: One Sauvignon Blanc from Von Winning.

Italy & Greece ~ White ~ Greece.title: Greece
Italy & Greece ~ White ~ Greece.line: One Assyrtiko from Santorini, crisp and saline, great with seafood.

Italy & Greece ~ White ~ Italy.title: Italy
Italy & Greece ~ White ~ Italy.line: Whites from the Alps to Campania and Liguria: Terlano, Friulano, Petite Arvine, Falanghina, Vitovska. Mostly crisp; some are textured.

United States ~ Chardonnay ~ California.title: Sonoma Chardonnay
United States ~ Chardonnay ~ California.line: Cooler, often brighter Chardonnay from the Sonoma Coast and Russian River: Kistler, Ramey, Hirsch, Lioco. Good with fish and crab.

United States ~ Chardonnay ~ California.title: Napa Chardonnay
United States ~ Chardonnay ~ California.line: Classic Napa: Montelena, Cakebread, Far Niente, Kongsgaard and the lean mountain wines of Mayacamas and Stony Hill. Ask rich or restrained.

United States ~ Chardonnay ~ California.title: Central Coast Chardonnay
United States ~ Chardonnay ~ California.line: Santa Barbara, Monterey and Mount Harlan: cool-climate, often lean and mineral Chardonnay, mostly under $150. Great value.

United States ~ Chardonnay ~ Oregon & Wa.title: Oregon and Washington Chardonnay
United States ~ Chardonnay ~ Oregon & Wa.line: Fresh, taut Chardonnay from Willamette Valley, plus library bottles from Eyrie. A strong pick for a Burgundy lover.

United States ~ Sauvignon Blanc ~ Califo.title: California Sauvignon Blanc
United States ~ Sauvignon Blanc ~ Califo.line: From Duckhorn and Mondavi to the richer, textured Arkenstone and Jonata Flor, $35 to $270.

United States ~ Sauvignon Blanc ~ Oregon.title: Oregon Sauvignon Blanc
United States ~ Sauvignon Blanc ~ Oregon.line: One bottle from Patricia Green, crisp and fresh.

United States ~ Other ~ White ~ Unique W.title: Unique American whites
United States ~ Other ~ White ~ Unique W.line: Unusual grapes and blends: Au Bon Climat's Hildegard, Matthiasson's Ribolla Gialla, Finger Lakes Riesling and more. Ask what the guest likes and suggest a discovery.

International ~ White ~ Argentina.title: Argentina
International ~ White ~ Argentina.line: High-altitude and Patagonian Chardonnay from Catena Zapata, Chacra and El Enemigo.

International ~ White ~ Australia.title: Australia
International ~ White ~ Australia.line: Chardonnay from Victoria, Riesling from Clare and Tasmania, Hunter Semillon. Giaconda is a rare collector's bottle.

International ~ White ~ Chile.title: Chile
International ~ White ~ Chile.line: One Chardonnay from the Atacama desert, crisp and saline.

International ~ White ~ New Zealand.title: New Zealand
International ~ White ~ New Zealand.line: Chardonnay from Kumeu River near Auckland, fine and taut, $50 to $155.

International ~ White ~ South Africa.title: South Africa
International ~ White ~ South Africa.line: Old-vine Chenin Blanc and white blends from Swartland and Stellenbosch, led by Sadie. Textured, characterful whites with great value at the lower end.

Rosé ~ France.title: French rosé
Rosé ~ France.line: Pale, dry Provence rosé, Whispering Angel and friends, then Tempier's Bandol and Sancerre from Crochet and Cotat for food. Magnums suit a table.

Rosé ~ Italy.title: Italian rosé
Rosé ~ Italy.line: One Ligurian rosé from the Ciliegiolo grape, fresh and fruity.

Rosé ~ United States.title: American rosé
Rosé ~ United States.line: Two bottles, Presqu'ile from Santa Barbara and Bon Vé; ask the sommelier about Bon Vé.

France ~ Loire ~ Red ~ Saumur-Champigny.title: Saumur-Champigny
France ~ Loire ~ Red ~ Saumur-Champigny.line: Cabernet Franc from the limestone around Saumur, fresh and red fruited, from good value to the cult Clos Rougeard. Steer lighter eaters here.

France ~ Loire ~ Red ~ Bourgueil.title: Bourgueil
France ~ Loire ~ Red ~ Bourgueil.line: Firmer, darker Cabernet Franc from the Touraine. Breton and Amirault are the names; a smart swap for a Bordeaux drinker who wants something lighter.

France ~ Loire ~ Red ~ Chinon.title: Chinon
France ~ Loire ~ Red ~ Chinon.line: Cabernet Franc from the Vienne valley: red cherry, pencil shavings and a fresh finish. Great value; Joguet is the classic name.

France ~ Loire ~ Red ~ Muscadet & Sancer.title: Muscadet and Sancerre reds
France ~ Loire ~ Red ~ Muscadet & Sancer.line: Light Pinot Noir from the Loire's white wine country. Suggest for fish or chicken when a guest wants red.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Bourgogne.title: Bourgogne and regional reds
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Bourgogne.line: Regional Pinot Noir, Passe-Tout-Grains and Côte de Nuits-Villages from top growers: the cheapest route to a famous name. Good for guests who want Burgundy under a modest budget.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Marsannay.title: Marsannay
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Marsannay.line: The northernmost village of the Côte de Nuits: light, crisp, red fruited Pinot Noir at fair prices.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Fixin Premier.title: Fixin premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Fixin Premier.line: Sturdy, earthy reds from Gevrey's northern neighbour, including Gelin's Clos Napoléon. Good value for a guest who likes firm red.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Fixin.title: Fixin
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Fixin.line: Village Fixin: sturdy, rustic Pinot Noir next to Gevrey at friendlier prices.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Ruchottes-Cham.title: Ruchottes-Chambertin grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Ruchottes-Cham.line: A small Gevrey grand cru on thin, rocky soil, giving fine, mineral wine. Rare; a collector's pick.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Mazis-Chambert.title: Mazis-Chambertin grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Mazis-Chambert.line: A Gevrey grand cru next to Clos de Bèze, dark and powerful. For guests who want depth.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Griotte-Chambe.title: Griotte-Chambertin grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Griotte-Chambe.line: The smallest Gevrey grand cru, often described as cherry scented and silky. Very rare.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Chambertin - C.title: Chambertin-Clos de Bèze grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Chambertin - C.line: One of Burgundy's two most famous Gevrey grand crus, majestic and long lived. Celebration price; decant.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Charmes-Chambe.title: Charmes-Chambertin grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Charmes-Chambe.line: The largest and most approachable Gevrey grand cru: generous, rounded fruit. The gentlest grand cru step for a Gevrey lover.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Chambertin Gra.title: Chambertin grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Chambertin Gra.line: The king of Gevrey: powerful, deep and long lived. A celebration bottle; involve the sommelier.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Latricières-Ch.title: Latricières-Chambertin grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Latricières-Ch.line: A Gevrey grand cru next to Chambertin, firm and spicy. Good for game and beef.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Mazoyères-Cham.title: Mazoyères-Chambertin grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Mazoyères-Cham.line: A Gevrey grand cru that may also be sold as Charmes; rich and ripe. A relative value among grand crus.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Chapelle-Chamb.title: Chapelle-Chambertin grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Chapelle-Chamb.line: A Gevrey grand cru below Clos de Bèze, finer and more fragrant than most. Rare.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Gevrey-Chamber.title: Gevrey-Chambertin premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Gevrey-Chamber.line: Dark, firm Pinot Noir with structure; Clos Saint-Jacques, Cazetiers and Lavaux Saint-Jacques are the famous names. Ask the budget; this page runs from moderate to grand cru prices.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Gevrey-Chamber.title: Gevrey-Chambertin
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Gevrey-Chamber.line: Village Gevrey: the deepest, most structured Pinot Noir of the Côte de Nuits. A steady choice for steak.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Clos de la Roc.title: Clos de la Roche grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Clos de la Roc.line: Morey-Saint-Denis's greatest grand cru, deep and mineral. Dujac and Ponsot are the names.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Clos Saint-Den.title: Clos Saint-Denis grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Clos Saint-Den.line: A Morey grand cru, finer and more fragrant than Clos de la Roche. For guests who love perfume.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Clos des Lambr.title: Clos des Lambrays grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Clos des Lambr.line: A Morey grand cru almost wholly owned by one estate, fragrant and fine.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Morey-Saint-De.title: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Morey-Saint-De.line: Between Gevrey and Chambolle in style: fragrant fruit with structure. Good value premier crus.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Morey-Saint-De.title: Morey-Saint-Denis
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Morey-Saint-De.line: Village Morey: fragrant, balanced Pinot Noir, often a better buy than its famous neighbours.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Bonnes Mares G.title: Bonnes-Mares grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Bonnes Mares G.line: A grand cru shared by Chambolle and Morey, firmer and darker than Musigny. Celebration price.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Musigny Grand.title: Musigny grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Musigny Grand.line: Chambolle's greatest grand cru, silk and perfume. Among the most prized wines on the list.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Chambolle-Musi.title: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Chambolle-Musi.line: The most fragrant, silky Pinot Noir of the Côte de Nuits; Les Amoureuses is the famous name. For guests who love elegance.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Chambolle-Musi.title: Chambolle-Musigny
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Chambolle-Musi.line: Village Chambolle: perfumed, silky and light on its feet. Lovely with duck or chicken.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Vougeot Premie.title: Vougeot premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Vougeot Premie.line: Premier cru from the village of Vougeot outside the great Clos, fragrant and fine.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Clos Vougeot G.title: Clos de Vougeot grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Clos Vougeot G.line: A large walled grand cru shared by many owners, so the producer matters most. Rich, firm wine; ask the budget and steer by name.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Echézeaux Gran.title: Échezeaux grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Echézeaux Gran.line: A Vosne grand cru, spicy and fragrant, often the gentlest priced grand cru from a great producer.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Grands-Echézea.title: Grands-Échezeaux grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Grands-Echézea.line: A smaller, deeper grand cru next to Clos de Vougeot. Celebration price.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Richebourg Gra.title: Richebourg grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Richebourg Gra.line: A Vosne grand cru of great richness and spice. Very high prices; involve the sommelier.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Romanée-Saint-.title: Romanée-Saint-Vivant grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Romanée-Saint-.line: A Vosne grand cru of great finesse and perfume, below Romanée-Conti. Celebration only.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Romanée-Conti.title: Romanée-Conti grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Romanée-Conti.line: The most famous vineyard in Burgundy, wholly owned by the Domaine de la Romanée-Conti. Only with the sommelier.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ La Tâche Grand.title: La Tâche grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ La Tâche Grand.line: A Vosne grand cru wholly owned by the Domaine de la Romanée-Conti, spicy and profound. Only with the sommelier.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Vosne-Romanée.title: Vosne-Romanée premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Vosne-Romanée.line: Velvety, spicy, refined Pinot Noir from Burgundy's most famous village. Beaux Monts, Brûlées and Suchots are names to know.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Vosne-Romanée.title: Vosne-Romanée
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Vosne-Romanée.line: Village Vosne: silky, spicy Pinot Noir from the home of the grandest grand crus.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Nuits-Saint-Ge.title: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Nuits-Saint-Ge.line: Dark, firm, earthy Pinot Noir with structure; Les Saints-Georges and Vaucrains are famous. Good with beef and game.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Nuits-Saint-Ge.title: Nuits-Saint-Georges
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Nuits-Saint-Ge.line: Village Nuits: sturdy, dark fruited Pinot Noir. A steady choice for red meat.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Pernand-Vergel.title: Pernand-Vergelesses premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Pernand-Vergel.line: Fresh, fine reds from the village behind Corton. Good value.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Pernand-Vergel.title: Pernand-Vergelesses
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Pernand-Vergel.line: Light, fresh reds from the village behind the hill of Corton. Good value.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Corton Grand C.title: Corton grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Corton Grand C.line: The only red grand cru of the Côte de Beaune, firm and earthy. Bressandes and Clos du Roi are the names; often the best value grand cru.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Savigny-lès-Be.title: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Savigny-lès-Be.line: Fresh, red fruited premier crus at gentle prices. Lavières is a name to know.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Savigny-lès-Be.title: Savigny-lès-Beaune
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Savigny-lès-Be.line: Village Savigny: light, fresh Pinot Noir and a reliable value.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Beaune Premier.title: Beaune premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Beaune Premier.line: Round, red fruited Pinot Noir from the wine capital; the big houses own much of it. Good with poultry and pork.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Beaune.title: Beaune
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Beaune.line: Village Beaune: soft, red fruited and approachable.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Pommard Premie.title: Pommard premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Pommard Premie.line: The firmest, darkest reds of the Côte de Beaune; Rugiens and Épenots are the famous names. Good with beef.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Pommard.title: Pommard
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Pommard.line: Village Pommard: sturdy, dark fruited Pinot Noir. For guests who want body.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Volnay Premier.title: Volnay premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Volnay Premier.line: The most fragrant, silky reds of the Côte de Beaune; Clos des Chênes, Caillerets and Santenots are names to know. Lovely with poultry.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Volnay.title: Volnay
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Volnay.line: Village Volnay: fragrant, silky and charming.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Monthélie.title: Monthélie
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Monthélie.line: Volnay's neighbour, with similar charm at lower prices; rare Coche-Dury and Roulot bottlings sit here too.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Saint Aubin Pr.title: Saint-Aubin premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Saint Aubin Pr.line: Light, fresh reds from a side valley behind Puligny. Good value.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Chassagne-Mont.title: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Chassagne-Mont.line: Red Chassagne, firm and fresh, from a village better known for white. An insider's value.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Chassagne-Mont.title: Chassagne-Montrachet
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Chassagne-Mont.line: Village red Chassagne: bright, firm Pinot Noir from great white wine families.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Santenay.title: Santenay
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Santenay.line: Sturdy, fruity reds from the southern Côte de Beaune at fair prices.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Maranges Premi.title: Maranges premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Maranges Premi.line: The southernmost Côte de Beaune premier crus: sturdy, fruity and among the best values on the list.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Maranges.title: Maranges
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Maranges.line: Village Maranges: firm, fruity and good value.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Other Côte d'O.title: Other Côte d'Or villages
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Other Côte d'O.line: Smaller villages and Côte Chalonnaise reds: Ladoix, Aloxe-Corton, Blagny, Chorey, Auxey-Duresses and Rully. A place for value and a few rarities.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Mercurey.title: Mercurey
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Mercurey.line: Côte Chalonnaise Pinot Noir: sturdy, red fruited and modestly priced.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Beaujolais.title: Beaujolais
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Beaujolais.line: Gamay from the granite crus: Morgon, Fleurie, Moulin-à-Vent, Brouilly and more. Juicy, fresh and great value; serve slightly cool.

France ~ Bordeaux ~ Red ~ Saint-Estèphe.title: Saint-Estèphe
France ~ Bordeaux ~ Red ~ Saint-Estèphe.line: The firmest Left Bank Cabernet. Cos d'Estournel, Montrose and Calon-Ségur are the names. Good with beef.

France ~ Bordeaux ~ Red ~ Pauillac.title: Pauillac
France ~ Bordeaux ~ Red ~ Pauillac.line: Home of three first growths, Lafite, Latour and Mouton: cassis, cedar and power. Ask the budget; from Légende to first growths.

France ~ Bordeaux ~ Red ~ Saint-Julien.title: Saint-Julien
France ~ Bordeaux ~ Red ~ Saint-Julien.line: Balanced, refined Cabernet; Léoville Las Cases and Ducru-Beaucaillou are the names.

France ~ Bordeaux ~ Red ~ Margaux.title: Margaux
France ~ Bordeaux ~ Red ~ Margaux.line: The most fragrant, silky Left Bank wines; Château Margaux and Palmer lead. For guests who love perfume.

France ~ Bordeaux ~ Red ~ Graves.title: Graves and Pessac-Léognan
France ~ Bordeaux ~ Red ~ Graves.line: Smoky, earthy, silky claret; Haut-Brion and La Mission are the names.

France ~ Bordeaux ~ Red ~ Pomerol.title: Pomerol
France ~ Bordeaux ~ Red ~ Pomerol.line: Soft, plummy Merlot from a small plateau; Pétrus, Lafleur and VCC are the trophies. Ask the budget.

France ~ Bordeaux ~ Red ~ Saint-Émilion.title: Saint-Émilion
France ~ Bordeaux ~ Red ~ Saint-Émilion.line: Merlot and Cabernet Franc on limestone and clay; Cheval Blanc, Figeac and Pavie lead. From friendly to celebration.

France ~ Bordeaux ~ Red ~ Other Bordeaux.title: Other Bordeaux
France ~ Bordeaux ~ Red ~ Other Bordeaux.line: Haut-Médoc, Moulis, Listrac, Castillon and the satellites: classic claret at friendly prices. A great place for value.

Austria, Germany & Lebanon ~ Red ~ Austr.title: Austrian reds
Austria, Germany & Lebanon ~ Red ~ Austr.line: Blaufränkisch from Burgenland and Carnuntum and a Thermenregion Pinot Noir: fresh, peppery, dark cherried reds, a smart swap for a Burgundy or Rhône drinker.

Austria, Germany & Lebanon ~ Red ~ Germa.title: German reds
Austria, Germany & Lebanon ~ Red ~ Germa.line: Pfalz Pinot Noir from Lukas Hammelmann: fresh, red fruited and light. Suggest for fish, poultry or a guest curious about German red.

Austria, Germany & Lebanon ~ Red ~ Leban.title: Lebanese reds
Austria, Germany & Lebanon ~ Red ~ Leban.line: Château Musar from the Bekaa Valley, in several vintages: spicy, earthy and mature. Ask the sommelier which vintage is drinking best.

France ~ Rhone ~ Red ~ Côte-Rôtie.title: Côte-Rôtie
France ~ Rhone ~ Red ~ Côte-Rôtie.line: Fragrant, peppery Syrah from steep slopes, often with a little Viognier. Guigal's single vineyards are the trophies. Ask the budget; decant older bottles.

France ~ Rhone ~ Red ~ St.-Joseph.title: Saint-Joseph
France ~ Rhone ~ Red ~ St.-Joseph.line: Fresh, peppery Syrah from the west bank of the northern Rhône. Good value with lamb.

France ~ Rhone ~ Red ~ Hermitage.title: Hermitage
France ~ Rhone ~ Red ~ Hermitage.line: Powerful, long lived Syrah from a single hill; Chave and La Chapelle are the great names. Celebration price.

France ~ Rhone ~ Red ~ Crozes-Hermitage.title: Crozes-Hermitage
France ~ Rhone ~ Red ~ Crozes-Hermitage.line: Fresh, dark fruited Syrah around the hill of Hermitage. Good value.

France ~ Rhone ~ Red ~ Cornas.title: Cornas
France ~ Rhone ~ Red ~ Cornas.line: The darkest, most powerful Syrah of the northern Rhône. Clape and Allemand are the names; decant.

France ~ Rhone ~ Red ~ Châteauneuf-du-Pa.title: Châteauneuf-du-Pape
France ~ Rhone ~ Red ~ Châteauneuf-du-Pa.line: Warm, spicy Grenache led blends from the southern Rhône. Rayas is the rarity; Beaucastel and Pégau the classics. Ask whether the guest wants fresh or rich.

France ~ Rhone ~ Red ~ Other Côte Du Rhô.title: Other southern Rhône
France ~ Rhone ~ Red ~ Other Côte Du Rhô.line: Gigondas, Vacqueyras, Côtes du Rhône and Vin de France: warm, spicy reds, many from great Châteauneuf names. Great value.

France ~ Other ~ Red ~ Alsace & Lorraine.title: Alsace
France ~ Other ~ Red ~ Alsace & Lorraine.line: Light, fresh Pinot Noir from a white wine region.

France ~ Other ~ Red ~ Jura.title: Jura
France ~ Other ~ Red ~ Jura.line: Light, fresh Pinot Noir and blends from the Jura hills. For Burgundy lovers who like something different.

France ~ Other ~ Red ~ Provence.title: Provence
France ~ Other ~ Red ~ Provence.line: Bandol Mourvèdre, firm and savoury, and Trévallon's Cabernet and Syrah. Good with lamb.

France ~ Other ~ Red ~ Languedoc-Roussil.title: Languedoc
France ~ Other ~ Red ~ Languedoc-Roussil.line: Deep, spicy southern reds, including the cult Grange des Pères. Good value.

France ~ Other ~ Red ~ Other French ~ Re.title: Other French reds
France ~ Other ~ Red ~ Other French ~ Re.line: Cahors Malbec, Corsican, Savoie, Jura Vin de France and rare still reds from Champagne. Ask about the guest's taste and steer by weight.

United States ~ Pinot Noir ~ Mendocino.title: Mendocino Pinot Noir
United States ~ Pinot Noir ~ Mendocino.line: Cool, foggy Anderson Valley and Mendocino hills: bright, fragrant Pinot Noir from Copain, Lioco, Maggy Hawk and others.

United States ~ Pinot Noir ~ Sonoma Coas.title: Sonoma Pinot Noir
United States ~ Pinot Noir ~ Sonoma Coas.line: Russian River, Sonoma Coast and Sonoma Valley Pinot: from plush Kosta Browne and La Crema to taut Hirsch and rare Marcassin. Ask ripe or restrained.

United States ~ Pinot Noir ~ Napa Valley.title: Napa Pinot Noir
United States ~ Pinot Noir ~ Napa Valley.line: A single Napa Valley Pinot Noir, from Brick & Mortar; ask the sommelier about its style.

United States ~ Pinot Noir ~ Central Coa.title: Central Coast Pinot Noir
United States ~ Pinot Noir ~ Central Coa.line: Santa Maria Valley, Sta. Rita Hills, Mount Harlan and Santa Lucia Highlands: Au Bon Climat, Calera and Domaine de la Côte for Burgundy lovers.

United States ~ Pinot Noir ~ Oregon.title: Oregon Pinot Noir
United States ~ Pinot Noir ~ Oregon.line: Willamette Valley Pinot Noir from Eyrie, Bergstrom, Ken Wright and others: fresh, red fruited and earthy, often a step towards Burgundy. Great with salmon and duck.

United States ~ Cabernet Sauvignon ~ Nap.title: Napa Cabernet
United States ~ Cabernet Sauvignon ~ Nap.line: Napa Cabernet from approachable to cult: Caymus and Duckhorn are friendly names, Heitz and Mayacamas classic, Harlan, BOND and Opus One for celebrations. Ask budget first, then ripe or restrained.

United States ~ Cabernet Sauvignon ~ Son.title: Sonoma Cabernet
United States ~ Cabernet Sauvignon ~ Son.line: Alexander and Knights Valley Cabernet from Jordan, Silver Oak, Peter Michael and Vérité: often a little fresher than Napa. A good steer for a guest who wants balance.

United States ~ Cabernet Sauvignon ~ Cen.title: Central Coast Cabernet
United States ~ Cabernet Sauvignon ~ Cen.line: Ridge Monte Bello from the Santa Cruz Mountains, DAOU from Paso Robles and a few others: firm and classic, or rich and modern.

United States ~ Cabernet Sauvignon ~ Was.title: Washington Cabernet
United States ~ Cabernet Sauvignon ~ Was.line: Quilceda Creek and Andrew Will: dark, polished Cabernet with fresh acidity, a smart swap for a Napa drinker.

United States ~ Other ~ Red ~ Syrah.title: American Syrah
United States ~ Other ~ Red ~ Syrah.line: California, Oregon and Washington Syrah: cool climate bottles from Peay, Radio-Coteau and Ex Post Facto are peppery and savoury; Charles Smith and Shafer are bigger.

United States ~ Other ~ Red ~ Merlot.title: American Merlot
United States ~ Other ~ Red ~ Merlot.line: Napa and Sonoma Merlot from Duckhorn, Pride, Keenan and Vérité: plush, plummy and soft. A good steer for a guest who finds Cabernet too firm.

United States ~ Other ~ Red ~ Zinfandel.title: Zinfandel
United States ~ Other ~ Red ~ Zinfandel.line: Ridge, Radio-Coteau, Grgich and others: spicy, brambly reds, from fresh and light to ripe and jammy. Good with richer, spicier dishes.

United States ~ Other ~ Red ~ Cabernet F.title: American Cabernet Franc
United States ~ Other ~ Red ~ Cabernet F.line: Cabernet Franc from Keenan, Vérité, Lang & Reed and Ancient Oak: fragrant, red fruited and lightly herbal. A swap for a Loire or Right Bank lover.

United States ~ Other ~ Red ~ Petite Sir.title: Petite Sirah and friends
United States ~ Other ~ Red ~ Petite Sir.line: Dark, firm reds: Dunn from Howell Mountain and Stag's Leap Ne Cede Malis. Big wines for beef.

United States ~ Other ~ Red ~ Unique Red.title: Unique American reds and blends
United States ~ Other ~ Red ~ Unique Red.line: Blends and unusual grapes: Nebbiolo, Gamay, Pinot Meunier, Malbec and Bordeaux style blends. A page for the curious; ask what they want to try.

Italy ~ Red ~ Valle d'Aosta.title: Valle d'Aosta
Italy ~ Red ~ Valle d'Aosta.line: Alpine reds from the far north west: Grosjean Gamay, light and fresh.

Italy ~ Red ~ Piedmont ~ Barbaresco.title: Barbaresco
Italy ~ Red ~ Piedmont ~ Barbaresco.line: Nebbiolo from Barbaresco: fragrant, firm and often a little more graceful than Barolo. Produttori for value, Gaja and Giacosa for celebration, Roagna for tradition.

Italy ~ Red ~ Piedmont ~ Barolo.title: Barolo
Italy ~ Red ~ Piedmont ~ Barolo.line: Nebbiolo from Barolo: rose, tar and firm tannin, long lived. Ask the budget and whether the guest wants traditional or modern; older vintages from Bartolo Mascarello and Oddero need the sommelier.

Italy ~ Red ~ Other Piemonte & Lombardy.title: Other Piedmont and Lombardy reds
Italy ~ Red ~ Other Piemonte & Lombardy.line: Langhe Nebbiolo, Gaja single vineyards, Dolcetto, Barbera, and alpine Nebbiolo from Carema, Gattinara, Ghemme, Boca and Valtellina: lighter, fragrant cousins of Barolo.

Italy ~ Red ~ Alto Adige & Friuli-Venezi.title: Alto Adige and Friuli reds
Italy ~ Red ~ Alto Adige & Friuli-Venezi.line: Pinot Nero from Alto Adige and Merlot from Friuli: fresh, fine reds from the north east, good with fish and poultry.

Italy ~ Red ~ Veneto.title: Veneto reds
Italy ~ Red ~ Veneto.line: Valpolicella and Amarone, made partly from dried grapes: from fresh Verona reds to rich, deep Amarone from Quintarelli, Dal Forno, Masi and Bertani. Ask how rich the guest likes it.

Italy ~ Red ~ Tuscany ~ Chianti.title: Chianti
Italy ~ Red ~ Tuscany ~ Chianti.line: Sangiovese from Chianti and Chianti Classico: cherry, herbs and fresh acidity. Gran Selezione is the top tier. Great with tomato, veal and pasta.

Italy ~ Red ~ Vino Nobile di Montepulcia.title: Vino Nobile di Montepulciano
Italy ~ Red ~ Vino Nobile di Montepulcia.line: Sangiovese from the hill town of Montepulciano in Tuscany, firm and savoury.

Italy ~ Red ~ Tuscany ~ Brunello & Rosso.title: Brunello di Montalcino
Italy ~ Red ~ Tuscany ~ Brunello & Rosso.line: Sangiovese from Montalcino: deeper and longer lived than Chianti. Ask the budget; Biondi-Santi and Poggio di Sotto for classic finesse, Casanova di Neri for richness.

Italy ~ Red ~ Tuscany ~ IGT & Super Tusc.title: Super Tuscans
Italy ~ Red ~ Tuscany ~ IGT & Super Tusc.line: Tuscan reds outside the old rules, often with Cabernet or Merlot: Sassicaia, Tignanello, Solaia and Masseto. Rich and polished; a natural steer for a Napa or Bordeaux lover.

Italy ~ Red ~ Marche.title: Marche
Italy ~ Red ~ Marche.line: Rosso Piceno from Colleleva: Montepulciano and Sangiovese, juicy and great value.

Italy ~ Red ~ Umbria.title: Umbria
Italy ~ Red ~ Umbria.line: Sagrantino from Montefalco, one of the most tannic reds anywhere, and lighter natural reds. Decant the Sagrantino and serve it with braised meats.

Italy ~ Red ~ Abruzzo.title: Abruzzo
Italy ~ Red ~ Abruzzo.line: Emidio Pepe Montepulciano d'Abruzzo in several vintages: earthy, deep and traditional. Ask the sommelier which is ready.

Italy ~ Red ~ Campania.title: Campania
Italy ~ Red ~ Campania.line: Aglianico from Taurasi and Irpinia: dark, smoky and firm, the great red of the south. Good with lamb and beef.

Italy ~ Red ~ Sicily.title: Sicily
Italy ~ Red ~ Sicily.line: Etna Nerello Mascalese, fragrant and mineral like a southern Burgundy, plus Cerasuolo di Vittoria and Faro. Ask whether the guest likes light and fragrant reds.

Spain ~ Red ~ Galicia.title: Galicia
Spain ~ Red ~ Galicia.line: Mencía and local grapes from steep Atlantic river slopes in Ribeira Sacra, Valdeorras and Ribeiro: light, fresh, peppery reds, a great swap for Pinot lovers.

Spain ~ Red ~ Rioja.title: Rioja
Spain ~ Red ~ Rioja.line: Tempranillo led reds from classic houses and new estates. Crianza is youngest, Reserva older, Gran Reserva longest aged. Ask whether the guest likes mellow and mature or fresh and fruity.

Spain ~ Red ~ Priorat.title: Priorat
Spain ~ Red ~ Priorat.line: Garnacha and Carignan from steep slate in Catalonia: deep, mineral and powerful. Big reds for lamb and beef.

Spain ~ Red ~ Penedes.title: Penedès
Spain ~ Red ~ Penedes.line: Torres Mas La Plana Cabernet and natural Sumoll from Els Jelipins: two very different Catalan reds.

Spain ~ Red ~ Castilla y Leon.title: Castilla y León
Spain ~ Red ~ Castilla y Leon.line: Ribera del Duero Tempranillo, including Vega Sicilia and Pingus, and fresh Bierzo Mencía. Ask rich and dark or fresh and floral.

Spain ~ Red ~ Toro.title: Toro
Spain ~ Red ~ Toro.line: Numanthia Termanthia: powerful old vine Tempranillo from a hot zone on the Duero.

Spain ~ Red ~ Madrid.title: Vinos de Madrid
Spain ~ Red ~ Madrid.line: Mountain Garnacha from west of Madrid: fresh, fragrant and light on its feet.

Spain ~ Red ~ Sierra de Gredos.title: Sierra de Gredos
Spain ~ Red ~ Sierra de Gredos.line: Granite mountain Garnacha from Comando G and Jiménez-Landi: fragrant and fine, often compared to Burgundy.

Spain ~ Red ~ Castilla-La Mancha.title: Castilla-La Mancha
Spain ~ Red ~ Castilla-La Mancha.line: Envínate Albahra from Almansa and Hand Work Garnacha: juicy, good value reds.

Spain ~ Red ~ Canarias.title: Canary Islands
Spain ~ Red ~ Canarias.line: Envínate reds from volcanic Tenerife: Listán Negro and Listán Prieto, light, smoky and fresh. Adventurous and very food friendly.

International - Red ~ Greece.title: Greek reds
International - Red ~ Greece.line: Xinomavro from Naoussa and a Meteora blend: firm, fragrant reds, a fun swap for a Nebbiolo lover.

International - Red ~ Portugal.title: Portuguese reds
International - Red ~ Portugal.line: Baga from Bairrada, Ramisco from sandy Colares and Alicante Bouschet from Alentejo: firm, characterful reds.

International - Red ~ Argentina.title: Argentine reds
International - Red ~ Argentina.line: Mendoza Malbec from Catena, Achával-Ferrer, Zuccardi and Viña Cobos, and a Cabernet: dark, ripe and smooth. A natural steak partner.

International - Red ~ Chile.title: Chilean reds
International - Red ~ Chile.line: Maipo Cabernet, Carmenère and cool Pinot Noir from Itata and the Atacama: good value and fresh.

International - Red ~ South Africa.title: South African reds
International - Red ~ South Africa.line: Pinotage, a Bordeaux blend and Sadie Columella: fresh, balanced reds from the Western Cape.

International - Red ~ Australia.title: Australian reds
International - Red ~ Australia.line: Barossa Shiraz from Penfolds, Torbreck and Amon-Ra, McLaren Vale Grenache and cooler Victorian Pinot and Syrah. Ask big and rich or fresh and light.

International - Red ~ New Zealand.title: New Zealand reds
International - Red ~ New Zealand.line: Central Otago and Marlborough Pinot Noir and a Hawke's Bay Cabernet Merlot: fresh and fine.

Selections from our Birth Year ~ Wine.title: Birth year Bordeaux
Selections from our Birth Year ~ Wine.line: Mature 1946 first growth and Right Bank Bordeaux, from the house's birth year. Celebration bottles; let the sommelier present and decant.

Dessert Wines ~ France.title: French dessert wines
Dessert Wines ~ France.line: Sauternes and Barsac, including Yquem and Climens, sweet Loire Chenin and a Jura half bottle. Honeyed and golden; lovely with bread pudding, fruit and blue cheese.

Dessert Wines ~ Canada.title: Canadian icewine
Dessert Wines ~ Canada.line: Inniskillin Cabernet Franc icewine: sweet, red berried and bright.

Dessert Wines ~ United States.title: American dessert wines
Dessert Wines ~ United States.line: Late harvest wines from Ridge, Grgich and Calera: sweet and fruity, in small bottles.

Dessert Wines ~ Italy.title: Italian dessert wines
Dessert Wines ~ Italy.line: Vin Santo, Torcolato, Moscadello, Pantelleria passito and Quintarelli's sweet wines: nutty, honeyed or apricot sweet. Ask the dessert, then match nuts with Vin Santo and fruit with Moscato.

Dessert Wines ~ Austria & Hungary.title: Austrian dessert wine
Dessert Wines ~ Austria & Hungary.line: Kracher Auslese from Burgenland: honeyed, fresh and fine with fruit desserts.

Fortified Wines ~ France.title: French fortified wine
Fortified Wines ~ France.line: Riveyrac Rivesaltes: long aged sweet wine from Roussillon, nutty and caramel edged.

Fortified Wines ~ Madeira.title: Madeira
Fortified Wines ~ Madeira.line: Single cask Malvasia and Verdelho and a Verdelho solera: tangy, nutty and caramel edged, from medium dry to rich.

Fortified Wines ~ Spain.title: Sherry
Fortified Wines ~ Spain.line: Manzanilla, Pale Cream and an old Valdespino solera: from bone dry and salty to gently sweet.

Fortified Wines ~ Portugal.title: Port
Fortified Wines ~ Portugal.line: Vintage, Late Bottled Vintage, Colheita and Garrafeira Port from the great houses. Vintage Port needs decanting; LBV and tawny are ready to pour. Lovely with chocolate, pecan and blue cheese.
